tm.summary: BrowserStack Test Management: author and organise test cases, plan and track their execution, and report on the results. Everything is scoped to a project, which owns the folders, cases, runs, plans and reports beneath it. Search and filter cases; create and update cases, runs and plans; record results; bulk edit, move, copy, archive and delete; restructure folders; manage tags and custom-field definitions; assign, clone and close runs; review AI duplicate recommendations; read the activity feed and a case's version history; and create, schedule and download reports. Cases are authored and their outcomes recorded here, but tests are not RUN here: execution happens in your own runner or another BrowserStack product. Renaming and deleting a project are not exposed. Destructive capabilities exist and always need explicit human approval.

capabilities.name: assign_test_run_owner

body.name: owner
body.description: The ID of the user to assign as the owner of the test run.

capabilities.intent: Assign a owner to the test run
guidance: The body nests: send the owner inside a `test_run` object, as {"test_run": {"owner": <user id>}}. A flat `owner` is rejected with a 400 naming the missing `test_run` key.

capabilities.name: assign_test_run_test_cases_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Run identifier in TR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to TR-\d+ — unlike the v1 run endpoints, a bare integer is NOT accepted here and returns a routing 404.

body.name: assign_to
body.description: One entry per case (or execution) to reassign. Top level — NOT wrapped in a test_run object, unlike the update calls on this run.

capabilities.intent: Hand specific test cases inside a run to the people who should execute them (or clear their assignee)
guidance: Queued, not applied: the 200 {success: true} only means the job was accepted. Re-read the run's test cases to confirm the assignees actually changed.
`assignee` is an email (or TM user id) resolved inside the run's group. An address that does not resolve is skipped silently — that case keeps its old assignee and nothing is reported.
Send `assignee: null` on an entry to unassign that case.

Each entry must carry `test_case_id` (TC-NNN) or `execution_id`; an entry with neither is dropped. Add `configuration_id` to target one configuration row when the case is mapped to several — omit it and every row for that case is reassigned.
The body is not validated before the 200: a missing or empty `assign_to` still answers 200 {success: true} and changes nothing.
Assignment is reversible — assign again (or to null) to undo.

200.description: Assignment job queued. Body is {success: true}; the assignments are applied asynchronously.

500.description: The job could not be enqueued; nothing was assigned.

DANGER, verified live: an unrecognised key here is SILENTLY DROPPED, so a typo widens the ta

body.name: folder_id
body.description: SOURCE folder to scope the selection to, at top level. Merged into the search scope and it OVERWRITES `q.folder_id` when both are present. Do not confuse it with the DESTINATION, which for move lives at `test_case.destination_folder_id` and for copy at top-level `destination_folder_id`.

body.name: p
body.description: Page of the scoped view, as the UI sends it. Only consulted when `select_all` is true and no `q` is present (the unfiltered folder-count path).

body.name: include_subfolders_tc
body.description: Extend the selection into subfolders of `folder_id`. Compared as the string `true`. The UI sets it for consolidated (non-folder) views.

body.name: ids
body.description: Integer ids of the cases to archive / retrieve.

body.name: de_selected_ids
body.description: Ids to exclude when `select_all` is true.

body.name: select_all
body.description: Apply to every case in scope, minus `de_selected_ids`.

capabilities.intent: Bulk Archive Test Cases
guidance: Archiving hides cases from the working set without deleting them; they can be retrieved again. Prefer it to deletion when the user says 'remove' or 'clean up' without being explicit.

capabilities.name: bulk_archive_test_plans_v1

body.name: test_plan_ids
body.description: Plan INTEGER ids. Three body shapes are accepted and tried in this order: test_plan.ids, then ids, then test_plan_ids — the first one present wins, so do not send two. Every entry is run through to_i and anything that yields 0 is silently dropped, so a TP-NNN identifier is discarded without an error.

capabilities.intent: Archive test plans in bulk — the reversible way to get plans out of the active listing; use this instead of delete whenever the user might want them back

200.description: Sync (<= 30 ids): `{success, plans, count}`. Async (above the threshold): `{success, async: true, unique_id}` — the plans are not archived yet.

400.description: No usable ids after coercion: `{success: false, errors: "Please provide test plan ids"}`.

404.description: Test-plan archiving is not enabled for this group: `{success: false, errors: "Feature not available"}`.

guidance: Archiving is gated on a group feature flag. When the flag is off the call returns 404 with {success: false, errors: 'Feature not available'} — a 404 here means the feature is unavailable, NOT that the plans are missing. The same gate covers bulk-retrieve and both archived reads.
Permission is the test-plan DELETE right, not write. A user who can create and edit plans can still be 403'd here, and on restore and on the archived listing/count.

Ids are coerced with to_i: 'TP-12' and any non-numeric entry become 0 and are dropped silently. If every id drops the call is 400 {success: false, errors: 'Please provide test plan ids'} — the same error you get for an empty list.

More than 30 ids is handed to a background job and returns {success: true, async: true, unique_id} — NOTHING is archived yet at that moment. Re-read the plans (or the archived listing) to confirm; there is no job-status endpoint for this in the profile.
The 30 counts the ids YOU send. Sub-plan expansion happens upstream, so archiving a parent can touch far more plans than the count you get back.
Failures use the plural key `errors`, not `error` — {success: false, errors: '...'}. Branch on `success`, not on the key name.
Unlike the public/v2 archive route, this path is not JSON-schema validated, so the 1000-id cap that route enforces is not applied here. Batch large sets yourself.
To undo, call the bulk-retrieve capability with the same ids.

capabilities.name: bulk_assign_test_cases_to_test_run

query.name: include_subfolders_tc
query.description: When a folder_id is given, also include cases in its sub-folders when resolving a select_all.

query.name: p
query.description: Page of the test-case listing returned AFTER the assignment. It does not affect which rows are assigned.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Page size of the listing returned after the assignment. Anything outside 1..100, or non-numeric, silently falls back to 30 rather than erroring.

query.name: sort_by
query.description: Sort of the listing returned after the assignment.

body.name: assignee_id
body.description: TM user id (not a BrowserStack user id, not an email) of the person to assign. The id must belong to the caller's group or the request 404s. Omit it entirely to clear the assignee on the selected rows — there is no separate 'unassign' call.

body.name: mapping_ids
body.description: TRTC MAPPING ids — the `mapping_id` field on the rows a test-run test-case listing returns — NOT test case ids. A case that runs against N configurations has N mapping ids, and passing the case's `id` here assigns nothing and still returns 200.

body.name: select_all
body.description: Assign every case the current filter resolves to, instead of an explicit mapping_ids list. The filter is `q` (plus folder_id / include_subfolders_tc); with no `q` this means the whole run.

body.name: de_selected_ids
body.description: Mapping ids to exclude. Subtracted from mapping_ids, and from the resolved set when select_all is true.

body.name: folder_id
body.description: Scope the selection — and the listing returned afterwards — to one folder of the run. Its presence also changes the response: the post-assign listing comes back from the folder view and carries an extra `folder` key.

body.name: q
body.description: The same filter object the run's test-case listing takes. Only read when select_all is true; it is what select_all resolves against.

body.name: automation
body.description: Automation-run path. When true the selection resolver is bypassed entirely: `test_run_ids` is taken as the id list and the operation is ALWAYS queued, whatever its size. Leave it off for manual runs.

body.name: test_run_ids
body.description: Only read when automation is true; ignored otherwise.

capabilities.intent: Set the assignee on many test cases inside a test run in one call — pick the rows explicitly, or select every row matching the current filter and deselect a few
guidance: The ids here are mapping ids, not test case ids. Read the run's test cases first and take `mapping_id` off each row — `id` is the test case and assigning by it silently does nothing.

Above 300 selected rows the call switches to a queued write and returns {success:true, async:true, unique_id} with NO test_cases — the assignment happens later. Below that it applies inline and returns the re-listed page. Branch on `async` rather than assuming the list is there, and never retry on the async acknowledgement.

The selected mapping ids are locked for the duration. A concurrent bulk operation on any of the same rows comes back 400 {success:false, message:'TestCases in progress with another operation'} — that is contention, not bad input; wait and retry.

An empty resolution is refused, not silently accepted: 400 'No test cases to update.' when nothing is selected, and 422 'Could not resolve the selected test cases. Please retry.' when select_all counted rows it could not turn into ids.
assignee_id must be a TM user id inside the caller's group; an id from another group raises a 404 rather than being ignored. Omitting it clears the assignee.

The 200 body is the run's test-case listing re-read after the write, not a report of what changed — it is paged, so it can show fewer rows than you assigned. Re-read and check `test_assignee` if you need confirmation.
Needs the test-run write permission; on an automation run the automation variant of that permission is demanded instead and a role that only holds the manual one gets 403.

capabilities.name: bulk_copy_test_cases

body.name: q
body.description: SCOPE for `select_all`, and a SIBLING of `test_case` at top level, not a field inside it. Same filter shape as the search-and-filter flow's `q`. With `select_all: true` the target set comes from this `q` merged with top-level `folder_id` and `ids` is ignored; with explicit ids it is unused. An unrecognised key here is dropped, not rejected, so a typo widens the selection to the whole scope.

body.name: p
body.description: Page of the scoped view, as the UI sends it. Only consulted when `select_all` is true and no `q` is present (the unfiltered folder-count path).

body.name: include_subfolders_tc
body.description: Extend the selection into subfolders of the top-level `folder_id`. Compared as the string `true`. Merged into the search scope, so it also changes what `select_all` resolves to.

body.name: ids
body.description: Integer test case ids. Ignored when `select_all` is true. Not required in itself — send EITHER `ids` OR `select_all: true`; a selection that resolves to zero cases is rejected with a bare 400 `{success:false}` before any work happens.

body.name: de_selected_ids
body.description: Integer ids to exclude. Only meaningful with `select_all: true` (with explicit `ids` they are subtracted from your own list). Optional — omit it or send `[]`.

body.name: select_all
body.description: Copy every case the scope resolves to, minus `de_selected_ids`. Compared as the string `true`; anything else means "use `ids`". The scope is top-level `q` + `folder_id` (+ `include_subfolders_tc`), NOT the whole project by default.

body.name: folder_id
body.description: SOURCE folder that scopes the selection, at TOP level (outside `test_case`). Merged into the search scope and it overwrites `q.folder_id` when both are sent. Do not confuse it with the destination: for copy that is top-level `destination_folder_id`, for move it is `test_case.destination_folder_id`, and for bulk edit a `test_case.folder_id` MOVES the cases.

body.name: destination_folder_id
body.description: Target folder for the copies, at TOP level (bulk-move puts its destination inside `test_case` instead). Required in practice: the request is pre-checked by looking the folder up inside `destination_project_id`, and a folder that does not exist there is a bare 400 with no message. The only way to omit it is the `copy_folder` flow below, which mints the destination first.

body.name: destination_project_id
body.description: Target project id. Only needed for a copy into ANOTHER project — it defaults to the source project when omitted, so a same-project copy can leave it out. Integer and string are both accepted. Ignored when `clone_in_place` is true, which always stays in the source project.

body.name: clone_in_place
body.description: Duplicate each selected case into its OWN source folder (the product's Clone action) instead of into one shared destination. Never crosses projects. `destination_folder_id` is still pre-validated even though the copies do not land there, so it must still name a real folder.

body.name: copy_folder
body.description: Compared as the string `true`. Creates the destination folder from `test_case_folder` before copying, and that new folder then wins over `destination_folder_id`. Leave it unset and pass an existing `destination_folder_id` for the normal case.

body.name: test_case_folder
body.description: Only read when `copy_folder` is true: the destination folder to create. `test_case_folder_id` is the PARENT folder's integer id (0 with `root: true` creates a root folder); `prev`/`next` position it among its siblings.

body.name: folders
body.description: Cross-folder selection: a map keyed by folder id, each value `{select_all, ids, de_selected_ids}`. When present it REPLACES the flat `ids`/`select_all` selection and the union is resolved per folder. Unknown keys inside an entry are dropped.

body.name: sort_by
body.description: Sort token for the listing that comes back in the response (`<column>-ASC|DESC`, or `cf#<id>#<type>-<dir>`). Malformed tokens are rejected with 400. It does not affect which cases the operation acts on.

capabilities.intent: Copy test cases into another folder or another project — by listing their ids, or by copying everything a filter matches — and clone cases in place.
guidance: Selection is one of two modes and they do not mix: either `test_case.ids` (explicit integer ids), or `test_case.select_all: true`, which resolves the set from top-level `q` + `folder_id` and ignores `ids` entirely.
The destination is TOP-LEVEL `destination_folder_id` here. Bulk-move puts its destination inside `test_case` — copying the move body onto this route silently sends no destination and 400s.

The destination folder is looked up before anything is copied, inside `destination_project_id` (which defaults to the source project). A folder id that does not exist there comes back as a bare 400 with no message — that is 'no such folder', not 'bad request'.
An empty selection is a bare 400 `{success:false}` with no message — that is what you get when `ids` is empty, or when `select_all` is true but `q` matched nothing.

Above 30 selected cases the work is handed to a background job and you get 200 `{success:true, async:true, unique_id:"<uuid>"}` with NO `test_cases` — treat that body as an acknowledgement, not a result, and re-read afterwards.
Concurrent bulk ops on the same cases are refused: 400 `{success:false, message:"TestCases in progress with another operation"}`. Retry rather than reading it as bad input.

The 200 body is the refreshed SOURCE view (or the search results) plus folder counts — it does NOT contain the new copies or their ids. To get them, list the destination folder afterwards; `cases_count[<destination_folder_id>]` only tells you the new total.
Copies are new test cases with new integer ids and new TC-NNN identifiers; the originals are untouched. There is no undo — the way back is to delete the copies.

capabilities.intent: Delete many test cases at once from the project-wide search/filter view — by id, or everything a filter matches.
guidance: Selection is either `test_case.ids` or `test_case.select_all: true` scoped by top-level `q` + `folder_id`. With select_all the `ids` you send are ignored, so a mis-typed filter key (which is dropped, not rejected) deletes the whole scope.

Whether this is recoverable depends on the workspace: with the move-to-bin feature enabled the cases go to the Bin and can be restored, otherwise the delete is permanent. Assume permanent unless you have confirmed the Bin is on for this group.
Deleting also drops the cases' results and unlinks them from schedules — those do not come back even when the case is restored from the Bin.
An empty selection is a bare 400 `{success:false}` with no message — that is what you get when `ids` is empty, or when `select_all` is true but `q` matched nothing.

Above 300 selected cases the work is handed to a background job and you get 200 `{success:true, async:true, unique_id:"<uuid>"}` with NO `test_cases` — treat that body as an acknowledgement, not a result, and re-read afterwards.
Concurrent bulk ops on the same cases are refused: 400 `{success:false, message:"TestCases in progress with another operation"}`. Retry rather than reading it as bad input.

The 200 body is the refreshed listing after the delete (`test_cases` + `info` + `cases_count`), not a report of what was deleted. The one exception: with `q.is_archived` set, the response is just `{success:true}`.

capabilities.name: bulk_delete_test_results_v1

body.name: result_ids
body.description: Result INTEGER ids. Non-empty, max 300.

capabilities.intent: Delete test results in bulk — PARTIAL SUCCESS is normal, always read `skipped`

200.description:
Partial success is normal — `deleted_ids` is what actually went, `skipped` is what
did not (usually authorisation).

result.description:
Both lists are nested HERE, not at the top level. Reading
response["deleted_ids"] directly finds nothing and makes a successful
delete look like a no-op.

skipped.description:
Entries are OBJECTS, not bare ids — {"id": 13, "reason": "not_found"}.
Common reasons: not_found, or the caller is neither author nor project admin.

400.description: `result_ids` missing or empty.

422.description: More than 300 ids in one request.

guidance: Partial success is the normal outcome and it still answers 200 with success:true. Both lists sit under a top-level `result` key: read result.deleted_ids and result.skipped. Never infer 'all deleted' from the status code — diff deleted_ids against the ids you sent and report the rest.
`skipped` entries are OBJECTS, not bare ids: {id, reason}. The only two reasons the handler produces are `not_found` and `not_authorised`.

Deletion is authorised per id: a project admin's whole batch is authorised wholesale, everyone else may only delete results they personally logged. A non-admin batch is resolved id by id against the recorded author.

The authorship lookup fails CLOSED. If that upstream call errors, you still get 200 / success:true with deleted_ids empty and EVERY id back in skipped with reason `not_found`. An all-not_found batch is as likely an upstream failure as genuinely missing ids — re-read the results before telling the user they do not exist.

`result_ids` is read from the top level of the body — it is not wrapped in an object. Ids are coerced with to_i and anything coercing to 0 (a non-numeric string, a null, 0 itself) is dropped silently; if that empties the list you get 400 'result_ids must be a non-empty array' even though you sent a non-empty array.
More than 300 ids is refused with 422 before anything is deleted — nothing partial happens, so just re-batch. Sending exactly the cap is fine.

There is no recycle bin for results. Deleting a case's latest result rolls that case's outcome in the run back to its previous attempt (or back to unexecuted if it was the only one); the deleted result itself is unrecoverable.

body.name: automation_status
body.description: Automation state as an internal_name string (e.g. `not_automated`). Forwarded verbatim on this path — no name-to-id resolution happens. Prefer `automation_state` with its numeric option id.

body.name: case_type
body.description: Numeric case-type option id — NOT the display name. Unlike single-case edit, this path always sends it as an id, so a name here is stored as a broken id. Resolve the id from the project's system field values first.

body.name: custom_fields
body.description: Map of custom-field id to value. ALWAYS SEND THIS KEY — pass `{}` when changing no custom fields. Omitting it returns 500 (the server dereferences a nil hash), the same defect as on PATCH .../test-cases.

body.name: issues
body.description: Linked issues, as `[{issue_id, issue_type}]` (bare strings are coerced to ``issue_id``). Read via a separate permit than the other fields, so it survives even though it is not in the edit allow-list. It is sent on EVERY bulk edit — as `[]` when you omit it — so treat it as a full replacement of the issue list, not an append.

body.name: owner
body.description: TM user id (not a BrowserStack user id, not an email). An id that does not resolve to a user is not a validation error — it dereferences nil and returns 500.

body.name: priority
body.description: Numeric priority option id — NOT the display name. Resolve it from the project's system field values first.

body.name: status
body.description: Numeric status option id — NOT the display name. Resolve it from the project's system field values first.

body.name: tags
body.description: REPLACES the entire tag list on every selected case. Read the existing tags and send the union if you mean to add.

body.name: review_status
body.description: Review state applied to every selected case (e.g. `pending`, `in_review`, `approved`). Only meaningful on a Team-Pro workspace with review-approve enabled on the project.

body.name: reviewers
body.description: Reviewer TM user ids. Honoured only on a Team-Pro workspace with review-approve enabled on the project; otherwise dropped without any error.

body.name: automation_state
body.description: Numeric automation-state option id. Takes precedence over `automation_status`.

body.name: template
body.description: Step-shape template applied to every selected case. Validated against a closed set (`test_case_text`, `test_case_steps`, `bdd`, `test_case_bdd`) and DROPPED WITHOUT ERROR if the value is not one of them — a template id or a custom template name here is a silent no-op.

body.name: estimate
body.description: Forwarded to the backend on this path (unlike single-case edit, which drops it), but every read serialises `estimate` as null, so you cannot confirm it and should not report it as saved. There is no bulk equivalent of `estimated_duration_seconds`.

body.name: comment
body.description: Free-text note carried with the bulk edit.

body.name: folder_id
body.description: DANGER — inside `test_case` this MOVES every selected case into that folder. The top-level `folder_id` of the same name only scopes the selection. Omit this unless you mean to move them.

body.name: folders

capabilities.intent: Set the same field values — owner, priority, status, case type, tags, custom fields, review state — on many test cases at once from the project-wide search/filter view.

200.description: Applied synchronously: the refreshed search listing. Above the async threshold the same 200 instead carries {success, async:true, unique_id} and no test_cases.

filter_details.description: Echo of the resolved filter; {} when no q was sent.

guidance: ALWAYS send `test_case.custom_fields`, `{}` when you are changing none. Omitting the key dereferences a nil hash and returns 500 — this is the single most common failure on this route.

priority, status, case_type and automation_state must be NUMERIC option ids here. The single-case edit accepts a display name for some of them; this path does not, and a name is written through as a broken id rather than rejected.

An empty selection is a bare 400 `{success:false}` with no message — that is what you get when `ids` is empty, or when `select_all` is true but `q` matched nothing.

Above 100 selected cases the work is handed to a background job and you get 200 `{success:true, async:true, unique_id:"<uuid>"}` with NO `test_cases` — treat that body as an acknowledgement, not a result, and re-read afterwards.
Concurrent bulk ops on the same cases are refused: 400 `{success:false, message:"TestCases in progress with another operation"}`. Retry rather than reading it as bad input.

Every successful edit writes a new version of each case, so an unwanted bulk edit can be undone case by case by restoring the previous version — subject to the workspace's plan, which may only keep 30 days of history.

body.description: Test case identifiers to target, e.g. ["TC-101","TC-102"]. OMITTING this (or sending an empty array) targets EVERY test case in the run. Identifiers not in the run are skipped silently.

capabilities.intent: Move many test cases in a test run to one status in a single call — the bulk 'mark these passed' or 'reset the run to untested' action, which replaces each case's current outcome instead of adding a new one
guidance: NO UNDO. Each targeted case's current outcome is superseded in place by the status you name; the status that was there is not kept as a separate history entry and cannot be restored. Recovering means knowing the old status per case and setting it back by hand.

Omitting `test_case_ids` (or sending []) applies the status to EVERY case in the run. There is no cap, no dry run and no confirmation step on the server — send an explicit list unless you really mean the whole run.
`status` must be a name already configured for the project; an unconfigured name is rejected 400 before anything is queued. Resolve the project's configured result statuses first.

Fire-and-forget: HTTP 200 {success: true} only means the job was queued. Identifiers that are not in the run are skipped with no error, and any failure inside the worker never reaches the caller — read results back to confirm.
No unrecognised keys are allowed in the body — `status` and `test_case_ids` only.

500.description: The job could not be queued; nothing was applied.

body.description: Keep the results already recorded against the cases being removed. Defaults to FALSE, i.e. the results are deleted with the mapping. Must be a real boolean (or "true"/"false"); anything else is a 400.

capabilities.intent: Change which test cases a run covers — bulk-add cases to it, or bulk-remove them, optionally per configuration
guidance: Everything goes inside a `test_run` object, and exactly one of add_test_cases / remove_test_cases may be present and non-empty — both, or neither, is a 400.

Always asynchronous. A 202 {success, async, unique_id} means only that the job was queued; nothing has changed yet. There is no status endpoint for unique_id over HTTP (completion is announced on a websocket channel), so confirm by re-reading the run's test cases.

Removing a case DISCARDS its recorded results unless you send preserve_existing_results: true. Runs keep no version history, so those results cannot be restored — ask before removing cases from a run that has been executed.

capabilities.name: clone_exploratory_session_v1
capabilities.intent: Copy an existing exploratory session — its description, timebox, configurations and custom fields, plus its log entries, and optionally its tags, linked issues and owner — to re-run the same exploration
guidance: The clone body is FLAT — it is not wrapped in an `exploratory_session` object, unlike create and update on this entity.

There are two completely different success shapes and you must branch on the source session's size. Fewer than 50 logs: 201 with {success, async:false, unique_id:null, exploratory_session:{...}} and the copy fully built. 50 logs or more: 202 with {success, async:true, unique_id} and NO session object — the copy exists but you are not told its id.

Read session_log_count on the source session first to know which branch you will get. If it is 50 or more, plan to find the new session by listing sessions afterwards (its default title is '<source title> - Copy').

unique_id is a realtime broadcast channel name, not a job id — there is no endpoint that reports the clone's progress or result. The only way to confirm an async clone is to re-read the sessions list.

The charter and the folder are NOT copied. The clone lands at the project root with an empty charter even though description, timebox, configurations and custom field values are copied. Set them with an update afterwards if they matter.

copy_tags, copy_issues and copy_session_owner all default to FALSE, so a plain clone arrives with no tags, no linked issues and nobody assigned. copy_issues also controls whether each copied log keeps its own linked defects.
The clone is always created in the active state, even when the source session is closed.
The three copy_* flags must be real JSON booleans — the request schema rejects the strings "true"/"false" with 400.
If the asynchronous log copy fails, the newly created session is deleted again, so a failed clone leaves nothing behind — and nothing over this API tells you it happened.
The source session is read before anything is created, so an unknown session_id fails as a bare {success:false} 404 with no session created.

body.name: name
body.description: Title for the new session. Sent at the top level of the body, not inside an exploratory_session wrapper. Defaults to '<source title> - Copy' when omitted — which is also how you find the copy after an async clone.

body.name: copy_tags
body.description: Copy the source session's tags. Must be a real JSON boolean; the string "true" is rejected with 400. Defaults to false, so the clone is untagged unless you ask.

body.name: copy_issues
body.description: Copy the linked issues — both the session's own issue links AND the defects on every copied log entry. Must be a real JSON boolean. Defaults to false.

body.name: copy_session_owner
body.description: Keep the source session's assignee. Must be a real JSON boolean. Defaults to false, which leaves the clone unassigned.

body.description: Attachment ids already uploaded via the attachments surface.

body.name: custom_fields
body.description: Custom-field values for the new plan, keyed as the test-plan form-fields read returns them. A bad key or value is 400 {success: false, error: <message>} before any cloning starts.

body.name: parent_plan_id
body.description: Set it to make the clone a SUB-plan of that parent (integer id). Omitted/null gives a top-level plan. This is fixed at clone time — a plan cannot be promoted or demoted later.

body.name: copy_all_runs
body.description: Copy every test run linked to the source plan. When true, test_runs is not consulted.

body.name: test_runs
body.description: Clone only these runs of the source plan, as run ids. Ignored when copy_all_runs is true; send neither and the clone is created with no runs.

body.name: copy_all_sub_plans
body.description: Clone every sub-plan of the source plan under the new plan.

body.name: sub_plan_ids
body.description: Clone only these sub-plans (integer ids). Ignored when copy_all_sub_plans is true.

body.name: status_ids
body.description: Run-level filter: keep only source runs that contain at least one test case in one of these result-status ids. Entries must be integers — anything else is 400 {success: false, error: 'status_ids must be a list of integers'}. It filters RUNS, not cases: every case inside a kept run is copied.

capabilities.intent: Copy a test plan into a brand-new plan, bringing its test runs (and optionally its sub-plans) with it — the copy is built in the background, so this hands back a job id rather than the new plan

400.description: Missing name (`{success: false, message: "Name field cannot be blank"}`), non-integer status_ids, or a rejected custom field (`{success: false, error: ...}`). Also used for a body with no `test_plan` wrapper.

guidance: This is ASYNC. A 200 means the clone job was queued, not that the plan exists — the body is {success: true, unique_id} and carries no plan id, no identifier and no name. The source plan is untouched either way.
unique_id is only a correlation id for logs; there is no job-status capability for it in this profile. To find the new plan, poll the project's plan listing for the name you sent.
The whole body must be wrapped in a `test_plan` object — without it the request is rejected before any field is read.
name is REQUIRED even though this is a clone. There is no automatic 'Copy of ...' name.
Nothing except the runs/sub-plans is inherited: description, dates, tags, owner and custom fields all come from THIS request, so a clone sent with only a name produces an otherwise empty plan.
Choose the run scope explicitly — copy_all_runs: true, or an explicit test_runs list. With neither, the job creates the plan with no runs at all and still returns success.
Copied runs come over whole: the job forces copy_all_cases, and keeps each case's assignee, issues and tags. status_ids narrows which RUNS are copied, never which cases inside them.
Date validation is a silent trap: end_date before start_date returns HTTP 200 with {success: false, error: 'Please check date params'}. Check the `success` field, not the status code.
Needs the test-plan write permission.

capabilities.name: clone_test_run

body.name: name
body.description: Name for the new run. Leave it out and the run is auto-named, which is how projects end up with several identically named clones.

body.name: copy_all_cases
body.description: Copy every case from the source run. WITHOUT this (and without status_id) the clone is created EMPTY — the default is a bare run, not a copy of the case list.

body.name: status_id
body.description: Copy only the cases whose latest result is one of these numeric status ids (resolve them via the project's result-status field values). Numeric ids only — this is the filter that is honoured on every backend flow.

body.name: status
body.description: Status NAMES to filter the copied cases by. Honoured only on the legacy backend flow; on the current (build-backed) flow it is dropped and a clone whose only case selector was `status` copies nothing and still returns 200. Send status_id instead.

body.name: copy_tc_assignee
body.description: Carry each copied case's assignee across. Only meaningful together with copy_all_cases / status_id — it applies to the copied rows, not to the run.

body.name: copy_issues
body.description: Carry the linked defects across onto the copied case rows.

body.name: copy_tags
body.description: Copy the source run's tags onto the new run.

body.name: source_build_id
body.description: Optional explicit source build to copy cases from, for callers that already resolved it. Normally omitted — it is looked up from the source run.

capabilities.intent: Copy an existing test run into a new one — optionally carrying over its cases, their assignees, tags and linked defects — to re-execute the same scope without rebuilding the selection
guidance: A clone with no case selector produces an EMPTY run. Send copy_all_cases:true, or status_id, or you get a 200 and a run with zero cases — this is the single most common surprise on this endpoint.

Filter the copied cases by status_id (numeric), not by `status` (names). The name form is only read on the legacy backend flow; on the current one it is ignored and the clone silently comes back empty.

The clone always starts in run_state `new_run` regardless of the source run's state, and its description is always copied. Tags, defects and per-case assignees are copied only when you ask. Configurations, the owner and the dynamic-filter rule are NOT carried over — set them afterwards with the edit call.

Cloning a run created before the current ingest flow, while asking for its cases, is refused with 422 'The source run has no test cases available to clone. Retry without case selection.' Retrying without copy_all_cases/status_id gives you an empty clone of the header.

Population is not synchronous on every path: the run exists as soon as the call returns, but re-read its cases rather than trusting an immediate empty list, and never retry the clone — that makes a second run.
Take `uuid` (the integer) from the response, not `id` — `id` is the TR-NNN string here as everywhere else on runs.

The new run comes back under `data.test_run` (with an underscore). The write endpoints on this entity — create, edit, assign, close, delete — use `data.testrun` instead. Do not reuse one reader for both.
Needs the test-run write permission; cloning an automation run demands the automation variant of it and 403s for a role that only holds the manual one.

capabilities.name: clone_test_run_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Run identifier in TR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to TR-\d+ — unlike the v1 run endpoints, a bare integer is NOT accepted here and returns a routing 404.

body.name: test_case_selection
body.description: Which cases of the source run the copy gets: every case, or only those whose latest result matches `statuses`. Any other value is a 400.

body.name: statuses
body.description: Result status NAMES (case-insensitive) — not ids. Required and non-empty when test_case_selection is "by_results"; an unknown name is a 400 naming it. Defaults plus any custom status configured for the group are accepted.

body.name: copy_tc_assignee
body.description: Carry per-case assignees over. Defaults to TRUE here (the v1 clone defaults it to false).

body.name: copy_tags
body.description: Carry the source run's tags over. Defaults to TRUE here (the v1 clone defaults it to false).

body.name: name
body.description: Name for the new run. Omitted or blank gives "<source run name> - Copy".

capabilities.intent: Copy an existing run into a brand-new run — the usual way to re-execute just the failed or blocked cases from the last cycle
guidance: The run comes back keyed by its TR-NNN string in `identifier`. There is NO `id` and NO `uuid` field on this v2 payload — the integer run id is not exposed here at all, so anything downstream that needs it has to come from a v1 read. Carry `identifier` forward; the other v2 run routes take the TR-NNN form.
Body is flat — these fields sit at the top level, not inside a `test_run` object like the update calls.

Identity is synchronous, data is not: the response carries the new run as soon as it exists, but its case mappings are filled in by a background worker. Reading the new run's test cases immediately can legitimately return zero rows — retry before concluding the clone was empty.
A 202 (instead of 200) means the run was cloned and one bookkeeping leg is still settling: do NOT retry, or you get a second clone.
Test plan / sub-plan links are NOT carried over; link the copy afterwards if you need it under a plan.
A dynamic source run passes its is_dynamic flag on, but the filter is not re-evaluated, so the copy starts from the source's case list.
Cloning an automation run is blocked by the write-permission gate (403) — this path is for manual runs.
The copy is a new run, so nothing about the source changes; discard it by deleting the copy.
The clone comes back at the top level as `test_run`, not under `data`. A 202 means the copy is still populating.

This payload is narrower than the v1 run reads. `owner`, `is_automation`, `is_dynamic`, `test_cases_count`, `overall_progress_by_status_id`, `environment`, `closed_at` and `closed_by` are v1-only — if you need any of them, read the run through v1 instead of assuming a missing key means an unset value.

202.description: Run cloned, background bookkeeping still in progress. Body is {success: true, build_pending: true, message, test_run}. Treat as success; retrying would create a duplicate run.

400.description: Clone options failed validation — unknown test_case_selection, missing statuses for "by_results", or an unknown status name. Body is {success: false, message}.

capabilities.name: close_exploratory_session
capabilities.intent: Mark an exploratory testing session finished so it leaves the active listing and is archived as completed work

200.description: Exploratory session closed successfully.

guidance: This call takes no body at all. The handler's actual_duration pass-through is commented out, so posting a duration here returns 200 and changes nothing. Write actual_duration with the session update call BEFORE closing.
Closing is one-way through the API: nothing accepts session_state, and there is no reopen endpoint. Treat it as irreversible even though it is not classed destructive.
After closing, the session disappears from the sessions listing unless you pass q[session_state]=closed — the listing defaults to active.

Closing also changes who may delete the session afterwards: deletion of a closed session is gated by the closed-test-run delete permission rather than the ordinary one, so a caller who could have deleted it a moment earlier may now get 403.
The response is only {success:true}. Re-read the session to see session_state, closed_at and closed_by.

Closing an already-closed session is not rejected here; whatever the store does with it surfaces, if at all, as the generic 400 {success:false, message:'The API request is invalid or improperly formed'}.
A session id that does not exist returns a bare {success:false} with 404 and no message.

capabilities.name: close_test_run_v1
capabilities.intent: Close a test run — freeze its results, mark the cycle finished and drop it out of the default run listing
guidance: No body at all. This is a fixed transition to run_state `closed`; anything you send is ignored.

Closing has side effects that reopening does not undo: a snapshot of every result is taken, and the run's linked build in Test Observability is closed too. Treat it as the end of the cycle rather than a toggle.

A closed run disappears from the default project run listing — it is only visible through the closed-runs listing or a listing that explicitly asks for it. Deleting it afterwards also demands a different permission from deleting an open run.
Reopening is possible by editing the run back to another run_state, but that edit must resend every mandatory test_run field, and the snapshot taken at close stays.

The run comes back under `data.testrun` — one word, no underscore — alongside `data.project`. The read endpoints use `data.test_run`. The 200 also carries a TOP-LEVEL `skipped_test_case_ids` array (a sibling of `data`, not inside it).

Client errors from the backing service come back as `{data: {success: false, error: <message>}}` with the 4xx status, not as the flat error envelope other endpoints use — read `data.success` before trusting `data.testrun`.
Needs the test-run write permission; an automation run demands the automation variant and 403s otherwise.

capabilities.name: copy_folder

body.name: source_folder_id
body.description: Integer id of the folder to copy. Must exist in the project named in the path. Blank/absent returns 400 {error:'source_folder_id is required'}.

body.name: destination_folder_id
body.description: Parent folder the copy is placed under, in destination_project_id. NOT required: omitting it (or sending null) is what switches the call into copy-to-root mode, exactly as copy_to_root:true does.

body.name: destination_project_id
body.description: Destination project. NOT required — defaults to the project in the path. Cross-project copies are allowed here (unlike cross-project moves, which are blocked when the folder has shared test cases).

body.name: copy_to_root
body.description: Place the copy at the destination project's root instead of under a parent folder. Accepts the boolean true or the literal string "true". It is also forced on whenever destination_folder_id is absent.

capabilities.intent: Duplicate a folder — its whole subtree of subfolders and every test case in them — into another folder, or to the root of any project you can reach; always runs as a background job
guidance: This endpoint only queues work. It answers 202 Accepted (not 200) with {success:true, async:true, unique_id, message} the moment validation passes — nothing has been copied yet when you get the response.

There is no way to poll the job over HTTP. `unique_id` is just the X-Request-ID header echoed back (a fresh UUID if you sent none), and progress is pushed over a websocket channel the API does not expose. Confirm the copy by re-reading the destination folder's contents after a delay.

`async` and `copy_test_cases` are not read anywhere in the handler or the worker. The copy is always asynchronous, and it always copies the full subtree — every nested subfolder and every test case. You cannot ask for a folders-only copy.

Name clashes are resolved silently, not rejected: an existing folder of the same name in the destination makes the copy land as `copy-of-<name>`, then `copy-of-2-<name>`, `copy-of-3-<name>` and so on. Match on the returned tree, not on the name you sent.

Copying a folder into itself or into one of its own descendants is refused with 400 {error:'Cannot copy folder into itself or its subfolder'} — but only for same-project copies that name a destination folder. Copy-to-root and cross-project copies skip that check entirely.
Missing source or destination is 404 with a bare {error:'...'} and no `success` key — this endpoint does not use the usual {success:false} envelope for that case.
If the worker fails partway it rolls the whole copy back, so a failed run should leave no half-copied tree — but you only learn that by re-reading, not from this response.
Requires the folder-create permission on the project in the path.

capabilities.name: count_run_selection_v1

body.name: select_all
body.description: Select every case in the project. Marked required because the request body must contain a `selection` object at all — sending only `configurations` is rejected 400 before anything is counted, and this is the cheapest field that materialises `selection`. Pass false alongside `folders` for a folder-scoped count.

body.name: unique_test_case_count
body.description: The caller's own count of distinct cases in the selection. Echoed through; it does not constrain the answer.

body.name: folders
body.description: Map of folder id (as a STRING key) to that folder's selection: {test_case_select_all, selected_test_cases:[ids], deselected_test_cases:[ids]}. Case ids must be integers — strings are rejected by the schema.

body.name: shared_selection
body.description: Map of project ids to their shared test-case selection, same inner shape as `selection`. Top level, NOT inside `selection`.

body.name: configurations
body.description: Configuration ids (integers). Required by the schema — send an empty array when there are none; omitting the key is a 400.

body.name: trtc_configuration_mappings
body.description: Per-configuration case mappings. An ARRAY of objects — an object here is rejected. Unknown keys inside an entry are rejected too.

capabilities.intent: Ask how many test cases a folder/case selection will actually resolve to — including the multiplication by configurations — before committing it to a run create or edit

200.description: The number of test-case x configuration rows the selection resolves to.

guidance: The body is schema-validated with unknown top-level keys REJECTED. Only `selection`, `shared_selection`, `configurations` and `trtc_configuration_mappings` are accepted; anything else — including run fields like `name` or `filters` — returns 400 {error: 'Invalid JSON data', details: [...]} before any counting happens.
`selection` and `configurations` are both mandatory. A body with a selection but no `configurations` key is refused; pass `configurations: []` when the run has none.

The answer is the number of case-times-configuration rows the run would get, not the number of distinct test cases — with two configurations selected the count is roughly double `unique_test_case_count`. That is the point of the call.
Read-only and side-effect free: it resolves the selection but creates nothing. Use it before a create or edit when the user needs to see the size of what they are about to commit.
The body must be sent as application/json; a form-encoded body skips the schema check entirely and then fails further in with a less useful error.
The response is flat — {success, count} with no `data` envelope.

capabilities.name: create_bulk_test_cases_v1

body.name: test_cases
body.description: One UNWRAPPED object per case (no per-item `test_case` key), max 10 on the synchronous path. Several fields are read from the FIRST item only and applied to all — see guidance. Send `template` and `test_case_steps` on every item.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Case title. Required.

fields.name: test_case_folder_id
fields.description: Target folder's integer id. Required in the body as well as in the path; the path folder is not substituted in.

fields.name: attachments
fields.description: Blob ids. Taken from the FIRST item only and copied onto EVERY case in the batch. A blob belonging to another group fails the whole request with 400.

fields.name: automation_state
fields.description: NOT accepted on the bulk path — dropped by the allow-list. Use `automation_status` here, or edit the cases afterwards.

fields.name: custom_fields
fields.description: Taken from the FIRST item only and applied to EVERY case in the batch. Per-item custom field values are silently discarded — create cases with differing custom fields one at a time, or edit them afterwards.

fields.name: estimate
fields.description: Accepted by the allow-list and then never written; every read serialises `estimate` as null. Do not report an estimate as saved.

fields.name: estimated_duration_seconds
fields.description: NOT accepted on the bulk path — dropped by the allow-list. Set it with an edit after creation.

fields.name: review_status
fields.description: NOT accepted on the bulk path — dropped by the allow-list. The created cases take the project's default review state.

fields.name: reviewers
fields.description: NOT accepted on the bulk path — dropped by the allow-list. Set reviewers with an edit after creation.

fields.name: send_for_review
fields.description: NOT accepted on the bulk path — dropped by the allow-list.

fields.name: shared_precondition_id
fields.description: NOT accepted on the bulk path — dropped by the allow-list.

fields.name: template
fields.description: Step-shape template name. Also decides, from the FIRST item only, which system template id every case in the batch falls back to (`test_case_steps` when the first item omits it) — so send it on every item, and keep the batch homogeneous.

fields.name: template_step_type
fields.description: NOT accepted on the bulk path — dropped by the allow-list. Use `template`.

fields.name: test_case_steps
fields.description: The only key read for steps. Items are `{step, result, test_data?, order?, shared_step_id?}`; `order` is filled in by position when omitted. A differently named key such as `steps` is dropped and the case is created with no steps, still 200.

fields.name: metadata
fields.description: JSON-encoded string of opaque metadata (this is where an AI prompt reference rides). Unparseable JSON degrades to `{}` rather than erroring.

body.name: unique_id
body.description: Client-supplied idempotency key. When present AND the group has the async bulk-create flag on, the request is queued instead: 202 with the echoed `unique_id`, the ≤10 item limit is replaced by a 500-item cap, and completion arrives over the WebSocket channel. Without the flag it is inert.

body.name: create_subfolder
body.description: Create (or reuse) a subfolder named `scenario_name` under the path folder and put every case in the batch there instead. Requires `scenario_name`. If the batch then fails, a subfolder created for it is deleted again.

body.name: scenario_name
body.description: Name of the subfolder to create or reuse when `create_subfolder` is set.

capabilities.intent: Create several test cases in one folder in a single call (up to 10) — the call to use whenever you have more than one case to add.

200.description: Test cases created successfully.

202.description: Accepted for asynchronous processing (feature-flag gated; requires unique_id). Completion is broadcast on common_channel_<bs_user_id> with operation bulk_create and the echoed unique_id.

guidance: Items are UNWRAPPED — `test_cases` is a plain array of case objects with no per-item `test_case` key. A non-array, or more than 10 items, is a 400 naming the problem.

Not everything single-create accepts survives here: `automation_state`, `review_status`, `reviewers`, `send_for_review`, `shared_precondition_id`, `template_step_type` and `estimated_duration_seconds` are all dropped by this route's allow-list, without error. Create then edit if you need them.
`custom_fields` and `attachments` are read from the FIRST item and applied to all of them. A batch where cases differ in custom field values will silently come out wrong — create those one at a time.
`test_case_folder_id` is required inside each item even though the folder is already in the path; omitting it is the usual cause of a 422 wrapping an upstream 404.
Steps only come from `test_case_steps`. A `steps` key is dropped, and the cases are still created — with no steps and a 200 — so verify against the response.

The created cases are at `data.test_cases`, with `data.path_folders` and a `data.request_trace_id` for the AI enrichment that runs afterwards. Take each new case's integer `id` and TC-NNN `identifier` from there.

With `unique_id` and the async flag enabled, you instead get 202 `{success, async, unique_id, count}` and NO cases — the work finishes on a WebSocket channel you cannot read through this API, so poll the folder listing instead.
Any unexpected failure inside this route is flattened to 500 `{success:false, message:"Failed to create test cases."}` — that message covers backend rejections too, so do not read it as an outage.

capabilities.name: create_configuration_v1
capabilities.intent: Create a named configuration — an OS / browser / device combination that test runs track their per-case results against

body.name: name
body.description: Display name of the configuration, e.g. "Chrome 120 on Windows 11". This is the ONLY field the handler reads — os, os_version, browser, device and every other attribute the read returns cannot be set here and are silently ignored if sent.

guidance: `name` is the only input. The structured attributes (os, browser, device, versions) that come back on the listing cannot be set through this call; anything else you put in the body is dropped without an error.

Group-scoped, not project-scoped: `project_id` matches the route but is never sent onward, so the configuration is created at workspace level and appears in EVERY project in the group. There is no such thing as a project-private configuration here.

No request-body schema is registered for this action, so an omitted or empty `name` is not caught locally — whatever the backing service does with it is what you get, and the failure arrives without a field name.

The created record comes back under `configuration` (not `data`) beside `success:true`. Carry `configuration.id` — that integer is what a test run's configuration list takes; the run APIs want configuration ids, not configuration objects or names.
Check the configuration listing first. Configurations accumulate at workspace level and duplicates by name are not prevented here, so search before creating.
There is no delete-configuration or rename-configuration capability in this profile — a configuration created by mistake has to be cleaned up in the Test Management UI.

This action is missing from the RBAC permission map, so it is not permission-gated even though the rest of the configurations controller is (the listing needs test_run_view and the group/option writes need test_run_write).

capabilities.name: create_custom_field_dataset_option_v2

path_params.name: custom_fields_id
path_params.description: Numeric custom field id. Not validated by this handler; a wrong value surfaces from storage.

path_params.name: dataset_id
path_params.description: Numeric dataset id the option is added to. Not validated by this handler.

body.name: option_value
body.description: The option label. Must be present — a null or missing value is a 400 'Invalid Params'. Must be unique within the dataset; a duplicate is rejected with the upstream message relayed.

body.name: is_default
body.description: REQUIRED — a missing or null value is a 400. Use false for every option of a multi_dropdown, and true for at most one option of a dropdown; this layer does not enforce either rule.

body.name: parent_option_id
body.description: nested_dropdown children only — the option id this one hangs under, from the dataset options listing. Forwarded only when non-empty; meaningless on a flat dropdown.

capabilities.intent: Add one more choice to a dropdown-style custom field — a new value in an existing dataset, for every project that dataset covers
guidance: `is_default` is required and must be present, not null: omitting it (or option_value) is a 400 {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'}, whatever else is wrong.
The new option appears in every project the dataset is linked to, not just one. Check the dataset's project list before adding.

Only set is_default true for a single-select `dropdown`, and only for one option; for a multi_dropdown every option must be is_default false. Nothing in this layer enforces it — a second default is accepted here and the behaviour downstream is undefined.
`parent_option_id` is forwarded only when non-empty, and only means anything for a nested_dropdown. Get the parent id from the dataset options listing.
The created option comes back under `data` with its `id` — capture it, that is what the update and delete calls take.

A duplicate option label is rejected upstream and relayed verbatim ('Value with same name already exists. Use a unique name.'); other upstream failures are masked as 400 'The API request is invalid or improperly formed'.

capabilities.name: create_custom_field_dataset_v2

path_params.name: custom_fields_id
path_params.description: Numeric custom field id to hang the dataset off. The route matches digits only; 0 is rejected as 'Invalid Params'.

body.name: linked_projects
body.description: Integer project ids this dataset applies to — this is what makes the field visible in a project. Must be an array (or omitted) or the call is a 400. Note the spelling differs from the project-mapping call, which uses link_projects / unlink_projects.

body.name: link_to_future_projects
body.description: Auto-link projects created after this dataset. Must be a literal true/false; any other value is a 400.

body.name: options
body.description: The allowed values, for dropdown-style fields. Each entry needs option_value and a non-null is_default or the call is a 400.

fields.name: option_value
fields.description: The option label.

fields.name: is_default
fields.description: Must be present (not null). False for every option of a multi_dropdown; at most one true for a dropdown.

fields.name: parent_option_id
fields.description: For nested_dropdown children only — the option this one hangs under.

capabilities.intent: Attach another option set and project scope to an existing custom field — the way to give one field different dropdown values in different projects
guidance: A dataset is the pairing of an option list with a set of projects. A field with no dataset, or a dataset with no linked projects, is invisible in every project even though the definition exists.
`linked_projects` takes INTEGER project ids, not PR-NNN identifiers. A non-array value is a 400 'Invalid Params'; a valid array of ids that are not real projects fails upstream and comes back masked.

`linked_to_all_projects` is NOT read by this endpoint — it is silently ignored. It works only inside the `datasets` entries of the create-a-field call. To cover every project from here, enumerate the ids, or use the dataset project-mapping call with select_all.

A project can belong to only one dataset per field. Linking a project that is already on another dataset of the same field fails upstream, and this endpoint does NOT relay the reason — you get 400 {success:false, message:'The API request is invalid or improperly formed'}. Read the field's existing datasets first.

Options are only meaningful for dropdown / multi_dropdown / nested_dropdown fields, but nothing rejects them on other types. Each option needs option_value and a non-null is_default; for a multi_dropdown every is_default must be false, and for a dropdown at most one may be true.
The response is the created dataset under `data`; take `data.id` — it is the dataset_id every option and project-mapping call needs.
This is additive and reversible by deleting the dataset, but deleting it later destroys the values stored against its options.

capabilities.name: create_custom_field_definition_v2

body.name: field_name
body.description: Display label. Stripped of surrounding whitespace before the reserved-name check and before storage. Blank or longer than 256 characters → 400 'Invalid Params'.

body.name: field_type
body.description: Data type. Use THIS vocabulary — the legacy `field_*` spellings that the project form-fields read returns (field_dropdown, field_string, …) are rejected here. `url` and `nested_dropdown` are not valid when entity_type is TestCaseStep.

body.name: entity_type
body.description: Which entity the field hangs off; a field belongs to exactly one and cannot be moved later. Any other value → 400 'Invalid Params'. TestCaseStep additionally requires the group's step-custom-fields flag.

body.name: is_required
body.description: Whether the field must be filled. Must be a literal JSON boolean — omitting it, or sending "true" as a string, is a 400.

body.name: datasets
body.description: REQUIRED for every field type — omitting it (or sending a non-array) is a 400. Carries the option values and the project scope. An empty array passes validation but leaves the field linked to nothing.

fields.name: linked_projects
fields.description: Integer project ids to link. Every entry must be a positive integer; PR-NNN identifiers are rejected.

fields.name: unlinked_projects
fields.description: Integer project ids to exclude; only read when linked_to_all_projects is true.

fields.name: linked_to_all_projects
fields.description: true makes the handler resolve every project in the workspace (max 3000) into linked_projects before sending upstream.

fields.name: link_to_future_projects
fields.description: Auto-link projects created later.

fields.name: options
fields.description: Option values for dropdown-style types. Each needs option_value (non-blank) and a non-null is_default; nested_dropdown entries may carry a `children` array of the same shape.

body.name: place_holder_text
body.description: Hint text shown in the form. Stripped before storage; longer than 256 characters → 400.

body.name: default_value
body.description: Honoured ONLY when field_type is `boolean`, and then it must be a literal true/false. For every other field type the handler overwrites it with null, so a default cannot be set at create time.

body.name: levels
body.description: REQUIRED when field_type is `nested_dropdown`: at least 2 entries, each with a non-blank `name` and `level_type`. Ignored for every other type.

body.name: parent_custom_field_id
body.description: Adds a child level under an existing nested_dropdown field. When present the handler validates ONLY field_name and forwards the rest untouched — field_type, is_required and datasets are not checked at all.

capabilities.intent: Define a new custom field for the workspace — pick its data type, whether it is mandatory, and (via datasets) which projects get it and what option values it offers
guidance: `datasets` is required for EVERY field type, dropdown or not. The validator only checks it is an array, so `datasets: []` passes — and creates a field linked to no project, invisible everywhere. Send one entry carrying `linked_projects` if you want the field to appear.

`is_required` must be a literal JSON boolean. The string "true" fails the check and the whole call comes back 400 {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'} with no indication of which field was wrong — that one error covers field_type, field_name, is_required, place_holder_text, default_value, levels and datasets alike.

`default_value` is read ONLY when field_type is `boolean`; for every other type the handler forces it to null before sending upstream. Setting a default on a string/int/date field through this call is impossible.

field_name is stripped before both the duplicate check and storage, so " Priority " is stored as "Priority" and collides with the reserved name. Reserved names (Title, Description, Preconditions, Steps, Result, Attachments, State, Owner, Priority, Type of Test Case, Automation Status, Tags, Jira Issues, Asana Issues, Review Status) return 400 'Field with same name already exists. Use a unique name.'; TestPlan and ExploratorySession fields may reuse 'Automation Status' and 'Type of Test Case'.

A duplicate-name rejection from storage is relayed verbatim (400 with the upstream message). Every OTHER upstream failure on this call is masked to {success:false, message:'The API request is invalid or improperly formed'} — do not try to parse a reason out of it.

Inside a `datasets` entry, `linked_to_all_projects: true` makes the handler expand the link list to every project in the workspace (capped at 3000) before sending. That flag works HERE but is ignored by the standalone add-a-dataset call.

entity_type `TestCaseStep` is accepted only when the group has step custom fields enabled; otherwise 400 'Step custom fields are not enabled for this group.'. Step fields also cannot be `url` or `nested_dropdown`.
The response echoes only the stored field attributes — no options, no project links. Read the field back, or read the project's form fields, to confirm what the datasets actually produced.
Nothing here is project-scoped: the definition is created for the whole workspace and the datasets decide where it shows up. Name the projects you are about to affect before creating.

capabilities.name: create_dataset

body.name: name
body.description: Dataset name. Must be unique within the project: a collision comes back as 400 {success:false, message:'Dataset name already exists.'}, which is the one 400 here that is NOT a schema rejection.

body.name: variables
body.description: The columns, in order — row_data positions map to this array by index. Duplicate names (compared case-insensitively) fail the call. A column with a blank name, or one empty in every row, is SILENTLY DROPPED with its slice of every row, so the stored column list can be shorter than what you sent. 40 is the default cap; groups on the raised-limit flag get 100.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Must start with a letter and contain only letters, digits and underscores — no spaces, hyphens or leading digits.

fields.name: uuid
fields.description: Omit on create; the server mints it. Present only so the value read back can be sent to update unchanged.

body.name: rows
body.description: The data rows. Heavily normalised before the write: all-blank rows are dropped, cell values are whitespace-trimmed, rows whose trimmed values are identical are de-duplicated to the first occurrence, and row_number is then REASSIGNED 1..N in the order you sent them — the numbers you supply are ignored. 100 rows is the default cap; groups with the raised-limit flag get 200.

fields.name: row_number
fields.description: Required by the schema but overwritten server-side with the row's final 1-based position. Send anything valid; do not rely on it round-tripping.

fields.name: row_data
fields.description: Cell values, positional against `variables`. Every element must be a STRING — a number or null is a schema rejection. After empty columns are pruned the remaining length must equal the remaining column count, else 422 'Row data size mismatch with column count.'

fields.name: uuid
fields.description: Omit on create; the server mints it.

body.name: tags
body.description: Free-text labels on the dataset. Plain strings, each at most 50 characters, at most 20. Accepted but undocumented in the spec.

body.name: metadata
body.description: Free-form key/value bag stored with the dataset, at most 20 top-level keys. Only settable here — the update endpoint accepts it through validation and then drops it, so metadata cannot be changed after creation through this API.

capabilities.intent: Create a dataset — a named table of columns (variables) and rows that drives data-driven execution, so one test case runs once per row with the row's values substituted in

201.description: Dataset created. The handler renders 201 Created, not 200.

400.description: Either a request-schema rejection ({error:'Invalid JSON data', details:[...]}) or a duplicate dataset name ({success:false, message:'Dataset name already exists.'}).

422.description: {success:false, message:...}. 'Feature not available' = the group lacks Team Pro (entitlement, not payload). Any other message is a dataset-shape validation failure.

guidance: The body must be wrapped in a `dataset` object. A flat body is rejected before any field is read.

Nothing outside the declared keys is allowed: the request schema sets additionalProperties:false at the top level, inside `dataset`, and inside each variable and row object. A misspelled or extra key fails the whole call with 400 {error:'Invalid JSON data', details:[...]} rather than being ignored.
Send Content-Type: application/json. The schema check is skipped for any other content type, and the handler then crashes on a missing `variables` instead of returning a clean 400.

What you get back is not what you sent: blank rows and all-blank columns are stripped, duplicate rows collapsed, cells trimmed, and row_number renumbered 1..N. Read `dataset.variables` and `dataset.rows` from the response rather than assuming your payload was stored verbatim.

422 is overloaded on every dataset endpoint. {message:'Feature not available'} means the group lacks the Team Pro plan — stop, do not retry with a different body. Any other 422 message ('Maximum 40 columns are allowed', 'Duplicate variable names found: ...', 'Row data size mismatch with column count.', 'Please add non null/ valid data.') is a payload problem you can fix.
Success is 201, not 200, and the dataset is at the top level as `dataset` — there is no `data` envelope.
Carry `dataset.uuid` forward: it is the id every other dataset call takes, and the integer id used internally is never exposed.
Needs the test-case write permission (tc_write), not a dataset-specific one.

capabilities.name: create_exploratory_session

body.name: title
body.description: Title of the exploratory session. The only field the store requires. Send it as `title` — `name` is accepted by the request schema and then silently dropped.

body.name: description
body.example: Explore edge cases in the checkout flow.
body.description: Optional free-text description.

body.name: charter
body.description: Testing charter describing the scope and goals. Note that cloning a session does NOT copy the charter.

body.name: timebox_duration
body.description: Planned duration of the session. TM's own exported reports render this value as minutes, while the upstream store documents the field as seconds — it is passed through unconverted, so agree the unit with the product before relying on it.

body.name: owner
body.description: TCM user id of the session owner. This is the field to use: it is translated to the upstream user id here. An id matching no user in this group is accepted and stored as no assignee.

body.name: assignee
body.description: NOT a safe alias on create — unlike `owner` it is forwarded without translation to an upstream user id, so it sets the wrong user. Use `owner` instead. Ignored entirely when `owner` is also present.

body.name: folder_id
body.description: Folder to place this session in; a numeric string is also accepted. Omit to create it at the project root.

body.name: test_plan_id
body.description: Integer id of the test plan to link this session to (not a TP-NNN identifier). Only reachable through the wrapped body — the unwrapped fallback does not permit it.

body.name: duration
body.description: Tracked duration. Accepted on create but normally left to be set later by the update call.

body.name: actual_duration
body.description: Final recorded duration. Accepted on create but normally set by the update call before closing — the close call does not accept it.

body.name: tags
body.description: Plain tag strings. The request schema rejects any non-string entry.

body.name: configurations
body.description: Configuration ids (integers, or numeric strings) — not the configuration objects returned on read. An id that does not exist in this project surfaces only as the generic upstream 400.

body.name: attachments
body.description: Integer blob ids from a prior generic attachment upload — never file content. A blob already used by another entity is refused with 422. Unknown ids error only when none of them resolve; otherwise they are silently skipped.

body.name: issues
body.description: Issues to link. Each entry is {issue_id, issue_type} and may also carry metadata {url, ticket_id, title, display_category, issue_category}. A list of bare id strings is coerced to jira issues. A list of anything else is silently reduced to no issues. Jira ids must match ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]+$ or the whole call fails. Linking is applied asynchronously after the 201.

body.name: custom_fields
body.description: Custom field values as a map of {custom_field_id: value}, converted server-side into the upstream write shape. This is NOT the array shape the read endpoints return. Resolve the ids for entity type ExploratorySession first; a misspelled key is dropped rather than rejected.

capabilities.intent: Start a new exploratory testing session in a project — give it a charter, a timebox, an owner, tags, configurations and a folder — so that observations can be logged against it
guidance: The body MUST be wrapped in an `exploratory_session` object. A JSON request schema runs before the action and rejects a flat body outright with 400 'Invalid JSON data'; the handler's flat fallback is only reachable for non-JSON content types.
`title` is the only field the store requires. Everything else is optional.

Set the assignee with `owner` (a TCM user id) — NOT with `assignee`. On this create path only `owner` is translated to the upstream user id; `assignee` is forwarded raw and lands as a wrong or invalid user. On update both are translated, so the two endpoints disagree.
An `owner` that resolves to no user in this group does not fail: the session is created 201 with no assignee at all. Re-read the session if the assignment matters.

`issues` is forgiving in dangerous ways. A list of bare strings is accepted and coerced to {issue_id, issue_type:'jira'}. Jira ids are validated against ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]+$ and a bad one fails the whole call. But a list whose entries are neither strings nor objects carrying both issue_id and issue_type is silently replaced with an empty list — the session is created with no issues and no error. Each entry may also carry a `metadata` object ({url, ticket_id, title, display_category, issue_category}) even though only issue_id/issue_type are declared.
Issue linking happens asynchronously after the 201, so the session in the response does not yet show the links. Re-read it, or read the session's defects, to confirm.

`attachments` are integer ActiveStorage blob ids from a prior generic attachment upload — not file content, and not URLs. A blob already attached to another entity is refused with 422 'the attachment has been referenced elsewhere'. Unknown ids only error when NONE of them exist; a mixed list quietly attaches the ids that resolve and drops the rest.
`session_state` and `name` pass the request schema and are then dropped by the parameter filter — a session cannot be created closed, and the title must be sent as `title`.
`custom_fields` goes in as a map of {custom_field_id: value} and comes back as the normalised array shape; the two are not symmetric.
Take `exploratory_session.id` (integer) from the response and carry it as session_id into every log, defect, close, clone, update and delete call for this session.

Any upstream validation failure — an unknown configuration id, a folder in another project, a malformed value — arrives as 400 {success:false, message:'The API request is invalid or improperly formed'}. The message is the same for every cause, so it never tells you which field was wrong.

capabilities.name: create_exploratory_session_log

body.name: content
body.example: Tapped checkout — spinner appeared but no order was created.
body.description: Rich-text HTML for the entry. Sanitised on write: anchors and images pointing outside this project/group are stripped. Reference already-uploaded images by blob id in tags here — this is the only way to attach media to a log.

body.name: status
body.description: Outcome recorded for this step. `skipped` is valid. Any other value is rejected by the request schema with 400 before the handler runs.

body.name: elapsed_time
body.description: Time spent on this step, in seconds. Must be an integer — a numeric string is rejected by the request schema.

body.name: defects
body.description: Issues raised by this observation. Each entry is {issue_id, issue_type} and may carry a metadata object. Bare id strings are coerced to jira issues; a list whose entries lack issue_id or issue_type is silently reduced to no defects. Jira ids must match ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]+$ or the call fails. Linked asynchronously after the response.

capabilities.intent: Record one observation during an exploratory session — a note about what was tried and what happened, its pass/fail/bug outcome, the time it took and any defects it raised
guidance: The body MUST be wrapped in a `session_log` object. A request schema runs before the handler and rejects a flat JSON body with 400 'session_log is required'.
