This is a child of a session: the session_id in the path is the parent, and the `id` you get back is the log_id you must carry — together with the same session_id — into the update and delete calls. A log id from one session is not addressable under another.

`status` accepts pass, fail, bug, retest, block, note and skipped. `skipped` is real and is missing from older declarations of this field; anything outside the seven is rejected by the request schema with 400.
Every field is optional — a log with no content, status or elapsed_time is created successfully. Nothing here rejects an empty observation.
`content` is rich-text HTML and is sanitised on write: anchors and images pointing outside this project or group are stripped, so the stored content can differ from what you sent.

Screenshots are not uploaded through this call. Upload the image first through the generic attachment upload, then reference the returned blob id in an tag inside `content`; the handler derives the attachment links from the blob ids it finds in the HTML. If ANY referenced blob id is not visible to your group or project, EVERY attachment link for the call is dropped and the log is still created 201 with no images attached.

`defects` behaves like the session's issues: bare id strings are coerced to jira issues, entries missing issue_id or issue_type silently reduce the list to empty, and a jira id must match ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]+$ or the whole call fails. A per-entry metadata object is accepted even though only issue_id and issue_type are declared.
Defect linking is applied asynchronously after the 201, so the log echoed back may not show the links yet — re-read the logs, or the session's defects, to confirm.
`elapsed_time` is seconds.
There is no bulk log-create on this path; one call per observation.

capabilities.name: create_filter

body.name: name
body.description: Display name of the saved view. Must be unique for this project and entity — a duplicate is rejected by the backing service as a 400 'Filter name already exists'. There is also a server-side maximum length, also reported as a 400.

body.name: entity
body.description: Which list this view filters. Validated by a request-body schema before the handler runs, so an unlisted value returns 400 'Invalid JSON data' with the accepted set echoed back. Cannot be inferred — it is required even though the conditions live in `filters`.

body.name: is_project_level
body.description: true publishes the view to everyone on the project; false/omitted keeps it to you. Must be a real JSON boolean — the string "true" fails schema validation with 400.

body.name: filters
body.description: The condition set the view applies. Sent only when non-empty: `{}` is treated as absent and the backing service then rejects the create with 400 'Filters cannot be empty'. Its inner shape is the same filter object the entity search takes and is not validated here.

capabilities.intent: Save a reusable named filter view on a project — the condition set behind a test case, test run, test plan or exploratory-session list — so the same selection can be reapplied later or shared with everyone on the project
guidance: The body is flat — there is no wrapper object. It is also closed: any key other than name, entity, is_project_level and filters is rejected with 400 'Invalid JSON data' by the request-body schema before the handler sees it.
name AND entity are both required on create even though the conditions live in `filters`. entity is what binds the view to a list type; it is not derived from the contents of `filters`.
`filters: {}` is dropped as blank before the request is built, so an empty object behaves exactly like omitting the key and the create then fails downstream. Send at least one real condition.

Conditions are not checked against the project's custom fields at write time. A condition on a custom field that does not exist is accepted here and is silently pruned — permanently — the first time anyone reads the filter back.
Carry `data.id` from the response: that integer is the filter_id every later read, update and delete takes.
Only the backing service's 400 is translated into `{success:false, message:...}`; any other failure from it is re-raised and surfaces as a 500, so a 500 here is not necessarily a server bug.
Not permission-gated — the filter controller has no entry in the RBAC map, so anyone with product access to the project can create a project-level view.

capabilities.name: create_project_v1

body.name: name
body.description: Project name. Leading/trailing whitespace is stripped. Not checked for uniqueness — a duplicate name is accepted.

body.name: description
body.description: Free text. HTML is escaped server-side, so what comes back can differ from what you sent.

body.name: access_type
body.description: Visibility of the new project. Only honoured when project-level RBAC is enabled for the group — otherwise accepted and ignored. When it IS enabled, a value outside this set fails the whole request with 400 'Invalid access type'.

body.name: users
body.description: Per-user grants applied at creation, as [{user, role}]. Only read when access_type is also sent AND project-level RBAC is on; ignored entirely otherwise.

capabilities.intent: Create a new project — the top-level container every folder, test case, run, plan and report lives under; returns both the integer id the v1 routes take and the PR-NNN identifier the v2 routes take

200.description: Project created. The project is at data.project — same envelope and same serializer as the v1 project-detail read.

guidance: The body must be wrapped in a `project` object — the server requires a `project` wrapper. A flat {name: ...} body returns 400 before any field is read.

`name` is the only field that must be present. It is stripped of surrounding whitespace, and name uniqueness is not enforced here — creating a second project with an existing name succeeds and gives you two projects that are indistinguishable by name.
`description` is HTML-escaped server-side, so the stored value can differ from what you sent.

`access_type` and `users` are read only when project-level RBAC is enabled for the group; with that off both keys are accepted and silently ignored, and the project is created with the group default. With it on, an access_type outside private/restricted/org_wide fails the whole call with 400 'Invalid access type'.

The new project is at `data.project` — this v1 route wraps its payload in a `data` envelope. Carry `data.project.id` (integer) for every other the v1 surface project route and `data.project.identifier` (PR-NNN) for anything under the v2 surface; the two id forms are not interchangeable.
Requires the project_create permission under RBAC; without it the call is 403 'This action is not permitted for the user'.
There is no delete-project capability in this index, so a project created by mistake cannot be removed through the registry — only through the UI.

capabilities.name: create_report

body.name: projectId
body.description: Integer project id. Alias for `project_id`; either satisfies the project requirement on create, and the project in the path is used when both are absent.

body.name: project_id
body.description: Integer project id the report is primarily filed under. Must be one of `project_ids` when that is also sent.

body.name: project_ids
body.description: Integer project ids for a cross-project report. Max 60 (max 5 for User Workload Report), and only accepted for the seven multi-project types — any other type with more than one id is 400. The first entry becomes the primary project when `project_id` is omitted.

body.name: report_type
body.description: Report type as its DISPLAY NAME, not a slug. `Defects Summary` and `Defects Detailed Report` are accepted but have no server-side data branch, so such a report always reads back `report_data: null` — for defect figures use `Test Run Summary` and its `issues_by_priority` / `issues_by_status` sections. `Test Plan Detailed Report` is feature-flagged: an unflagged group gets 403.

body.name: report_timeframe
body.description: The window the report covers, and the value of `reportTimeRange` on the summary-by-type read. The four relative windows and `custom` compute dates; `custom` REQUIRES `custom_date_range` (omitting it is an unhandled 500, not a 422). The remaining five carry no dates — each selects entities through one matching `report_filters` key.

body.name: report_creation_mode
body.description: `system_generated` is the one-click report the product creates for you; `custom_report` is user-configured. For a Requirement Traceability Report, `system_generated` makes the server auto-populate `report_filters.requirements` with every requirement in the project — do not also send that filter.

body.name: grain
body.description: Requirement Traceability Report only: `test_plan` renders Requirement to Test Plan to Sub-Test Plan rows. Any other report type is 400, and it is single-project only. Immutable — a later edit that changes it is refused 400 (resending the same value is fine).

body.name: is_dynamic
body.description: Whether the report re-resolves its selection each run. Omit and the server infers it from whether any `dynamic_filters` value is non-blank.

body.name: test_run
body.description: Dynamic (re-evaluated each run) run selection. Accepted under either `dynamic_filters` or `filters`; presence of any non-blank value here is what flips the report to dynamic when `is_dynamic` is omitted.

body.name: test_runs
body.description: Run ids, and they must be INTEGERS — a quoted id or a TR-NNN identifier fails the whole request 400 'Invalid report filters'. Pairs with report_timeframe=specific_test_runs.

body.name: test_plans
body.description: Plan ids, and they must be INTEGERS — a quoted id or a TP-NNN identifier fails the whole request 400 'Invalid report filters'. Pairs with report_timeframe=specific_test_plans.

body.name: test_cases
body.description: Case selection — pairs with report_timeframe=specific_test_cases. Must be an OBJECT (an array is rejected 400 'Invalid report filters'), folder-keyed like SelectionData. Folder ids are STRING keys; case ids are INTEGERS (the numeric `id`, not TC-NNN). A wrong-but-object shape saves an UNSCOPED project-wide report at 200.

body.name: shared_selection
body.description: Cross-project case selection: { "<project_id>": <same shape as test_cases> } for the report's non-primary projects. A project id outside `project_ids` is dropped silently.

body.name: session_ids
body.description: Exploratory session ids — pairs with report_timeframe=specific_sessions.

body.name: requirements
body.description: { issue_type: [issue_id, ...] } — pairs with report_timeframe=requirements. Must be an object; an array is rejected 400. Auto-populated by the server when report_creation_mode is system_generated on a traceability report.

body.name: test_plan_selection
body.description: Per-plan sub-plan selection: { plan_id: { select_all, selected_sub_plan_ids, deselected_sub_plan_ids } }. `select_all` is required on each entry and must be a real boolean; a malformed entry is silently discarded rather than rejected.

body.name: test_runs_by_project
body.description: Cross-project run selection: { "<project_id>": [run_id, ...] }. Keys must be numeric strings and values arrays of numeric ids or the request is 400. When present it REPLACES the flat `test_runs` key, which is then ignored.

body.name: test_plans_by_project
body.description: Cross-project plan selection: { "<project_id>": [plan_id, ...] }. Same validation as test_runs_by_project, and it replaces the flat `test_plans` and `test_plan_selection` keys.

body.name: builds
body.description: Internal build ids paired 1:1 with `test_runs`. Sent back by the read path for round-tripping an edit; do not invent values.

body.name: tc_custom_fields
body.description: Keyed by custom-field id (an OBJECT, not an array). ONLY consumed for `Test Run Summary`, `Test Run Detailed Report` and `Test Case Activity` — on the other types the server never reads it and drops it silently. Persisted, and read back, under the name `custom_fields`.

body.name: custom_date_range
body.description: "YYYY-MM-DD YYYY-MM-DD", space separated. REQUIRED whenever report_timeframe is `custom` — omitting it is a 500, not a validation error. Ignored (and nulled on edit) for every other timeframe.

body.name: users
body.description: TM user ids to mail the report to. Every id must belong to your group or the whole request is 400 'Invalid mail to users'. Only persisted when the report is scheduled.

body.name: external_mails
body.description: Email addresses outside the group. Only persisted when the report is scheduled.

body.name: frequency
body.description: Scheduling cadence. Send `frequency` and `frequency_details` together or omit BOTH — omitting both creates a valid unscheduled, on-demand report (and `mail_to` is then dropped silently). The enum is daily/weekly/monthly only: `once` passes body validation and then raises 'Unsupported frequency type' as a 500.

body.name: time
body.description: 24-hour HH:MM, UTC. Required for every cadence; missing or malformed is 400 'Invalid report frequency'.

body.name: day
body.description: Required for weekly — a lowercase English day name, nothing else — and for monthly, where it is an integer 1-28 (29-31 are rejected). Omit for daily.

capabilities.intent: Save a report definition over a project's runs, plans, cases, sessions or requirements — scheduled to email on a cadence, or unscheduled and read on demand
guidance: Four body fields are required by the validator, not just the three the spec marks: `report_type`, `report_timeframe`, `report_creation_mode`, and a project (either `project_id`/`projectId` in the body or the project in the path). Any one missing comes back 400 `Validation error. Invalid report type|timeframe|creation mode.` — the message names which.

This returns HTTP 200, not 201, despite creating a record. The new report is at `data`; carry `data.id` (an integer) forward as the `report_id` for every other report call. `data.identifier` is the SC-NNN display string and is NOT accepted anywhere as an id.
Creating the report does NOT compute it. The response `data` is the definition only; there is no `report_data` here. Read the report afterwards to get figures, and name the sections you want.

`report_timeframe` and `report_filters` must agree. The five entity timeframes each read exactly one filter key — specific_test_runs reads `test_runs`, specific_test_plans reads `test_plans`, specific_test_cases reads `test_cases`, specific_sessions reads `session_ids`, requirements reads `requirements`. Naming the timeframe and leaving its filter empty saves a report that resolves to nothing, at 200.

`report_filters.test_runs` and `.test_plans` must be arrays of INTEGERS. A string id ("123") or a TR-NNN/TP-NNN identifier fails the whole request with 400 `Validation error. Invalid report filters.`, and `test_cases` / `requirements` must be objects, not arrays.

Scheduling is inferred, never declared: the report is scheduled iff BOTH `frequency` and `frequency_details` are present. `mail_to` is only persisted for a scheduled report — recipients sent on an unscheduled one are dropped silently and `next_run_at` stays null. Use the send-email-now capability to mail an unscheduled report.
`report_timeframe: custom` without `custom_date_range` is an unhandled 500, not a 422 — the server splits the value unconditionally. Send "YYYY-MM-DD YYYY-MM-DD", space separated.
`frequency: once` is accepted by body validation and then raises 'Unsupported frequency type' as a 500. Omit both scheduling fields for a one-off report instead.

Cross-project: send `project_ids` (integers). At most 60, and only for Test Run Summary, Test Plan Summary, Test Run Detailed Report, Test Plan Detailed Report, Test Case Activity, Requirement Traceability Report and User Workload Report — anything else is 400. User Workload Report caps at 5 projects. When both are sent, `project_id` must be one of them; when only `project_ids` is sent the first entry becomes the primary project.

`report_creation_mode: system_generated` on a Requirement Traceability Report makes the server fetch every linked requirement in the project and populate `report_filters.requirements` for you — do not also send that filter.
`grain: test_plan` is Requirement Traceability Report only, single-project only, and immutable after creation (a later edit that changes it is refused 400). Omit it for the normal test-case grain.
Requires the report_create permission on the project; 403 otherwise. `Test Plan Detailed Report` additionally needs a per-group feature flag and returns 403 `Operation not permitted` without it.
The write also syncs the report to Test Observability. If that sync fails the created row is deleted again and the call errors — a 5xx here means nothing was kept.

capabilities.name: create_root_folder_v1

body.name: name
body.description: Folder name. Must be wrapped in a `folder` object — the handler reads a required `folder` wrapper, so a flat body is a 400 before any field is looked at.

body.name: notes
body.example: This folder contains all regression test cases
body.description: Free-text description, HTML allowed. It is unescaped, sanitised and re-escaped server-side, so the stored value can differ from what you sent. Note the key is `notes`: `description` is silently dropped by the permit list on this v1 route.

body.name: auto_rename
body.description: Send the literal string "true" to have a clashing name auto-suffixed instead of rejected. Any other value, and any boolean, is treated as false — the comparison is against the string "true".

body.name: attachments
body.description: Integer ids of already-uploaded attachment blobs to bind to the folder. Each must belong to this group/project and must not already be attached to anything else — a reused blob fails the whole call with 422 and the bare string "the attachment has been referenced elsewhere".

capabilities.intent: Create a top-level folder in a project — the first thing you need before test cases can be filed anywhere
guidance: The body must be wrapped: {"folder": {"name": "...", "notes": "..."}}. Sending name/notes flat returns 400 {error:'param is missing or the value is empty: folder'} — this entry shipped without that wrapper and was unusable.

Uniqueness is always enforced against sibling root folders. A duplicate name comes back with the entity store's own message and status relayed verbatim — this is one of the few folder endpoints that does NOT mask the upstream text. Send auto_rename:"true" if you want it renamed instead.
The created folder is at `data.folder`, not at the top level. `data.project` carries the project it landed in. The id you carry forward is `data.folder.id`, a plain integer.
Passing the literal path segment `new` as project_id CREATES a default project and puts the folder in it. Only do that deliberately.
Requires the folder-create permission; 403 otherwise.
Folders keep no version history, so a folder created here can only be undone by deleting it — and folder deletion is itself not reversible through this API.

capabilities.name: create_shared_step_v1

body.name: title
body.description: Name of the shared step block. Only presence of the key is checked here — an empty string passes this layer and is rejected by the backing service, so a blank title fails late with a different error than a missing one.

body.name: folder_id
body.description: Shared-field folder to file the block under. The key is forwarded only when present; omit it (or send null) to leave the block at the root (Unassigned).

body.name: tags
body.description: Plain tag name strings on the shared step itself (separate from the tags on the test cases that embed it). Accepted here but previously undeclared.

body.name: shared_step_details
body.description: The ordered step rows. Required — omitting the key entirely fails local validation with a flat 400 'Validation Error' that names no field. An empty array IS accepted and creates a titled block with no steps.

fields.name: order
fields.description: 1-based position. Every row needs order >= 1; a missing or 0 order fails the whole request, not just that row.

fields.name: step
fields.description: Step body, HTML. Each row must carry at least one of step or result or the whole request is rejected.

fields.name: result
fields.description: Expected result, HTML. Each row must carry at least one of step or result.

capabilities.intent: Create a reusable shared step block in a project — a titled set of step/result rows that many test cases can then embed by reference instead of copying

query.name: render_image_urls
query.description: When true, inline image attachments referenced in the step/result HTML are returned as resolved URLs rather than raw references.

guidance: The body is flat — title, folder_id, tags and shared_step_details sit at the top level with no wrapper.

shared_step_details is required even when empty. Every row must have order >= 1 and at least one of step/result; one bad row fails the entire call with a bare 400 `{data:null, success:false, message:"Validation Error"}` that does not say which row or which field.
Success is 200 with `{data, success:true}` — not 201, and the body is not empty.
Carry `data.id`. That integer is the shared_step_id you put on a test case's `test_case_steps[].shared_step_id`, and the id for every later read, update and delete of this block.
Creating a shared step attaches it to nothing. Embedding is done from the test case side; this call only makes the block available.
step and result are HTML. Inline attachment references are validated server-side and an unresolvable one fails the call with 400 'attachment in text is invalid'.
Requires tc_write — the same permission as editing a test case.

capabilities.name: create_step_result_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id (this route only matches digits; a PR-NNN identifier never reaches the API).

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Run id. This v1 route accepts both the bare integer and the TR-NNN identifier.

path_params.name: step_id
path_params.description: Numeric id of the step on the test case (from the case detail), not its position in the step list. The route only matches digits.

body.name: status
body.description: Step outcome as a NAME. This is the value that is actually written. A same-named key at the top level of the body is validated but never written.

body.name: status_id
body.description: Numeric status id. Accepted and forwarded, but the step surface is name-based — prefer `status` unless you know the backing service expects an id here.

body.name: description
body.description: Note for this step. Rich text; links to uploaded attachments are rewritten server-side, so the stored value can differ from what you sent. Also copied onto the case-level result.

body.name: attachments
body.description: Integer blob ids from a prior generic attachment upload (or {id: <blob id>} objects) — NOT filenames and NOT file bytes. An unresolvable or already-used blob fails the whole call with 422.

body.name: custom_fields
body.description: Custom field values keyed by custom field id. Copied onto the case-level result as well as the step.

body.name: issues
body.description: Linked defects. Each entry must be an OBJECT; a bare string is dropped by the parameter filter with no error, so the link is silently never created.

capabilities.intent: Log the outcome of ONE step inside a test case's execution in a run — the per-step pass/fail you record while working through a manual test case, as opposed to the case's overall result

200.description: The full test result for the case, at the top level of the body (no envelope). The step's own outcome is nested under `test_run_step_result`.

400.description: Either a duplicate request inside the one-second lock ({success:false, message:'Request is already being processed'}) or a top-level `status` outside the supported step statuses ({error:'Validation error'}).

403.description: Caller lacks execute permission on this test run ({success:false, message:"You don't have permission to execute test cases in this test run"}).

422.description: An attachment blob id could not be resolved or is already referenced elsewhere ({base: [reason]}).

guidance: The body must be wrapped in `test_run_step_result`. That object is forwarded to the backing service essentially verbatim, so only the keys below are acted on locally and unrecognised keys are passed through rather than rejected.

The step's status travels as a NAME inside the wrapper (`status`), not as the numeric status id the case-level result endpoints take. The supported names are untested, passed, failed, retest, blocked, skipped, in_progress.

There is a decoy: a TOP-LEVEL `status` key is validated against that same list and 400s {error:'Validation error'} when it is not in it — but it is not the value that gets written. Sending only a top-level status passes validation and logs nothing.

Repeat calls for the same project/run/case/step within one second are refused with 400 {success:false, message:'Request is already being processed'} by a one-second lock. That is a de-duplication guard, not a validation failure — pause and retry.

Logging a step result also rewrites the CASE's result in that run: if the wrapper carries any of description, attachments, custom_fields or issues, those are copied onto the case-level result and its status is taken from the step write. A status-only step write leaves the case result's fields alone.

`attachments` here are integer blob ids from a prior generic attachment upload — not filenames and not file content. An id that cannot be resolved, or a blob already attached elsewhere, fails the whole call with 422.
Requires execute permission on the run (403 otherwise). `step_id` is the numeric id of the step on the test case — read it from the case detail; it is not the step's 1-based position.
The 200 body is the full CASE result object at the top level — no envelope, no `success` key, and no separate step-result record. The step's own outcome is nested under `test_run_step_result` on it.

query.name: configuration_id
query.description: Target the execution for one configuration when the case runs against a configuration matrix. Forwarded as configId.

query.name: mapping_id
query.description: Target one specific run/case row. Also selects the newer write path, on which the response is an optimistic payload built from the submitted body rather than a re-read of the stored result.

capabilities.name: create_sub_folder_v1

body.name: name
body.description: Name of the new subfolder. Must be wrapped in a `folder` object — the handler reads a required `folder` wrapper, so a flat body is a 400 before any field is read.

body.name: notes
body.description: Free-text description, HTML allowed; sanitised server-side so the stored value can differ from what you sent. The key is `notes` — `description` is silently dropped by the permit list on this v1 route.

body.name: auto_rename
body.description: Literal string "true" to auto-suffix a clashing sibling name instead of failing. Any other value, including the boolean true, reads as false.

body.name: attachments
body.description: Integer ids of already-uploaded attachment blobs. Each must belong to this group/project and must be unattached; a reused blob fails the call with 422 and the bare string "the attachment has been referenced elsewhere".

capabilities.intent: Create a folder inside an existing folder — use this to build out a nested test-case tree one level at a time
guidance: The body must be wrapped: {"folder": {"name": "..."}}. A flat body returns 400 for a missing `folder` you never sent.
`folder_id` in the path is the PARENT. It is fetched first, so a folder id from another project comes back as a bare 404 {success:false} with no message telling you which id was wrong.
folder_id must be a positive integer. Literal 0 raises an unhandled ArgumentError and surfaces as a 500, not a 400.

Sibling-name uniqueness is always checked and the upstream message is relayed verbatim on failure (unusually — most folder endpoints mask it). auto_rename:"true" turns the rejection into a silent rename.
The new folder is at `data.folder`; there is no `folder` at the top level and no `project` key on this action (unlike root creation). Carry `data.folder.id` forward.
Requires the folder-create permission.

capabilities.name: create_template_v2

body.name: name
body.description: Template name. Must be unique within the workspace for the entity type; a duplicate is rejected upstream with a 400 carrying the reason.

body.name: entity
body.description: What the template applies to. Only test-case templates are supported today; leave this out and it defaults to TestCase.

body.name: description_fields
body.description: Ordered fields placed in the template's description section. Resolve real field ids first — an invented id is rejected upstream. Omitting this creates a template with an empty description section.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The system field id when is_system is true, otherwise the custom field id.

fields.name: is_system
fields.description: True for a built-in field, false or absent for a custom field.

fields.name: is_mandatory
fields.description: Whether a test case using this template must fill the field.

body.name: properties_fields
body.description: Ordered fields placed in the template's properties section. Unlike an update, a create does NOT auto-add the Review & Approve system fields — the template gets exactly the ids you send.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The system field id when is_system is true, otherwise the custom field id.

body.name: linked_projects
body.description: Projects the template is linked to at creation. Omit it and the server defaults every flag to false with no projects, so the template exists but is offered in no project until it is linked.

fields.name: link_to_future_projects
fields.description: Automatically link projects created later.

fields.name: linked_to_all_projects
fields.description: Link every existing project.

fields.name: link_projects
fields.description: Integer project ids to link. These are the numeric project ids, not the PR- identifiers.

fields.name: unlink_projects
fields.description: Integer project ids to unlink. Meaningless on a create.

capabilities.intent: Create a new test-case template — define which description and property fields a test case gets and, optionally, which projects it applies to.
guidance: Paid plans only. On a free plan the gate answers with HTTP 200 and a body of success:false / 'This Feature is only for paid customers'. Check the success flag, not the status code, before reporting the template as created.
Field ids cannot be guessed. Resolve the workspace's system fields and custom-field definitions first and mark is_system true for built-in fields.
Nothing is validated locally — name, field ids and project ids all go straight upstream, so a malformed body surfaces as a 400 with a single message rather than a per-field error list.
A create does not auto-inject the Review & Approve system fields, but a later update of properties_fields will. The two calls therefore do not behave the same way on the same field list.
The 201 body carries the full template including its fields — read it rather than re-fetching, and keep the returned id.

capabilities.name: create_test_case_v1
capabilities.intent: Create one test case at the project level — the call to use to seed the FIRST case in a project that has no folders yet, via create_at_root.
guidance: This route has no folder in its path, so you must supply one: either `test_case.test_case_folder_id` (an existing folder) plus a top-level `folder_id` naming the same folder, or `create_at_root: true` to have the folder minted.
Without a resolvable folder the create still reaches the backend and then fails while building the response, surfacing as a 422 rather than a clear validation error. Resolve the folder id first.

`create_at_root: true` only works on a project with ZERO folders — it creates a folder called 'New Folder' and puts the case there. On a project that already has folders it is 400 'Root Folder Already Exists'.
For any project that already has folders, prefer the folder-scoped create instead; this route exists for the empty-project case.
Steps only come from `test_case_steps`, and only when `template`/`template_step_type` selects a step-shaped template — the default is `test_case_text`, which stores no steps and still returns 200.
The new case comes back at `data.test_case`; take its integer `id` and its TC-NNN `identifier` from there. `data.folder`, `data.project` and `data.path_folders` describe where it landed.

If the project has e-signature enabled and you set `review_status: in_review` (or `send_for_review`), the call needs a `test_case.reauth_token`; without it the response is 401 `{success:false, error_code:"reauth_required"}`.
A test case keeps version history, so an edit is recoverable — but nothing undoes a create except deleting the case.

body.name: test_case
body.description: The case to create. Everything about the case goes inside this wrapper — the handler requires it, so a flat body is a 400 before any field is read.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Case title. Required.

fields.name: test_case_folder_id
fields.description: Target folder's integer id. Required in the body — the project-level route has no folder in its path, and with `create_at_root` the folder is minted for you instead.

fields.name: attachments
fields.description: Attachment blob ids to attach to the new case. A blob from another group fails the request with 422.

fields.name: automation_status
fields.description: Legacy alias for `automation_state`, as an internal_name string (e.g. `not_automated`). Applied only when `automation_state` is omitted.

fields.name: case_type
fields.description: Numeric case-type option id, or the project's display name for it.

fields.name: estimate
fields.description: Accepted and then never written; every read serialises `estimate` as null. Use `estimated_duration_seconds`.

fields.name: estimated_duration_seconds
fields.description: Per-case estimated execution time in SECONDS. This is the field that actually stores an estimate.

fields.name: is_dataset_modified
fields.description: Ignored on create — dataset mappings are always regenerated from `test_case_dataset`.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: TM user id. An id that is not a member of the group is replaced with the caller instead of being rejected.

fields.name: priority
fields.description: Numeric priority option id, or the project's display name for it (a string is resolved by name, an integer by id).

fields.name: review_status
fields.description: Review state. Never left untouched on create: when omitted it is set from the project's review-approve setting, falling back to `pending`.

fields.name: reviewers
fields.description: Reviewer TM user ids (emails also resolve). Honoured only on a Team-Pro workspace with review-approve enabled; otherwise dropped without error. Including the owner is rejected with 422 'Owner cannot be a reviewer'.

fields.name: send_for_review
fields.description: Dropped on create — the create flow already notifies from `reviewers` + `review_status`. Setting `review_status: in_review` is what triggers the send-for-review path, including its re-authentication gate.

fields.name: shared_precondition_id
fields.description: Link a shared precondition. Only applied when `preconditions` is sent in the same body.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Numeric status option id. Unlike priority/case_type, a display NAME is not resolved here — it is written through as the id and breaks the field.

fields.name: template
fields.description: Step-shape template name. Defaults to `test_case_text` when neither this nor `template_step_type` is sent, which silently discards `test_case_steps`.

fields.name: test_case_steps
fields.description: The only key read for steps. Items are `{step, result, test_data?, order?, shared_step_id?}`; `order` is filled in by position when omitted. A `steps` key instead is dropped and the case is created with no steps, still 200.

body.name: create_at_root
body.description: Create the project's first folder ('New Folder') and put this case in it. Only valid when the project has NO folders — otherwise 400 'Root Folder Already Exists'.

body.name: folder_id
body.description: TOP-LEVEL folder id, outside `test_case`. This is what the ownership check reads and what the success response's folder block is built from; without it (and without `create_at_root`) the response build fails and you get a 422.

body.name: create_subfolder
body.description: Compared to the literal boolean `true`. Creates or reuses a subfolder named `scenario_name` under `test_case.test_case_folder_id` and puts the case there. The subfolder is deleted again if the create then fails.

body.name: scenario_name
body.description: Name of the subfolder to create or reuse when `create_subfolder` is true.

capabilities.name: create_test_cases

body.name: test_case
body.description: The case to create. Everything about the case goes inside this wrapper — the handler requires it, so a flat body is a 400 before any field is read.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Case title. Required.

fields.name: test_case_folder_id
fields.description: Target folder's integer id. Required in the body — the project-level route has no folder in its path, and with `create_at_root` the folder is minted for you instead.

fields.name: attachments

fields.name: automation_status
fields.description: Legacy alias for `automation_state`, as an internal_name string (e.g. `not_automated`). Applied only when `automation_state` is omitted.

fields.name: case_type

fields.name: estimate
fields.description: Accepted and then never written; every read serialises `estimate` as null. Use `estimated_duration_seconds`.

fields.description: Per-case estimated execution time in SECONDS. This is the field that actually stores an estimate.

fields.name: is_dataset_modified
