fields.name: owner
fields.description: TM user id. An id that is not a member of the group is replaced with the caller instead of being rejected.

fields.name: priority
fields.description: Numeric priority option id, or the project's display name for it (a string is resolved by name, an integer by id).

fields.name: review_status
fields.description: Review state. Never left untouched on create: when omitted it is set from the project's review-approve setting, falling back to `pending`.

fields.name: reviewers
fields.description: Reviewer TM user ids (emails also resolve). Honoured only on a Team-Pro workspace with review-approve enabled; otherwise dropped without error. Including the owner is rejected with 422 'Owner cannot be a reviewer'.

fields.name: send_for_review
fields.description: Dropped on create — the create flow already notifies from `reviewers` + `review_status`. Setting `review_status: in_review` is what triggers the send-for-review path, including its re-authentication gate.

fields.name: shared_precondition_id
fields.description: Link a shared precondition. Only applied when `preconditions` is sent in the same body.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Numeric status option id. Unlike priority/case_type, a display NAME is not resolved here — it is written through as the id and breaks the field.

fields.name: template
fields.description: Step-shape template name. Defaults to `test_case_text` when neither this nor `template_step_type` is sent, which silently discards `test_case_steps`.

fields.name: test_case_steps
fields.description: The only key read for steps. Items are `{step, result, test_data?, order?, shared_step_id?}`; `order` is filled in by position when omitted. A `steps` key instead is dropped and the case is created with no steps, still 200.

body.name: create_at_root
body.description: Not useful on this route — the folder is already in the path. It only has an effect on a project with zero folders, where it mints 'New Folder'; otherwise it turns the call into a 400 'Root Folder Already Exists'.

body.name: create_subfolder
body.description: Compared to the literal boolean `true`. Creates or reuses a subfolder named `scenario_name` under `test_case.test_case_folder_id` and puts the case there instead of in the path folder.

body.name: scenario_name
body.description: Name of the subfolder to create or reuse when `create_subfolder` is true.

capabilities.intent: Create one test case in a folder — the normal single-case create. For more than one case, use the bulk create instead.
guidance: Despite the plural name this creates exactly ONE case: the body is a single `test_case` object, not a list. The bulk route is the one that takes an array.

`test_case.test_case_folder_id` is required in the BODY as well as in the path — the path folder is not substituted in, and omitting it is the most common create failure (a 422 wrapping an upstream 404).

Steps only come from `test_case_steps`, and only when the template is step-shaped. Neither `template` nor `template_step_type` sent means `test_case_text`, which stores no steps and still returns 200 — verify `test_case_steps` in the response.

priority and case_type accept either the numeric option id or the project's display name; `status` does NOT — a status name is written through as an id. Resolve the ids from the project's system field values first.

`review_status` is never left alone on create: omitted, it is set from the project's review-approve setting, falling back to `pending`. `reviewers` is only honoured on a Team-Pro workspace with review-approve enabled, and including the owner is a 422.
The new case is at `data.test_case` — its integer `id` and TC-NNN `identifier` are both there. `data.request_trace_id` refers to the AI enrichment that continues after the response.
Linked `issues` are processed asynchronously after the response, so a 200 does not mean the links exist yet.

capabilities.name: create_test_plan_v1

body.name: name
body.description: Plan name. REQUIRED — a missing or blank name is 400 {success: false, message: 'Name field cannot be blank'}, and nothing else in the body is looked at.

body.name: description
body.description: Rich text. Sanitised against the RTE allowlist and rewritten server-side, so the stored value can differ from what you sent.

body.name: start_date
body.description: ISO-8601 date. Stored as midnight UTC. An unparseable value is silently dropped rather than rejected.

body.name: end_date
body.description: ISO-8601 date. If it is earlier than start_date the call returns HTTP 200 with {success: false, error: 'Please check date params'} and creates nothing.

body.name: plan_status
body.description: ACCEPTED BUT NEVER APPLIED ON CREATE — it is not forwarded upstream, so every new plan starts as `new`. Move it on with a follow-up plan update.

body.name: owner
body.description: Owner as the internal TM user id (the `id` from the project users read — NOT a BrowserStack user id and not an email). Omit the key to own it yourself. An id that does not resolve inside the caller's group is swallowed, not rejected, and the plan is created with no real owner.

body.name: parent_plan_id
body.description: Parent plan's INTEGER id. Set it to create a SUB-plan — the result carries an STP-NNN identifier. Null/omitted means a top-level plan. This choice is effectively permanent: a plan can never later be demoted into a sub-plan or promoted out of one.

body.name: tags
body.description: Plain tag strings. If ANY entry is not a string the whole list is silently replaced with [] — the plan is created with no tags and no error.

body.name: reviewers
body.description: Reviewer user ids. Attach-only — adding reviewers does NOT send the plan for review, and reviewers are only emailed once the plan is actually in review. Rejected if the project restricts reviewers and one is not on the allowed list.

body.name: attachments
body.description: Ids of attachments already uploaded via the attachments surface. An id that does not verify against this group returns 422 with the verifier's own body, not the usual {success, error} envelope.

body.name: custom_fields
body.description: Custom-field values keyed as the test-plan form-fields read returns them. A bad key or value is 400 {success: false, error: <message>}.

body.name: issues
body.description: Linked tracker issues. Structured — NOT a flat array of keys. A bare string entry is coerced to {issue_id: <string>}, losing the tracker type. Only url and ticket_id are kept inside metadata; other metadata keys are dropped.

body.name: test_runs
body.description: Test runs to link, as run INTEGER ids (a run's `uuid`, not its TR-NNN `id`). Linking MOVES a run: it leaves whatever plan held it, with nothing in the 200 to say so.

capabilities.intent: Create a test plan to group test runs for a release or milestone — or create a SUB-plan under an existing plan by setting parent_plan_id

200.description: The created plan under a top-level `test_plan` key (no `data` wrapper). `identifier` is the `TP-NNN` (or `STP-NNN` for a sub-plan) and `id` is the integer the other v1 routes take.

400.description: Missing name (`{success: false, message: "Name field cannot be blank"}`) or a rejected custom field (`{success: false, error: ...}`). A body with no `test_plan` wrapper lands here too.

404.description: Also used for an upstream payload rejection: `{success: false, error: "Invalid Params"}`.

guidance: Every field goes inside a `test_plan` object. A flat body is rejected before any field is read.
name is the only required field, and it is checked first — a 400 {success: false, message: 'Name field cannot be blank'} means exactly that and nothing about the rest of the body.
plan_status is accepted and then ignored. A new plan is always `new`; drive it to started/completed with the plan update capability, which needs the matching date in the same request.
Bad dates are a 200 trap: end_date < start_date returns HTTP 200 carrying {success: false, error: 'Please check date params'}. Branch on `success`, never on the status code.
An upstream rejection of the payload is reported as HTTP 404 with {success: false, error: 'Invalid Params'} — a 404 from this endpoint usually means a bad body, not a missing project.
Linked issues are processed on a background job, so they are usually absent from the plan you get back in this response even though the call succeeded. Re-read the plan to see them.
Carry `test_plan.id` (the integer) forward for every other v1 plan route; `test_plan.identifier` is the TP-NNN (STP-NNN for a sub-plan) used for display and by the newer API surface.
The reply is the re-read plan under a top-level `test_plan` key — there is no `data` wrapper.

capabilities.name: create_test_result_for_test_case

body.name: status_id
body.description: Result status id — resolve the name ("Passed", "Failed") to an id first; this field takes the id. Effectively required, though a missing value is accepted and leaves the result unstatused.

body.name: issues
body.description: Linked defects. Each entry is an OBJECT — a bare string is silently dropped by the server's parameter filter, so the issue link is never created and no error is returned.

body.name: configuration_id
body.description: Which configuration this result is for. TOP level — the server does not read it from inside `test_result`, so nesting it silently logs the result against the default configuration.

body.name: mapping_id
body.description: Target a specific run/case mapping. Top level.

body.name: test_case_count
body.description: Total number of test cases linked to the automation execution

capabilities.intent: Create a new test result for a test case in a test run
guidance: This is how a pass or fail is recorded against a case in a run. Editing the run or the case does not record an outcome.

capabilities.name: create_test_results_for_test_run_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR- form. A bare integer does not match the route and 404s.

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Test run identifier in TR- form. A bare integer does not match the route and 404s.

body.name: results
body.description: Bulk form: one entry per test case. Mutually exclusive with the single form below — send `results` OR `test_result`, never both. Each entry needs `test_result` plus `test_case_id` or `execution_id`. No other keys are allowed on an entry.

fields.name: test_case_id
fields.description: Test case identifier, e.g. TC-101. Required unless execution_id is given.

fields.name: execution_id
fields.description: Automation execution id, as an alternative target to test_case_id.

fields.name: test_result
fields.description: The outcome itself: status (name), description, issues, step_results. Same shape as the single-result `test_result` below.

fields.name: attachments
fields.description: Multipart file part filenames for this entry. Ignored on a plain JSON request.

body.name: status
body.description: Result status by NAME as configured for the project ("Passed", "Failed", "Untested"). v1's numeric status_id is NOT accepted here. Required unless step_results is sent instead.

body.name: description
body.description: Notes on the outcome. Rich text is accepted. Silently truncated at 16 KB rather than rejected.

body.name: issues
body.description: Linked defects as plain KEY STRINGS (e.g. ["JIRA-12"]) — unlike v1, which takes objects. Pair with issue_tracker to type them.

body.name: issue_tracker
body.description: Types the linked issues, e.g. {"name": "jira"}. Only read from inside test_result.

body.name: elapsed_time
body.description: Execution time in seconds. Stored as time_elapsed.

body.name: custom_fields
body.description: Result custom fields keyed by field name; resolved against the project's TestResult custom fields.

body.name: step_results
body.description: Per-step outcomes. Send these INSTEAD of a top-level status; each entry needs `status` plus `step_id` or `step_index`. The parent case status is rolled up from the steps.

body.name: test_case_id
body.description: Single form: which case in the run this result is for. TOP level — not inside test_result. One of test_case_id, execution_id or shared_test_case_ids is required.

body.name: execution_id
body.description: Single form: target an automation execution instead of a case identifier. Top level.

body.name: shared_test_case_ids
body.description: Single form: target a case shared from another project, as {project identifier: [test case identifiers]}. Must resolve to EXACTLY ONE case — zero or several gives 400 "Test Case ID is invalid".

body.name: configuration_id
body.description: Which configuration this result is for. TOP level. Omitting it logs against the default configuration.

body.name: attachments
body.description: Filenames of multipart file parts to attach to this result. Only binds on a multipart/form-data request whose JSON body rides in a `payload` part; on a plain JSON request it is accepted and silently does nothing. Each entry is a bare filename string of 1-255 characters.

body.name: validate_tc
body.description: Bulk only. "true" pre-checks every test_case_id exists in the project and 400s listing the invalid ones. Rejected outright when the request carries 300 or more unique test case ids.

capabilities.intent: Record the outcome of running test cases in a test run — pass/fail/blocked with notes, per-step results, linked defects and attachments — for one case or for many in a single call
guidance: Two shapes on one endpoint: `results: [...]` for many cases, or `test_result` plus one target (`test_case_id`, `execution_id` or `shared_test_case_ids`) for one. Sending both, neither, or any unrecognised top-level key is rejected 400 as invalid params.
Status is a NAME configured for the project, not an id. An unconfigured name fails that entry with INVALID_STATUS_VALUE.
Each submission ADDS a result to the case's history in this run; it never replaces the previous one. To move many cases to one status instead, use bulk_set_test_result_status_v2.

The bulk form is queued, not applied inline: 200 means accepted. Read `results[]` — every entry is ACCEPTED or FAILED. A mix of good and bad entries still returns HTTP 200 but with `success: false` and `status: "PARTIAL"`; only an all-bad request returns 400. Treating 200 as 'all logged' will misreport.
A project can restrict which review statuses may be executed. Blocked cases come back with a REVIEW_STATUS_GATE error and are never logged, whatever the status you sent.

Attachments require a multipart/form-data request: JSON body in a `payload` part, each file in its own part, and every name in `attachments` must match a part's filename or the request is rejected. Limits are 10 files per result, 100 per request, 50 MB per file, and filenames must be unique across the request.
Attachments cannot be combined with step_results on the same bulk entry — that request is rejected 400.
Success is HTTP 200 here, not the 201 the v1 create returns.
Requires the execute permission on the run; a caller without it gets 403 before anything is written.

400.description: Invalid params, unconfigured status for every entry, every case blocked by the review-status gate, or a multipart/attachment rejection. Bulk bodies carry per-case `results` entries with an `error.code` such as INVALID_STATUS_VALUE or REVIEW_STATUS_GATE.

422.description: Rich-text description referenced an attachment that could not be resolved.

schema.example: attachment in rich text editor is invalid

capabilities.name: create_test_run_v1

body.name: filters
body.description:
Forward-sync rule for a DYNAMIC run, at the TOP level of the body — not inside `test_run`. This does NOT select cases: it never back-fills existing ones, so a create whose only case-bearing key is `filters` returns 200 with an EMPTY run. Use `test_case_ids` or `selection` to put cases in the run, and send `filters` only in addition, when the user asked the run to stay in sync.
Sending a non-empty

body.name: dynamic_filter
body.description: Filter criteria (backward compatible format - use `filters` instead). Top level, same as `filters`, including that it selects no cases and flips the run dynamic.

body.name: shared_selection
body.description: Selection of cases shared in from other projects. Top level, same as `selection`.

body.name: run_state
body.description: MANDATORY. The v1 endpoint validates this against the enum and hard-rejects anything else (including a missing key) with `400 "invalid data"`. Use `new_run` for a freshly created run. Note: v2 defaulted this to `new_run` server-side; v1 does NOT.

body.name: owner
body.description: TM user id of the run owner. Unresolvable ids are silently treated as unassigned rather than erroring.

body.name: is_dynamic
body.description: Keep the run's membership live against `filters`. Must be sent INSIDE `test_run` — v1 does not read a top-level `is_dynamic` and will silently create a static run if you put it there.

body.name: configurations
body.description: Configuration ids to run against — ids, not the configuration objects returned on read.

body.name: test_plans
body.description: Test plan ids. Only the first entry is linked; a run belongs to at most one plan.

capabilities.intent: Create a test run for a project
guidance: Discovering cases does not put them in a run. Carry the case ids you found into this call — a create whose only case-bearing field is a filter rule succeeds and creates an EMPTY run.
run_state is required and is validated before the selection, so a bare 'invalid data' error means a bad run field, not a bad selection.
A filter rule also makes the run keep syncing as cases change, even if you did not ask for that. Create runs static unless the user explicitly wants a run that keeps updating.

Dynamic runs match on priority, status, category, owner, automation status, automation state, folder, tags and issues only. Creation and update dates are echoed back but never matched, so a 'last 7 days' dynamic run silently drops the date window and keeps collecting.
Preview the selection first if the count matters — it reports what the selection resolves to before anything is created.

capabilities.name: delete_custom_field_dataset_option_v2

path_params.name: custom_fields_id
path_params.description: Numeric custom field id. Not validated by this handler.

path_params.name: dataset_id
path_params.description: Numeric dataset id holding the option. Not validated by this handler.

path_params.name: option_id
path_params.description: Numeric option id to delete, from the dataset options listing. Not validated by this handler; a wrong value surfaces as a bodyless 404.

capabilities.intent: Permanently remove one choice from a dropdown-style custom field, dropping that value from every case that had it selected
guidance: Irreversible, and it takes data with it: every case, result or plan holding this option loses that value, across every project the dataset covers. There is no bin.
If the value is simply wrong, rename it through the option update instead — a rename keeps the option id, so nothing stored is lost.
On a nested_dropdown, deleting a parent option orphans the children that pointed at it; list the options first and delete the subtree deliberately.

None of the three path ids is validated in this layer, so a wrong or mismatched triple reaches storage and returns a bare 404 {success:false} with no message — indistinguishable from a permissions failure.
Saved report filters referencing this field are cleaned up asynchronously afterwards, so a report's advanced filter can change after the call returns.
Success is only `{success: true}`; capture the option's label and id beforehand if you need to report what went.

capabilities.name: delete_custom_field_dataset_v2

path_params.name: custom_fields_id
path_params.description: Numeric custom field id. Not validated by this handler — a wrong value surfaces as a bodyless 404 from storage.

path_params.name: dataset_id
path_params.description: Numeric dataset id. Not validated by this handler; a dataset that belongs to a different field returns the same bodyless 404.

capabilities.intent: Remove one option set and its project scope from a custom field — the field survives, but every value its projects stored through this dataset is gone
guidance: Irreversible. The dataset, all of its options, and the values recorded against those options in every project the dataset linked are removed together. There is no bin.
Count and name the affected projects first (read the dataset, or the field with its datasets). Callers routinely think a dataset belongs to one project.

Neither path id is validated before the upstream call, so a wrong or mismatched pair reaches storage and returns a bare 404 {success:false} with no message. Confirm the pair with a dataset read first.
Saved report filters referencing this field are cleaned up asynchronously afterwards, so a report's advanced filter can change shape after the call returns.
If you only want to stop one project seeing the field, unlink that project through the dataset project-mapping call instead — narrower, though it also drops that project's stored values.
Success is only `{success: true}`; nothing about what was removed is echoed back.

capabilities.name: delete_custom_field_definition_v2

path_params.name: custom_fields_id
path_params.description: Numeric custom field id, as returned by the workspace field list. The route matches digits only; 0 is rejected as 'Invalid Params'.

capabilities.intent: Permanently remove a custom field from the workspace, together with every value stored against it in every project that used it
guidance: Irreversible and workspace-wide. The field, its datasets, its options and every value stored on every test case / result / plan in every linked project go at once. There is no bin and no restore.
Read the field first and report how many projects its datasets link to before asking to proceed — the caller usually thinks of a field as belonging to one project.

A side effect reaches outside the field: saved report filters that referenced this field are cleaned up asynchronously afterwards, so a report's advanced filter can change shape minutes after the call returns.

The path id is the numeric custom field id. The route only matches digits, and an id of 0 returns 400 'Invalid Params'. A well-formed id that does not exist comes back as a bare 404 {success:false} with no message — the same body a permissions failure would give.
Success is only `{success: true}`; nothing is echoed back, so capture the field's name and id before deleting if you need them for the report.

capabilities.name: delete_dataset

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id; this route only matches digits.

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: The dataset's uuid string. There is no integer-id form of this route.

capabilities.intent: Permanently delete a dataset and all of its rows

200.description: Dataset deleted.

404.description: No dataset with this uuid in the project; nothing was deleted.

422.description: {success:false, message:'Feature not available'} — the group lacks the Team Pro plan.

guidance: Irreversible and unguarded: there is no soft delete, no recycle bin and no restore endpoint for datasets, and the handler performs no check for test cases still bound to this dataset — it deletes and reports success either way.
Check what depends on it first with the dataset's linked-test-cases listing, and read the dataset itself if the contents matter, because neither is recoverable afterwards.
An unknown uuid is 404 {success:false, message:'Dataset <uuid>  not found.'} — the lookup happens before the delete, so a 404 means nothing was removed.
422 {message:'Feature not available'} is the Team Pro entitlement gate, not a bad request.
The success body is {success:true, message:'DatasetV2 deleted successfully'} — the internal 'DatasetV2' name is not a typo you can rely on staying.
Needs the test-case write permission (tc_write).

capabilities.name: delete_exploratory_session
capabilities.intent: Permanently remove an exploratory session and everything recorded inside it — every log entry and every defect link goes with it

200.description: Exploratory session deleted successfully.

403.description: Forbidden. Insufficient permissions to delete this session.

message.example: You don't have permission to delete this exploratory session

guidance: There is no recycle bin for exploratory sessions. Unlike test cases, a deleted session has no restore path: it and all of its log entries are gone.

Permission depends on the session's state, and the handler reads the session before deciding: a closed session needs the closed-test-run delete permission, an active one the ordinary test-run delete permission. The refusal is 403 {success:false, message:"You don't have permission to delete this exploratory session"} and nothing is deleted.
Because the session is fetched first, an unknown session_id fails as a bare {success:false} 404 with no message.
Delete the logs individually first only if you want them removed selectively — deleting the session needs no cleanup of its children.
The response is only {success:true}; there is no echo of what was removed, so capture anything you need from the session before calling this.

capabilities.name: delete_exploratory_session_log
capabilities.intent: Permanently remove one observation from an exploratory session, discarding its note, outcome, elapsed time and defect links

200.description: Session log deleted successfully.

guidance: Both ids are integers and both must match: log_id is only addressable under the session_id that owns it.
There is no bin or restore for session logs — the entry, its embedded screenshots' links and its defect links are gone.
This removes one log only. It does not touch the issues linked at session level, so a defect raised here can still appear in the session's defects listing through the session-level link.
The session's session_log_count drops, which can move a session back below the 50-log threshold that pushes a clone onto the asynchronous path.
The response is only {success:true}. An unknown log id surfaces as a bare {success:false} 404 with no message.
Deleting a log needs the test-run delete permission — the same permission as deleting a whole session, with no separate closed-session variant at log level.

capabilities.name: delete_filter
capabilities.intent: Delete a saved filter view from a project permanently
guidance: Removes the saved view only. The test cases, runs or plans it selected are untouched — this deletes a query, not data.
There is no undo and no bin for filter views, and no version history to restore from. Recreating one means re-authoring the whole condition set, so read the filter first if you might want it back.

A project-level view is deleted for everyone on the project, not just for you, and the filter controller is not RBAC-gated — any user with product access to the project can delete a view someone else created.
The success body is `{success:true}` and nothing else: no id echo, no copy of what was deleted, nothing to carry forward.
Deleting an id that does not exist comes back as 400 `{success:false, message:...}` rather than 404 — only the backing service's 400 is translated here, and its other failures surface as a 500.

capabilities.name: delete_folder_and_contents
capabilities.intent: Permanently delete a folder together with everything beneath it — every nested subfolder and every test case in the whole subtree

200.description: Folder and its contents deleted successfully

guidance: This is recursive and total. It removes the folder, all of its descendant folders, and every test case in that entire subtree — not just the cases filed directly in it. There is no option to keep the contents or to delete the folder only.

Run the folder remove-summary dry run first. It is the only way to see, before committing, how many active test cases, archived test cases, subfolders and low-code test recordings this call will destroy.

Recoverability depends on a group feature flag you cannot read from this API. When Move to Bin is enabled for the group, the folder's TEST CASES land in the project recycle bin and can be listed and restored from there until they auto-purge. When it is not enabled, the test cases are deleted outright.

The FOLDERS themselves are never recoverable, under either setting. Nothing in this API restores a deleted folder — the bin holds test cases only, and restored cases do not bring their folder tree back with them. Treat the folder structure as gone and be ready to recreate it.
Do not plan on the undo-remove endpoint as your way back. It is a dead alias that re-issues this same delete; it does not restore anything (see the flag on undo_remove_folder).

Linked low-code test recordings belong to a different product and are destroyed too. The summary's has_other_product_entity flag is true exactly when the subtree contains such recordings — check it before deleting if anyone else depends on them.
Requires the folder-delete permission (403 otherwise), which is a higher bar than the edit permission most other folder writes need.

On success the deleted folder is echoed at `data.folder` with cases_count and total_cases_count forced to 0 — those zeros are cosmetic, not a report of what was removed. `data.path_folders` is the surviving breadcrumb of the deleted folder's parent, useful for re-pointing a UI.
Failure does not use the usual envelope: an upstream rejection is relayed as the raw upstream body with the upstream status code, so do not expect {success:false, message} to be there to parse.
folder_id must be a positive integer; literal 0 raises an unhandled ArgumentError and comes back as a 500.

capabilities.name: delete_report_schedule

query.name: q[query]
query.description: Only filters the listing returned AFTER the delete (matches report type, title, or owner name) — it does not scope what is deleted.

query.name: q[scheduled]
query.description: Only the exact string `true` does anything (restricts the returned listing to scheduled reports). `false` or any other value is ignored and returns everything.

query.name: p
query.description: Page of the listing returned after the delete. Fixed 30 per page; past the last page returns 400.

capabilities.intent: Permanently delete a report — the whole saved report and its filters, not just its email schedule
guidance: This deletes the report record itself. Despite the path, there is no way to remove only the schedule: to stop the emails but keep the report, edit it and omit `frequency` / `frequency_details` instead.

The delete is unconditional and silent. A `schedule_id` that does not exist, or belongs to another group, still returns 200 with `success: true` — there is no 404 and no count of what was removed. Confirm by checking that the returned `data` list no longer contains the id.
The report is matched on group + id only; the project in the path does not scope it, so an id belonging to a sibling project in the same group IS deleted.
The response body is not the deleted report — it is the CURRENT page of the caller's remaining reports, plus `scheduled_report_count` and `total_report_count`. Treat it as a fresh listing.
That embedded listing is paged at a fixed 30 per page, honours `p`, and `p` past the last page returns 400 `page_out_of_bounds`. Do not page it by re-issuing the delete — call list_schedules instead.

Deleting also removes the report's filter rows and mail recipients and propagates a delete to Test Observability; there is no undo and no restore endpoint. Requires the report_delete permission (403 otherwise).

capabilities.name: delete_shared_step_v1
capabilities.intent: Delete a shared step from a project permanently — every test case that embeds the block loses it, in one operation
guidance: This is the widest single delete in the shared-step surface. A shared step is embedded by reference by many test cases at once, so removing it takes that block out of all of them together. The blast radius is not visible from the id — read the shared step, or find its row in the shared-step listing, and look at `test_case_count`. That number is exactly how many test cases this affects; anything above zero means you are editing that many cases, not deleting an unused fragment.
The delete is not blocked by references. A block used by hundreds of cases deletes as readily as an unused one, and nothing warns you.

There is no undo: shared steps have no bin, no archive and no version history. Recreating a block with the same title and steps does NOT re-link the test cases that referenced the old one — their references are gone and each case has to be re-edited by hand. Capture the block's steps (and, if it matters, which cases used it) before deleting.
Deleting the block is not the way to stop one test case using it — edit that test case's steps instead. This call is for retiring a fragment project-wide.
Success is 200 with `{success:true}`, not 204 with an empty body. Do not treat a body-less 204 as the success signal.

A zero or non-numeric shared_step_id is rejected locally with 400 `{data:null, success:false, message:"Validation Error"}` before any call is made — and the route segment only matches digits, so a non-numeric id never reaches the handler at all.
Requires tc_write, the same permission as editing a test case; there is no separate shared-step delete permission, so anyone who can edit cases can do this.

capabilities.name: delete_template_v2

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Template id — a plain integer with no prefix, discovered from the template list.

capabilities.intent: Permanently delete a template together with its field and project links — there is no bin and no undo; disable it instead if you might want it back.
guidance: This removes the template record itself, along with its field mappings and its project mappings. Test Management exposes no restore for a deleted template.
If the goal is only to stop people picking the template for new test cases, DISABLE it instead — disabling is reversible and keeps the fields and project links intact.
System templates and the workspace default template cannot be deleted; the attempt comes back as a 400 with the reason.
Paid plans only. On a free plan the response is HTTP 200 with success:false and the paid-feature message, and nothing is deleted — check the flag, not the status code.
Success returns only success:true, with no record of what was removed. Read the template first if you need its name or field list for the record.

capabilities.name: delete_test_case_attachment
capabilities.intent: Remove one file from a test case and purge the stored blob — takes a screenshot, log or document off the case for good
guidance: The response is wrapped in `data`: read data.attachments for the removed record and data.success. This action wraps; the attachment list and upload on the same path do not. Reading a top-level `attachments` finds nothing.
Irreversible. The link is removed AND the underlying stored file is scheduled for purge, so the file itself goes, not just the association. There is no undo and no recycle bin for attachments.

`attachment_id` must be an id from this case's own attachment listing. The handler looks it up inside the case's in-memory attachment list and does not return a clean 404 when it is absent, so verify the id with a list read first rather than probing.
`folder_id` is in the route but is NOT used to find the case — the lookup is by project and test case id, so a stale folder id after a move still resolves.
Note the shape: a POST to .../delete, not a DELETE.
The v2 attachment surface is the maintained one for listing and reading attachments; use this only when you specifically need to remove a v1 test-case attachment.

capabilities.name: delete_test_plan_v1
capabilities.intent: Permanently delete a test plan or sub-plan — there is no recycle bin and no undo; archive it instead if there is any chance it is wanted back

200.description: Plan deleted: `{success: true}`.

404.description: No such plan: `{success: false, error: "Test Plan not found"}`.

guidance: Irreversible. Plans have no bin and no version history, so a deleted plan cannot be restored by any capability here — the reversible option is bulk-archive, which keeps the plan and can be undone with bulk-retrieve.
The path segment is the plan's INTEGER id. A TP-NNN / STP-NNN identifier does not match the route and never reaches the handler.

The only miss signal is 404 {success: false, error: 'Test Plan not found'}; a success is a bare {success: true} with no echo of what was removed. Read the plan first if you need to tell the user what is about to go.
Needs the test-plan DELETE permission, which is separate from the write permission used by create/update.
Deleting emits an activity-feed event and a personal alert to the plan's owner, so the side effect is visible outside this API.
What happens to the plan's sub-plans and to the test runs it held is decided upstream and is not echoed in the response — read the sub-plans and linked runs first if that matters.

capabilities.name: delete_test_result_v1
capabilities.intent: Delete one logged test result by its id — removes that single execution record while leaving the case's other attempts in the run intact

200.description: Result deleted.

403.description: Caller is neither the result's author nor a project admin.

guidance: Authorship-gated: only the user who logged the result may delete it, unless the caller is a project admin. Anyone else gets 403 {success:false, message:"You can delete only results logged by you, unless you're a project admin"} and nothing is removed.
Irreversible — there is no recycle bin for results. After the delete the case's outcome in that run rolls back to its previous attempt, or to unexecuted if this was the only result.
Note the shape: a POST to .../delete, not a DELETE, and `test_result_id` must be numeric — the route only matches digits, so a TR-/TC-style identifier 404s at routing.
To remove several results use the bulk delete instead: it authorises per id and reports what it skipped, whereas this one refuses the entire call on the first authorisation failure.
Success is only {success: true} — the deleted record is not echoed back, so capture anything you need from it first.

capabilities.name: delete_v1_test_run
capabilities.intent: Permanently delete a test run and every result recorded in it — there is no bin and no restore
guidance: Irreversible. A test run has no version history and no recycle bin: the run, its case mappings and every result recorded against them go, and nothing in this API brings them back. Confirm with the user before calling.

Deleting a CLOSED run needs a different permission (closed-run delete) from deleting an open one — a role that can delete working runs can be 403'd on a finished one. Automation runs demand the automation variant again.
The run's build in Test Observability is archived FIRST, and a rejection there aborts the delete, so a failure can leave the run intact. Re-read before assuming it is gone.
The run is also stripped out of every saved report filter that referenced it; those reports silently narrow rather than erroring.
The deleted run is echoed back under `data.testrun` — one word, no underscore — with `data.project`. Do NOT read `data.test_run` here; that key does not exist on this response.
The path accepts either the TR-NNN identifier or the integer id, but the body key and every downstream reference wants the integer from `uuid`.

capabilities.name: discard_duplicate_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id; this route only matches digits.

path_params.name: duplicate_id
path_params.description: Integer duplicate id, from the `id` of a listing row. Here it is a path segment — unlike the resolve call, which takes it in the body.

body.name: discard_reason
body.description: Short reason code or label for why this is not a duplicate. Flat in the body (no wrapper object). Optional and unvalidated — no closed set is enforced, and omitting it stores null.

body.name: user_feedback
body.description: Free-text feedback. Flat in the body. Stored under a different name (`discard_feedback`) than the one you send, so do not expect it echoed back under this key.

capabilities.intent: Dismiss a duplicate suggestion as wrong — removes it from the review queue and feeds the reason back to the model, without touching either test case

200.description: Duplicate discarded. Body is {success:true} only.

403.description: The caller lacks the test-case write permission (tc_write).

404.description: {success:false, error:'Duplicate not found.'} — no such pair for this project, or it is no longer in `suggested` status.

409.description: {success:false, error:'Duplicate review is paused while this data is being migrated. Please try again shortly.'} — a dedupe data migration is in progress. Nothing was discarded; retry later.

guidance: This is the 'not a duplicate' verdict. Neither test case is touched — nothing is archived, merged, commented on or tagged. Use the resolve call when a case should actually go away.

The body is flat: `discard_reason` and `user_feedback` sit at the top level, with no wrapper object and no request-schema check, so a misspelled key is silently dropped and you get 200 with the feedback lost.
One-way. The pair moves to `discarded` and leaves every listing; there is no un-discard endpoint and the pair can no longer be read, so confirm the verdict before calling.
Suggested-only: a pair already merged, archived or discarded is 404 {success:false, error:'Duplicate not found.'} — usually 'already handled' rather than 'never existed'.

Undeclared until now, and retryable: while a dedupe data migration is in progress this is refused with 409 {success:false, error:'Duplicate review is paused while this data is being migrated. Please try again shortly.'}. Nothing was discarded; retry later.
Note the envelope differs from the resolve call, which uses `errors` for its failures where this one uses `error`.
Needs the test-case write permission (tc_write) — lighter than the delete permission the resolve call demands.

capabilities.name: download_report

body.name: file_type
body.description: Export format, as a single STRING. Anything outside the three values is 422 `Invalid file_type.`. Note the same-named field on send-email-now is an ARRAY.

body.name: required
body.description: Optional column selection, honoured only for `Test Run Detailed Report` and `Test Plan Detailed Report`; ignored elsewhere. Shape `{ "<entity>": { "fields": ["id","title",...] } }`; `fields` may also be a comma-separated string, and `["all"]` expands to every supported column. Invalid names are NOT rejected here — the export silently reverts to defaults.

body.name: columns
body.description: Alias for `required`, and it WINS when both are sent. Same shape and same silent-fallback behaviour.

capabilities.intent: Kick off an async export of a report to CSV, PDF or XLSX — returns a job channel, not the file
guidance: This returns immediately with `{ channel: <uuid>, success: true }` and nothing else. The export runs in a background worker and the finished file's URL is pushed over a realtime channel named from that uuid — there is NO endpoint to poll it and no way to fetch the artefact through the API. If you need the file itself, use the send-email-now capability and have it mailed, or hand the channel to a UI client.
No bytes come back from this call and no download URL appears anywhere in the response — a `channel` that you cannot resolve is the whole result, so do not report the export as delivered.

`file_type` is a single STRING here (`csv` / `pdf` / `xlsx`). The same-named field on send-email-now is an ARRAY — they are not interchangeable. An unsupported value is 422 `Invalid file_type.`, not 400.

Column selection (`required`, or its alias `columns`, which wins when both are sent) is only honoured for `Test Run Detailed Report` and `Test Plan Detailed Report`. On every other report type it is ignored. Shape is `{ "<entity>": { "fields": [...] } }` with entities test_run_test_case / test_run / test_result (and test_plan for the plan report).

Unlike the on-screen read, this path does NOT validate your column list: a misspelled field name is not an error here — the worker silently falls back to the report's default columns, so the export arrives missing what you asked for. Verify field names against the report read first.
`fields: ["all"]` for an entity expands to every supported column for that entity.

The report is matched on group + id, so the project in the path does not scope the lookup; an unknown id is 404 `Report not found.`. A `Test Plan Detailed Report` on a group without the feature flag is 403 `Operation not permitted`. Requires the report_view permission.

capabilities.name: edit_test_case_partial_v1

body.name: attachments
body.description: The COMPLETE set of attachment blob ids the case should end up with, not a list to append — any currently-attached id missing from the array is detached. Read the case's existing attachments first and send them back alongside the new ids.

body.name: automation_status
body.description: Legacy alias for `automation_state`, given as an internal_name string (e.g. `not_automated`, `automated`). Applied only when `automation_state` is omitted.

body.name: case_type
body.description: Numeric case-type option id, or the project's display name (a string is resolved by name, an integer by id).

body.name: custom_fields
body.description: Map of custom-field id to value, applied only when the key is present AND non-empty — `{}` is a no-op here (it is the BULK edit that 500s when the key is missing). Values replace the field's current value.

body.name: estimate
body.description: ACCEPTED BUT NOT PERSISTED — passes validation and is then dropped before the write, on this path as well as create. Use `estimated_duration_seconds`; never report an estimate as saved.

body.name: estimated_duration_seconds
body.description: Per-case estimated execution time in SECONDS; `null` clears it. This is the field that actually stores an estimate.

body.name: expected_result
body.description: Overall expected outcome, distinct from a step's own `result`.

body.name: is_dataset_modified
body.description: Must be `true` for a `test_case_dataset` change to be applied; with any other value the dataset payload is ignored.

body.name: issues
body.description: Linked issues/defects. Processed ASYNCHRONOUSLY after the response returns, so a 200 does not mean the links exist yet — re-read the case to confirm.

body.name: name
body.description: The name/title of the test case.

body.name: owner
body.description: TM user id. Unlike the POST edit path, an id that does not resolve is silently skipped rather than rejected, so the owner is left unchanged with a 200.

body.name: priority
body.description: Numeric priority option id, or the project's display name (a string is resolved by name, an integer by id).

body.name: review_status
body.description: Review state, e.g. `pending` / `in_review` / `approved`. Unlike POST .../edit, omitting it here leaves the stored value untouched.

body.name: reviewers
body.description: Reviewer TM user ids (emails also resolve). Honoured only on a Team-Pro workspace with review-approve enabled on the project — otherwise silently ignored. Including the owner is rejected with 422 'Owner cannot be a reviewer'. This path does NOT run the send-for-review checks or send review emails.

body.name: status
body.description: Numeric status option id. A display NAME is not resolved on this path — it is written through as the id.

body.name: steps
body.description: LEGACY — use `test_case_steps` instead. This param skips the request allowlist and is read with JSON.parse, so it must be a JSON-encoded STRING. Sending a real JSON array parses to `[]` and WIPES the case's steps while still returning 200.

body.name: tags
body.description: Tag names. `[]` removes all tags; omit the field to keep the existing ones.

body.name: template
body.description: Template NAME (the same values the create paths accept) — not an id. Sending an integer is rejected with 422 "Invalid template value <n>"; use `template_id` for the numeric custom-template reference.

body.name: template_id
body.description: Custom-template id.

body.name: template_step_type
body.description: Takes precedence over `template` when both are sent.

body.name: test_case_dataset
body.description: Dataset binding for a data-driven case. On this path it is applied only when `is_dataset_modified` is true.

body.name: test_case_folder_id
body.description: Move the case to a different folder (integer id). Dropped server-side when it matches the current folder, so passing the existing folder is a safe no-op.

body.name: test_case_steps

example.result: The user lands on the dashboard

body.description: The structured step list — same shape as the create body. `order` is filled in by position when omitted. `[]` removes all steps; omit the field to keep them.

body.name: third_party_identifier
body.description: External identifier, only read in workspaces that issue project-level ids. A value already used in the project is rejected.

body.name: isMergedDuplicate
body.description: Compared to the literal boolean `true`. Tells the backend to keep the case's existing attachments rather than reconciling them against `attachments`. Used by the duplicate-merge flow.

capabilities.intent: Change just the fields you name on one test case, leaving everything you omit untouched — the safe path for an inline single-field edit.
guidance: The response is `{success: true}` and NOTHING ELSE. It does not return the updated case, so re-read the case if you need to confirm or show the new values. (The POST .../edit sibling does return `data.test_case`.)
Only the keys present in `test_case` are applied — this is the partial-update path. The POST .../edit on the same case rebuilds more of the record, including resetting `review_status`.
The body must be wrapped in `test_case`; a flat body is a 400 before any field is read.

`steps` is legacy and is read with a JSON parse, so it must be a JSON-encoded STRING. Sending a real JSON array parses to `[]` and WIPES the case's steps while still returning 200. Use `test_case_steps`.

`attachments` is the complete set the case should end up with, not an append — anything currently attached and missing from the array is detached. `test_case_steps: []` and `tags: []` likewise clear; omit the key to keep what is there.
A workflow that forbids the status transition comes back as 422 with `code: "transition_not_allowed"` and a `violations` list — that is a rule rejection, not bad input.
This path does not accept `send_for_review` or `shared_precondition_id`, and does not run the review-payload checks; use the POST .../edit path for a send-for-review flow.
Every successful edit writes a new version, so an edit is recoverable by restoring the previous version — subject to the workspace's plan, which may only keep 30 days of history.

capabilities.name: edit_test_case_v1

body.name: attachments
body.description: The COMPLETE set of attachment blob ids the case should end up with, not a list to append — anything currently attached and missing from the array is detached. Read the case's existing attachments first.

body.name: automation_status
body.description: Legacy alias for `automation_state`, taken as an internal_name string (e.g. `not_automated`, `automated`). Only applied when `automation_state` is omitted. Prefer `automation_state`.

body.name: case_type
body.description: Numeric case-type option id, or the project's display name (a string is resolved by name, an integer by id).

body.name: custom_fields
body.description: Map of custom-field id to value. Values replace the field's current value; a field id the project does not define is rejected by the backend with a field-named 400 message.

body.name: estimate
body.description: ACCEPTED BUT NOT PERSISTED — the field passes request validation and is then dropped before the write on both the create and the edit paths. Use `estimated_duration_seconds` instead; do not report an estimate as saved.

body.name: estimated_duration_seconds
body.description: Per-case estimated execution time in SECONDS. `null` clears it. This is the field that actually persists an estimate.

body.name: expected_result
body.description: Overall expected outcome (distinct from a step's own `result`). Rich-text field — send plain text/HTML, not a JSON document.

body.name: is_dataset_modified
body.description: Set with `test_case_dataset` on an edit to signal the dataset changed; on create the mappings are always regenerated and this is ignored.

body.name: issues
body.description: Linked issues as `[{issue_id, issue_type, metadata?}]` (bare strings are coerced to ``issue_id``). Processed ASYNCHRONOUSLY after the response, so a 200 does not mean the links exist yet.

body.name: owner
body.description: TM user id. An id that is not a member of the group is silently replaced with the caller rather than rejected.

body.name: priority
body.description: Numeric priority option id, or the project's display name (a string is resolved by name, an integer by id).

body.name: review_status
body.description: Review state, e.g. `pending` / `in_review` / `approved`. When omitted it is set from the project's review-approve setting, falling back to `pending` — it is never left untouched on create or on POST .../edit.

body.name: reviewers
body.description: Reviewer TM user ids (emails also resolve). Only honoured when the workspace is on a Team-Pro plan AND the project has review-approve enabled; otherwise silently ignored. Including the `owner` is rejected with 422 "Owner cannot be a reviewer".

body.name: send_for_review
body.description: EDIT PATHS ONLY — drives the per-reviewer review-request email. Dropped without error on create (the create flow already notifies from `reviewers` + `review_status`) and not accepted by PATCH .../edit-v2.

body.name: shared_precondition_id
body.description: Link a shared precondition. Only applied when `preconditions` is sent in the same body.

body.name: status
body.description: Numeric status option id. A display NAME is not resolved on this path — it is written through as the id.

body.name: template
body.description: Step-shape template NAME, not an id. When neither this nor `template_step_type` is sent it DEFAULTS to `test_case_text` on this path — which silently discards `test_case_steps`. Always send it on an edit that touches steps.

body.name: template_step_type
body.description: Step shape — `test_case_steps` | `test_case_text` | `test_case_bdd`. OPTIONAL; when sending `template_id`, use that template's own `step_type` from the templates listing rather than assuming.

body.name: test_case_dataset
body.description: Dataset binding for a data-driven case. On create the mappings are always regenerated from this, so `is_dataset_modified` is ignored here.

body.name: test_case_folder_id
body.description: Target folder's integer id. On create this is REQUIRED IN THE BODY as well as in the path — omitting it is the most common create failure (422 wrapping an upstream 404). Integer or string are equivalent; the server coerces with .to_i, so the distinction does not matter.

body.name: test_case_steps
body.description: The ONLY key the server reads for steps — on single create, bulk create and the update paths alike. Items are `{step, result, test_data?, order?, shared_step_id?}`; `order` is filled in by position when omitted. A differently named key such as `steps` is silently ignored and the create still returns 200 for a case with NO steps, so verify against `test_case_steps` in the response.

body.name: steps
body.description: LEGACY — use `test_case_steps`. Read with a JSON parse, so it must be a JSON-encoded STRING. A real JSON array parses to `[]` and WIPES the case's steps while still returning 200.

body.name: reauth_token
body.description: One-shot re-authentication token, required only when the project has e-signature on send-for-review enabled AND this edit sets `send_for_review` or `review_status: in_review`. Missing or expired is 401 with `error_code: "reauth_required"`.

body.name: third_party_identifier
body.description: External identifier, only read in workspaces that issue project-level ids. A value already used in the project is rejected.

body.name: isMergedDuplicate
body.description: Compared to the literal boolean `true`. Keeps the case's existing attachments instead of reconciling them against `attachments`. Used by the duplicate-merge flow.

capabilities.intent: Edit one test case through the full edit form — rename it, rewrite its steps, preconditions and expected result, retag it, or send it for review.
guidance: This is the FULL edit path, not a patch: `review_status` is recomputed on every call (omitted, it falls back to the project's review-approve default), and `template` defaults to `test_case_text` when you omit it, which discards any `test_case_steps` you sent. Send the case's current template unless you mean to change it.
For a targeted single-field change prefer the PATCH .../edit-v2 sibling, which applies only the keys you send.
The body must be wrapped in `test_case`; a flat body is a 400 before any field is read.
Array fields REPLACE rather than append: `attachments`, `tags` and `test_case_steps` are each the complete intended set, and `[]` clears. Read the case first and send the union.

Reviewers and the owner cannot overlap: this path rejects it up front with 400 `code: "OWNER_AS_REVIEWER"`, and sending `send_for_review` with no reviewers is 400 `code: "NO_REVIEWERS"`. (Create, which skips that check, surfaces the same conflict as a 422.)

If the project has e-signature enabled, an edit that sets `send_for_review` or `review_status: in_review` needs `test_case.reauth_token`; without it the answer is 401 `{success:false, error_code:"reauth_required"}`.
The updated case comes back at `data.test_case` — note the `data` envelope, and note that `estimate` always serialises as null regardless of what you sent.
Every successful edit writes a new version, so this is recoverable by restoring the previous version — subject to the workspace's plan, which may only keep 30 days of history.

capabilities.name: edit_test_run

body.name: run_state
body.description: MANDATORY on every edit, even one that is not changing the state — resend the run's current value. It is validated against the enum before anything else, so a missing or misspelled value returns 400 {success:false, message:'invalid data'} with no hint about which field was wrong.

body.name: name
body.description: Only applied when non-empty. Sending "" leaves the existing name rather than clearing it.

body.name: description
body.description: HTML is escaped and sanitised server-side, so the stored value can differ from what you sent. Unlike name, an empty string here DOES clear the description.

body.name: owner
body.description: Run owner as a TM user id (a BrowserStack user id is also accepted and resolved). An id that matches nobody in the group is silently treated as unassigned — the run's owner is cleared rather than the call failing.

body.name: is_dynamic
body.description: Keep the run's membership live against `filters`. On EDIT a TOP-LEVEL `is_dynamic` is also read and OVERRIDES this one; on create only the nested form exists. Send it in one place only. Omit the key entirely to leave the run's current dynamic flag alone — sending false on a full resend flips a dynamic run back to static.

body.name: configurations
body.description: Configuration ids (integers) the run executes against — not the configuration objects returned on read.

body.name: test_plans
body.description: Test plan ids. Only the FIRST entry is used; a run belongs to at most one plan. Send the plan's integer id.

body.name: tags
body.description: Plain tag strings. The list you send REPLACES the run's tags — omit the key to leave them alone, since there is no history to restore a cleared list from.

body.name: issues
body.description: Linked defects. Each entry is an object; a bare string is coerced to {issue_id: ...} and loses the tracker type. Linking kicks off an asynchronous fetch of the ticket metadata, so titles appear on a later read.

body.name: attachments
body.description: Attachment blob ids to attach to the run. Sending [] to remove every attachment only works where the clear-all behaviour is enabled for the group; elsewhere an empty array is a no-op. An id that does not verify fails the whole edit with 422 'attachment is invalid'.

body.name: metadata
body.description: Free-form metadata. Only forwarded when non-empty; sending {} does not clear it.

body.name: build_group_id
body.description: Only forwarded when present; there is no way to unset it through this call.

body.name: filters
body.description: Forward-sync rule for a DYNAMIC run, at the TOP level of the body — NOT inside `test_run`. It selects nothing and never back-fills, so an edit whose only case-bearing key is `filters` returns 200 having added none; add cases with test_case_ids or selection. Every `owner`/`reviewers` entry must resolve to a user in this group or the edit 400s. Labels are resolved to ids for you.

body.name: dynamic_filter
body.description: Backward-compatible alias of `filters`, same top-level position and same semantics. `filters` wins when both are sent.

body.name: test_case_ids
body.description: Test case ids to ADD to the run. Top level, not inside `test_run`. Must be an array — a scalar is rejected.

body.name: auto_assign
body.description: Top level. Forwarded to the backing service to auto-assign the newly added cases.

body.name: shared_selection
body.description: Cases shared in from other projects, as a map of project id to a selection object with the same inner shape as `selection`. Top level.

body.name: select_all
body.description: Add every case in the project.

body.name: folders
body.description: Map of folder id (as a STRING key) to {test_case_select_all, selected_test_cases:[ids], deselected_test_cases:[ids]}.

body.name: trtc_configuration_mappings
body.description: Per-configuration case mappings, at the TOP level of the body. An ARRAY of objects.

capabilities.intent: Update a test run in place — rename it, move its state on, change owner, tags, configurations or linked plan, and add more test cases to it
guidance: The run's own fields must be wrapped in a `test_run` object; the case-selection keys (test_case_ids, selection, shared_selection, filters, dynamic_filter, trtc_configuration_mappings, auto_assign, is_dynamic) sit at the TOP level beside it. Flattening everything into one object 400s before any field is read.

run_state is mandatory on every call, including edits that only rename the run. It is validated first, so a bare 400 'invalid data' almost always means a missing or misspelled run_state — not a bad selection.
This is additive for cases: test_case_ids and selection ADD to the run and never remove. Taking a case out is a separate operation, and that one discards the results recorded against it.
There is no undo. A test run keeps no version history, so an overwritten name, a replaced tag list or a cleared description cannot be restored — confirm destructive-looking edits with the user first.

Changing which cases the run covers is queued: the call returns before the new cases are attached, and an immediate re-read of the run's cases can be short. Re-read rather than retrying, which can double-add.
`filters` is a sync rule, not a selection. An edit carrying only `filters` returns 200 and adds nothing, while quietly marking the run dynamic if you also sent is_dynamic.

is_dynamic is read from BOTH the top level and inside `test_run`, and the top-level one wins on this endpoint. Pick one place. Omitting it entirely is the only way to leave the run's current mode untouched.

An owner id that matches nobody in the group unassigns the run instead of erroring — but an unresolvable user inside `filters.owner` or `filters.reviewers` hard-fails the whole edit with 400 'invalid data'. The two behave oppositely.

The updated run comes back under `data.testrun` — one word, no underscore — with `data.project`, plus a TOP-LEVEL `skipped_test_case_ids` array listing cases the review gate refused to add. Check it: those cases are silently missing from the run.
Backing-service client errors are returned as `{data: {success: false, error: <message>}}` with the 4xx status, so read `data.success` before reading `data.testrun`.
Needs the test-run write permission, with the automation variant demanded on automation runs.

capabilities.name: export_dashboard_analytics

body.name: type
body.description: Export format. Only the literal 'csv' is accepted — any other value is dropped and the export record is created with no file type, while the worker still writes CSV. Must be nested under `q`; a top-level `type` is never read.

body.name: created_at
body.description: Relative window on creation date, <N>_<hour|day|week|month|year>[_gte]. 'all_time' is honoured here and applies no bound. Send this explicitly whenever you send any other filter.

body.name: closed_at
body.description: Relative window on close date, same token format. Only read when created_at is absent or 'all_time'. 'all_time' is NOT honoured on this key — it becomes 1_year.

body.name: owner
body.description: Comma-separated TM user ids. Unresolvable ids are dropped silently; if none resolve the filter is omitted rather than erroring.

capabilities.intent: Queue a CSV export of the whole project dashboard (active + closed runs, issue counts, case-type split, automation stats) and get back an export id — the file itself is delivered out of band
guidance: The inputs are the same q[...] filter object the dashboard reads take, NOT flat body fields. The handler reads params[:q]; a top-level {"type":"csv"} is ignored and the export runs unfiltered. On this POST the object may be sent in the JSON body as {"q": {...}} or as a query string — both land in the same place.

CSV is the only format. Anything other than the literal 'csv' is discarded by the handler, and the worker writes a CSV regardless — there is no PDF or Excel export behind this route despite what the format name suggests.

You cannot collect the file through this API. The worker uploads the CSV to S3 and pushes the URL over a websocket channel addressed to the requesting user; it never attaches the file to the export record and never advances the export's status past 'pending'. The generic export status/download endpoints therefore report pending forever and 404 on download for this export type, and neither is exposed as a capability here. Treat the returned export_id as a correlation token, not as something you can redeem.

Date filtering follows the dashboard rules: q[created_at] wins over q[closed_at], and sending any q key without an explicit q[created_at] defaults both to 'all_time', which on the closed_at path becomes the last 1 year — so an owner-only filter silently produces a 12-month export.
The response is immediate and says nothing about whether the export succeeded; a failure happens later in the background and is only signalled on the websocket.
project_id is the INTEGER id; the route segment only matches digits (or the literal 'new'), so a PR-NNN identifier is a routing 404 that never reaches the API.

capabilities.name: get_active_test_runs_info_v1
capabilities.intent: Chart the result-status breakdown across the project's currently active test runs — how many results are passed / failed / blocked / untested right now
guidance: The payload is an OBJECT with a `data` array, not a bare array: read `data`, not the response root.

When more than six result statuses exist, the response is collapsed: only the top six by count survive and everything else is merged into a single row named 'Other'. That 'Other' row has NO `result_status` object — it carries a `links.filter` URL instead — so code that reads row.result_status.id must tolerate its absence.
Counts are results across active runs, not runs and not test cases. There is no drill-down here; to see the runs themselves use the test-run listings.

The filter trap: sending ANY q key without an explicit q[created_at] makes the handler default both created_at and closed_at to 'all_time', and the closed_at path rewrites 'all_time' to '1_year' — so filtering only by owner silently narrows the chart to the last 12 months. Sending no q at all applies no date bound. Always pass q[created_at] explicitly whenever you pass any other filter.
project_id is the INTEGER id; the route segment only matches digits (or the literal 'new'), so a PR-NNN identifier is a routing 404 that never reaches the API.
A project that exists but is not visible to this caller renders as 404 {success:false}, not 403 — 'no such project' and 'no access' are indistinguishable here.

query.name: q[created_at]
query.description: Relative date window on creation date, as <N>_<hour|day|week|month|year>, optionally suffixed _gte for 'older than' (e.g. 3_month, 7_day_gte). 'all_time' is honoured on this key and applies no bound. An unrecognised unit raises server-side rather than returning 400.

query.name: q[closed_at]
query.description: Same token format, applied to close date. Only read when q[created_at] is absent or 'all_time' — created_at wins. 'all_time' is NOT honoured here: it is silently rewritten to 1_year.

query.name: q[owner]
query.description: Comma-separated TM user ids (resolve them with get_project_users_v2_v1). Translated to BrowserStack ids server-side; ids that do not resolve are dropped, and if none resolve the owner filter is omitted entirely rather than returning an empty chart.

query.name: filter_details
query.description: Echo the filters you sent back, resolved, as a `filter_details` key merged into the response (owner ids become user objects). Has no effect unless q is also present.

capabilities.name: get_archived_test_cases
capabilities.intent: List the test cases that have been archived in a project — the source of the ids the bulk-retrieve (un-archive) call needs.
guidance: Plan-gated, and it fails OPEN-LOOKING: on a workspace that is not a paid plan this returns HTTP 200 with `{success:false, error:"..."}` and no test cases. Check `success`, not the status code, before concluding the archive is empty.
Project-wide only — there is no folder scoping on this route. Each row carries its original folder path so you can tell where a case will be restored to.
Take the integer `id` of each row: that is what bulk-retrieve takes to un-archive them.
Paged with `p`; there is no per_page on this route, so walk pages until `info.next` is null.
`cases_count` in the response is keyed by folder id, and on this route that key is null because no folder was scoped — read `info.count` for the total instead.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. There is no per_page here; the page size is the server default.

query.name: sort_by
query.description: Sort token (`<column>-ASC|DESC`). `case_type` is translated to the backend's `category` for you.

capabilities.name: get_archived_test_plan_count_v1
capabilities.intent: How many test plans in this project are archived — the badge number for the archived view; use the archived-plans listing when you need the plans themselves

200.description: Archived plan count: `{success, count}`.

404.description: Test-plan archiving is not enabled for this group: `{success: false, errors: "Feature not available"}`.

guidance: This is a fixed literal route on the project's plan collection, not a plan-scoped read — it takes no plan id and no filters. Counting archived plans is all it does.
Counts top-level archived plans only, matching the archived listing; archived sub-plans are not included, so the number can look low against what a user expects.
Gated on the same group archive flag as archive/restore: when it is off the call is 404 {success: false, errors: 'Feature not available'} — a feature gap, not an empty project.
Needs the test-plan DELETE permission, not view. Someone who can read plans normally may still be 403'd here.
The read is forced onto the primary store, so the number is correct immediately after an archive or restore rather than lagging behind it.
A count the upstream page info does not carry comes back as 0 rather than an error, so 0 can mean 'none archived' or 'upstream returned no paging info'.

capabilities.name: get_automation_stats_v1
capabilities.intent: Get the project's automation coverage — what percentage of its test cases are automated, with the automated / manual / total counts behind it
guidance: This is the one dashboard chart assembled in this service rather than passed through, so the field names below are exact: `automated_coverage` is a percentage (0–100, a float), and the three counts are test cases.

capabilities.name: get_configurations_v1
capabilities.intent: List the configurations a project's test runs can execute against — search by name or fetch specific ids, to resolve the configuration_id a run needs

200.description: Successfully retrieved configurations

query.name: q
query.description: Name search. `name` is an accepted alias and `q` WINS when both are sent.

query.name: name
query.description: Alias for `q`. Only used when `q` is absent.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. `page` is an accepted alias and `p` WINS. Only `p` is validated — a non-positive or non-numeric `p` is rejected globally with 400 `{success:false, error:"Invalid Params"}`, while a bad `page` is forwarded as-is.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Rows per page. `count` is an accepted alias and `count` WINS when both are sent. Forwarded unchanged to the backing service, which owns the real ceiling — nothing bounds it here.

query.name: count
query.description: Alias for `per_page`, and the one that wins when both are sent.

query.name: ids
query.description: Comma-separated configuration ids to fetch, as a STRING — not a JSON array. Split on commas before being forwarded.

query.name: type
query.description: Configuration source filter, validated locally: anything else returns 400 `{success:false, error:"Invalid type parameter. Must be one of: system, custom, all"}`.

query.name: custom
query.description: CHANGES THE RESPONSE KEY. When 'true' the rows come back under `custom_configurations` instead of `configurations`; everything else about the response is identical. Code that always reads `configurations` gets nothing back.

query.name: is_suggested
query.description: Forwarded unchanged to the backing service to filter on whether the configuration is a suggested/default one. Ignored on the `custom=true` branch.

guidance: The `custom=true` branch renames the array: rows arrive under `custom_configurations`, not `configurations`. Read the key that matches the request you made — this is the easiest way to get an apparently empty result from a call that worked.
Group-scoped, not project-scoped: the list is the workspace's configurations and `project_id` only matches the route. The same set comes back for every project in the group.
`ids` is a comma-separated string, not an array; sending `ids[]=101&ids[]=102` does not filter.
Alias pairs and which one wins: q beats name, p beats page, count beats per_page. Only `p` is validated, so a typo'd `page` is forwarded and ignored rather than rejected.

Rows carry os, os_version, device, browser, browser_version and is_valid_on_bstack in addition to id/name/group_id/record_status/is_suggested — more than the Configuration schema in this index describes. `is_valid_on_bstack` is what tells you the combination is still runnable on BrowserStack.
Carry `id` from the row: the run APIs take configuration ids, not names or objects.
Paged via `info` {page, page_size, count, prev, next}; stop when `next` is null.
Requires test_run_view — configurations are gated on the test-run permissions, not the test-case ones.

capabilities.name: get_custom_field_dataset_v2

path_params.name: custom_fields_id
path_params.description: Numeric custom field id. The route matches digits only; 0 is rejected as 'Invalid Params'.

path_params.name: dataset_id
path_params.description: Numeric dataset id, from the field read or from the create-dataset response. 0 is rejected as 'Invalid Params'.

capabilities.intent: Read one dataset of a custom field — which projects it covers and, on request, the option values it holds
guidance: Options are NOT returned by default. Pass fetch_options=true or you get project links only and will wrongly conclude the dataset has no values.

There is no `info` in this response even though the linked-projects list is paged: `p` is honoured, the page size is fixed at 30, and you get no total and no next-page marker. Use `linked_project_count` on the dataset to tell whether more pages exist.
`linked_to_all_projects` is computed here by comparing linked_project_count against the workspace project count — it is derived per request, not stored.
Both path ids must be positive integers; 0 in either position is a 400 'Invalid Params'. A well-formed id that does not exist is a bare 404 {success:false} with no message.
Nothing checks that the dataset actually belongs to the field in the path before the upstream call — a mismatched pair surfaces as that same bodyless 404.

query.name: fetch_options
query.description: Include the dataset's option values in the response. Omit it and `options` is absent entirely — which reads identically to a dataset that has none.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number over the dataset's linked projects. Page size is fixed at 30 and `per_page` is ignored; no page metadata is returned.

capabilities.name: get_custom_field_definition_v2

path_params.name: custom_fields_id
path_params.description: Numeric custom field id. The route matches digits only; 0 is rejected as 'Invalid Params'.

capabilities.intent: Read one custom field's stored definition together with its datasets and the projects each dataset is linked to — the call to make before any edit, since edits here are full replaces
guidance: Use this to build an update body: the edit call requires field_name, field_type and is_required together and clears place_holder_text and default_value when they are omitted.
`entity_type` is NOT in this response. If you need to know whether the field belongs to TestCase, TestResult, TestPlan or ExploratorySession, take it from the workspace field list instead.
The response carries datasets with their project links but NOT their option values. Read a dataset's options through the dataset options list.
Paging is per dataset row and is controlled only by `p`; the page size is fixed at 30 and `per_page` is ignored. `info` carries the page metadata.
`linked_to_all_projects` on a dataset is computed by comparing its linked project count against the workspace project count — it is derived, not a stored flag.
A field id that does not exist comes back as a bare 404 {success:false} with no message; id 0 is a 400 'Invalid Params'.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number over the field's datasets. The only pagination control — `per_page` is read but discarded, the page size is always 30.

capabilities.name: get_custom_field_values_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id. The route also matches the literal 'new', which returns an empty 200 rather than an error. PR-NNN identifiers do not match the route.
