path_params.name: entity_type
path_params.description: Hyphenated, lower-case entity segment. Anything outside this set fails the route constraint and 404s. It must match the field's own entity type or the lookup returns nothing.

path_params.name: field_id
path_params.description: Numeric custom field id, from the workspace field list or the project's form fields. Whatever you send here becomes the top-level key of the response, verbatim.

query.name: q
query.description: Substring search over the option labels (or user names for a `user` field). Forwarded upstream as the value filter.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number, forwarded unchanged. There is no per-page control on this endpoint — the backing service owns the page size; read it back from `info`.

query.name: parent_option_id
query.description: nested_dropdown only: return the child options of this parent instead of the level's own values. Get the parent id from a previous call on the parent level.

capabilities.intent: List the values one custom field offers inside a given project — the dropdown choices, or the users for a user field — so you can pick a valid value before writing it onto a test case or result
guidance: This is the project-scoped value lookup, not a definition read. Use it to turn a value a human named into something you can send; the field's definition, type and project scope live in the workspace field list.

The response has no fixed top-level key: the payload sits under the field id exactly as you spelled it in the path (`{"4821": {field_type, values}, info, success}`). Read it back by that same string, not by a constant name.

`field_type` comes back in the LEGACY spelling — field_dropdown, field_multi_dropdown, field_string, field_user, field_boolean … — not the canonical vocabulary the admin write calls take. Translate before feeding it anywhere else.
A nested_dropdown field has no legacy spelling, so its `field_type` comes back null. Do not treat that as 'field not found'.
For a nested_dropdown, pass `parent_option_id` to get the children of one parent; without it you get the level's own values.
A field that does not exist, or any upstream failure, returns 400 {success:false, error:'Something went wrong'} — there is no 404 here and no way to tell a bad field id from a backend outage.
A project_id the route accepts but which is not numeric (the literal 'new') returns 200 with field_type null, values null and info null — an empty success, not an error.
The entity_type segment is hyphenated and lower-case (test-case / test-result / test-plan / exploratory-session); anything else does not match the route and 404s before reaching the API.
Boolean fields have their values converted to real true/false before rendering; every other type returns them as stored.

capabilities.name: get_dataset

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id; this route only matches digits, so a PR-NNN identifier never reaches the API.

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: The dataset's uuid string, as returned by the list or create calls. There is no integer-id form of this route.

capabilities.intent: Read one dataset in full — its columns, every row of data, tags and metadata — by dataset uuid

200.description: The dataset with its full column and row contents.

404.description: No dataset with this uuid in the project: {success:false, message:'Dataset <uuid>  not found.'}

422.description: {success:false, message:'Feature not available'} — the group lacks the Team Pro plan. Entitlement, not payload.

guidance: This is the only dataset call that returns the actual data: the list endpoint returns counts and metadata but no `variables` or `rows`.
Read this before any update — update is a full replace with no history, so the response here is the only copy of the prior contents you will get.
`rows_count` is computed from the rows in this payload, so it always agrees with `rows.length`.
`created_by` is resolved against users in the caller's group; a creator who has left resolves to the placeholder {id:0, full_name:'Former User'} rather than null.
An unknown uuid is 404 {success:false, message:'Dataset <uuid>  not found.'} — note the doubled space in the message if you are matching on it.
422 {message:'Feature not available'} means the group lacks the Team Pro plan. That is an entitlement answer, not a bad request; do not retry.
The dataset is at the top level as `dataset`; there is no `data` envelope.

capabilities.name: get_dataset_linked_test_cases

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id; this route only matches digits.

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: The dataset's uuid string, from the dataset list or a create response.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number, forwarded as-is to the backing store. A non-numeric or non-positive value is rejected globally with 400 {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'}. No page-size parameter is exposed.

capabilities.intent: List the test cases bound to a dataset — check what a dataset drives before you edit or delete it

200.description: A page of linked test cases. Note there is no `success` key in this envelope.

test_cases.description: Test cases linked to the dataset, forwarded from the backing store; the per-row field set is not shaped by this service.

400.description: {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'} — a non-positive or non-numeric page value.

404.description: Either 'Dataset <uuid>  not found.' (no such dataset) or 'No test cases found for dataset <uuid>.' (the backing store returned nothing).

422.description: `Feature not available` — the group lacks the Team Pro plan. Not a payload error; do not retry with a different body.

guidance: Run this before deleting or rewriting a dataset — nothing else warns you that test cases depend on it, and the delete gives no preview.
This response has NO `success` key, unlike every other dataset endpoint: it is exactly {test_cases, info}. Do not branch on `success` here.

Two different 404s: an unknown dataset uuid fails in the lookup with 'Dataset <uuid>  not found.', while a dataset the backing store returns nothing at all for fails with 'No test cases found for dataset <uuid>.'. Neither distinguishes 'exists but has no linked cases' reliably — treat a 404 as 'nothing to read', not as proof the dataset is gone.
The test-case rows are passed through from the backing store unchanged; their field set is not shaped by this service and is not declared here.
422 {message:'Feature not available'} is the Team Pro entitlement gate shared by every dataset endpoint.

capabilities.name: get_dataset_variables

query.name: q[name]
query.description: Partial, case-insensitive match on the column name. This is the search this endpoint exists for.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. A non-numeric or non-positive value is 400 {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'}. There is no page-size parameter; read `info.page_size` for what you got.

capabilities.intent: List every dataset column defined anywhere in the project, each with the dataset it belongs to — use this to find which dataset holds a variable name you saw in a test case

200.description: A page of dataset columns, each with its owning dataset, plus paging metadata under `info`.

400.description: {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'} — a non-positive or non-numeric page value.

422.description: {success:false, message:'Feature not available'} — the group lacks the Team Pro plan.

guidance: This is project-wide, not per dataset. `variables` on this path is a fixed route segment, not a dataset uuid — it lists columns across every dataset in the project. To see one dataset's columns, read that dataset instead.
Each row carries its owning dataset inline as `dataset` {uuid, name, count_rows}, so this call resolves a bare variable name to the dataset uuid you need for every other dataset operation.
Column names are not unique across datasets — the same name in two datasets is two rows here. Disambiguate on `dataset.uuid`.
The page size is set by the backing store and cannot be requested from here; page with `p` and read `info` for page/page_size/next.
422 {message:'Feature not available'} is the Team Pro entitlement gate shared by every dataset endpoint.
`success`, `variables` and `info` are all top level — `variables` is the array itself, not a wrapper object.

capabilities.name: get_dedupe_status_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id; this route only matches digits.

capabilities.intent: Check whether duplicate detection has ever run for a project and where the latest scan got to — the only way to tell 'dedupe is off or has never run' from 'it ran and found nothing'

200.description: The latest dedupe job for the project. When no job has ever run, only {status:'NOT_ENABLED', message:'No dedupe job found for this project'} is returned and the job fields are absent.

status.description: Latest job status, or the synthesised 'NOT_ENABLED' when no job exists.

job_id.description: Pipeline job id. Absent when status is NOT_ENABLED.

scheduled_run_time.description: When the scan was scheduled to run. Nullable; absent when status is NOT_ENABLED.

actual_end_time.description: When the scan finished. Null while the job is still in flight; absent when status is NOT_ENABLED.

updated_at.description: Last status change. Absent when status is NOT_ENABLED.

message.description: Present only with NOT_ENABLED: 'No dedupe job found for this project'.

400.description: {error:'Missing project_id'} — unreachable through this route, where project_id is a required path segment.

guidance: Call this first whenever a duplicates listing comes back empty. An empty listing is returned both when the feature is off and when a completed scan found nothing; only this endpoint separates them.

`NOT_ENABLED` is synthesised, not stored: it means no scan job row exists for this project at all, and it arrives with an explanatory `message` and none of the job fields. Every other value is a real job status and comes with job_id and timestamps.
Only the MOST RECENT job is reported, by last update. There is no history and no way to page back to earlier runs.

Statuses are not just running/done. COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, RETRY_FAILED, STATISTICAL_FAILED, CLUSTERING_FAILED, CLUSTERING_LIMIT and LLM_ANALYSIS_SKIPPED are terminal; QUEUED, PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, CLUSTER, CLUSTERING, BACKFILLING, RETRY, STATISTICAL_RETRY and CLUSTERING_RETRY mean a scan is still in flight and the duplicates listing may be incomplete.
This is a plain read of the last job record — it does not start a scan, and nothing in this API can. Scans are scheduled by the dedupe pipeline.
Unlike the rest of this family, no role permission is checked here; project access is enough.
The documented 400 for a missing project id is unreachable through this route, since the id is a required path segment.

capabilities.name: get_duplicate_source_test_case_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id; this route only matches digits.

path_params.name: duplicate_id
path_params.description: Integer duplicate id of an ALREADY-MERGED pair. The route only matches digits.

capabilities.intent: Read the pre-merge snapshot of the test case that was folded away when a duplicate was merged — the only record of what the archived case contained at merge time

200.description: The pre-merge snapshot, wrapped in a `data` envelope: {data:{success:true, test_case:{...}}}. `test_case` is the frozen full test-case serialisation stored at merge time (steps, attachments with signed URLs, template); its field set is whatever was captured then and is not shaped by this endpoint.

test_case.description: Frozen pre-merge serialisation of the source test case.

404.description: Two distinct bodies: {data:{success:false, error:'Source test case snapshot not available'}} when the pair merged but retained no snapshot, and {success:false, error:'Duplicate not found.'} (no `data` key) when the pair is unknown or was never merged.

422.description: {success:false, message:'Invalid source_tc data'} — the stored snapshot could not be parsed.

guidance: This works only for a pair whose status is `merged` — the exact opposite of the read/resolve/discard calls, which work only while a pair is `suggested`. Calling it on a live suggestion is a 404.

The snapshot is written only by the merge path. A pair resolved by archiving instead of merging is also marked merged but stores no snapshot, so it answers 404 with the message 'Source test case snapshot not available'. Treat that as 'not retained', not as a retryable error.

The two 404s have DIFFERENT envelopes. Missing snapshot: {data:{success:false, error:'Source test case snapshot not available'}}. Unknown or unmerged pair: {success:false, error:'Duplicate not found.'} with no `data`. Check for `data` before reading `error`.
Success is wrapped: the test case is at `data.test_case`, not at the top level. This is the only duplicate endpoint with a `data` envelope.

The snapshot is a frozen serialisation taken at merge time, including steps, attachments (with freshly signed, short-lived URLs) and the template — it is not re-read from the live test case, so it will not reflect anything that happened afterwards.
A stored snapshot that cannot be parsed comes back 422 {success:false, message:'Invalid source_tc data'} — a data fault, not something a different request fixes.

To find the merged pair id in the first place: it is no longer in the duplicates listing, so you need the id you saw before resolving, or the id embedded in the merge comment left on the surviving test case.

capabilities.name: get_duplicate_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id; this route only matches digits.

path_params.name: duplicate_id
path_params.description: Integer duplicate id, taken from the `id` of a row in the duplicates listing or search. The route only matches digits.

capabilities.intent: Read one suggested duplicate pair — the two test cases side by side with their titles, descriptions, folders and owners, plus the confidence score and the model's reason — so a human can decide how to resolve it

200.description: The duplicate pair with both test cases resolved, at the top level as `duplicate`.

404.description: {errors:'Duplicate not found.'} — no such pair in this project, or its status is no longer `suggested`. Or {errors:'Test case not found.'} — the pair exists but a member test case could not be resolved.

guidance: Suggested-only. A pair that has already been merged, archived or discarded answers 404 {errors:'Duplicate not found.'} — here a 404 usually means 'already handled', not 'never existed'. Check the listing before concluding the id is wrong.
The error key is `errors` (plural), not `error` or `message`, on both 404 paths from this endpoint.

A second 404, {errors:'Test case not found.'}, means the pair exists but one of its two test cases could not be resolved (deleted or moved out of reach). The pair is unusable — it is also silently dropped from the listings for the same reason.
Unlike the listings, this has NO feature-flag gate: a single pair stays readable by id even for a group whose dedupe listing returns empty.

The pair is at the top level as `duplicate`; there is no `data` envelope. Inside it, `test_cases` always holds exactly two entries and each entry's `id` is the integer test-case id you pass to the resolve call as source or target.
`owner` is a resolved display name and is an empty string when the owner cannot be resolved; `owner_id` is the raw BrowserStack user id. `description` is '' rather than null when absent.
`ai_score` is the model's confidence and `duplicate_type` is exact vs semantic — read both before merging, since an exact pair and a low-confidence semantic pair warrant different treatment.

capabilities.name: get_entity_filter_details_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id. The route segment only matches digits (or the literal 'new'); a PR-NNN identifier is a routing 404.

path_params.name: entity
path_params.description: Which entity's filter vocabulary to resolve against — this also decides which user fields are resolved. 'test-plans' is allowed by the route but rejected by the handler with 400.

query.name: q[status]
query.description: Comma-separated numeric status IDs to resolve. Returned under filter_details.status as objects with id, field_value, internal_name and colour.

query.name: q[priority]
query.description: Comma-separated numeric priority IDs to resolve; returned under filter_details.priority.

query.name: q[case_type]
query.description: Comma-separated numeric case-type IDs to resolve; returned under filter_details.case_type.

query.name: q[automation_state]
query.description: Numeric ids, or the literal word 'automated' / 'manual' which is expanded to this project's ids first; returned under filter_details.automation_state.

query.name: q[automation_status]
query.description: Comma-separated values; split on commas and echoed back as an array, not resolved against anything.

query.name: q[folder_ids]
query.description: Comma-separated folder ids; returned under filter_details.folders as a folder tree with paths and ancestors. At most 600 folders are resolved.

query.name: q[owner]
query.description: Comma-separated TM user ids. Resolved for entity=test-cases and entity=test-runs only; ignored for trtc.

query.name: q[reviewers]
query.description: Comma-separated TM user ids. Resolved for entity=test-cases only.

query.name: q[assignee]
query.description: Comma-separated TM user ids. Resolved for entity=trtc only.

query.name: q[last_executed_by]
query.description: Comma-separated TM user ids. Resolved for entity=trtc only.

query.name: q[test_case_tags]
query.description: Must be a JSON-encoded string containing an array of tag names — it is JSON.parse'd and echoed back. A bare comma-separated list raises rather than filtering. `q[tags]` is not a recognised key.

query.name: q[custom_fields]
query.description: Custom-field selections keyed by field id; returned resolved under filter_details.custom_fields. Date custom fields echo back the raw value you sent rather than the normalised one.

query.name: q[result_custom_fields]
query.description: Test-result custom-field selections; resolved separately and returned under filter_details.result_custom_fields.

query.name: q[configuration_id]
query.description: Comma-separated configuration ids; resolved to configuration objects under filter_details.configurations.

query.name: q[created_at]
query.description: Echoed back verbatim under filter_details.created_at — not parsed, not validated.

query.name: q[updated_at]
query.description: Echoed back verbatim under filter_details.updated_at.

query.name: q[latest_status]
query.description: Comma-separated values, split and echoed back as an array.

capabilities.intent: Resolve a set of filter IDs you already hold into their display objects — turn priority/status/case-type/custom-field ids, folder ids and user ids into names, colours and folder paths so a saved filter can be rendered; it does NOT list the filter options available in a project

200.description: Everything is nested under `filter_details`; only the keys you supplied under q are present, and an empty q yields filter_details:{}.

filter_details.description: Resolved form of the filters that were sent. Keys absent from the request are absent here.

priority.description: Resolved priority options for the ids that were sent.

status.description: Resolved status options for the ids that were sent.

case_type.description: Resolved case-type options for the ids that were sent.

automation_status.description: The q[automation_status] value split on commas and echoed back unresolved.

test_case_tags.description: The JSON-decoded q[test_case_tags] value, echoed back.

latest_status.description: The q[latest_status] value split on commas and echoed back.

custom_fields.description: Resolved custom-field values keyed by field id. Date fields carry the raw value that was sent, not the normalised one.

result_custom_fields.description: Resolved test-result custom-field values keyed by field id.

owner.description: Resolved users for q[owner] — test-cases and test-runs only.

reviewers.description: Resolved users for q[reviewers] — test-cases only.

assignee.description: Resolved users for q[assignee] — trtc only.

last_executed_by.description: Resolved users for q[last_executed_by] — trtc only.

folders.description: Folder structure for q[folder_ids]; at most 600 folders are resolved.
Flattened list of the same folders.

400.description: Unsupported entity (including test-plans, which the route allows but the handler rejects), or malformed filter values.

guidance: This is an echo/hydration endpoint, not a discovery one. It returns only the keys you actually passed under `q`: send q[status]=9319 and you get back `status` resolved; send nothing and you get {success:true, filter_details:{}} with a 200. To enumerate the options a project offers, use the system/custom field value capabilities instead.
The result is nested one level down under `filter_details` — read filter_details.status, filter_details.priority, filter_details.folders. The keys are not at the top level.
Only three entity values work here: test-cases, trtc and test-runs. 'test-plans' passes the route constraint but is not in the handler's map and returns 400 — the route and the handler disagree.

Which user fields get resolved depends on the entity: owner and reviewers for test-cases, assignee and last_executed_by for trtc, owner for test-runs. A user id sent under the wrong key for that entity is ignored without comment.

Filter keys are renamed internally (q[priority] -> priority_id, q[status] -> status_id, q[case_type] -> category_id) but you send the un-suffixed names. q[automation_state] additionally accepts the literal words 'automated' / 'manual'.
q[test_case_tags] must be a JSON-ENCODED STRING of an array; it is JSON.parse'd and echoed back verbatim. `q[tags]` is not a key this endpoint knows and is dropped silently.
q[created_at] and q[updated_at] are echoed back exactly as sent — they are not parsed or normalised here.
Folder resolution caps out at 600 folders per call, so a very wide folder selection comes back truncated rather than paged.
q[query] has no effect on this endpoint — it is sanitised and then ignored.

capabilities.name: get_exploratory_session
capabilities.intent: Read one exploratory session in full — its charter, state, timings, assignee, tags, configurations, linked test plan, linked issues, custom fields and how many logs it holds — before reading its logs or changing it

200.description: Successfully retrieved the exploratory session.

guidance: session_id is a plain integer. The route segment only matches digits, so the display identifier (ES-NNN) never reaches the API — it fails as a routing 404, not as an API error.

Read `session_log_count` first: it tells you how many log pages to walk, and it is the same number that decides whether a clone of this session runs synchronously or asynchronously (50 or more logs switches clone to the async path).

custom_fields is always present on this read — normalised into the flat TCM shape, and an empty array when the session has none. That normalisation is applied here, on create, update and clone, but NOT on the sessions listing.

assignee, created_by and closed_by are expanded into {id, email, full_name, group_id} objects by looking the user up locally. If the stored user is not a TM user in this group the field comes back null even though a user is set upstream.
A session id that does not exist comes back as a bare {success:false} with the 404 status and no message — the upstream error text is deliberately not relayed.
The session is at the top level under `exploratory_session`. There is no `data` envelope on any endpoint of this entity.
Requires the test-run view permission: exploratory sessions are gated by the test run permission set, not by a permission of their own.

capabilities.name: get_exploratory_session_summary_v1

query.name: mode
query.description: `time_period` scopes by dates and ignores session_ids; `session_selection` scopes by session_ids and ignores the dates. Mismatched parameters are dropped silently, not rejected.

query.name: start_date
query.description: Inclusive start, YYYY-MM-DD. Only read in time_period mode; omitted entirely from the upstream call when absent.

query.name: end_date
query.description: Inclusive end, YYYY-MM-DD. Only read in time_period mode.

query.name: session_ids
query.description: Comma-separated session ids as a STRING, not an array. Only read in session_selection mode.

capabilities.intent: Get exploratory-session testing figures for a project directly — sessions, outcomes and top testers over a date range or a chosen set of sessions, with no saved report needed

200.description: Summary figures under `data`.

data.description: Exploratory-session summary payload — session counts, outcome breakdown, `sessions` (with `assignee` expanded to a user object) and `top_testers` (each `{ user, bug_count }`, `user` null when the tester is no longer in the group).

guidance: Use this for an ad-hoc question about exploratory testing. It computes live from the project and needs no report to exist; the saved equivalent is an `Exploratory Session Summary` report read through the report capabilities.

The figures are under `data`, not at the top level. `data.top_testers[].user` and `data.sessions[].assignee` are expanded from ids into user objects server-side, and come back `null` for a tester who is no longer a TM user.

`mode` decides which of the other parameters matter: `time_period` (the default) uses `start_date` / `end_date` and ignores `session_ids`; `session_selection` uses `session_ids` and ignores the dates. Sending the wrong pair for the mode is not an error — it is silently ignored and you get an unintended scope.
`session_ids` is a comma-separated STRING here, not an array. Dates are plain YYYY-MM-DD.
Omitted parameters are dropped rather than defaulted locally, so the upstream service picks the window — always send explicit dates when the range matters.
This route only exists under a project; it reads the project from the path and requires the report_view permission (403 otherwise).

capabilities.name: get_filter
capabilities.intent: Read one saved filter view — its name, scope and the exact condition set it applies — before reusing, editing or deleting it
guidance: This read is not side-effect free. The handler validates every custom-field condition in the saved view against the project's current custom fields and, when any no longer exist, it rewrites the stored filter without them. Reading a filter can permanently change it.
So `data.filters.customFields` can legitimately be a subset of what was saved, and a second read will not put the pruned conditions back. Treat what you get as the new truth.

The entity_type to custom-field-entity map has no entry for `testrun`, so a run filter is validated against TEST CASE custom fields and conditions that were valid for runs can be pruned. Be cautious about reading run filters you do not want altered.

Known defect: if the custom-field lookup or the write-back fails with a 400, the action returns without rendering anything at all — you get an empty/500 response rather than the filter. Fall back to the filter listing, which does no validation.
The filter is under `data` with a sibling `success`; the conditions are at `data.filters` and the list type at `data.entity_type` (not `entity`, which is the request-side spelling).
Only a 400 from the backing service is translated to `{success:false, message:...}`; anything else from it surfaces as a 500, so an unknown filter_id does not reliably produce a 404.

capabilities.name: get_folder_remove_summary
capabilities.intent: Dry-run a folder deletion — count the test cases, subfolders and cross-product recordings that would be destroyed — before committing to it
guidance: Read-only despite the delete machinery behind it: the handler calls the delete path with dry_run set, so nothing is removed. This is the safety check to run before deleting a folder.
It is nonetheless gated on the folder-DELETE permission, not the view permission. A caller who can read folders but not delete them gets 403 here.
The counts are nested under `deleted_entity_count` — active_test_case_count, archived_test_case_count, sub_folders and test_recordings_count all live inside that object, not at the top level.

`has_other_product_entity` is derived from one thing only: it is true exactly when test_recordings_count is greater than zero, meaning the subtree holds low-code test recordings owned by another product that the delete would take with it.
The folder is not fetched before the dry run, so a folder id that does not exist in this project surfaces as a bare 404 {success:false} with no message identifying the id.
folder_id must be a positive integer; literal 0 raises an unhandled ArgumentError and comes back as a 500.

capabilities.name: get_folder_tree_v1
capabilities.intent: Fetch a project's entire folder tree in one call — every root folder with its children nested under `contents` — to resolve a folder name to the integer id every other folder and test-case call needs

200.description: Folder tree.

query.name: folder_sort_by
query.description: Sibling ordering. Comma-separated combinations are accepted and each element is validated; anything outside this set returns 400 {error:'Invalid folder_sort_by parameter'}. Either name- sort silently gains a secondary created_at-asc tiebreak.

query.name: shared
query.description: Any truthy presence switches the tree to the shared-folder view. Presence alone is what counts — sending shared=false still enables it, because only presence is tested.

guidance: This returns the WHOLE tree in one response and is not paginated — no page or per-page parameter is read. On a large project it is a big payload; use the per-folder listing instead if you only need one level.
The tree is at `structure`, a top-level array. There is no `data` envelope on this endpoint. Children hang off each node's `contents` array, recursively.
Folder ids in the tree are plain integers, and they are what every other folder capability expects in its path.

An unresolvable project (including the literal path segment `new`) returns 200 with {structure: [], success: true}, not a 404. An empty structure is therefore ambiguous between 'no folders' and 'no such project' — confirm the project separately.

When Review & Approve is switched on for the project, the per-folder test-case counts in the tree are silently narrowed to review-eligible statuses. If you also pass a review_status filter, it is intersected with the project's eligible set — and when the intersection is empty your filter is discarded and the project's set is used instead, so you can get counts you did not ask for rather than an error.
Counts here are aggregates over the tree; they are not a list of test cases. Read test cases through the test-case listings.

capabilities.name: get_group_users_v2_v1

query.name: q
query.description: As a bare string: filters on FULL NAME only, as a SQL LIKE '%value%'. Email is not matched by this form and there is no partial-email search. Whitespace is not trimmed.

query.name: q[email]
query.description: Exact email lookup — no partial matching. Returns at most one user, and this branch OMITS the `info` pagination block entirely, so a reader that always dereferences info.next breaks on it.

query.name: q[id]
query.description: Comma-separated Test Management user ids. This does NOT filter — it only re-orders, putting the named ids first and returning the rest of the workspace behind them. It also raises the page size to the number of ids when that exceeds 30.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. Previously undeclared. A non-positive or non-numeric value is rejected globally with 400 `{success:false, error:"Invalid Params"}`. Has no effect on the q[email] branch, which is unpaginated.

capabilities.intent: List or look up the people in this workspace — search by name, resolve an exact email, or read your own identity — to get the user id that owner and assignee fields take
guidance: Scope is the whole WORKSPACE (group), not a project — every active user in the group is returned regardless of which projects they can see, and no project id can be supplied. This is not a way to answer 'who is on this project'.

`q[id]` is a sort, not a filter. Passing ids re-orders the full user list so those ids come first; you still get everyone. Filtering to specific people is not supported here — match on the ids yourself after reading.

The response shape varies by branch: the default, name-search and id branches return `{users, myself, success, info}`, but the `q[email]` branch returns `{users, myself, success}` with NO `info` at all.

`id` is the Test Management user id; `browserstack_user_id` is the separate BrowserStack account id for the same person, and the two are different numbers. Owner and assignee fields on cases and runs take the TM `id`; some listing filters take browserstack_user_id instead. Sending the wrong one usually resolves to nobody rather than erroring, so check which the target capability wants.
Only active users are returned. A deactivated person cannot be resolved here, which means an assignee who has left the workspace cannot be looked up to explain an existing assignment.
`myself` is the calling user as {id, full_name, email, reports_and_notification_enabled} — the cheapest way to get your own TM user id, with no search needed.
Page size is fixed at 30 (the q[id] branch excepted, where it becomes the number of ids); there is no per_page parameter.
No project is involved, so this works without a project_id and is not project-permission gated.

capabilities.name: get_issues_count_info_v1
capabilities.intent: Chart how many defects/issues were linked from this project per period — the defect-discovery trend
guidance: Each entry in `data` is a positional pair — period label first, count second — not a {label, count} object; the CSV exporter reads them by index. Read them positionally and do not rely on key names.
This counts issues per period; it does not list them. There is no way to reach the individual defects from this response.
`empty_data` is the 'nothing to plot' flag; the series is padded with zeroes otherwise.

The filter trap: sending ANY q key without an explicit q[created_at] makes the handler default both created_at and closed_at to 'all_time', and the closed_at path rewrites 'all_time' to '1_year' — so filtering only by owner silently narrows the chart to the last 12 months. Sending no q at all applies no date bound. Always pass q[created_at] explicitly whenever you pass any other filter.
project_id is the INTEGER id; the route segment only matches digits (or the literal 'new'), so a PR-NNN identifier is a routing 404 that never reaches the API.
A project that exists but is not visible to this caller renders as 404 {success:false}, not 403 — 'no such project' and 'no access' are indistinguishable here.

query.name: q[created_at]
query.description: Relative date window on creation date, as <N>_<hour|day|week|month|year>, optionally suffixed _gte for 'older than' (e.g. 3_month, 7_day_gte). 'all_time' is honoured on this key and applies no bound. An unrecognised unit raises server-side rather than returning 400.

query.name: q[closed_at]
query.description: Same token format, applied to close date. Only read when q[created_at] is absent or 'all_time' — created_at wins. 'all_time' is NOT honoured here: it is silently rewritten to 1_year.

query.name: q[owner]
query.description: Comma-separated TM user ids (resolve them with get_project_users_v2_v1). Translated to BrowserStack ids server-side; ids that do not resolve are dropped, and if none resolve the owner filter is omitted entirely rather than returning an empty chart.

query.name: filter_details
query.description: Echo the filters you sent back, resolved, as a `filter_details` key merged into the response (owner ids become user objects). Has no effect unless q is also present.

capabilities.name: get_project_by_integer_id_v1
capabilities.intent: Get a project by INTEGER id (v1) — full detail + its PR-NNN identifier

200.description: Project detail; data.project.identifier is the PR-NNN form.

404.description: No project with that integer id, OR the project exists but is not visible to this user — both render as 404 {success:false}.

guidance: The path segment only matches digits (or the literal string 'new'), so a PR-NNN identifier never reaches this action — it is a routing 404, not an API error.
This is the integer-id -> PR-NNN translation step: read `data.project.identifier` and carry it into any the v2 surface route, which will not accept the integer.
The project sits under a `data` envelope: `data.project`. The paginated/minified project listings do NOT use `data` — they return `projects` at the top level. Do not reuse a path across the two.

A project that exists but is not visible to this caller comes back as 404 {success:false} — the underlying 403 is deliberately rewritten. You cannot distinguish 'no such project' from 'no access' on this route.

`test_cases_count`, `test_runs_count` and `test_plans_count` are fetched with the detail here (they are absent from the lean listings), which is the reason to use this call rather than filtering a listing.
`permissions` is the caller's own permission list for this project and `user_role` their role name — both reflect the requesting user, not the project.
Requires the project_view permission under RBAC.

capabilities.name: get_project_id_custom_fields_v2_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id. PR-NNN identifiers do not match the route; the literal 'new' matches the route but is rejected with 400 'Invalid Params: project_id must be a valid integer'.

capabilities.intent: Get the test-case form for one project — the custom fields it shows, the built-in system fields, and the pick lists behind the standard priority / state / type / automation-status dropdowns
guidance: This is the read to make before creating or editing a test case: it tells you which fields that project actually shows, which are mandatory, and what the standard dropdowns accept.

The response is three lists at the top level — `custom_fields`, `default_fields`, `system_fields` — with NO `data` envelope and no pagination. Every custom field the project has comes back in one call.

`field_type` inside `custom_fields` uses the LEGACY spelling (field_dropdown, field_string, field_user, field_boolean …), not the canonical vocabulary the admin create/update calls take. Translate in both directions.
TestCase only. Result, plan, exploratory-session and step custom fields are served by different endpoints and never appear here.
`optional` and `is_required` are both present and are inverses of one another; prefer is_required.
Each row carries `links.self` — the ready-made path to that field's values in this project (or to the project user list for a `user` field). Follow it rather than building the path.
`option_values` / `field_values` appear only when the upstream row carried them, so an absent key does not mean the field has no options — follow links.self to be sure.
project_id must be numeric. The route also matches the literal 'new', but this handler rejects a non-numeric value with 400 'Invalid Params: project_id must be a valid integer'.
`automation_status` under default_fields is assembled in this layer, not read from storage, and the automation-status custom field is omitted for groups without that feature.

capabilities.name: get_project_settings

query.name: in_review_count
query.description: Compute meta_data.in_review_count and meta_data.test_plan_in_review_count for the CALLING user. Without it both are returned as 0 rather than omitted, so an unrequested 0 is not evidence of an empty queue.

query.name: fetch_dedupe_button
query.description: Append a duplicate-review marker string to the project_settings array ('show_review_duplicates', 'disable_review_duplicates' or 'hide_review_duplicates'). Any failure computing it is swallowed and no marker is appended.

query.name: p
query.description: Page of the underlying settings rows (30 per page) before they are flattened into project_settings[0].

capabilities.intent: Read a project's configuration flags — review/approval gating, the custom test-case id prefix, time-tracking, Part 11 re-auth, Jira/Azure linking — and optionally the caller's own pending-review counts

200.description: project_settings[0] is a flat attribute->value object (all values are strings); later elements, when present, are bare marker strings. info and meta_data are omitted entirely when the project has no stored settings.

project_settings.description: Element 0 is a single object mapping each stored setting name to its string value. Any further elements are duplicate-review marker strings appended when fetch_dedupe_button=true. Empty array when nothing is stored.

items.description: Either the flattened settings object or a marker string.

info.description: Paging over the underlying settings rows. Absent when the project has no stored settings.

meta_data.description: Per-caller review counts. Present whenever settings exist; both fields are 0 unless in_review_count=true was passed.

in_review_count.description: Test cases in review where the calling user is a reviewer.

test_plan_in_review_count.description: Test plans in review for the calling user. Best-effort — a backend error yields 0.

guidance: `project_settings` is an ARRAY, but not a list of settings. Element 0 is a single flat object holding every stored setting as attribute -> value; any further elements are bare marker STRINGS ('show_review_duplicates' / 'disable_review_duplicates' / 'hide_review_duplicates') appended only when fetch_dedupe_button=true. Read project_settings[0] for the settings and expect mixed types in the rest of the array.

A project with no stored settings returns {success:true, project_settings:[]} with NO `info` and NO `meta_data` at all — not an object of defaults. Absence of a key means 'never set', and the effective behaviour is the group default, which is not visible here.
Every value is stored as a string (the settings are an EAV store), so booleans come back as "true"/"false" and numbers as strings. Compare against strings, not native types.
`meta_data` is always present when any setting exists, but both counts are hard-zero unless you pass in_review_count=true — a 0 you did not ask for means 'not computed', not 'nothing in review'.

in_review_count counts test cases where the CALLER is a reviewer and the case is in review; it is per-user, not per-project. test_plan_in_review_count is computed on a separate path and is best-effort — a backend hiccup silently yields 0.
The underlying rows are paged at 30 per page (`p` selects the page) before being flattened, so a project with an unusually large settings set can produce an incomplete first-page object.
This read is not feature-gated, but the matching write is: update_project_settings returns 422 unless the new-project-settings flag is on for the group or user.

capabilities.name: get_project_users_v2_v1

query.name: q
query.description: Flat string: case-sensitive LIKE match on full_name (substring). Paginated, 30 per page.

query.name: q[email]
query.description: Exact email lookup, at most one row. This branch returns NO `info` block — do not read pagination from it. An unknown address returns an empty `users` array, not a 404.

query.name: q[id]
query.description: Comma-separated TM user ids. This does NOT filter — it moves those users to the front of the full group list. Page size grows to the id count when more than 30 ids are given.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number (the param is `p`, not `page`). Overflow returns the last page rather than an empty one.

capabilities.intent: Find the users in this group — by name fragment, by exact email, or by id — and get the caller's own identity back alongside them; use this to resolve a person's name or email to the numeric user id that owner/assignee/reviewer filters and writes require
guidance: Despite the path, this is GROUP-scoped, not project-scoped: it lists every active user in the caller's group and never filters by the project in the URL. The project_id only has to be a real project the caller can see.

`q` is polymorphic and the three forms behave differently. `q=jane` (a flat string) is a name LIKE match and is paginated. `q[email]=jane@acme.com` is an exact lookup that returns at most one user AND OMITS the `info` block entirely. `q[id]=12,34` reorders those ids to the front of the full list rather than filtering to them — it is a sort, not a filter.
Page size is fixed at 30 and there is no size parameter. The one exception is `q[id]` with more than 30 ids, where the page grows to fit the id list.
Use `p` for the page number (not `page`). An out-of-range page returns the LAST page rather than an empty list, so never treat a non-empty response as proof the page number was valid.
`myself` is the caller's own record and is always present, but it is a reduced shape — id, full_name, email, reports_and_notification_enabled only, with no browserstack_user_id.

The `id` on each user is the TM user id. That is what the owner/assignee/reviewer search filters and test-run writes expect; `browserstack_user_id` is a different number and is only correct where a capability explicitly says BrowserStack id.
Only active users are returned — a deactivated user who still owns test cases will not appear here, so an unresolvable owner id is not necessarily invalid.

capabilities.name: get_projects_basic_v1

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. Validated as an integer; a non-integer returns 400.

query.name: count
query.description: Rows per page. Validated as an integer here but NOT bounded in this service before being forwarded to the backing store; 300 is the documented maximum.

query.name: q[query]
query.description: Free-text match on project name.

query.name: q[identifier]
query.description: Exact PR-NNN identifier lookup. Note the matched rows do not echo `identifier` back.

capabilities.intent: Look up projects by name or by PR-NNN identifier, or page through them cheaply — the lean listing, and the only one with an identifier search; note the rows it returns do NOT include the identifier itself
guidance: `q` must be a structured object here — q[query] for a name match, q[identifier] for an exact PR-NNN lookup. A flat `q=foo` string returns 400 'Invalid Params: q must be an object with identifier/query keys'. This is the exact opposite of list_projects_v1, which demands a flat string.

Asymmetry worth planning around: you can FILTER by q[identifier], but the rows come back without `identifier` — the serializer here omits it. If you need the PR-NNN form back, use list_projects_v1 or the single-project read.
Only q[query] and q[identifier] are read; any other key under q is dropped silently and the search runs unfiltered, which reads as 'matched everything' rather than as an error.

Default page size is 30 (not 300). `count` is forwarded to the backing service and is not bounded in this codebase — 300 is the documented ceiling, so treat larger values as unsupported rather than assuming they are clamped.
Rows carry `permissions` (the caller's own rights on that project) but no counts — test_cases_count/test_runs_count are absent from this payload. Fetch the single project if you need them.
The response is `projects` + `info` at the top level; there is no `data` envelope.

capabilities.name: get_projects_minify_v1

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. Non-positive or non-numeric values return 400 'Invalid Params'.

query.name: count
query.description: Rows per page. Clamped to 300 — a larger value is silently reduced, not rejected. Omitting it gives 300, not 30.

capabilities.intent: Page through every project in the group as a flat dropdown list, 300 at a time — the fastest way to enumerate all projects, but it cannot search and it returns no pagination metadata
guidance: There is no search on this route at all — no `q` in any form. To find a project by name or identifier use get_projects_basic_v1.
The response has NO `info` block: `{success, projects}` only. You cannot tell from one page whether more exist — keep requesting pages until one comes back with fewer than `count` rows (or empty).
Default page size is 300, not 30, and `count` is hard-clamped to 300: a larger value is silently reduced rather than rejected. That makes this the cheapest full enumeration in the index.
Rows are the same lean dropdown shape as get_projects_basic_v1 — id, name, description, starred, the caller's `permissions` — with no identifier and no test case / run counts.
`p` is validated globally: a non-positive or non-numeric page returns 400 'Invalid Params'.

capabilities.name: get_report_attachment_url

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id. Part of the lookup key — an attachment filed under a different project is a 404 even with the correct id.

path_params.name: attachment_id
path_params.description: Integer stored-file id for the attachment. Not a report id and not an export channel id; no report capability returns one.

capabilities.intent: Exchange a report attachment's id for a short-lived direct download URL

200.description: Successfully retrieved report attachment URL

guidance: Returns a presigned URL you can fetch yourself — the bytes never pass through this API. It expires in 100 minutes, so fetch it promptly rather than storing it.

`attachment_id` is a stored-file id, not a report id and not a channel id. No capability in this index hands one out: the report reads do not return attachment ids, and the export path only broadcasts its result over a realtime channel. In practice you need the id from an attachment link the product rendered elsewhere.
A miss returns HTTP 404 with a normal-looking body `{ url: null, success: false }` rather than an error envelope — check `success`, not just the status, and never treat `url: null` as a valid URL.
The lookup is scoped by BOTH the attachment id and the `project_id` in the path (plus your group), so the right id under the wrong project is a 404. Requires the report_view permission.

capabilities.name: get_report_detail

query.name: sections
query.description: Comma-separated widget names to compute, from the report type's allow-list. Anything else fails the whole call 400 `Invalid sections passed`. Omit for the report's default (often nearly empty) payload.

query.name: is_print
query.description: Send `true` to compute EVERY section for `Test Run Summary` and `Test Plan Summary` in one call, ignoring `sections`. Ignored by the other report types. Compared as the literal string 'true'.

query.name: report_data_only
query.description: Return ONLY the `report_data` object, dropping the definition and filters. Any non-empty value is truthy — `report_data_only=false` also strips the envelope. Omit it entirely for the full body.

query.name: widget_type
query.description: Required when `sections` names a `*_drilldown` widget; the allowed set differs per drilldown (see get_report_section_v1). Missing or unknown is 400.

query.name: segment
query.description: Drilldown sub-slice, sent as a JSON-ENCODED STRING (e.g. `{"outcome":"bugs_found"}`), not a nested object. Unparseable values are ignored rather than rejected.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number for the row-bearing sections (drilldowns, trtc_details, traceability rows). Does not page the definition.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Rows per page, forwarded only for the `Test Run Detailed Report` detail table. Ignored by the other report types, which use their own page size.

query.name: today
query.description: Overrides the server's notion of 'today' for Test Plan Summary overdue/near-completion maths. Unparseable values fall back to the real date silently.

query.name: issue_categories
query.description: Requirement Traceability Report only: restrict to these issue types. Accepts a comma-separated string or a repeated array param. The catch-all value `other` is stripped before the upstream call.

capabilities.intent: Read one saved report — its definition, resolved filters, and computed figures — the general-purpose report read
guidance: This is the read to reach for when you have a report id and want everything: the definition is at `data`, the resolved filter selection at `report_filters`, and the numbers at `report_data`. Use get_report_section_v1 instead when you want one widget and nothing else.

`report_data` is computed per report type and is mostly EMPTY unless you name sections. A bare read fills a Test Case Activity report's headline counts but leaves Test Run Summary's issues_data / test_run_status / test_cases_status / issues_by_priority / issues_by_status null. A null section means NOT COMPUTED — never read it as 'no data'. Request the section, then judge.

Shortcut: `is_print=true` forces ALL sections for `Test Run Summary` and `Test Plan Summary` in a single call, which is usually what you want rather than guessing section names. User Workload Report already returns every section when `sections` is omitted.

`report_data_only` is a trap: any non-empty value is truthy, INCLUDING the string "false". Sending `report_data_only=false` collapses the response to the bare `report_data` object with no `data`, no `report_filters` and no envelope. Omit the parameter entirely when you want the full body.

A section name not in the report type's allow-list is 400 `Invalid sections passed` for the whole call. Do not answer that by retrying without `sections` — you get a stripped body, not the data. Fix the name (see get_report_section_v1 for the per-type lists).

A report saved with `report_timeframe: specific_test_plans` whose plan filters have since gone returns 422 `This report is invalid. Please create a new Report`. That report cannot be read at all; recreate it.

`Defects Summary` and `Defects Detailed Report` have no data branch on the server — they always read back `report_data: null` no matter what you ask for. For defect figures use a Test Run Summary and its issues_by_priority / issues_by_status sections.
The report is resolved by group + id; the project in the path does not scope the lookup. 404 `Report Not Found` means no such report in your group. Requires the report_view permission.

`*_drilldown` sections (tr_drilldown, tc_activity_drilldown, es_drilldown, tp_drilldown) return PAGINATED ROWS and additionally require `widget_type` — never tally those rows into a total, read the aggregate section instead.

capabilities.name: get_report_section_v1

path_params.name: section_name
path_params.description: One widget name from the report type's allow-list (see guidance for the per-type lists). A name outside the list is 400 `Invalid sections passed`; report types with no list accept anything and return a default payload.

query.name: widget_type
query.description: Required for the `*_drilldown` sections and validated against a set that differs per drilldown (see guidance). Missing or unknown is 400 `invalid widget_type`.

query.name: segment
query.description: Drilldown sub-slice as a JSON-ENCODED STRING, not a nested object. For es_drilldown + session_outcomes the `outcome` value is validated (400 otherwise); elsewhere an unparseable value is ignored.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number for row-bearing sections.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Rows per page, forwarded only for the `Test Run Detailed Report` detail table; ignored elsewhere.

capabilities.intent: Fetch one report widget on its own — a single chart, table or drill-down slice from a saved report, without the report definition

200.description: The bare section payload (the report read's `report_data` object) — no success flag and no envelope. `null` for report types with no data branch.

400.description: Section name not in the report type's allow-list, or a missing/invalid widget_type or segment on a drilldown section.

422.description: The report's saved plan selection no longer resolves — the report must be recreated.

guidance: The response is the BARE widget payload. This route runs the report read with `report_data_only` forced on, so there is no `success`, no `data` and no `report_filters` — just the section object keyed by the section name.

The section name must be in the report type's allow-list or the call is 400 `Invalid sections passed`. Test Run Summary: test_run_data, issues_data, test_run_status, test_cases_status, user_result_stats, issues_by_priority, issues_by_status, time_tracking, estimated_vs_actual, tr_drilldown. Test Run Detailed Report: trtc_details, trtc_filter_options, test_run_data, issues_data, trtc_performance, tr_drilldown.

Test Case Activity: test_case_created_count, test_case_updated_count, test_case_deleted_count, test_case_automation_coverage, test_case_top_creators, test_case_trend, test_case_created_priority, test_case_ai_coverage, test_case_list, tc_activity_drilldown. Test Plan Summary: test_run_data, test_run_status, test_plans_progress, test_plans_near_completion, overdue_test_plans, test_plans_execution_trend_list, test_plans_execution_trend_graph, test_result_user_stats, test_run_requirements, test_result_defects, defects_by_status, defects_by_priority, tp_drilldown. Exploratory Session Summary: es_drilldown. User Workload Report: cards, user_table, workload_distribution, execution_trend, status_distribution.

Requirement Traceability Report, Test Plan Detailed Report, Defects Summary and Defects Detailed Report have NO allow-list, so any section name is accepted and forwarded — a typo there returns an empty or default payload at 200 instead of a 400.
On `Defects Summary` / `Defects Detailed Report` the body is literally `null`: those types have no data branch at all. That is the report type, not a failure of your section name.

Drill-down sections need `widget_type` and reject anything outside their own set. tr_drilldown: active_runs, closed_runs, tr_performance, total_test_cases, linked_issues, requirements_linked, runs_by_state, defects_linked, assignee_breakdown, tcs_by_status. tc_activity_drilldown: created_test_cases, updated_test_cases, deleted_test_cases, automation_coverage, ai_coverage, trend, priority, top_creators. es_drilldown: total_sessions, linked_test_plans, session_outcomes. tp_drilldown has no allow-list and passes through.
For `es_drilldown` with widget_type `session_outcomes`, `segment` must carry an `outcome` from bugs_found, issues_found, needs_followup, skipped, no_issues, no_activity — anything else is 400.
Drill-downs return PAGINATED ROWS, not aggregates. Page them with `p`; never sum rows into a count — read the matching aggregate section instead.
Every precondition of the full report read still applies: 404 for an unknown report, 422 for a specific_test_plans report whose plan filters are gone, and the report_view permission.
The section name occupies a wildcard path segment. Two-segment paths with a reserved word (for example `detail`) are matched by other routes first, so only use real section names here.

capabilities.name: get_report_summary_by_type

path_params.name: report_type
path_params.description: Which renderer to run. This is NOT checked against the report's stored report_type — a mismatch still computes and returns 200. Any other value is 400 `Report type not found`.

query.name: reportTimeRange
query.description: Window to compute over. Required for test_runs_summary / test_runs_details — missing or unrecognised is an unhandled 500, not a 400. `custom` reads dates off the REPORT's stored custom_date_range. Ignored by requirement_traceability_report; optional for test_plan_details.

query.name: sections
query.description: Comma-separated widgets. test_runs_details defaults to `test_run_data,issues_data,trtc_performance` when omitted. Not allow-list-checked on this route.

query.name: widget_type
query.description: Only read when `sections` includes `tr_drilldown`, and then required — an unknown value is 400 `invalid widget_type`.

query.name: segment
query.description: Drilldown sub-slice as a JSON-ENCODED STRING, not a nested object.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number for the row-bearing renderers (test_runs_details, test_plan_details, traceability).

query.name: per_page
query.description: Rows per page for the test_runs_details table. The upstream ceiling is not enforced here.

query.name: required
query.description: Column selection for test_runs_details / test_plan_details: `{ "<entity>": { "fields": [...] } }`, entities test_run_test_case / test_run / test_result (plus test_plan). `fields` may be a comma-separated string, and `["all"]` expands to every supported column. Unknown names are 400 here.

query.name: issue_categories
query.description: requirement_traceability_report only: restrict to these issue types. Comma-separated string or repeated array param; the catch-all `other` is stripped before the upstream call.

query.name: today
query.description: Overrides 'today' for plan overdue/near-completion maths. Unparseable values fall back silently.

capabilities.intent: Render a saved report through one of four fixed renderers — run summary, run detail table, test plan detail table, or requirement traceability
guidance: The `report_type` path segment selects a RENDERER, not the report's own type, and the server never checks the two agree. Pointing `test_runs_summary` at a Test Case Activity report computes a run summary from that report's filters and returns 200 — so the figures may not be the report the user asked about. Prefer get_report_detail unless you specifically want one of these four renderings.

The path segment takes four values, one more than the spec lists: `test_runs_summary`, `test_runs_details`, `test_plan_details` and `requirement_traceability_report`. Anything else is 400 `Report type not found`, as is omitting it.

`reportTimeRange` is genuinely required for `test_runs_summary` and `test_runs_details`: omitting it, or sending a value outside the timeframe enum, is an unhandled 500 rather than a validation error. `test_plan_details` falls back to the report's saved timeframe, and `requirement_traceability_report` ignores it entirely.

`reportTimeRange=custom` reads the dates off the REPORT's stored `custom_date_range`, not from the request — on a report saved without one it is a 500. Use the report's own timeframe value unless you know it has a custom range.
The response is the renderer's payload merged onto `{ success: true }` — the keys differ per renderer, so read what came back rather than assuming a fixed shape.

`test_runs_details` defaults `sections` to `test_run_data,issues_data,trtc_performance`, pages with `p` / `per_page`, and accepts a column selection under `required` which IS validated here (an unknown field name is 400 `Invalid fields: ... for <entity>`).
`test_plan_details` is feature-flagged: a group without the flag gets 403 `Operation not permitted`.
`requirement_traceability_report` accepts `issue_categories` (comma-separated or repeated) to restrict issue types; the catch-all value `other` is stripped before the upstream call.
`widget_type` here is the tr_drilldown set, and only applies when `sections` includes `tr_drilldown`. 404 `Report Not Found` for an unknown id; requires the report_view permission.

capabilities.name: get_root_folders_v1

query.name: folder_name
query.description: Name search across the project's folders, not just root ones. It is trimmed and ignored when blank, so an all-whitespace value quietly returns the unfiltered root listing instead of an empty result.

query.name: include_folder_hierarchy
query.description: Adds a `folder_hierarchy` map of folder id to its ancestor chain — the only way to learn a matched folder's path from this endpoint. Enabled only by the literal string "true" (case-insensitively); any other value is false.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number, and the switch that turns paging on at all. With `p` absent NO page parameters are sent upstream, `per_page` and `case_count` are ignored entirely, and you get the upstream default page. Always send `p` if you intend to page.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Rows per page. Read only when `p` is also present, and forwarded upstream unchanged — this service enforces no ceiling of its own, so the real maximum is the upstream one (documented as 100; not enforceable from this codebase). Trust `info` for what you actually got.

query.name: case_count
query.description: Send the literal string "false" to drop the expensive per-folder test-case counts and the total count, keeping only subfolder counts — a worthwhile speedup on wide projects. Read only when `p` is present; any value other than "false" leaves counts on.

query.name: folder_sort_by
query.description: Ordering. Comma-separated combinations are accepted; anything outside this set returns 400 {error:'Invalid folder_sort_by parameter'}. Either name- sort silently gains a secondary created_at-asc tiebreak.

capabilities.intent: List a project's root folders, or search folders anywhere in the project by name — the paginated way in when the full tree is too big to pull at once
guidance: Without `folder_name` or a filter this returns ROOT folders only — it is not a flat list of every folder in the project. To reach nested folders either search by name, ask for the hierarchy, or walk the tree.
Paging is conditional on `p`. Sending only `per_page` does nothing at all: the handler never builds page parameters unless `p` is present, so you silently get the upstream default page size.
The payload is {folders: [...], info: {...}} with no `data` envelope, and `folder_hierarchy` appears only when you asked for it. Page forward using `info`, not by counting rows.
Folder ids are plain integers. `parent_id` is null on root folders.

Test-case filters passed under `q` narrow which folders come back (folders whose cases match). Using a 'contains only' match type without the feature flag returns 403 {success:false, message:'This feature is not available'} — that is a feature gap, not a permission problem.
Requires the folder-view permission.

capabilities.name: get_selected_report_testcases
capabilities.intent: Read a report's saved test-case selection in the folder-keyed shape the editor uses — the value to round-trip back when editing the report
guidance: Use this before editing a report's case selection. The report edit treats `report_filters.test_cases` as authoritative and deletes what you omit, and a flat id list cannot express folder-level or project-level 'select all' — this returns the exact object to send back.

`selection` is the primary project's saved selection (`{}` when nothing is saved); `shared_selection` is `{ "<project_id>": <selection> }` for the report's other projects on a cross-project report, and `{}` otherwise. `selection_data` is the project's full folder/case tree used to render the picker, not the saved selection — do not confuse the two.
Despite the name it is not traceability-specific: it works for any report type. It simply returns an unfiltered project selection tree when the report has no case filters saved.
Unlike the other report reads, the `project_id` in the path IS used — `selection_data` is built for that project, so pass the report's own project or the tree will not match the saved ids.
Case ids inside the selection are INTEGERS (the numeric id), not TC-NNN identifiers.
404 `Report Not Found` for an id that is not in your group. Requires the report_view permission.

capabilities.name: get_shared_steps_by_i_d_v1

query.name: p
query.description: Page number over the block's step ROWS (not over shared steps). A non-positive or non-numeric value is rejected globally with 400 `{success:false, error:"Invalid Params"}`.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Step rows per page. Forwarded unchanged to the backing service, which owns the ceiling — it is not bounded here. Previously undeclared, which is why long blocks silently truncated at 150.

query.name: paginated
query.description: Does NOT control whether the rows are paginated — they always are. It only controls whether `page_info` is included in the response. Send 'true' or you get a page of rows with no way to tell that more exist.

capabilities.intent: Read one shared step with its full ordered step/result rows — the block that every referencing test case renders, and the row ids those references point at
guidance: The rows are always fetched a page at a time (150 by default) regardless of `paginated`. What `paginated=true` buys you is the `data.page_info` block; without it a block with 400 steps returns its first 150 and looks complete. Always send paginated=true when you care about the whole list.

Each row in `data.shared_step_details` carries its own `id` — that integer is the `shared_step_detail_id` a referencing test-case step holds. Carry the row id, not its `order`, when you need to line up a test case's steps with this block.
Send these rows back verbatim (with their ids) when updating the block; the update replaces the whole array, so anything you did not read here is lost on the next write.
`test_case_count` and `step_count` appear only when the backing service returns them on this path — do not rely on them here. The shared-step listing always carries both.
A zero or non-numeric shared_step_id is rejected locally with 400 `{data:null, success:false, message:"Validation Error"}`; a block that does not exist returns 404 `{data:null, success:false}`.
`created_by`/`updated_by` are null when the original author is no longer a user in this workspace.
Requires tc_view.

capabilities.name: get_shared_steps_v1

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. A non-positive, non-numeric or array-valued `p` is rejected globally with 400 `{success:false, error:"Invalid Params"}`. There is no per_page here — the page size is whatever the backing service defaults to.

query.name: q[query]
query.description: Free-text match on the shared step TITLE only — it does not search step or result text. A bare scalar ``q` foo` is ignored rather than rejected, so the nested form is required.

query.name: q[tags]
query.description: Filter to shared steps carrying this tag. Match mode is fixed to 'any' server-side; a match_object you send is not read.

query.name: q[empty][system_fields][]
query.description: Find blocks with the named field empty. Only `tags` is honoured — any other field name is filtered out silently and the condition simply disappears.

query.name: folder_id
query.description: Restrict to one shared-field folder. Forwarded only when present.

query.name: include_sub_collections
query.description: Include blocks in sub-folders of folder_id. Only the literal string 'true' turns it on.

query.name: field_type
query.description: Shared-field type filter, shared with the shared-components listing. Leave unset for ordinary shared steps.

query.name: sort_by
query.description: Sort column, forwarded unchanged to the backing service, which owns the accepted set and the default.

query.name: pre_fetch
query.description: Inline the first row's step details under `pre_fetched_shared_step`. Only takes effect on page 1 and only for the first row — it is a UI optimisation, not a way to fetch details in bulk.

capabilities.intent: List a project's shared steps with how many steps each holds and how many test cases embed it — use this to find a shared_step_id and to size the blast radius before editing or deleting a block
guidance: `test_case_count` on each row is the number of test cases embedding that block. It is the number to read before any edit or delete, and this listing is the cheapest place to get it.
`step_count` is how many step rows the block holds; the rows themselves are not in this response — read the block by id for those.
Search is title-only via `q[query]`. Sending `q` as a bare string is silently ignored, so a search that returns everything usually means the parameter was flat instead of nested.
Page with `p`; there is no page-size parameter on this listing at all, so you cannot pull it in fewer, larger pages. Walk until `info.next` is null.

`created_by` and `updated_by` are resolved from BrowserStack user ids to `{id, full_name}` where that person still exists in this workspace, and come back **null** when they do not. A null author means a missing or removed user, not a missing field.
Requires tc_view.

capabilities.name: get_system_field_values_v1

query.name: q
query.description: Filter the options by display value (substring match).

query.name: p
query.description: Page number.

capabilities.intent: List the option ids and display names a project defines for one system field (priority, status, case type, automation state) — resolve these before writing any of them.
guidance: This is the lookup that makes writes correct: priority, status, case type and automation state are per-project configurable, and the bulk-edit paths require the NUMERIC id, not the display name.

The list is keyed by the field name you asked for, so the options are at `<field_name>.values`, not at a fixed key. Each entry is `{value: <numeric id>, name: <display name>}` — `value` is the id to send.
`field_name` is one of priority, status, case_type, automation_state, defects. Any other name is not rejected by the route; it resolves to nothing and you get an empty list back with `success: true`.
`q` filters the options by value text and `p` pages them — a project with many options needs paging, so check `info` rather than assuming one page is the whole vocabulary.
Custom fields are not here; this covers system fields only.

capabilities.name: get_template_v2

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Template id — a plain integer with no prefix. Discover it from the template list; a non-numeric value does not reach this endpoint at all.

capabilities.intent: Get one template in full, including every description, property and step field it carries — read this before editing a template so you can resend the complete field set.
guidance: This is the only read that returns the field layout; the list returns metadata and counts only.
The Review & Approve property fields (reviewers, review status) are filtered out of this response on this surface even when the template stores them. Do not conclude from a read that they are absent.
A field update replaces the whole section, so treat this response as the baseline: drop what you want gone, keep everything else, then send the full array back.
An unknown or out-of-workspace id comes back as a 404 saying the template was not found, not as an empty success.

capabilities.name: get_test_case_attachments_v1
capabilities.intent: List the files attached to one test case — id, filename, MIME type and size per file, so you can see what evidence is on the case and pick an id to remove

200.description: Attachments retrieved successfully

guidance: Metadata only: id, filename, content_type, byte_size. There is NO url and no download endpoint on this v1 surface — if you need to read the file, use the v2 attachment listing, which returns a readable URL per file.
`attachments` and `success` are at the top level; there is no `data` envelope here, even though the sibling delete on the same path wraps its payload in one.
Not paginated and not filterable — every attachment on the case comes back in one array.
`folder_id` is part of the route but is not used to locate the case; the lookup is by project and test case id, so a stale folder id after a move still resolves.
An empty array means the case has no attachments; it is not an error.

capabilities.name: get_test_case_by_integer_id_v1
capabilities.intent: Read one test case by its INTEGER id inside a folder — the v1 lookup, and the way to translate an integer id into the TC-NNN identifier the v2 surface needs.

200.description: Test case detail; data.test_case.identifier is the TC-NNN form.

404.description: No test case with that integer id in that folder (or not visible).

guidance: All three path segments are plain integers here, and the route only matches digits — a TC-NNN or PR-NNN identifier never reaches the API and 404s at the router.
The folder id must be the case's CURRENT folder. A correct case id under the wrong folder is a 404, not a redirect.

The case is at `data.test_case` — there is a `data` envelope on this v1 read. `data.test_case.identifier` is the TC-NNN form (or the workspace's third-party identifier when the workspace issues project-level ids); the field is called `name`, not `title`.
`estimate` always comes back null on every read path — the stored estimate, if any, is in `estimated_duration_seconds`.
This returns the case record only. For its linked runs, results and issue metadata use the detail read instead.

capabilities.name: get_test_case_count_trend_v1
capabilities.intent: Chart how the project's test case count grew month by month, broken down by case type — use this for 'how fast is the suite growing'
guidance: `data` is keyed BY CASE TYPE NAME, not by month — the keys are whatever case types this group has defined (including custom ones), so treat it as an open map and iterate it rather than looking up fixed names.
The monthly numbers sit one level deeper, under each entry's `graphData`, keyed by three-letter month abbreviation (Jan…Dec) for the trailing 12 months. `data.<Type>` itself is not the series.
Read `order` for the intended display sequence of those keys; object key order is not meaningful.
`Total` is a sibling key in the same map alongside the real case types (the CSV exporter special-cases it), so summing every key double-counts.

The filter trap: sending ANY q key without an explicit q[created_at] makes the handler default both created_at and closed_at to 'all_time', and the closed_at path rewrites 'all_time' to '1_year' — so filtering only by owner silently narrows the chart to the last 12 months. Sending no q at all applies no date bound. Always pass q[created_at] explicitly whenever you pass any other filter.
project_id is the INTEGER id; the route segment only matches digits (or the literal 'new'), so a PR-NNN identifier is a routing 404 that never reaches the API.
A project that exists but is not visible to this caller renders as 404 {success:false}, not 403 — 'no such project' and 'no access' are indistinguishable here.

query.name: q[created_at]

custom_fields comes back as [] (an empty array, not an object) when the plan has none.
parent_plan is present only on a sub-plan; on a top-level plan parent_plan_id is null and sub_plans_count tells you whether it has children.

Sub-plans and their runs are not embedded. Use the plan's test-runs listing (with include_sub_test_plan_runs) to see what is under it.

Exactly one scope. Both ids → 400 {success: false, message: 'Provide either test_plan_id or test_run_id, not both'}; neither → 400 {success: false, message: 'test_plan_id or test_run_id is required'}. Note the error key is `message`, not `error`.
The series is nested: read data.test_plans_execution_trend_graph. `data` is the report envelope and carries only the section that was requested.

The payload is unwrapped for you — where the upstream reply nests everything under `result`, that inner object is what lands in `data`.
