It also returns `issues` (defects linked to the run) and `test_result_issues` (defects linked to individual results), which the plain run read omits.
The run's `id` is the TR-NNN STRING; the integer is in `uuid`. Take `uuid` whenever a numeric run id leaves this read.
The run sits under `data.test_run` — with an underscore, inside a `data` envelope. The write endpoints on this entity use `data.testrun` instead, and the v2 run read has no `data` at all.
`trtc_folder_progress_enabled` is a group feature flag, and a lookup failure is reported as false — treat false as 'not available', not as a confirmed setting.
Needs the test-run view permission, with the automation variant demanded on automation runs.

capabilities.name: get_test_run_test_cases_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Run identifier in TR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to TR-\d+ — unlike the v1 run endpoints, a bare integer is NOT accepted here and returns a routing 404.

query.name: p
query.description: PAGE NUMBER, and the parameter really is named `p`. `page=2` is not read: you silently get page 1 again.

query.name: page_size
query.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 30 when omitted. Above 300 the request errors ('Page limit exceeds the maximum limit of 300'); with fetch_steps=true the ceiling drops to 30.

query.name: count
query.description: Alias for page_size and read first when both are sent. Same ceilings.

query.name: fetch_steps
query.description: Include each case's steps. Pass the literal string 'true'. Doing so lowers the maximum page size from 300 to 30.

query.name: minify
query.description: Compact row shape. Pass the literal string 'true'.

query.name: is_shared
query.description: Restrict to cases shared in from another project.

query.name: source_project_id
query.description: Numeric id of the origin project, to narrow shared cases to one source project.

query.name: include_subfolders
query.description: Make folder_id include all descendant folders.

query.name: match
query.description: Per-field operator, e.g. match[tags]=all&match[assignee]=none. Multi-value fields (tags) take all|any|none|only; single-value fields take only any|none — anything else is a 400. match[global]=all (default) ANDs the fields, match[global]=any ORs them. `only` needs a group entitlement, else 403.

query.name: latest_status
query.description: Comma-separated latest execution statuses (untested, passed, failed, retest, blocked, skipped, in_progress, plus any custom group status). Unknown values are a 400 listing what is valid.

query.name: assignee
query.description: Comma-separated assignee emails. Use match[assignee]=none for unassigned cases. An email that does not resolve in the group is a 400, never a silently ignored filter.

query.name: priority
query.description: Priority label, resolved to an id inside the group.

query.name: tags
query.description: Comma-separated tags. Combine with match[tags]=all|any|none|only.

query.name: folder_id
query.description: Folder id. Pair with include_subfolders=true to include descendants.

query.name: configuration
query.description: Configuration label, resolved to an id inside the group.

query.name: name
query.description: Substring match on the test case name.

query.name: identifier
query.description: Exact test case identifier, e.g. TC-42.

query.name: query
query.description: Free-text search across name and identifier.

query.name: test_case_status
query.description: Test case status label, resolved to an id inside the group.

query.name: test_case_owner
query.description: Comma-separated test case owner emails.

query.name: case_type
query.description: Category / type label, resolved to an id inside the group.

query.name: automation_status
query.description: Automation status label, resolved to an id inside the group.

query.name: created_by
query.description: Comma-separated creator emails.

query.name: updated_by
query.description: Comma-separated last-updater emails.

query.name: template
query.description: Template label, resolved to an id inside the group.

query.name: created_between
query.description: Two comma-separated dates (start,end) bounding creation time.

query.name: updated_between
query.description: Two comma-separated dates (start,end) bounding last-update time.

capabilities.intent: List the test cases inside a run with their latest result, assignee and configuration — the read to answer "what is still untested / failing in this run?"
guidance: Page with `p` (NOT `page`) and `page_size` (or `count`). The default page is 30 rows and the hard ceiling is 300; asking for more errors instead of clamping.
fetch_steps=true drops the ceiling to 30 rows per page, so a run of any size takes many more calls with steps on.
Deep paging is capped by rows, not pages: once p x page_size passes roughly 30,000 the call returns 429 'request_limit_exceeded'. Filter the run down rather than walking a huge run to the end.
Filters fail closed — an unknown status, an unresolvable email or an invalid match mode returns 400 listing the valid values, so a filtered read never quietly degrades into the whole run.

Rows are per case-and-configuration mapping: a case mapped to three configurations comes back as three rows, each with its own configuration_id and latest_status. configuration_id is null for cases with no configuration.
Use latest_result_id from a row when you need to fetch or amend that case's recorded result.

capabilities.name: get_test_run_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Run identifier in TR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to TR-\d+ — unlike the v1 run endpoints, a bare integer is NOT accepted here and returns a routing 404.

query.name: minify
query.description: Return the compact run payload (drops the heavier analytics/detail fields). Pass the literal string 'true'.

capabilities.intent: Look up one test run — its state, owner, tags, configurations, linked plan and per-status progress counts
guidance: The run comes back keyed by its TR-NNN string in `identifier`. There is NO `id` and NO `uuid` field on this v2 payload — the integer run id is not exposed here at all, so anything downstream that needs it has to come from a v1 read. Carry `identifier` forward; the other v2 run routes take the TR-NNN form.
Both ids are prefixed strings here (PR-1 / TR-14). The v2 route only matches PR-\d+ and TR-\d+, so the integer ids the v1 run capabilities take give a 404 on this path.
This returns the run header only — progress is aggregated counts. To see which cases are in the run, or their latest results, read the run's test cases instead.
403 means the caller lacks view permission for this run type (automation runs are gated separately from manual ones).
The run is at the top level of the response as `test_run`; there is no `data` envelope here. The v1 run endpoints wrap their payload in `data` — these v2 ones do not.

This payload is narrower than the v1 run reads. `owner`, `is_automation`, `is_dynamic`, `test_cases_count`, `overall_progress_by_status_id`, `environment`, `closed_at` and `closed_by` are v1-only — if you need any of them, read the run through v1 instead of assuming a missing key means an unset value.

capabilities.name: get_test_runs_form_fields_v1

query.name: all
query.description: Include the project's custom result fields as well as the defaults. PRESENCE-checked, not value-checked: `all=false` and `all=0` behave exactly like `all=true`. The only way to get the compact shape is to omit the parameter entirely.

capabilities.intent: Discover the fields available when recording a test RESULT in this project — the built-in status options and, on request, the project's custom result fields — so a result can be submitted with valid values
guidance: These are TEST RESULT fields, not test run fields — despite the path. Use them to build a valid result submission (status id, custom field ids and their allowed option values).
The response SHAPE changes with `all`: omit it and you get {success, default_fields} only; send it and `custom_fields` appears alongside. Code that reads custom_fields must send the parameter.

`default_fields` is an object keyed by field name (today just `status`), not an array. Each entry lists its allowed values with their numeric ids — those ids, not the display labels, are what result writes take.
The import-only pseudo-fields (owner_imported, owner_imported_email) are stripped from custom_fields, so a field visible in an exported CSV can be missing here.
The response is flat — {success, default_fields, custom_fields} with no `data` envelope.

capabilities.name: get_test_runs_selection

body.name: select_all
body.description: Select every case in the project. When false, `folders` decides the set.

body.name: unique_test_case_count
body.description: The caller's own count of the selection. Echoed through; it does not constrain the result.

body.name: folders
body.description: Map of folder id (as a STRING key) to that folder's selection: {test_case_select_all, selected_test_cases:[ids], deselected_test_cases:[ids]}. A folder with test_case_select_all takes the whole folder minus deselected_test_cases; otherwise only selected_test_cases counts.

body.name: show
body.description: `filtered` (the default, and what ANY value other than the literal 'all' means) returns only the cases matching both the selection and `q`. `all` returns the whole selection and adds a `selected` array naming which of those rows also match `q`.

body.name: q
body.description: Test-case filter/search object, intersected with the selection. Omit it to get the selection as-is. Free-text goes in as a search string matched against case name and identifier.

body.name: count
body.description: PAGE SIZE, despite the name — not a count to return. Defaults to 30 when absent or unparseable, and a value above 20000 is refused with a page-size error.

body.name: p
body.description: Page number.

body.name: shared_selection
body.description: Accepted by the parameter filter but NOT read by this action — cases shared in from other projects are not resolved here. Use the count endpoint if you need shared selections accounted for.

capabilities.intent: Resolve a folder/case selection into the actual list of test cases it covers — use it to preview or page through what a run create or edit would pull in before committing it
guidance: This returns TEST CASES, not test runs, despite sitting under the test-runs path and despite the older wording of its name. It is the preview step for a run's case selection.
`selection` is effectively mandatory: the backing service reads straight into it and a body without it fails rather than defaulting to everything.
Page size is the `count` field, not `per_page`, and it caps at 20000; leaving it out gives 30 rows, which is how a selection preview looks far smaller than the run it will create.
`selected` only appears when show='all'. In the default mode the rows already ARE the filtered set, so its absence is not a failure.
Folder ids are STRING keys in the `folders` map, while the case ids inside are integers. Mixing those up drops the folder silently.
shared_selection is ignored here. A selection that pulls cases from other projects will preview short.
The response is flat — {success, info, test_cases, selected} with no `data` envelope.
Needs the test-run write permission even though it only reads — a viewer-only role is 403'd.

capabilities.name: get_test_runs_v1

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. There is no page-size parameter: the page is fixed at 30 rows (5000 when filter_mapping is set).

query.name: ignore_run_type
query.description: Pass the literal string 'true' to stop the backing service filtering by run type, so manual and automation runs are listed together. Any other value, including boolean true in some encodings, leaves the default filtering in place.

query.name: include_test_plan
query.description: Pass the literal string 'true' to include each run's linked test plan on the row, so you can tell which runs are already attached to a plan without a second read.

query.name: filter_mapping
query.description: Pass the literal string 'true' for the lightweight picker shape: the page grows to 5000 rows, progress analytics are skipped, and every run is reduced to {id, identifier} ONLY. Every other field disappears — do not use it when you need run state, owner or counts.

capabilities.intent: List a project's active test runs with their progress counts, owner and linked plan — the starting point for finding a run to read, execute or report on
guidance: Closed runs are NOT in this list. A run count or an 'all our runs' answer built from this endpoint alone silently omits every finished cycle — read the closed-runs listing too.
Page size is fixed at 30 and there is no per_page; only `p` moves. The one exception is filter_mapping=true, which raises it to 5000 and strips every field but id and identifier.

Each run's `id` is the TR-NNN STRING, and the integer id is in `uuid`. Take `uuid` whenever a numeric run id leaves this read — passing the string into a test plan's run list reaches the backing service uncoerced and fails there.
The three boolean query params are compared against the literal string 'true'; anything else, including 1 or the word yes, is treated as not set.
The response is flat — {success, test_runs, info, count} with no `data` envelope. `count` is the project-wide per-state totals, not this page's size; the page's size is in `info`.
Per-run analytics can be suppressed for large groups, in which case the progress fields come back empty rather than absent — do not read a zeroed `overall_progress` as 'nothing was executed'.
To filter or search runs rather than page through them, use the project entity search with the test-runs entity; this endpoint takes no filter parameters.
Needs the test-run view permission, with the automation variant demanded for automation runs.

capabilities.name: import_dataset_c_s_v
capabilities.intent: Parse an uploaded CSV file into column headers and rows — NOT INVOKABLE from this profile: it takes a multipart file upload, and it does not create a dataset

200.description: Parsed CSV contents, wrapped in a `data` envelope (unlike every other dataset endpoint, which returns at the top level). Nothing was written.

headers.description: The CSV header row, in file order — the candidate column names.

rows.description: Data rows as header-keyed objects, not positional arrays — they are NOT in the shape the dataset create call expects.

400.description: {error:'No file uploaded'} — what every invocation from this profile returns, because no file part can be sent.

422.description: {success:false, error:...} — oversized file, non-.csv extension, blank headers, too many rows or columns, or malformed CSV. Also the Team Pro gate, which renders {success:false, message:'Feature not available'}.

guidance: QUARANTINE CANDIDATE — do not attempt to call this. The only input is a multipart/form-data file part; a byte stream has to cross the boundary and there is no way to declare it here, so this record has no parameter for the one input it needs and any invocation fails with 400 {error:'No file uploaded'}.

The name is misleading: this does not import anything. It validates and parses the CSV and returns the parsed headers and rows to the caller. Nothing is written — no dataset is created or modified by this call.

To get the same result without a file upload: parse the CSV yourself and call the dataset create capability with the header row as `variables` and the data rows as `rows`. That is what the UI does with this endpoint's output.

If it is ever reachable, the limits enforced are: .csv extension only, 50 MB max (the published spec's 10 MB is wrong), every header non-blank, and at most 40 columns / 100 rows for a standard group (100 / 200 for groups on the raised-limit flag). Failures come back as 422 {success:false, error:...}.
Still behind the Team Pro plan gate and the test-case write permission like the rest of the dataset family.

capabilities.name: list_activity_events_v1

query.name: project_id
query.description: Narrow the group-wide feed to one project. A query filter, not a path segment.

query.name: cursor
query.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page's pagination.next_cursor. There is no page number.

query.name: limit
query.description: Page size, forwarded to the backing service which owns the default and ceiling; the empty-starred short-circuit reports 50. Trust pagination.limit for what you actually got.

query.name: actor_id
query.description: Filter to one actor, as a BrowserStack user id (the same id events carry in actor_id).

query.name: starred_only
query.description: Send the literal string 'true' to restrict to the caller's starred projects. With none starred the response is {events: [], no_starred_projects: true} — that is 'nothing starred', not 'no activity'.

query.name: entity_type
query.description: Filter by subject entity type. An array parameter — repeat the key rather than sending a comma-joined string.

query.name: origin_channel
query.description: Restrict to events raised from the UI or from the API. Any other value is silently DROPPED rather than rejected, so a typo quietly widens the result instead of erroring.

capabilities.intent: Read the activity feed (audit trail) — CURSOR paged, 15-day window

200.description: A cursor page of activity events.

projects.description: Project id → metadata, for resolving event project references.

no_starred_projects.description: Present and true only when starred_only was set and the user has none starred.

guidance: Cursor paging only: follow pagination.next_cursor and stop when pagination.has_next_page is false. There is no page number and no total count, so you cannot state how many events exist or jump to a page.

The server clamps every query to the last 15 DAYS regardless of what you ask for. For anything older, say the history is not retrievable through the API and point at the Test Management UI — reporting 'no activity' for an older period is a false negative.

Group-wide, not project-scoped: `project_id` is a query filter, not a path segment. The response's `projects` map (project id to metadata) resolves the project each event refers to without a second read.

`starred_only` is compared against the literal string 'true'. When the caller has no starred projects the reply is {events: [], no_starred_projects: true} — that means 'nothing is starred', NOT 'no activity'. Check that flag before reporting emptiness.

Gated by a group feature flag. A 403 {success:false, error:'Activity feed is not enabled'} means the feed is off for the group, not that the caller lacks permission — say so rather than reporting no activity.

Every event is enriched with `actor_name`; an actor who cannot be resolved inside the caller's group renders as 'Unknown User' rather than being dropped, so an unfamiliar name is not necessarily a data gap.

`entity_type` is an array filter — repeat the key rather than sending a comma-joined string. `origin_channel` accepts only 'ui' or 'api'; any other value is dropped silently instead of erroring, which widens the result rather than narrowing it.
Read-only by design: activity rows are emitted as a side effect of other writes. There is no create, update or delete, so an audit entry cannot be edited or removed on request.

Per-project visibility is applied downstream — the feed is already scoped to projects the caller can access, so an empty page can mean 'no accessible projects had events' rather than 'nothing happened'.

capabilities.name: list_archived_test_plans_v1

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. A non-positive or non-numeric value is 400 {success: false, error: 'Invalid Params'}. Page size is fixed at 30; there is no per_page.

query.name: search
query.description: Free-text match on the archived plan's name or identifier.

query.name: plan_status
query.description: Status filter for the archived view, forwarded upstream as given (a comma-joined list such as 'new,started' is accepted). Unlike the active listing, an unrecognised value is not rejected here — it simply matches nothing.

query.name: sort_by
query.description: Sort order. Forwarded WITHOUT validation on this route (the active listing validates the same parameter), so a typo is passed upstream rather than returning a 400.

capabilities.intent: Page through the test plans that have been ARCHIVED in a project — the place to find a plan to restore; archived plans do not appear in the normal plan listing at all

404.description: Test-plan archiving is not enabled for this group: `{success: false, errors: "Feature not available"}`.

guidance: This is a fixed literal route on the plan collection — it takes no plan id. It is a different endpoint from the plan detail read that sits on the same path prefix.
Gated on the group archive flag: when it is off the call is 404 {success: false, errors: 'Feature not available'}, which means the feature is unavailable, not that nothing is archived.
Needs the test-plan DELETE permission, not view — a user who can list plans normally can still be 403'd here.
Archived SUB-plans are not listed; there is no include_sub_plans switch on this route. Only top-level archived plans come back.
Rows are serialized exactly like the active listing (same fields, plus record_status: 'archived'), so anything that consumes the normal plan list works unchanged here.
Page size is fixed at 30; page with `p` and stop using the `info` envelope. There is no `count` object on this response, unlike the active listing.
To put a plan back, pass its integer id to the bulk-retrieve capability.

capabilities.name: list_custom_field_dataset_options_v2

path_params.name: custom_fields_id
path_params.description: Numeric custom field id. Not validated by this handler; a wrong value surfaces as a bodyless 404.

path_params.name: dataset_id
path_params.description: Numeric dataset id. Not validated by this handler; a dataset belonging to another field returns the same bodyless 404.

capabilities.intent: List the option values a dataset offers, with the numeric option id each one carries — the ids you need to rename, re-default or delete an option
guidance: This is where option ids come from. The dataset read returns options only when asked and without a stable contract; this call always returns them with their ids.

Each row is {id, option_value, is_default, colour, parent_option_id}. When any row carries a parent_option_id the whole list is rebuilt as a tree and children appear under a `children` key on their parent instead of at the top level — a flat scan of `data` then misses them.
Exception: if every row in the page has a parent (a single level of a nested_dropdown read on its own), the tree build finds no root and falls back to returning the rows flat.

Paging is `p` only; the page size is fixed at 30 and `per_page` is ignored. `info` carries the page metadata. On a nested field the tree is built per page, so a parent and its children can land on different pages.
Neither path id is validated here, so a wrong field/dataset pair reaches storage and returns a bare 404 {success:false} with no message.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. The only pagination control — page size is fixed at 30 and `per_page` is ignored.

capabilities.name: list_datasets

query.name: q[name]
query.description: Partial, case-insensitive match on dataset name. Use this to find a dataset you only know by name.

query.name: q[uuid]
query.description: Exact match on dataset uuid.

query.name: sort_by
query.description: Sort order, forwarded unchanged to the backing store; the accepted values are not validated or enumerated here, and an unrecognised one is not rejected by this service. Omit it unless you know the store's vocabulary.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. Validated globally: a non-numeric or non-positive value is 400 {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'}; p=0 is treated as page 1. There is no page-size parameter — see max_page_size.

capabilities.intent: Find datasets in a project — browse them or look one up by name or uuid to get the uuid the other dataset calls need

200.description: A page of datasets, with paging metadata under `info`.

400.description: {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'} — a non-positive or non-numeric page value.

422.description: {success:false, message:'Feature not available'} — the group lacks the Team Pro plan.

guidance: Rows are the compact form: name, uuid, counts, tags, metadata, creator and timestamps — but NOT the columns or rows. Read a single dataset by uuid to get its contents.
Page size is fixed at 30 and cannot be requested; ask for successive `p` values and stop when `info.next` is null.
`test_cases_count` here is the cheapest way to tell whether a dataset is in use before deleting it.
A creator no longer in the group resolves to the placeholder {id:0, full_name:'Former User'} rather than null.
422 {message:'Feature not available'} means the group lacks the Team Pro plan — every dataset endpoint answers this way, and it is an entitlement answer, not a payload error.
`success`, `datasets` and `info` are all top level; there is no `data` envelope and no second nesting under `datasets`.

capabilities.name: list_duplicates_v1

query.name: page
query.description: Page number. `p` is accepted as an alias and `page` WINS if both are sent. Unlike `p`, `page` is NOT validated: a non-numeric value silently becomes 0 and is forwarded as page 0. Send a positive integer.

query.name: entity_type
query.description: Accepted and IGNORED — the handler never reads it. Every pair links test cases; there is no other entity type. Sending it changes nothing.

query.name: entity_id
query.description: Integer test-case id. Restricts the listing to pairs involving that case AND strips that case out of each returned pair, so each row's `test_cases` holds only the OTHER case. Use it to answer 'what is this test case a duplicate of'.

query.name: duplicates
query.description: Duplicate-type filter (`near` is a legacy alias for `semantic`). Forwarded verbatim to the backing store and not validated here, so an unrecognised value narrows to nothing rather than returning an error. Omit for both types.

query.name: owner
query.description: The 'My duplicates' tab. ANY non-empty value scopes the listing to pairs involving the CALLER's own test cases — the value itself is discarded, so this cannot select another user. Omit for all duplicates in the project.

capabilities.intent: List the AI-suggested duplicate test-case pairs awaiting review in a project, highest-confidence first — optionally only those involving one test case, or only the caller's own

200.description: Suggested duplicate pairs. This exact shape with an empty `duplicates` is also what comes back when the group lacks the dedupe feature flag, so an empty list is not evidence the project has none.

guidance: An empty list is ambiguous. When the group lacks the dedupe feature flag this returns 200 with exactly {success:true, duplicates:[], info:{count:0,total_pages:0}} — indistinguishable from a genuinely clean project. Read the dedupe status capability to tell 'feature off / never run' from 'nothing found'.
Only pairs still in `suggested` status appear. Once a pair is merged, archived or discarded it leaves this listing permanently; there is no filter to bring it back.

Page size is fixed at 10 and cannot be requested. Pairs are ordered by confidence (ai_score descending, then id descending), NOT by age — the oldest suggestion is not on page 1 and a bigger page cannot be asked for.

`info.count` can exceed the rows you actually receive: a pair whose test case cannot be resolved is dropped from the page after the count is taken. Do not derive page counts from row arithmetic; use `info.total_pages` / `info.next`.
Carry each row's `id` forward — that integer is the duplicate id the read, resolve and discard calls take.
`last_scan_time` at the top level is the project's last dedupe run, not a property of this page; it is fetched separately and can be null when no scan has completed.
Duplicate REVIEW is all that is exposed here. There is no way to create a suggestion or trigger a scan through this API.

capabilities.name: list_exploratory_session_defects

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. The only page parameter read on this path — `page` is ignored. A non-positive or non-numeric value is rejected as 400 {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'}.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Accepted but NOT honoured — the handler overwrites it with the fixed page size of 30.

capabilities.intent: List the defects and issues raised during an exploratory session — the external tracker tickets linked to the session and to its individual log entries — to review what the exploration found
guidance: This is the session-wide view: rows carry entity_type and entity_id, so the list can include both links made on the session itself and links made on individual log entries. Read entity_type to tell them apart; read a log's own `defects` if you only want that log's.

Rows are full issue-link records, not just {issue_id, issue_type}. Each also carries id, issue_status, priority, record_status, entity_type, entity_id, project_id, created_at, updated_at and a free-form metadata object (ticket url, title, category) — the fields a caller normally needs to render a defect.
Paging uses `p`, NOT `page`. A `p` that is not a positive integer is rejected globally as 400 {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'}.
`per_page` is accepted and ignored — the page size is fixed at 30. Walk `p` until a page comes back short.
There are no filters on this endpoint: no status, tracker or date narrowing. Filter client-side.
Defect links written by the session or log write calls are applied asynchronously, so a defect linked a moment ago may not be here yet — retry rather than concluding the link failed.
Everything is at the top level: defects, info. There is no `data` envelope.
An unknown session_id returns a bare {success:false} with 404 and no message.

capabilities.name: list_exploratory_session_logs

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. The only page parameter read on this path — `page` is ignored. A non-positive or non-numeric value is rejected as 400 {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'}.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Accepted but NOT honoured — the handler overwrites it with the fixed page size of 50.

query.name: q[status]
query.description: Comma-separated list of statuses as a single string (e.g. 'retest,block') — not a repeated array parameter. Every value is allowlisted before the upstream call; anything else, or an empty list, returns 400 'Invalid status value.'. Does not affect status_counts.

capabilities.intent: Read the observations recorded during an exploratory session — the timestamped notes, their pass/fail/bug status, elapsed time, linked defects and embedded screenshots — optionally narrowed to particular statuses
guidance: Logs are children of one session: session_id in the path scopes the whole listing, and a log id is only meaningful together with the session it belongs to.
Paging uses `p`, NOT `page` — `page` is read by nothing here. A `p` that is not a positive integer is rejected globally as 400 {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'}.

`per_page` is accepted and ignored: the handler overwrites it with the fixed page size of 50. Walk `p` until a page comes back short. Compare against session_log_count on the session to know when you have them all.

q[status] is a COMMA-SEPARATED STRING, not an array, and it is allowlisted before the upstream call: any value outside pass, fail, bug, retest, block, note, skipped returns 400 'Invalid status value.'. Note `skipped` — it is a real status that older documentation of this entity omits.

status_counts is meant to be the whole-session per-status totals, deliberately unfiltered by q[status]. Do not rely on it today: the typed upstream response object carries no such field, so this key is currently rendered as an empty object on every call.

There is no sort parameter on this endpoint and the upstream default is not ascending — the internal session-copy path has to ask for ascending order explicitly. Sort by created_at yourself rather than assuming chronological order.

`content` is sanitised HTML, not plain text, and embedded images are TM-hosted attachment URLs. What is stored can differ from what was written: links and images pointing outside the project or group are stripped on write.
Each log's `defects` are the issue links on that log. The session-level defects listing is a different, broader set — read that one for everything linked to the session.
Everything is at the top level: session_logs, info, status_counts. There is no `data` envelope.

capabilities.name: list_exploratory_sessions

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. This is the only page parameter read on this path — `page` is ignored. A non-positive or non-numeric value is rejected as 400 {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'}.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Accepted but NOT honoured — the handler overwrites it with the fixed page size of 30. There is no way to widen the page from the caller side.

query.name: q[session_state]
query.description: Lifecycle state. Defaults to 'active' when omitted, so closed sessions are invisible unless you ask for them. Not validated locally — an unrecognised value is forwarded upstream rather than rejected.

query.name: q[assignee]
query.description: TCM user id of the session assignee; translated to a BrowserStack user id before the query is sent. Wins over q[owner] when both are given. An id that resolves to no user is sent as null instead of erroring.

query.name: q[owner]
query.description: Alias for q[assignee], used only when q[assignee] is absent. Same TCM user id semantics.

query.name: q[created_by]
query.description: TCM user id of the session creator; translated to a BrowserStack user id. An unresolvable id is sent as null rather than rejected.

query.name: q[created_at_from]
query.description: Created on or after this date. Forwarded verbatim — not parsed or validated here.

query.name: q[created_at_to]
query.description: Created on or before this date. Forwarded verbatim — not parsed or validated here.

query.name: q[tags][]
query.description: Tag names to match. Forwarded verbatim.

query.name: q[configuration_ids][]
query.description: Configuration ids (integers) the session runs against.

query.name: q[search]
query.description: Free-text match, forwarded upstream as-is.

query.name: q[query]
query.description: Second free-text key the handler forwards alongside q[search]; both are passed through independently. Undocumented upstream — prefer q[search].

query.name: q[status]
query.description: Filter by the log statuses recorded inside the session. Forwarded verbatim and not allowlisted here, unlike the same-named filter on the session logs listing.

query.name: q[test_plan_id]
query.description: Only sessions linked to this test plan. Takes the integer test plan id, not a TP-NNN identifier.

query.name: sort_by
query.description: Combined field+direction token. There is no separate sort_order parameter. Any other value is rejected with 400 'Invalid sort_by value.' before the upstream call.

capabilities.intent: Find exploratory testing sessions in a project — filter by state, assignee, creator, tags, configurations, linked test plan, date range or free text — to pick the session whose logs or defects you want to read next
guidance: The default listing hides closed work: when q[session_state] is omitted the handler substitutes 'active'. Pass q[session_state]=closed explicitly to find a finished session, and expect a session to vanish from the default list the moment it is closed.

Paging is driven by `p`, NOT `page`. `page` is read by nothing on this path. A `p` that is not a positive integer is rejected globally as 400 {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'} before the action runs.
`per_page` is accepted and ignored — the handler overwrites it with the fixed limit of 30 rows. There is no way to ask for a larger page; walk `p` until a page comes back short.

q[assignee] / q[owner] / q[created_by] take TCM user ids (integers) and are translated to BrowserStack user ids before the query is sent. q[owner] is only a fallback for q[assignee] — if both are present, q[assignee] wins. An id that matches no user in this group is not an error: the filter is sent as null and you get back a result set that silently does not mean what you asked for.
sort_by is a single combined token ('id-asc', 'id-desc', 'title-asc', 'title-desc') — there is no separate sort_order. Anything else is 400 'Invalid sort_by value.'.
`count` is an OBJECT of per-state totals ({active, closed}), not the number of rows matching your filter. The row total lives in info.count. Do not use `count` to size a pagination loop.

Rows are NOT put through the custom-field normaliser that the single-session read applies, so custom_fields on a list row is the raw upstream shape (or absent). Re-read the session by id if you need normalised custom fields.

assignee / created_by / closed_by come back as user objects resolved from the local user table, and resolve to null when the underlying user is not a TM user in this group — a null assignee here does not prove the session is unassigned.

Take `id` (integer) from a row and carry it as session_id into the logs, defects, close, clone, update and delete calls. `identifier` (ES-NNN) is display-only and is not accepted by any route on this entity.
Everything is at the top level: exploratory_sessions, info, count. There is no `data` envelope.

capabilities.name: list_filters

query.name: entity
query.description: Optional, despite being published as required: omit it and every entity type comes back in one mixed list (read `entity_type` on each row to tell them apart). An unlisted value is rejected with 422 `{success:false, message:"Invalid payload"}` — 422 here, not 400.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. This is the only page parameter the handler reads — a `page` query parameter is ignored and you silently get page 1. A non-positive, non-numeric or array-valued `p` is rejected globally with 400 `{success:false, error:"Invalid Params"}`.

capabilities.intent: List the saved filter views available in a project — yours and the project-wide ones — to find the filter_id to read, apply, update or delete
guidance: Page with `p`. The previously published `page` parameter is never read — sending it returns page 1 and looks like a successful call.
Page size is fixed at 30 and cannot be changed; there is no per_page or limit here. Walk pages until `info.next` is null.
The list mixes your private views with the project-level ones; `is_project_level` on each row is the only thing that distinguishes them, and `owner` is who created it.
An invalid `entity` returns 422, not the 400 the other filter endpoints use for validation failures.
Unlike reading a single filter, this listing does no custom-field validation and never rewrites anything — use it when you want to inspect filters without altering them.
Not permission-gated — the filter controller has no RBAC entry.

capabilities.name: list_folder_contents
capabilities.intent: Open one folder — its immediate subfolders, the folder's own record, and optionally its ancestor breadcrumb — to walk the tree a level at a time or work out where a folder sits

query.name: p
query.description: Page number over the SUBFOLDERS. A non-positive or non-numeric value returns 400 {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'}.

query.name: detail
query.description: Send the literal string "true" to populate `ancestors` with the folder's breadcrumb up to the root. Without it `ancestors` comes back null. Only the exact string "true" enables it.

query.name: nested_sub_folders
query.description: Literal string "true" asks for the whole descendant subtree rather than one level. It is additionally gated on a group flag, so it silently does nothing when the group is not enabled. When it does take effect, `self.contents` is stripped from the response.

query.name: case_count
query.description: Literal string "true" to include per-folder test-case counts. Read only on the nested_sub_folders path; ignored on a plain one-level listing.

query.name: total_count
query.description: Literal string "true" to include the total row count. Read only on the nested_sub_folders path; ignored on a plain one-level listing.

query.name: folder_sort_by
query.description: Subfolder ordering. Comma-separated combinations accepted; anything else returns 400 {error:'Invalid folder_sort_by parameter'}. Either name- sort gains a secondary created_at-asc tiebreak.

guidance: Page size is fixed at 300 subfolders and cannot be changed: `per_page` from the caller is discarded and the ceiling is applied unconditionally. Only `p` moves you through the pages. (A group-level flag can lift the limit to unbounded, which you cannot detect from the response.)
`test_cases` is ALWAYS null. The key exists but this endpoint never returns test cases — fetch them from the folder's test-case listing instead.
`folders` holds the immediate children only. The folder you asked for is at `self`, its parent id is duplicated at the top level as `parent_id`, and `ancestors` is null unless you passed detail=true.
Folder notes come back HTML-escaped with signed image URLs injected, at every level of the response — do not treat them as the literal text that was stored.
folder_id must be a positive integer; literal 0 raises an unhandled ArgumentError and comes back as a 500. A folder id from another project is a bare 404 {success:false} with no message.
This action has no RBAC entry, so it is not permission-gated the way the other folder reads are; it is also the action reachable through a public share link, scoped to the shared folder.

capabilities.name: list_folder_test_cases_v1

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. Walk pages until `info.next` is null.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Rows per page. Bounded to 1..100; anything outside that range, or non-numeric, silently falls back to the default of 30.

query.name: required[fields]
query.description: Comma-separated extra columns to join into each row (e.g. `owner,priority`). If you also send `sort_by`, the sorted column MUST appear in this list or the call is rejected with 'Sort by column X is not present in required fields'.

query.name: required[custom_fields]
query.description: Comma-separated custom field ids to include on each row.

query.name: sort_by
query.description: Sort token, `<column>-ASC|DESC` or `cf#<id>#<type>-<dir>`. A malformed token is a 400 listing the allowed columns. `case_type` is translated to `category` for you.

query.name: include_subfolders_tc
query.description: Send the string `true` to include cases from this folder's subfolders, and add a `folders` block to the response.

query.name: shared
query.description: Scope the listing to cases shared in from other projects.

query.name: for_test_run
query.description: Send the string `true` when building an 'add cases to run' picker: on a project with review gating configured it hides cases whose review status makes them ineligible, so the same folder returns FEWER rows than a plain read.

query.name: hasDuplicates
query.description: When true, fills `duplicates_tc_count` on each row from the dedupe store; otherwise it is null.

capabilities.intent: List the test cases in one folder — the repository browser read, with optional extra columns and custom fields.
guidance: Folder-scoped and non-recursive by default: pass `include_subfolders_tc=true` to reach cases in child folders. To read the whole project use the project-level listing with all_folders=true instead.
`per_page` is clamped to 1..100 and silently falls back to 30 for anything else — so trust `info.page_size`, not your request. Walk `p` until `info.next` is null.
Combining `sort_by` with `required[fields]` has a trap: the sorted column must be inside `required[fields]` or the call is rejected outright.
`for_test_run=true` deliberately returns FEWER rows on a review-gated project — do not use it for a plain repository read or you will under-report the folder.
A backend 404 is swallowed into an empty list with `success: true`, so an empty result is not proof the folder is empty or that the id is right.
Each row's `id` is the integer id the v1 write paths take and `identifier` is the TC-NNN the v2 surface takes; `estimate` is always null.

capabilities.name: list_projects_v1

query.name: q
query.description: Free-text match on project name. Must be a flat string — a nested q[...] value returns 400 'Invalid Params: q should be a String'.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. Non-positive, non-numeric or array values return 400 'Invalid Params'.

query.name: sort_by
query.description: Sort order. Any other value returns 400 echoing the allowed list.

query.name: starred
query.description: Restrict to starred projects. Forwarded to the backing service verbatim, so sending the string 'false' is still a filter, not 'no filter' — omit the key instead.

query.name: shared
query.description: Restrict to projects that have shared test cases. Any present value is treated as true; omit the key to not filter.

query.name: is_hidden_projects
query.description: Include projects hidden from the dashboard. Only the exact string 'true' turns this on.

capabilities.intent: List the group's projects with their PR-NNN identifiers, case/run counts and duplicate badge — the listing to use when you need each project's identifier; for a plain name lookup or a count, get_projects_basic_v1 is leaner

200.description: Projects at the top level as `projects` (no `data` envelope), with pagination under `info`. Each row also carries duplicates_tc_count; project_creator is NOT emitted despite being on the shared Project schema.

guidance: Page size is fixed at 30 on this route. There is no size parameter — `count` and `page_size` are ignored here (only the basic and minify project listings honour `count`). Walk pages with `p` and stop when `info.next` is null.

`q` must be a flat string on this route, not a nested object: `q=checkout`. Sending q[query]=... returns 400 'Invalid Params: q should be a String'. The nested q[query]/q[identifier] form belongs to get_projects_basic_v1.
`sort_by` is validated against a closed set; anything else returns 400 listing the allowed values. Omitting it leaves the backing service's default order.
Unlike the other project listings, each row carries `identifier` (PR-NNN) — this is the cheapest way to resolve project names to the v2 id form in bulk.

`duplicates_tc_count` is a decorative badge and is zero whenever the AI duplicate-detection feature is off for the group; a failure computing it is swallowed and also reads as 0, so never treat 0 as 'no duplicates'.
`project_creator` is documented on the shared Project schema but is NOT emitted by this endpoint — it is commented out in the serializer. Do not branch on it.
`starred` and `shared` are forwarded to the backing service verbatim, including the string 'false', so send them only when you mean to filter.
Requires the project_view permission under RBAC.

capabilities.name: list_schedules

query.name: q[query]
query.description: Case-insensitive substring search over report type, title and owner full name. Also enables the `owner_id` and `created_between` filters, which are ignored without it.

query.name: q[scheduled]
query.description: Only the exact string `true` filters (to scheduled reports). `false` and every other value are ignored and return all reports.

query.name: owner_id
query.description: Restrict to one owner. Only honoured alongside `q[query]`; supplying it also drops the owner name from the search match.

query.name: created_between
query.description: Two timestamps, [from, to], bounding created_at. Only honoured alongside `q[query]`, and only when exactly two entries are given — otherwise ignored.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Accepted and then IGNORED — the page size is fixed at 30 on both code paths.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number, 30 per page. A page past the last one returns 400 `page_out_of_bounds`, not an empty list.

capabilities.intent: List a project's reports — scheduled and unscheduled alike, with type, window, cadence and owner — the way to find a report_id

200.description: A successful response containing a list of schedules.

guidance: This is the discovery call for the report entity: every other report capability needs an integer `report_id`, and this is where it comes from (`data[].id`; `identifier` is the SC-NNN display string and is not accepted as an id anywhere).

It lists ALL of the project's reports, not only scheduled ones — the route name is misleading. `scheduled_report_count` and `total_report_count` are counts over the whole project, not over the returned page.

`q[scheduled]` only acts on the exact string `true`. `q[scheduled]=false` is silently ignored and returns everything, so you cannot filter for unscheduled reports — filter client-side on `frequency == null` instead.

Page size is a hard-coded 30 and cannot be changed: `per_page` is read from the request and then never applied. Page with `p`; requesting a page past the end returns 400 `page_out_of_bounds` rather than an empty list.
Ordering is always newest first by id. An `order_by` parameter is parsed and then ignored.

`q[query]` is a case-insensitive substring match over report type, title, and (unless `owner_id` is also given) the owner's full name. Supplying it switches to a different code path that additionally honours `owner_id` and `created_between` — those two do nothing without `q[query]`.
Requires the report_view permission on the project (403 otherwise).

capabilities.name: list_templates_v2

query.name: name
query.description: Narrow the list to templates whose name contains this value. It is a substring filter, not an exact lookup, so it can return several templates or none.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. This is the page parameter for this endpoint — `page` is ignored. A value that is not a positive integer is rejected with a 400 before the search runs.

query.name: count
query.description: Page size. This is the size parameter for this endpoint — `per_page` is ignored. Above 300 the request is REJECTED with a 400, it is not clamped. A non-numeric value silently falls back to 30.

capabilities.intent: List the workspace's test-case templates — start here to find a template's id before creating a test case from it or before editing the template itself.
guidance: Asking for more than 300 per page fails the whole call with a 400 rather than returning a clamped page; page through at 300 or below instead.
List items carry only template metadata and counts — no field detail. Read a single template when you need its description or property fields.
Only test-case templates are returned. The entity type is fixed server-side and cannot be widened from the request, so result/plan/exploratory-session templates are not reachable here.
project_count and the field counts can come back null: on some workspaces the expensive per-project count is skipped server-side. Treat a null count as 'not computed', not as zero.

capabilities.name: list_test_case_tags_v1

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. IGNORED whenever `q` is also sent: the search branch drops the pagination options entirely and always returns the first page. A non-positive or non-numeric value is rejected globally with 400 `{success:false, error:"Invalid Params"}`.

query.name: q
query.description: Free-text match on tag name. Trimmed; an all-whitespace value is treated as absent. Sending it silently disables paging (see `p`).

capabilities.intent: List a project's test-case tag vocabulary with usage counts — the set of tag names to pick from when tagging a case or filtering a list by tag
guidance: `tags` is a plain array of tag NAMES; `tag_objects` carries the same tags with `created_at` and `usage_count`. Tags are referenced by name everywhere else in this product, so `tags` is usually the field you want and `usage_count` is what tells you which are actually in use.

Combining `q` with `p` does not work: when `q` is present the handler forwards only the query and never the page, so you always get page 1 and a second page request returns the same rows. To walk the whole vocabulary, page with `p` and no `q`; to search, accept the first page and narrow the query.
Page size is fixed at 30 and there is no per_page parameter.
This is the TEST-CASE tag vocabulary only. Run, plan and shared-step tags are separate vocabularies with separate listings, and a name existing here says nothing about the others.
No tag ids are returned here. If you need an id (the tag merge takes integer ids), use the group-level tag search.
Not permission-gated — the tags controller has no RBAC entry.

capabilities.name: list_test_case_templates_v2

query.name: entity_type
query.description: Which kind of template to list. Effectively required — omitting it errors rather than defaulting. Only these two values are accepted; TestPlan and ExploratorySession templates are not listable here.

query.name: project
query.description: Integer project id — restricts the list to templates linked to that project.

query.name: name
query.description: Fuzzy match on template name (not an exact match).

query.name: paginated
query.description: Must be the literal string 'true' to turn paging on. Without it `p` is ignored, every matching template is returned in one array, and `info` is absent from the response.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. Only read when paginated=true is also sent; page size is then fixed at 10.

capabilities.intent: List the workspace's test-case (or test-result) templates with their ids — the lookup to run before creating a case from a template or editing a template's field layout

200.description: `{success, templates: [{id, name, entity, enabled, step_type, is_default, is_system, future_projects_applicable, field_count, linked_to_all_projects, project_count, created_at, updated_at}]}`. `info` is present only when paginated=true was sent.

guidance: `entity_type` is effectively REQUIRED even though it reads as optional: it is forwarded straight to the backing client, which refuses a missing value outright rather than defaulting to TestCase. Always send it.

Only two values are accepted: `TestCase` and `TestRunResult`. `TestResult` is not the accepted spelling, and TestPlan / ExploratorySession templates cannot be listed from here at all — anything outside the pair errors rather than returning an empty list.

Paging is opt-in and easy to miss: `p` is IGNORED unless `paginated=true` is sent alongside it. With paging on, page size is fixed at 10 and `info` appears in the response; with it off you get every matching template in one array and no `info`.
`project` narrows to templates linked to that integer project id; `name` is a fuzzy match on the template name, not an exact one.

Rows are the summary shape — id, name, entity, step_type, is_system, is_default, enabled, project_count, field_count, linked_to_all_projects. The field layout itself is not here; read a single template for that.
Templates belong to the workspace, not to a project: the same id is valid in every linked project, so do not look for a per-project id.
Responses are served from a short-lived per-group cache, so a template created or edited through a different surface can take a moment to show up here.
A validation failure from the backing service is passed through raw at its original status rather than being reshaped into the usual {success:false} envelope.

capabilities.name: list_test_plans_v1

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. A non-positive or non-numeric value is 400 {success: false, error: 'Invalid Params'}. There is no per_page — the page size is fixed at 30.

query.name: include_sub_plans
query.description: Include sub-plans in the page. Off by default, so a sub-plan the user named looks missing until this is set. Pass the literal string 'true'.

query.name: status
query.description: Plan status filter. Anything outside the three values returns HTTP 200 carrying {success: false, error: 'Check query params for test plan status'} and NO plans — it does not 400.

query.name: sort_by
query.description: Sort order. Validated: anything else is 400 with the allowed list in the message. Must be a string — an array form is 400 'Invalid Params: sort_by should be a String'.

query.name: minify
query.description: Ask for the slim plan rows. A group-level flag can force this on regardless of what you send, so rows may be slimmer than requested.

query.name: q
query.description: Filter object (must be a nested object, not a string, or the call is 400). Recognised keys include query (free text), tags, ids, parent_plan_id, owner, team, created_at / created_between, days_left, overdue_days, tp_custom_fields, issue_type + issue_ids (both needed together), and match. Keys outside that set are ignored silently.

query.name: ignore_type
query.description: Drop the implicit plan_status narrowing that the filter path otherwise applies (active plans unless status=completed). Pass the literal string 'true'.

query.name: filter_details
query.description: Add a filter_details object resolving the owner and custom-field filters you sent in `q` back into displayable values. Only populated for q.owner and q.tp_custom_fields.

query.name: filter_mapping
query.description: Id-picker mode: raises the page size to 5000 but returns ONLY {id, identifier} per plan — no name, no status, no dates. Do not use it to read plan detail.

capabilities.intent: Page through a project's test plans — filter by status, search and sort, and optionally include sub-plans; this is how you resolve a plan name a user mentioned to the integer id every other v1 plan route needs
guidance: Sub-plans are hidden by default. Without include_sub_plans=true you see only top-level plans, so a sub-plan the user named will look missing.
An invalid `status` is a 200 trap: the response is HTTP 200 with {success: false, error: 'Check query params for test plan status'} and no plans. Branch on `success`, not on the status code.

Page size is fixed at 30 and there is no per_page parameter. Page with `p` and stop using the `info` envelope. filter_mapping=true is the only way to get more rows and it strips every row down to {id, identifier}.
`count` is {active, completed} for the whole project (active = every plan not completed), not for the current page — do not use it as a page total.
Each row carries both ids: `id` is the integer every v1 plan route takes, `identifier` is the TP-NNN / STP-NNN for display. Carry the integer forward.

Rows are full plan objects, same serializer as the single-plan read, unless a minify/skip-analytics path trims them — a group-level flag can turn that on without you asking, so check for the fields you need rather than assuming.

`q` must be sent as a nested object; a scalar q is 400 'Invalid Params: q should be a ActionController::Parameters'. Custom-field filters inside q.tp_custom_fields are validated and a bad field id fails the whole request.
Archived plans are NOT in this listing under any filter — they have their own archived listing.
Needs the test-plan VIEW permission.

capabilities.name: list_workspace_fields_v2

query.name: entity_type
query.description: Which entity's fields to list. Any other value is a 400 'Invalid Params'. TestCaseStep returns an empty list when the group's step-custom-fields flag is off.

query.name: field_source
query.description: Case-insensitive. `system` returns every system field on a single page (total_pages 1) and no custom fields; `custom` skips the system fields entirely. Anything else is a 400 naming the valid values.

query.name: field_type
query.description: Filter custom fields by data type, using the canonical vocabulary (string, text, user, dropdown, multi_dropdown, url, boolean, int, date, nested_dropdown). System fields all report as `dropdown`, so any other value silently excludes every one of them.

query.name: q
query.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the field name. Applied to system fields in this layer and forwarded as a search for custom fields.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. The only pagination control — page size is fixed at 10 and cannot be raised. Must be a scalar; `p[]=1` is a 400.

query.name: sort_by
query.description: Sort column. Also accepts a combined `<column>-<direction>` form, e.g. `name-desc`, in which case sort_order is ignored. `name` is an alias for field_name. Any unrecognised column falls back to sorting by id.

query.name: sort_order
query.description: Direction, used only when sort_by does not already carry one. Compared case-insensitively; anything that is not `desc` sorts ascending.

query.name: selected_ids
query.description: Custom field ids to EXCLUDE from the custom-field half of the result. Has no effect on the system fields injected on page 1.

capabilities.intent: Browse or search every field configured for the workspace — built-in system fields and user-defined custom fields together — to find a field's numeric id, type and how many projects it reaches
guidance: Start here. This is the only listing that returns both system and custom fields, and the numeric `id` it gives is what every other custom-field call takes in its path.
The page size is fixed at 10 and there is no way to raise it: only `p` is read. Expect to page. `info` carries {count, page, page_size, total_pages}.

System fields are injected on page 1 ONLY, ahead of the custom fields, and they eat into that page's 10 slots. Page 2 onward is custom fields only. Row order is therefore not stable across pages unless you also send sort_by.

Every system field is reported as field_type `dropdown`, so a field_type filter with any other value silently drops all of them. Set field_source=custom when you only want user-defined fields, or field_source=system to get them all on one page.

An unsupported field_source is a 400 naming the three valid values; an unsupported entity_type is a 400 'Invalid Params'. entity_type=TestCaseStep returns an empty list (not an error) when the group lacks the step-custom-fields flag.

sort_by also accepts a combined form like `name-desc`; `name` is an alias for field_name. Sorting is applied in this layer AFTER the system fields are merged in, so it reorders only the rows on the page you asked for.
`q` matches on field name only, case-insensitively, and is applied to both system and custom fields.
Rows carry `dataset_count` and a derived `linked_to_all_projects`, but no option values and no project list — read the field, then its datasets, for those.

capabilities.name: merge_tags_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Needed to match the route, and nothing else — it is never sent to the backing service. The merge is NOT scoped to this project; it applies across the whole workspace.

body.name: source_id
body.description: The tag that LOSES. It is absorbed into the target and ceases to exist; every entity carrying it is re-pointed at the target tag. Integer id — the project tag listings return names only, so resolve the id from the group tag search first.

body.name: target_id
body.description: The tag that SURVIVES. It keeps its own name and picks up all of the source tag's usages. Nothing about the target's name or metadata changes.

body.name: entity_type
body.description: Which tag vocabulary the two ids belong to. NOT validated here — only checked for presence — so an unknown or mismatched value is forwarded and comes back as an opaque 400 from the backing service.

capabilities.intent: Merge one tag into another — everything tagged with the source tag ends up carrying the target tag instead, and the source tag stops existing

200.description: The backing service's merge result, passed through unchanged. No `success` flag and no envelope are added by this API; the exact keys are owned by the tag service.

400.description: Missing source_id/target_id/entity_type, or any failure reported by the backing service (including an unknown tag id), as `{error: "<message>"}`.

403.description: Production only: caller is not an owner or admin — `{error: "Only admins can manage tags"}`.

guidance: Which tag loses: `source_id`. After the merge the source tag no longer exists as a tag, and every test case, run, plan or shared step that carried it carries the target's tag instead. `target_id` is unchanged apart from gaining those usages. Getting the two the wrong way round destroys the tag you meant to keep.

There is no unmerge. The response does not list what was re-tagged, so nothing here tells you which entities to fix afterwards — capture the source tag's usage list (search by that tag) BEFORE calling, or the mapping is unrecoverable.

Not project-scoped despite the path: `project_id` is used for routing only and never reaches the backing service, so the merge applies across the entire workspace and can touch projects you were not looking at.
Both ids are integers. Every project-level tag read in this profile returns names rather than ids — resolve the ids through the group-level tag search, and never send a tag name here.
`entity_type` must match the vocabulary both tags live in. It is not validated locally, so a mismatch is not caught until the backing service rejects it.
The admin gate only bites in production: outside production the owner/admin role check is skipped entirely and any role can merge tags. Do not rely on it as a safety net when testing.

Every downstream failure — unknown tag id, mismatched entity_type, permission problem — is flattened to 400 `{error: "<message>"}`. There is no 404 and no `success` flag; the message text is the only signal.
On success the body is the backing service's raw merge result passed straight through, with no envelope added by this API.

capabilities.name: move_folder_v1

body.name: new_base_folder_id
body.description: Destination parent folder. NOT required despite what the name suggests: omit it or send null to move the folder to the project ROOT. It must exist in the destination project.

body.name: new_base_project_id
body.description: Destination project; omit for a same-project move. Send it as a JSON NUMBER — the cross-project test is a raw inequality against the integer project id, so the string "456" against project 456 is misread as a cross-project move and takes the slow async path with all its extra restrictions.

body.name: auto_rename
body.description: Defaults to TRUE here, unlike create and rename. A name clash in the destination is silently renamed rather than rejected; send false explicitly if you would rather the move fail.

body.name: prev
body.description: Optional: after the move, place the folder immediately after this sibling id. Must be an integer; sending prev or next triggers a second reorder call whose failure is not reported in this response.

body.name: next
body.description: Optional: after the move, place the folder immediately before this sibling id. Must be an integer.

capabilities.intent: Move a folder — with everything under it — to a different parent, to the project root, or into another project; same-project moves complete immediately, cross-project ones run in the background

200.description: Folder moved successfully

400.description: Invalid input or move not allowed

guidance: Two completely different responses come out of this one route. A same-project move is synchronous and returns {data:{folder, source_path_folders, destination_path_folders, success:true, async:false}}. A cross-project move returns only {data:{success:true, async:true, unique_id}} and has done nothing yet — branch on `data.async` before reading `data.folder`.

For the async path there is no HTTP status endpoint. `unique_id` is the X-Request-ID echoed back and progress goes over a websocket the API does not expose; confirm the move by re-reading the destination folder.
Omit new_base_folder_id to move to the project root. That is the only way to promote a nested folder to root level.

Moving a folder into one of its own descendants is NOT blocked. The only self-move check compares the folder id to the destination id, so a move into a child is accepted here (the copy endpoint does check for this — the move endpoint does not).

Cross-project moves carry two hard limits: the subtree may contain at most 50 folders counting all nesting, and the folder must contain no shared test cases at all. Either one fails the request with 422 {success:false, error:'...'} before anything moves.

The error shape varies by stage: local validation failures are 422 {success:false, error}, upstream rejections are 400 {success:false, error, message} (both keys, same text), and anything unexpected is 500 {success:false, error:'An unexpected error occurred. Please try again.'}.
`user_action` appears nowhere in the codebase — it is accepted and ignored. Do not build anything on it.
This action has no RBAC entry, so it is not permission-gated the way rename and reorder are.
A move is reversible by moving the folder back, but the async cross-project path recreates folders rather than relocating them, so ids on the far side are new.

capabilities.name: rename_folder_v1

body.name: name
body.description: New folder name. Must be wrapped in a `folder` object — the handler reads a required `folder` wrapper, so a flat body is a 400. Not strictly required: a notes-only edit is accepted, but the `folder` object itself must be present and non-empty.

body.name: notes
body.description: New description, HTML allowed; unescaped, sanitised and re-escaped server-side, so the stored value can differ from what you sent. The key is `notes` — `description` is silently dropped by the permit list on this v1 route.

body.name: auto_rename
body.description: Literal string "true" to auto-suffix a clashing sibling name instead of failing. Any other value, including the boolean true, reads as false.

body.name: attachments
body.description: Replaces the folder's attachment set with these blob ids. Sending the key at all switches the handler into attachment mode and re-reads the folder's relations; an invalid set returns 422 with the bare string "attachment is invalid".

capabilities.intent: Rename a folder or rewrite its notes — despite the name this is the general folder-edit call, and it changes whichever of the two fields you send
guidance: The body must be wrapped: {"folder": {"name": "..."}}. A flat body returns 400 for a missing `folder` you never sent, and an empty `folder` object does the same.

Sibling-name uniqueness is always checked. A clash relays the entity store's own message and status verbatim rather than the generic masked text most folder endpoints return — read `message` for the real reason. auto_rename:"true" turns the rejection into a silent rename.
There is no undo. Folders keep no version history, so an overwritten name or notes value is gone and the only way back is to send the old value again — capture it with a read first if it matters.
The updated folder is at `data.folder`. The `cases_count` and `sub_folders_count` in that echo are copied from the read taken BEFORE the update, not re-derived — do not treat them as fresh counts.
This endpoint does NOT return a request_trace_id, despite what the index previously claimed; the only keys are `data.folder` and `data.success`.
folder_id must be a positive integer; literal 0 raises an unhandled ArgumentError and comes back as a 500.
Requires the folder-edit permission.

capabilities.name: reorder_folders

body.name: current
body.description: The folder ids being repositioned. Must be a JSON array of NUMBERS — the check is a strict integer type test, so ["21"] or a form-encoded current[]=21 fails with 422 {success:false, message:'test_case_folders must be an array of integers.'}.

body.name: prev
body.description: Id of the sibling the moved folders should land AFTER. Integer or null only — a string is 422. Null means 'place at the top', but see next: prev and next cannot both be omitted.

body.name: next
body.description: Id of the sibling the moved folders should land BEFORE. Integer or null only. At least one of prev/next must be a real id.

capabilities.intent: Change the display order of sibling folders by dropping one or more of them between two named neighbours — ordering only, it never changes nesting

200.description: Folders reordered successfully

guidance: `current` alone is not enough, whatever the required flags say. Sending neither prev nor next fails with 422 {success:false, message:'Both top_folder_id and bottom_folder_id cannot be nil.'} — you must anchor the move against at least one neighbour.
Every id is type-checked as a Ruby Integer before anything is sent upstream. Numeric strings are rejected, so send a JSON body with real numbers rather than form-encoded parameters.
All the validation failures come back as 422, not 400, even though they are plainly bad-request conditions — the status the code intended is not the status that is sent.

The response is only {data:{success:true, message:'Folders reordered successfully'}}. It does not echo the new order and it does NOT contain a request_trace_id, despite what the index previously claimed. Re-read the folder listing to confirm the result.

Nothing about the ids is validated locally — existence, project ownership and sibling-ness are all the upstream service's problem, so a wrong-but-well-typed id can return success-shaped output without moving what you meant.
This reorders siblings within their existing parent. To change a folder's parent, use the move call instead.
Requires the folder-edit permission.

capabilities.name: reorder_test_cases_by_folder_v1

body.name: top_test_case
body.description: Integer id of the case the moved block should sit BELOW. Omit it to move the block to the top of the page.

body.name: bottom_test_case
body.description: Integer id of the case the moved block should sit ABOVE. Omit it to move the block to the bottom of the page.

body.name: page
body.description: Page of the folder listing the move happens on. Ordering is resolved against that page's window, so a neighbour that is not on this page cannot anchor the move.

body.name: test_cases
body.description: Integer ids of the cases to move, in the order they should end up in. These are moved as one block between `top_test_case` and `bottom_test_case`.

capabilities.intent: Change the manual order of test cases within a folder by dropping a block of them between two neighbours.

200.description: Test cases reordered successfully.

info.description: Additional metadata about the reorder operation.

guidance: The body is wrapped in `re_order`, NOT `test_case` like every other test-case write on this surface. A flat body, or a `test_case` wrapper, is a 400 before any field is read.

Position is expressed by NEIGHBOURS, not by index: `top_test_case` and `bottom_test_case` are the case ids the moved block lands between. Omit `top_test_case` for the top of the page, `bottom_test_case` for the bottom.
Everything is integer case ids — the anchors and the moved list alike. TC-NNN identifiers are not accepted here.
Ordering is resolved within the page named by `page`, so both anchors must be on that page of the folder listing for the move to mean what you intend.
A rejection comes back as 400 `{errors: "<message>"}` — not the usual `{success:false}` — and covers 'ids not in this folder' as well as malformed input.
The 200 body is the folder's listing in its NEW order, so you can confirm the result without a second read. Ordering is not versioned: the only way back is another reorder.

capabilities.name: replace_test_run_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Run identifier in TR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to TR-\d+ — unlike the v1 run endpoints, a bare integer is NOT accepted here and returns a routing 404.

body.name: name
body.description: Run name. Only applied when non-empty; sending an empty string leaves the existing name.

body.name: description
body.description: HTML is escaped and sanitised server-side, so the stored value can differ from what you sent.

body.name: assignee
body.description: Run owner, given as an email (or a TM user id). An address that does not resolve to a user in this group fails the whole request with 400 'invalid data' — it is not skipped.

body.name: tags
body.description: Plain tag strings; the list you send replaces the run's tags.

body.name: configurations
body.description: Configuration IDs (integers) the run executes against — not the configuration objects returned on read. Duplicates are collapsed.

body.name: issues
body.description: Linked defects. Each entry is an object; a bare string entry is coerced to {issue_id: ...} but loses the tracker type.

body.name: test_plan_id
body.description: Parent test plan to link. Send null or "" to unlink the current plan. Mutually exclusive with sub_test_plan_id.

body.name: sub_test_plan_id
body.description: Sub test plan to link. Send null or "" to unlink. Mutually exclusive with test_plan_id.

body.name: test_cases
body.description: Test case identifiers to ADD to the run. The write is a union: cases already in the run stay, and nothing listed elsewhere is removed.

body.name: include_all
body.description: Select every test case in the project. Overrides folder_ids and filter_test_cases when true.

body.name: folder_ids
body.description: Folder IDs whose cases are added to the run.

body.name: filter_test_cases
body.description: Filter criteria used to resolve cases, and the only place is_dynamic is read. is_dynamic:true needs at least one other key here or the call 400s; is_dynamic:false turns a dynamic run static. Omitting is_dynamic leaves the run's current dynamic flag alone.

body.name: configuration_map
body.description: Per-case configuration assignment overlay: each entry is {test_case_id: "TC-1" or ["TC-1","TC-2"], configuration_ids: [101,102]}. Unresolvable case or configuration IDs return 422. It is an overlay, not the case list — cases you list elsewhere are still included, with a null-configuration row.

body.name: filter_scope
body.description: Accepted by the parameter filter but NOT honoured on either update path — the selection is always built in global mode here. Only create reads it.

capabilities.intent: Rewrite a test run from a complete payload — every metadata field you leave out is reset, so the run ends up as whatever this one body says. Use the partial update instead when you only mean to change some fields.
