guidance: Two different operations share this path. This POST rebuilds the whole run payload; the PATCH applies only the keys you send. If you are renaming a run, closing it, or linking a plan, pick the PATCH.

Omission is destructive here: no run_state resets the run to new_run, no test_plan_id/sub_test_plan_id unlinks the plan it was under, and no issues clears its linked defects. Read the run first and re-send its current values for anything you do not mean to change.
An invalid run_state is not rejected on this call — it is silently coerced to new_run. The partial-update call on the same run returns 400 instead, so use that one if you want the error.
shared_test_cases and filter_scope are accepted by the parameter filter and then ignored on this path. Cross-project cases only land through the PATCH.
Case membership is union-only: test_cases / folder_ids / include_all ADD cases, and nothing here removes one. Use the bulk test-cases call to remove.
The body must be wrapped in a `test_run` object; without it the request 400s before any field is read.
400 'invalid data' also covers an assignee email that cannot be resolved in this group — the run is left untouched in that case.
There is no undo: test runs keep no version history, so a field this call clears cannot be restored.
The updated run comes back at the top level as `testrun` — one word, no underscore, and no `data` envelope.

capabilities.name: resolve_duplicate_v1

body.name: duplicate_id
body.description: The duplicate to resolve, from the `id` of a listing row. Passed in the BODY, not the path — this endpoint posts to the collection path, unlike discard which puts to the item path.

body.name: merge_action
body.description: Exactly `merge` or `archive`. There is no default and no fallback: any other value, including a missing one, is rejected with 400 {error:'Invalid action'} and nothing happens.

body.name: source_testcase_id
body.description: Required when merge_action is `merge`. The integer id of the case that will be archived and folded into the other. Must be one of the pair's two test cases.

body.name: target_testcase_id
body.description: Required when merge_action is `merge`. The integer id of the case that survives and receives the merge comment. Must be one of the pair's two test cases.

body.name: archive_testcase_id
body.description: Required when merge_action is `archive`, and ignored otherwise. The integer id of the single case to archive; must be one of the pair's two test cases. Without it the archive path fails with 'Test case not found in duplicates'.

capabilities.intent: Act on a duplicate suggestion — merge one test case into the other (archiving the source and commenting on the survivor), or archive one of the pair outright

200.description: Duplicate resolved. Body is {success:true} only — nothing about the affected test cases is returned.

400.description: {error:'Invalid action'} when merge_action is neither `merge` nor `archive`, or {errors:'Invalid Input'} when the backing store rejects the merge/archive.

403.description: The caller lacks the test-case delete permission (tc_delete).

404.description: {errors:'Duplicate not found.'} — no such pair in this project, or it is no longer in `suggested` status.

409.description: {errors:'Duplicate review is paused while this data is being migrated. Please try again shortly.'} — a dedupe data migration is in progress. Nothing was changed; retry later.

422.description: A test case id that is not part of this pair. Body is {errors:'Test case not found in duplicates'} on the merge path and {success:false, message:'Test case not found in duplicates'} on the archive path.

guidance: Two different operations behind one field. `merge` archives source_testcase_id, tags it 'Archived as Duplicate', posts a comment on target_testcase_id recording the merge, stores a snapshot of the source, and marks the pair merged. `archive` archives archive_testcase_id only — no comment, no snapshot — and still marks the pair merged.

Ids are not interchangeable: the SOURCE is the case that disappears. Getting source and target the wrong way round archives the case you meant to keep, and the only route back is unarchiving it manually.

Archived is not deleted — a merged-away or archived case is recoverable from the project's archived cases, findable by the 'Archived as Duplicate' tag on the merge path. Nothing here is a hard delete, but the merge comment, the snapshot and the pair's status change are not undone by unarchiving.
Resolving requires the test-case DELETE permission (tc_delete), not write. A caller who can edit test cases may still be refused here with 403.
The pair must still be `suggested`. An already-resolved pair is 404 {errors:'Duplicate not found.'}, which usually means someone else handled it, not that the id is wrong.

Undeclared until now, and retryable: while a dedupe data migration is in progress the call is refused with 409 {errors:'Duplicate review is paused while this data is being migrated. Please try again shortly.'}. It is deliberately not a 200 — nothing was merged. Retry later.

A test case id that is not part of the pair is rejected AFTER the pair lookup and reports 422, not 404, with two different bodies depending on the action: merge gives {errors:'Test case not found in duplicates'} and archive gives {success:false, message:'Test case not found in duplicates'}.

Success is just {success:true} — the affected test cases are not echoed back. Re-read the surviving case if you need its post-merge state, and note the pair leaves every duplicates listing at this point.

After a merge the source case's pre-merge contents are readable only through the merged pair's source-snapshot call. Keep the duplicate id if you might need it; it is no longer discoverable from any listing.

capabilities.name: restore_history_v1
capabilities.intent: Roll a test case back to an earlier revision — reapplies that snapshot's name, description, preconditions, steps, status, priority, owner, tags, defects, custom fields, attachments and reviewers to the live case

200.description: Restore applied. Body is only {success: true} — read the test case back to see the restored content.

422.description: Plan gate: not on an Enterprise or Team Pro plan ({success:false, message:'Not Allowed'}); or the entity type is not restorable ({success:false, message:'Not supported'} / 'Not supported for build').

guidance: Paid feature. Without an Enterprise or Team Pro plan this returns 422 {success:false, message:'Not Allowed'} and nothing is changed.
`history_id` is the numeric revision id from the listing, not the V1/V2 position label.

It is a full OVERWRITE of the snapshotted fields, not a merge. A custom field that has a value today but was empty in the snapshot is CLEARED. Steps are rewritten from the snapshot, so steps added since are removed, and steps whose ids no longer exist come back with new ids. The attachment set is rewritten too, unlinking files added after that revision.

There is a way back, but only one: the restore is applied as an ordinary edit of the live case, so the pre-restore state remains in the revision trail and can itself be restored. There is no undo call.
Say what will be lost before calling. The caller cannot see the delta from this endpoint — read the diff (or the two revisions) first and tell the user which fields will change.
Only test cases are restorable on this route; the same shape against another entity type answers 422 'Not supported'.

Success is only {success: true}. Read the case back to confirm what the restore actually produced — in particular, custom fields whose definition no longer exists in the project are not recreated and stay absent.

capabilities.name: search_duplicates_v1

body.name: q
body.description: Test-case filter object, the same grammar the test-case search takes; a pair matches when its test cases match. Sharp edges here: `owner`/`reviewers` take TM user ids and are translated server-side (an id resolving to nobody filters to nothing, never to everything); date filters must use `date_range` or the relative `created_at`/`updated_at` tokens, and `all_time` is dropped rather than applied.

fields.name: query
fields.description: Free-text match on test case title / identifier.

fields.name: folder_ids
fields.description: Folder ids, comma-separated string or array.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: TM user ids, comma-separated. Translated to backing-store ids before the search.

fields.name: reviewers
fields.description: TM user ids, comma-separated. Translated like owner.

fields.name: tags
fields.description: Tag names, comma-separated string or array.

fields.name: priority
fields.description: Priority option ids, not display labels.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Status option ids, not display labels.

fields.name: case_type
fields.description: Case-type option ids.

fields.name: automation_state
fields.description: Option ids, or the literals `automated` / `manual` which the server resolves.

fields.name: issue_ids
fields.description: Linked issue ids, comma-separated.

fields.name: custom_fields
fields.description: Keyed by custom-field id, e.g. {"179720": ["Yes"]}.

fields.name: match
fields.description: Per-field operator map (all / any / none). Values stay beside it under their own key — a value placed inside `match` applies no filter at all.

fields.name: empty
fields.description: Is-empty filter: {system_fields:[...], custom_fields:[...]}.

fields.name: date_range
fields.description: Absolute created-at range; takes precedence over created_at when both are sent.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: Relative token such as `7_day`. `all_time` is dropped, applying no bound.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.description: Relative token, same form as created_at. `all_time` is dropped.

body.name: match_scope
body.description: Whether ONE test case of a pair matching `q` is enough (`any`) or BOTH must match (`all`). Defaults to `any` — with `all` a filter that matches only one side returns nothing.

body.name: duplicates
body.description: Duplicate-type filter (`near` is a legacy alias for `semantic`). Forwarded verbatim and not validated here; an unrecognised value narrows to nothing.

body.name: owner
body.description: The 'My duplicates' tab. ANY non-empty value scopes results to the CALLER's own test cases; the value is discarded, so it cannot select another user. This is separate from the `owner` filter inside `q`, which does take user ids.

body.name: page
body.description: Page number. `p` is an accepted alias and only `p` is validated (a bad `p` is 400 {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'}); `page` wins when both are sent and a non-numeric `page` silently becomes 0.

body.name: filter_details
body.description: Send the literal string 'true' (with a non-empty `q`) to get a `filter_details` object back that resolves the filter's ids to display labels. Any other value, or a missing `q`, omits the key entirely.

capabilities.intent: Search the AI-suggested duplicate pairs with the full test-case filter grammar — narrow the review queue by folder, owner, tags, priority, status, custom fields or free text

200.description: Matching suggested duplicates, plus `filter_details` when it was requested. The same shape with an empty `duplicates` is returned when the dedupe feature flag is off.

400.description: {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'} — a non-positive or non-numeric `p`.

422.description: {success:false, message:...} — the backing store refused the filter combination (usually because it resolves to too many test cases). This is NOT 'no results'.

guidance: A POST, but a read — it changes nothing. It exists because the filter object is too long for a query string.

Same feature gate as the plain listing: with the dedupe flag off this returns 200 {success:true, duplicates:[], info:{count:0,total_pages:0}} and never reaches the filter. An empty result is not evidence that nothing matched.

'Nothing matched' and 'the filter could not be evaluated' are different answers. A filter the backing store refuses (typically one resolving to too many test case ids) comes back 422 {success:false, message:<the store's own limit message>}, not an empty list — do not treat that as zero results.
Page size is fixed at 10, ordering is by confidence (ai_score descending), and `info.count` can exceed the rows on the page because pairs with an unresolvable test case are dropped after counting.

Send only the filter keys you mean. `q` is forwarded to the search engine, which discards keys that would take it off the duplicate-pair scope, so an unexpected key fails silently rather than erroring.
Carry each row's `id` forward as the duplicate id for the read, resolve and discard calls.
Response adds two keys the plain listing has: `filter_details` (only when requested) and, as there, `last_scan_time` for the project's last dedupe run.

capabilities.name: search_group_tags

path_params.name: entity_type
path_params.description: Which tag vocabulary to search. Hyphens are normalised to underscores, so `test-case` and `test_case` both work. Not validated against a list here — an unrecognised value is forwarded to the backing service rather than rejected.

query.name: q
query.description: Name search, trimmed. Omit it to get the first page of the whole vocabulary.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. A non-positive or non-numeric value is rejected globally with 400 `{success:false, error:"Invalid Params"}`.

capabilities.intent: Search the workspace-wide tag vocabulary for one entity type and get each tag's id — the only tag read here that returns ids, so it is where you resolve the source_id and target_id a tag merge needs
guidance: Group-scoped: no project is involved and none can be supplied, so tags from every project in the workspace come back together. A name you find here may not be in use in the project you care about.
This read returns the tag `id` alongside the name — that is what makes it the resolution step for a tag merge, which takes integer ids. The project-level tag reads return names only.
Page size is fixed at 30 and there is no per_page parameter; page with `p`.
`created_at` and `usage_count`, which the project-scoped tag search returns, are not guaranteed on this group-scoped path — treat `id` and `name` as the fields you can rely on.
Not permission-gated — the search-filter controller has no RBAC entry, and this route deliberately skips project resolution.

capabilities.name: search_project_entities

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id. The route segment only matches digits (or the literal 'new'); a PR-NNN identifier is a routing 404.

path_params.name: entity
path_params.description: What to search. 'trtc' means the test cases inside one test run and needs test_run_id. 'test-plans' matches the route but has no handler branch and always returns an empty list. 'reports' is NOT a valid value — it fails the route constraint with a 404.

query.name: q[query]
query.description: Free-text match on title/identifier. Special characters are stripped before the match.

query.name: q[folder_ids]
query.description: Comma-separated folder ids to restrict to (test-cases). Add include_subfolders_tc=true to descend into sub-folders.

query.name: q[folder_id]
query.description: Single folder id; read on the trtc path only.

query.name: q[status]
query.description: Comma-separated numeric status IDs, not display names — resolve them first. Renamed to status_id internally.

query.name: q[priority]
query.description: Comma-separated numeric priority IDs, not display names. Renamed to priority_id internally.

query.name: q[case_type]
query.description: Comma-separated numeric case-type IDs, not display names. Renamed to category_id internally.

query.name: q[automation_state]
query.description: Either the literal word 'automated' / 'manual' (resolved to ids for this project) or comma-separated numeric ids. The only filter here that accepts words.

query.name: q[owner]
query.description: Comma-separated TM user ids (test-cases and test-runs). Pass use_bstack_id=1 if you are supplying BrowserStack ids instead.

query.name: q[assignee]
query.description: Comma-separated TM user ids; the trtc equivalent of owner (mapped to owner internally).

query.name: q[reviewers]
query.description: Comma-separated TM user ids; translated to BrowserStack ids server-side because reviews are stored against the BrowserStack id.

query.name: q[test_case_tags]
query.description: Tag filter. Must be a JSON-ENCODED STRING containing an array of tag names, not a bare comma list and not a real array. `q[tags]` is not a recognised key here and is dropped.

query.name: q[created_at]
query.description: Relative window as <N>_<hour|day|week|month|year>[_gte], or 'all_time' for no bound. Converted to an absolute range server-side.

query.name: q[updated_at]
query.description: Same token format, on last-updated date.

query.name: q[review_status]
query.description: Comma-separated review-status tokens (approved, rejected, in_review, pending, changes_requested), test-cases only.

query.name: q[configuration_id]
query.description: Comma-separated configuration ids; trtc path.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. Non-positive or non-numeric values return 400 'Invalid Params'.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Rows per page — this is the size parameter, NOT page_size or count. Above 300 on test-cases the call silently switches to id-only compact rows; on test-runs it is overridden to 30 regardless.

query.name: required[fields]
query.description: Comma-separated list of extra columns to hydrate. The single value 'count' switches the endpoint into count-only mode: the response becomes {success, count} with no rows.

query.name: sort_by
query.description: Column and direction as <column>-<asc|desc>. For test-cases the column must also appear in required[fields] when that is used, or the request fails.

query.name: use_bstack_id
query.description: Set to '1' when the user ids in q[owner]/q[assignee]/q[reviewers]/q[last_executed_by] are BrowserStack ids; they are then translated to TM ids. Without it BrowserStack ids simply match nothing.

query.name: test_run_id
query.description: Required when entity=trtc — the run whose test cases you are searching. Omitting it yields an empty page, not an error.

query.name: include_subfolders_tc
query.description: Descend into sub-folders of q[folder_ids] (test-cases). Only the exact string 'true' enables it.

query.name: include_test_plan
query.description: Decorate each run with its linked test plans (test-runs only). Only the exact string 'true' enables it.

query.name: filter_details
query.description: Also return the filters you sent, resolved into display objects, under `filter_details`. Ignored when q is empty.

query.name: compact
query.description: Force compact mode for test-cases: id-only stub rows grouped by folder, empty filter_details. This is the same mode per_page>300 triggers implicitly.

capabilities.intent: Search and filter a project's test cases, test runs, or the test cases inside one run — the general-purpose finder: free text plus status / priority / type / owner / folder / tag / date filters, with an id-only count mode

200.description: Top-level result; the collection key depends on entity (test_cases for test-cases and trtc, test_runs for test-runs) and there is no `data` envelope. Compact mode and count-only mode return reduced shapes — see guidance.

test_cases.description: Present for entity=test-cases and entity=trtc. In compact mode the rows degrade to {id, test_case_folder_id, project_id} stubs.

folders.description: Folders touched by the result set; test-cases only.

count.description: Total matches. Always present for entity=test-runs; the sole payload (with success) in count-only mode.

filter_details.description: The filters you sent, resolved to display objects. Empty {} unless filter_details=true and q was non-empty, and always empty in compact mode.

guidance: Four entity values route here: test-cases, test-runs, trtc (the test cases inside one test run) and test-plans. Anything else — 'reports' included — does not match the route constraint and is a 404 before the API is reached.

entity=test-plans is accepted by the route and by the controller but has no implementation behind it: it always renders {test_plans: [], info: null} with a 200. It is a dead branch, not an empty result — use the test-plan listing capabilities instead.
entity=trtc additionally requires a `test_run_id` query param. Without it the run filter is built from 0 and you get an empty page rather than an error.
The page-size parameter is `per_page`, not `page_size` or `count`; `page_size` is ignored and you silently get the 30-row default.

Ceiling behaviour differs per entity and this is the sharpest edge here. For test-cases, asking for more than 300 rows (or passing compact=true) flips the call into compact mode: the rows degrade to id-only stubs {id, test_case_folder_id, project_id}, filter_details comes back empty, and the page size jumps to 20000. For test-runs, per_page is overridden to 30 no matter what you ask for. Only trtc forwards per_page unchanged.
Count-only mode: send required[fields]=count (exactly that one field) and the response collapses to {success, count} with no rows — far cheaper than paging for a total.

Filter keys are renamed on the way through: q[priority] -> priority_id, q[status] -> status_id, q[case_type] -> category_id. They take numeric IDs, not display labels — resolve them with the system/custom field value capabilities first. q[automation_state] is the exception: it accepts the literal words 'automated' or 'manual' as well as ids.

Any key under q that the backing allow-list does not recognise is dropped silently. A misspelled filter therefore widens the result set to everything instead of erroring — always sanity-check the count against an unfiltered call.

q[owner] / q[assignee] / q[reviewers] take TM user ids by default. Pass use_bstack_id=1 if your ids are BrowserStack ids and they will be translated first; without it, BrowserStack ids match nothing and the response is simply empty.

Response shape depends on the entity: test-cases returns {success, test_cases, folders, info, filter_details}; trtc returns {success, info, test_cases, filter_details}; test-runs returns {success, test_runs, info, count} plus filter_details only when filter_details=true and q is non-empty. There is no `data` envelope on any of them.
For test-cases, `sort_by` must name a column that is also present in required[fields] when required[fields] is used, or the call fails with 'Sort by column X is not present in required fields'.
Binned (recycle-bin) and archived test cases are excluded from this search; they have their own listing capabilities.

capabilities.name: search_project_entities_v2

body.name: query
body.description: Search query string

body.name: reviewers
body.description: Filter by reviewer, same form as `owner` — comma-separated TM user ids as a string, `$none` for none.

body.name: last_executed_by
body.description: Filter by who last executed the case, same form as `owner`. A non-string value raises server-side rather than returning empty.

body.name: folder_id
body.description: Filter by folder ID (single value or array)

body.name: folder_ids
body.description: Filter by multiple folder IDs (comma-separated string or array)

body.name: priority
body.description: Filter by priority IDs (comma-separated string or array)

body.name: status
body.description: Filter by status IDs (comma-separated string or array)

body.name: issue_type
body.description: Filter by issue type (e.g., jira, github)

body.name: issue_ids
body.description: Filter by issue IDs (comma-separated string or array)

body.name: tags
body.description: Filter by tags (comma-separated string or array)

body.name: case_type
body.description: Filter by case-type option ids (comma-separated string or array).

body.name: automation_state
body.description: Option ids, or the literals `automated` / `manual` which the server resolves.

body.name: automation_status
body.description: Filter by automation status.

body.name: review_status
body.description: Filter by review status (only meaningful where review/approval is configured).

body.name: created_at
body.description:
Relative token `<n>_<unit>` with a SINGULAR unit (`day`, `hour`, `week`, `month`,
`year`) — e.g. `7_day`, `24_hour`; `_gte` inverts it (`7_day_gte` = older than).
Also accepts `all_time` or an absolute `"YYYY-MM-DD YYYY-MM-DD"` range. A PLURAL
unit such as `7_days` is an unhandled server error (500), not a 400.

body.name: updated_at
body.description: Same form as `created_at`.

body.name: date_range
body.description: Absolute created-at range as epoch milliseconds: `"<epochMs>,<epochMs>"`.

body.name: ids
body.description: Fetch specific cases by integer id (comma-separated string or array).

body.name: is_archived
body.description: Restrict to archived (or non-archived) cases.

body.name: match
body.description:
Per-field **operator** map — how to combine a field's values, NEVER the values
themselves. The value stays beside `match` under its own key; `match` only says
how to read it. A value placed inside `match` sets a meaningless operator and
applies NO filter, which is the silent no-op described on `q`.

Any filterable field may appear here, plus `custom_fields` keyed by field id.
Modes: `all`, `any`,

body.name: empty
body.description:
Is-empty / is-unset filter. `system_fields` accepts the payload names `status`,
`priority`, `case_type`, `automation_state`; `custom_fields` takes field ids.

body.name: p
body.description: Page number

body.name: per_page
body.description: Results per page. Rows are large and vary with the data, so probe rather than assume: send p=1 with a moderate per_page and take the rows that actually come back as your ceiling (for entity=test-cases a row is ~40 keys / 5-9 KB, so start around 5). Then keep per_page FIXED for the whole walk — the offset is (p-1)*per_page, so changing it part-way shifts the window and SKIPS rows (page 1 at 5 then

body.name: fields
body.description: Comma-separated JOINED columns to hydrate (owner, tags, issues, reviewers, priority, status, case_type, automation_state, defects; unlisted names pass through). It selects joins ONLY — it can never remove the base fields (name, description, preconditions, steps, test_case_steps, custom_fields, attachments), so naming fewer changes how many rows fit per page, NOT the order of magnitude, and it cann

body.name: result_custom_fields
body.description: Same idea for test-RESULT custom fields, on the result-bearing listings.

capabilities.intent: Search for entities within a project (v2 - POST with body)
guidance: The general way to find cases by attribute. Ask for a large page when collecting ids to feed into another call, so the follow-up gets the whole set rather than the first page.

200.description: Search results successfully retrieved

capabilities.name: search_project_users

query.name: q
query.description: Matches FULL NAME only, case-insensitive contains. Email is not searched — a query that looks like an address returns nothing. Omit it to list everyone in the workspace.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. A non-positive or non-numeric value is rejected globally with 400 `{success:false, error:"Invalid Params"}`. Paging overflows to the last page rather than returning an empty one.

query.name: sort
query.description: Sort column. The allowlist is shared across entities — `identifier` is not a user column and has no effect. An unlisted value is ignored rather than rejected, leaving the default order.

query.name: sort_order
query.description: Lower-case only; an unlisted value silently falls back to the default ordering.

capabilities.intent: Find people by name and read their role, permissions and product access — the search behind owner and assignee pickers; note it searches the whole workspace, not just this project's members
guidance: This is NOT project-scoped, despite the path and the name. The query filters on the caller's group only — `project_id` resolves the route and is never used in the lookup — so every user in the workspace comes back, including people with no access to this project.
`has_access` on each row is the user's product-access flag, not project membership. Do not read it as 'is on this project'; there is no project-membership field in this response at all.
`q` matches full_name only, case-insensitive contains. Searching by email returns an empty list, which looks identical to 'no such person'.
`id` is the Test Management user id — the one owner and assignee fields take. `browserstack_user_id` is the BrowserStack account id for the same person and is a different number.
Page size is fixed at 30: the `page_size` parameter that was published here is not read, and asking for 100 still returns 30.

Paging overflows to the LAST page — a `p` beyond the end returns the final page again rather than an empty list. Stop on `info.next == null`, never on 'the page came back empty', or you will loop forever on the last page.
Default order is creation date descending, so the newest members appear first; it is not alphabetical.

`permissions` is computed per request from the user's product role and this workspace's feature flags, so the same person can show a different permission list in a different workspace, and the list is not a stored attribute.
Not permission-gated — the search-filter controller has no RBAC entry.

capabilities.name: search_test_case_tags

query.name: q
query.description: Name search, trimmed; an all-whitespace value is treated as absent and you get the backing service's default first page. This is the ONLY query parameter the handler reads.

capabilities.intent: Check whether a test-case tag name exists in a project, or complete a partial one, before tagging a case or building a tag filter
guidance: This search cannot be paged. `p` and `page_size` are accepted by the URL and never read — no page parameter reaches the backing service, so every call returns its first page and a request for page 2 silently returns the same rows. If a project has more tags than one page, narrow with `q` rather than paging.
The response still carries an `info` block; it describes the one page you were given, not a page you can navigate away from.
`tags` is an array of names, `tag_objects` the same tags with `created_at` and `usage_count`. No tag ids here — use the group-level tag search when you need an id.

If the project cannot be resolved the handler returns 200 with `{tags: []}`. An empty vocabulary and an unknown/inaccessible project are indistinguishable, so do not read an empty result as 'this project has no tags'.
Test-case tags only. Run tags are a separate vocabulary on a separate path, and a name present in one says nothing about the other.
Not permission-gated — the search-filter controller has no RBAC entry.

capabilities.name: search_test_cases_by_folder_v1

query.name: id
query.description: Exact integer test case id. Blank values are skipped.

query.name: name
query.description: EXACT case title match — not a substring search. Blank values are skipped.

query.name: identifier
query.description: Exact identifier match. Blank values are skipped.

capabilities.intent: Legacy id/name/identifier lookup against the deprecated local test-case table — do NOT use it to find test cases; use the project search or the folder listing instead.
guidance: DEPRECATED AND EFFECTIVELY DEAD. It queries the legacy local test-case table, which is no longer the system of record — for any project whose data lives in the current backend it returns an empty list with 200, whatever you search for. An empty result here is not evidence that a case does not exist.
It does NOT accept a free-text `query` parameter. The only filters read are `id`, `name` and `identifier`, each matched for EXACT equality, and a blank value is skipped.

The response is a BARE JSON ARRAY of legacy rows — no `success`, no `info`, no `test_cases` wrapper, and the rows are the old table's columns, not the serialised test case the rest of this surface returns.
The folder id in the path is not used to scope the query; only the project and group are.
Use the project-wide entity search for finding cases by text, or the folder listing to enumerate a folder.

capabilities.name: send_report_email_now_v1

body.name: emails
body.description: Recipient addresses. MUST be an array, even for one address. 1-10 entries, each matching a standard address syntax — invalid entries fail the whole call 400 and are listed in the message. Any address is accepted; recipients need not be TM users.

body.name: file_type
body.description: Format to attach. MUST be an array with EXACTLY ONE entry — two entries, or an explicit empty array, crash the allow-list check and return 500. Omit the field entirely to default to ["pdf"].

capabilities.intent: Email an existing report to specific people right now, as a PDF/CSV/XLSX attachment, without changing its schedule

200.description: Generation job enqueued; the mail is sent asynchronously.

message.example: Report generation started. Email will be sent shortly.

guidance: This is the only way to get a report's file out of the product through the API — the download capability hands back a channel id you cannot resolve. Mail it to yourself to obtain the file.

Send a SINGLE entry in `file_type`. The server checks the allow-list with a splat, so an array of two formats (or an explicit empty array) raises an ArgumentError and comes back 500, not 400. Call the endpoint once per format you need.
Both fields must be JSON arrays even for one value — a bare string is 400 `emails should be an array` / `file_type should be an array`.

`emails` is effectively required: it defaults to an empty array which then fails the count check with 400 `Please provide between 1 and 10 email addresses.` Between 1 and 10 addresses, each syntactically valid; invalid ones are named in the 400 rather than skipped.
Recipients are arbitrary addresses — they need not be TM users, and the mail goes out immediately with no further confirmation. Treat this as an irreversible external side effect.

The 200 only means the job was enqueued (`Report generation started. Email will be sent shortly.`). Generation or delivery can still fail afterwards and there is no job id and no status endpoint — you cannot confirm the mail was sent.
Unlike every other report call, this one is NOT permission-gated: any user with access to the project can share a report. An unknown report id is 404 `Report not found`.
The report's own `mail_to` recipients are untouched: this does not add them, and it does not affect the schedule.

capabilities.name: undo_remove_folder
capabilities.intent: DOES NOT restore a deleted folder — this route currently deletes the folder and its entire subtree, identically to the delete call; there is no folder-restore API

200.description: Folder successfully restored

guidance: Do not call this to undo a deletion. The handler is a one-line alias that forwards to the delete action, and the two arguments it passes to signal 'restore' are never read by that action — the request that reaches the backing service is exactly the same DELETE the remove endpoint sends.

The effect is therefore identical to deleting the folder: the folder, every subfolder beneath it and every test case in the subtree are removed, with test cases landing in the recycle bin only if the group's Move to Bin flag is on.

It is also the cheaper way to cause that damage: this route is gated on the folder-EDIT permission while the real delete route requires folder-DELETE, so an edit-only caller can destroy a folder through it.

There is no folder-restore capability anywhere in this API. Binned TEST CASES can be listed and restored from the project bin; folders cannot be brought back at all. If you need the structure again, recreate it.
The response is the delete response: {data:{folder, path_folders, success}}, with the echoed folder's counts zeroed.

capabilities.name: unlink_test_runs_from_test_plan

body.name: test_runs
body.description: Run ids to unlink, as the INTEGER `uuid` from a run read — NOT the TR-NNN string that run endpoints return in `id`. Sent at the TOP LEVEL of the body: this call has no `test_plan` wrapper, unlike plan create/update.

capabilities.intent: Detach test runs from a test plan without deleting them — the runs survive and become plan-less, ready to be linked somewhere else

200.description: `{"success": true}` on an unlink. Also returned with `{"success": false, "error": "Please check test runs"}` when `test_runs` is missing or not an array — a 200 that did nothing.

guidance: The body is FLAT here — {"test_runs": [...]} at the top level. Wrapping it in `test_plan` the way create and update require means the handler sees nothing and the call silently no-ops.

A missing test_runs, or one that is not an array, returns HTTP 200 with {success: false, error: 'Please check test runs'} and changes nothing. This is the main failure mode and it does not look like a failure.
Use each run's integer `uuid`. Run endpoints put the TR-NNN string in `id`, and passing that fails upstream rather than being rejected here.

The 200 is returned without checking what actually happened: ids that were never linked to this plan, or that do not exist, are absorbed silently. Read the plan's run list before and after if you need to report what changed.
This only breaks the plan↔run link. The runs themselves, and their test cases and results, are untouched — they just stop belonging to any plan.
To re-link runs, send them in the plan update's test_runs list (which REPLACES the whole link set) rather than looking for a link endpoint here.

capabilities.name: update_custom_field_dataset_option_v2

path_params.name: custom_fields_id
path_params.description: Numeric custom field id. Not validated by this handler.

path_params.name: dataset_id
path_params.description: Numeric dataset id holding the option. Not validated by this handler.

path_params.name: option_id
path_params.description: Numeric option id, from the dataset options listing. Not validated by this handler; a wrong value surfaces as a bodyless 404.

body.name: option_value
body.description: The option label. REQUIRED even when unchanged — a missing or null value is a 400. Must stay unique within the dataset.

body.name: is_default
body.description: REQUIRED even when unchanged — a missing or null value is a 400. Setting it true does not clear any other option's default.

capabilities.intent: Rename one dropdown choice, or make it the default — the option id stays the same, so cases already holding this value follow the new label
guidance: A full replace of the option's label and default flag: both option_value and is_default must be sent, even when only one is changing. A missing or null either way is a 400 {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'}.
`parent_option_id` cannot be changed here — the handler does not forward it, so an option cannot be re-parented in a nested_dropdown. Delete and recreate instead, which drops the stored values.
The option id is stable across a rename, and stored values reference the id, so renaming does not lose data and can be undone by renaming back.
The rename lands in every project the dataset is linked to, with no per-project variant.
Making an option the default does not clear the previous default; on a single-select dropdown clear the old one yourself. On a multi_dropdown every option should stay is_default false.

Neither path id nor the option id is validated in this layer — a wrong triple surfaces as a bare 404 {success:false} with no message. A duplicate label is relayed verbatim from upstream; every other failure is masked as 400 'The API request is invalid or improperly formed'.

capabilities.name: update_custom_field_dataset_project_mapping_v2

path_params.name: custom_fields_id
path_params.description: Numeric custom field id. Validated only on the synchronous path; an async (>300 project) request does not check it at all.

path_params.name: dataset_id
path_params.description: Numeric dataset id. Validated only on the synchronous path; an async request does not check it at all.

body.name: link_projects
body.description: Integer project ids to ADD. Note the spelling — `linked_projects` is silently dropped here. Send [] rather than omitting it: unless select_all is present, a missing array makes the request 500.

body.name: unlink_projects
body.description: Integer project ids to REMOVE. Destroys those projects' stored values for this field, irreversibly. Send [] rather than omitting it — unless select_all is present, a missing array makes the request 500.

body.name: link_to_future_projects
body.description: Auto-link projects created after this call. Forwarded as-is; omitting it sends null.

body.name: select_all
body.description: true = link every project in the workspace except unlink_projects; false = UNLINK every project except link_projects, deleting their stored values. Only literal true/false are recognised — any other value falls back to the two explicit lists. Over 300 projects the call goes async.

capabilities.intent: Change which projects a custom field's dataset applies to — link projects so they see the field, or unlink them, which deletes the values those projects already stored
guidance: Send BOTH `link_projects` and `unlink_projects`, even when one is empty. Unless `select_all` is present, the handler adds their two lengths together, and a missing array raises an unhandled error — the call comes back 500, not 400.

The spelling is link_projects / unlink_projects here. The create calls use linked_projects / linked_to_all_projects; those names are silently dropped on this path, so the call returns 200 with nothing changed.
Unlinking is destructive to data: the values every case in those projects stored for this field are removed, and there is no undo. Name and count the projects before proceeding.

`select_all: true` links every project in the workspace except those in unlink_projects. `select_all: false` is the inverse and UNLINKS every project except those in link_projects — a whole-workspace data deletion from a single boolean. Only the literal strings/values true and false are recognised.

Above 300 affected projects the call switches to a background job and returns {success: true, async: true, unique_id: "<uuid>"} with NO dataset body. The unique_id is a job handle only; there is no endpoint here to poll it, so verify by re-reading the dataset.
In that async case the path ids are never validated, so a bad field or dataset id is accepted with a 200 and the work fails silently in the worker.

A project may belong to only one dataset per field. Linking a project already held by a sibling dataset fails with the upstream message relayed verbatim (e.g. 'Projects already linked to a different dataset for this custom field...', 'invalid project mapping', 'Dataset id is invalid').
On the synchronous path the response is the re-read dataset under `data`, with its options included.

capabilities.name: update_custom_field_definition_v2

body.name: field_name
body.description: Display label. REQUIRED even when unchanged. Stripped before comparison and storage.

body.name: field_type
body.description: REQUIRED for validation. Send the field's CURRENT type — this surface does not compare it to what is stored, it forwards it.

body.name: is_required
body.description: REQUIRED, literal JSON boolean. Omitting it, or sending the string "true", is a 400.

body.name: entity_type
body.description: Used only to select the valid field_type set and the reserved-name list; never sent upstream, so it cannot move the field to a different entity. Send the field's real entity_type.

body.name: place_holder_text
body.description: Hint text. Omitting it sends null and CLEARS the stored value — resend it to keep it.

body.name: default_value
body.description: Applied only when field_type is `boolean`. For any other type the handler sends null regardless of what you pass, clearing any stored default.

capabilities.intent: Rename a custom field, or change whether it is mandatory, its placeholder or its boolean default — a full replace of the field's attributes, not a partial edit
guidance: This is a REPLACE, not a patch. field_name, field_type and is_required must all be present or the call is 400 'Invalid Params' — read the field first and resend the whole set.

Omitting place_holder_text sends null and clears the stored hint text. Likewise, for any non-boolean field the handler always sends default_value as null, so a stored default on a string/int/date field does not survive this call. Resend every value you want to keep.

field_type must be sent and must be valid for the entity_type, but this surface does NOT compare it against the stored type — it is forwarded upstream. Send the field's CURRENT type. (Its sibling on the the v2 surface custom-fields surface rejects a changed type outright with 400 'Field type cannot be changed'.)

entity_type is used only to pick the valid field_type list and the reserved-name list; it is never sent upstream, so a field cannot be moved between TestCase / TestResult / TestPlan. Send the field's real entity_type or the validation applies the wrong rules.

Datasets, options and project links are NOT touched here — this call carries no `datasets` key upstream. Change option values through the dataset option calls and project scope through the dataset project-mapping call.

Renaming onto a reserved name (Title, Description, Priority, State, Owner, Tags, …) is a 400, except when the field already carries that name — an import-created field keeps its name and stays editable.

There is no version history for a field definition: an overwritten label, placeholder or default cannot be restored. A rename is workspace-wide and lands in every project the field's datasets link to.

Upstream duplicate-name errors come back verbatim; every other upstream failure is masked as 400 {success:false, message:'The API request is invalid or improperly formed'}, and a field id that does not exist comes back as a bare 404 {success:false} with no message.

capabilities.name: update_dataset

body.name: name
body.description: Dataset name. REQUIRED on update despite reading like a partial edit — update shares the create request schema. A name already used by another dataset in the project returns 400 {success:false, message:'Dataset name already exists.'}.

body.name: variables
body.description: The complete new column list — this REPLACES the existing columns, it does not merge. Required. Send each column's existing `uuid` (from a read) for the columns you are keeping; omit it only for genuinely new columns. Blank-named or entirely-empty columns are silently dropped. 40 is the default cap, 100 for groups with the raised-limit flag.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Letters, digits and underscores only, must start with a letter. Duplicate names (case-insensitive) fail the call.

fields.name: uuid
fields.description: The existing column's uuid, taken from a read. Forwarded to the store so the column keeps its identity; leave it out and you are creating a new column.

body.name: rows
body.description: The complete new row set — REPLACES the existing rows. Required. Same normalisation as create: blank rows dropped, cells trimmed, duplicate rows collapsed, row_number reassigned 1..N. 100 is the default cap, 200 for groups with the raised-limit flag.

fields.name: row_number
fields.description: Required by the schema, then overwritten with the row's final position.

fields.name: row_data
fields.description: Strings only, positional against `variables`; length must match the surviving column count after empty-column pruning.

fields.name: uuid
fields.description: The existing row's uuid from a read, for rows you are keeping.

body.name: tags
body.description: Replaces the dataset's tags when the key is present; omit the key entirely to leave existing tags alone. Sending [] clears them. Each tag is a string of at most 50 characters, at most 20 tags.

capabilities.intent: Replace a dataset's contents — rename it, or write a new set of columns and rows over the existing table

200.description: Dataset updated; the full stored dataset is returned at the top level as `dataset`.

400.description: Request-schema rejection ({error:'Invalid JSON data', details:[...]}) — including a body missing name/variables/rows — or a duplicate dataset name ({success:false, message:'Dataset name already exists.'}).

404.description: No dataset with this uuid in the project: {success:false, message:'Dataset <uuid>  not found.'}

422.description: {success:false, message:...}. 'Feature not available' = no Team Pro entitlement; any other message is a dataset-shape validation failure.

guidance: This is a full replace, not a patch, and `name`, `variables` and `rows` are ALL required — the update reuses the create request schema verbatim. A body with only `name` is rejected with 400 {error:'Invalid JSON data'}; the spec marking these optional is wrong.
To rename without losing data: read the dataset first and send its existing `variables` and `rows` (uuids included) back alongside the new name.
There is no undo. Datasets keep no version history and there is no restore endpoint, so an overwritten column or row set is gone. Read the current contents before writing.

`metadata` passes validation here and is then silently discarded — the handler forwards only name, columns, rows and tags. Sending metadata returns 200 with metadata unchanged. It can only be set at creation.

The body must be wrapped in a `dataset` object, and nothing beyond the declared keys is permitted anywhere in it (additionalProperties:false at every level) — an extra or misspelled key fails the whole call with 400.
The `uuid` in the path is the dataset's uuid string, resolved by looking it up in the project's dataset list; an unknown one is 404 {success:false, message:'Dataset <uuid>  not found.'}.
Rows and columns come back normalised (blank rows and empty columns removed, cells trimmed, duplicate rows collapsed, row_number renumbered) — trust the response, not your payload.
422 {message:'Feature not available'} is the Team Pro entitlement gate, not a bad body; any other 422 message is a real validation failure.
Needs the test-case write permission (tc_write).

capabilities.name: update_exploratory_session

body.name: title
body.description: New title. `name` is accepted by the request schema and silently dropped, so use this field.

body.name: description
body.description: Replacement description.

body.name: charter
body.description: Replacement testing charter.

body.name: timebox_duration
body.description: Planned duration. Rendered as minutes by TM's own exports but documented upstream as seconds; passed through unconverted.

body.name: duration
body.description: Tracked duration. Same unit ambiguity as timebox_duration.

body.name: actual_duration
body.description: Final actual duration. This is the ONLY place it can be set — the close call ignores any duration you send it — so write it here before closing the session.

body.name: folder_id
body.description: Move the session to a different folder; a numeric string is also accepted.

body.name: test_plan_id
body.description: Integer id of the test plan to link (not a TP-NNN identifier). Only reachable through the wrapped body.

body.name: owner
body.description: TCM user id of the new owner; translated to the upstream user id. Wins over `assignee` when both are sent. An unresolvable id clears the assignee instead of failing.

body.name: assignee
body.description: Genuine alias for `owner` on this endpoint — both are translated here. (On create only `owner` is, so prefer `owner` in code shared between the two.)

body.name: tags
body.description: REPLACES the session's tags with this list; an empty array clears them. Non-string entries are rejected by the request schema.

body.name: configurations
body.description: REPLACES the session's configuration ids (integers or numeric strings). An empty array clears them.

body.name: attachments
body.description: REPLACES the attached blob ids. Every id you leave out is detached and its blob freed for reuse. Ids must be integer blob ids from a prior generic attachment upload; an invalid set returns 422 with the bare string body "attachment is invalid".

body.name: issues
body.description: REPLACES the linked issues. Bare id strings are coerced to jira issues; entries missing issue_id or issue_type silently reduce the whole list to empty. Jira ids must match ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]+$ or the call fails. A per-entry metadata object is accepted. Applied asynchronously after the response.

body.name: custom_fields
body.description: Custom field values as a map of {custom_field_id: value} for entity type ExploratorySession, converted server-side. Not the array shape returned on read. Only sent when non-empty — an empty object is ignored rather than clearing values.

capabilities.intent: Change fields on an existing exploratory session — retitle it, revise the charter, record the time spent, reassign it, move it to another folder, or replace its tags, configurations, attachments and linked issues

200.description: Exploratory session updated successfully.

guidance: The body MUST be wrapped in an `exploratory_session` object; a flat JSON body is rejected with 400 'Invalid JSON data' by the request schema before the handler runs.

Scalar fields are patched by presence: only title, description, charter, timebox_duration, duration, actual_duration, folder_id and test_plan_id keys actually present in the body are sent. Omitted keys are left alone.

The collection fields are NOT patched, they are replaced. Sending `tags`, `configurations`, `issues` or `attachments` overwrites the whole list; sending an empty array clears it. Omitting the key is the only way to leave a collection untouched.

Replacing `attachments` detaches every blob you left out and frees it for reuse. An invalid set is rejected with 422 whose body is the bare JSON string "attachment is invalid" — not the usual {success:false, message} envelope, so do not parse it like one.

`owner` and `assignee` are both translated to the upstream user id here (unlike create, where only `owner` is). `owner` wins when both are sent. An id that resolves to no user clears the assignee rather than failing.
There is no way to change `session_state` through this call, and no reopen endpoint exists — closing a session is one-way.
`name` is accepted by the request schema and then dropped by the parameter filter; retitle with `title`.
Exploratory sessions keep no version history and there is no undo: an overwritten title, description, charter or tag list cannot be restored.
Issue linking is applied asynchronously after the 200, so the session echoed back may not yet reflect the new links.

Upstream validation failures all arrive as 400 {success:false, message:'The API request is invalid or improperly formed'} — the same text for a bad configuration id, a folder in another project or a malformed value.

capabilities.name: update_exploratory_session_log

body.name: content
body.example: Confirmed the spinner issue on iOS 17 as well.
body.description: Replacement rich-text HTML. Sanitised on write. Re-sending it re-derives the log's image attachments from the blob ids in the HTML, so an image removed from the HTML is detached. A null is stripped rather than clearing the field — send an empty string to blank it.

body.name: status
body.description: Replacement outcome. `skipped` is valid; anything outside the seven is rejected by the request schema. A null is stripped rather than clearing the status.

body.name: elapsed_time
body.description: Replacement time spent, in seconds. Must be an integer. A null is stripped rather than clearing the value.

body.name: defects
body.description: REPLACES the log's defect links when non-empty; omit the key to leave them untouched. An empty array is treated as 'not supplied' and does NOT clear the links. Bare id strings are coerced to jira issues; entries missing issue_id or issue_type silently reduce the list to empty; a bad jira id fails the whole call. Applied asynchronously after the response.

capabilities.intent: Revise an observation already recorded in an exploratory session — correct the note, change its pass/fail/bug outcome, adjust the time spent or restate which defects it raised

200.description: Session log updated successfully.

guidance: Both ids matter and both are integers: log_id identifies the entry, session_id in the path identifies its parent session. A log_id that belongs to a different session is not addressable here.
Send the body wrapped in a `session_log` object. Only content, status, elapsed_time and defects are read, and only the keys present are forwarded — everything else is left as it is.

You cannot blank a field out: nulls are stripped from the outgoing payload, so sending content:null or status:null leaves the existing value in place. Send an empty string for content instead, and expect status and elapsed_time to be un-clearable.

`defects`, when non-empty, REPLACES the log's defect links; omit the key to leave them alone. The same coercion applies as on create — bare id strings become jira issues, malformed entries silently reduce the list to empty, and a bad jira id fails the whole call. Linking is applied asynchronously after the 200.

You cannot unlink every defect from a log: sending defects:[] is treated as 'not supplied' and the existing links survive. This differs from the session update, where an empty tags/configurations/issues array does clear the list.

Re-sending `content` re-derives the log's image attachments from the blob ids in the HTML: an image you drop from the HTML loses its attachment link, and if any referenced blob id is not visible to your group or project then ALL of the call's attachment links are silently dropped while the update still succeeds.
`content` is sanitised on write, so the stored HTML can differ from what you sent.
Session logs keep no version history and there is no undo — an overwritten note cannot be recovered.
`status` must be one of pass, fail, bug, retest, block, note, skipped; anything else is a 400 from the request schema.

capabilities.name: update_filter

body.name: name
body.description: Required on every update, even when you are only changing the conditions. Read the filter first and resend its current name rather than inventing one — the value you send is what it is renamed to.

body.name: entity
body.description: Required on every update. Resend the filter's existing entity_type; sending a different one repoints the saved view at another list type. An unlisted value returns 400 'Invalid JSON data'.

body.name: is_project_level
body.description: Forwarded whenever the key is present, including `false` — this is how you demote a project-wide view back to private. Omit the key to leave the current scope alone.

body.name: filters
body.description: Replacement condition set. Omit to leave the stored conditions untouched. `{}` is treated as absent, so conditions cannot be cleared to empty through this call.

capabilities.intent: Rename a saved filter view, replace its conditions, or switch it between private and project-wide — resending name and entity on every call
guidance: This is a POST, not a PATCH or PUT, and it is only half a partial update: `name` and `entity` are required by the request-body schema on every call, while `is_project_level` and `filters` are forwarded only when you send them. Read the filter first and resend name + entity_type unchanged.
The body is flat and closed — an extra key returns 400 'Invalid JSON data' before the handler runs.
`filters: {}` is dropped as blank, so there is no way to empty a view's conditions here; delete and recreate instead.
Saved filter views keep no version history, so an overwritten name or condition set cannot be restored. Read the filter before you overwrite it if you may need the old value.
Changing is_project_level to true publishes a previously private view to the whole project immediately.
An unknown filter_id comes back as 400 `{success:false, message:...}`, not 404 — this action only translates the backing service's 400, and every other failure from it becomes a 500.
Not permission-gated: the filter controller has no RBAC entry, so a project-level view can be edited by anyone with product access to the project, not only its owner.

capabilities.name: update_latest_test_result_for_test_case

body.name: status_id
body.description: Result status id (resolve via the statuses-and-states concept — this path takes ids, not names; a `status` name is accepted by the filter and then discarded).

body.name: description
body.description: Rich text note on the result. Links to uploaded attachments are rewritten server-side, so the stored value can differ from what you sent.

body.name: custom_fields
body.description: Custom field values keyed by custom field id (not by field name — that is the v2 contract).

body.name: issues
body.description: Linked defects. Each entry is an OBJECT — a bare string is silently dropped by the server's parameter filter, so the issue link is never created and no error is returned.

body.name: attachments
body.description: Integer blob ids from a prior generic attachment upload — not filenames and not file bytes.

body.name: elapsed_time
body.description: Accepted by the parameter filter and then DROPPED before the write on this path — setting it here does nothing and reports no error.

body.name: configuration_id
body.description: Which configuration's latest result to patch. TOP level — the server does not read it from inside `test_result`.

body.name: mapping_id
body.description: Target a specific run/case mapping. Top level.

capabilities.intent: Amend the most recent result logged for a test case in a run — correct its status, note, linked defects or custom fields in place, without adding another attempt to the case's history

200.description: Test result successfully updated

400.description: Bad request - Test run is closed or invalid parameters

404.description: No test results found

guidance: This EDITS the latest existing result; it never creates one. With nothing logged yet it answers 404 {success:false, message:'No test results found'} — log a result first, then amend it.
A closed test run is refused with 400 {success:false, error:'Cannot Update Closed Test Run'} before any field is written. Reopen the run or edit nothing.

The body must be wrapped in `test_result`: a before-filter requires that key, so a flat body 400s before a single field is read. An empty `test_result` object is legal and re-saves the current values unchanged.

Only description, status_id, custom_fields, attachments and issues survive to the write. `status` (the name) and `elapsed_time` are accepted by the parameter filter and then dropped on this path — set the status by id here, and use the v2 result surface if you only have a status name.
Keys you omit keep their current values (the handler re-reads the result and fills them in), so this is a genuine partial update.

configuration_id and mapping_id are read at the TOP level — query string or body root, never from inside `test_result`. Without one of them 'latest' means latest across all configurations, which on a configuration matrix is usually not the row you meant.

Unlike the id-addressed result update, this path applies NO authorship check — only the standard project permission gate runs, so it will overwrite a result logged by someone else. The edit is in place and the previous values are not recoverable; log a new result instead if you want the earlier outcome preserved.
The 200 body is the bare updated result object at the TOP level — no `data` envelope and no `success` key, unlike the create-result endpoint on the same path.

capabilities.name: update_project_settings
capabilities.intent: Turn a project's configuration flags on or off — review/approval gating, the custom test-case id prefix, test-case sharing, the manual-execution timer, Part 11 re-authentication, Jira/Azure linking and test-plan review

200.description: Written settings echoed back as one object per setting. A body containing no recognised setting name also returns 200, with success:false and an empty array — nothing was written.

success.description: False (with HTTP 200) when nothing was written — including when the body contained no recognised setting name.

project_settings.description: One single-key object per setting written, {settingName: value}. Note this differs from the read, which returns a single flattened object at index 0.

400.description: Invalid test_case_id_prefix (format, reserved, or already used elsewhere) or an unknown review-status token.

403.description: Timer settings written without the project-settings write permission.

422.description: New project settings not enabled for this group/user, or a plan gate (Team Pro / Enterprise) not met.

guidance: Settings are sent as FLAT top-level body keys, one per setting — there is no wrapper object and no generic {key, value} pair. Only the names listed below are read; everything else is ignored.

The silent no-op to watch for: if the body contains none of the known setting names, the request still returns HTTP 200 with {success:false, project_settings:[]} and nothing is written. A 200 here is not confirmation — check `success` and check that the setting you sent comes back in project_settings.
This is a partial update: only the keys you send are touched, and the others keep their stored values. It does NOT reset omitted settings.
There is no undo and no history — the previous value is gone the moment the write lands. Re-read get_project_settings first if you need to be able to restore it.
Feature-gated for the whole endpoint: without the new-project-settings flag for the group or user the call fails 422 'Feature not available' before any key is examined.

Per-setting gates, all raised before the write: review_approve and the two eligible-review-status settings need a Team Pro plan (422); part_11_reauth and part_11_reauth_send_for_review need an Enterprise plan (422); the four timer settings need the project-settings write permission (403 'Only admins can update Time Tracking settings').

test_case_id_prefix is validated twice — locally against 2-10 uppercase alphanumerics starting with a letter and not equal to 'TC', then against the backing service for reserved prefixes and cross-project collisions. Either failure returns 400 with the reason, and it is checked before anything else in the body is written.

The two eligible-review-status settings take a comma-separated list drawn from approved / rejected / in_review / pending / changes_requested. An unknown token fails the whole request with 400; an empty string is valid and means gating is OFF.
Values are stored as strings in an EAV table, so send booleans as the strings "true"/"false" and numbers as numeric strings; that is also how they read back.
The response echoes one object PER setting written ([{name: value}, ...]) — a different shape from the read, which flattens everything into a single object at project_settings[0].

Removing a setting entirely is a different operation (a delete on the same path with the attribute name) and is not exposed as a capability here; writing an empty string is not the same as unsetting it.

body.name: review_approve
body.description: Enable the test-case review/approval workflow. Requires a Team Pro plan — otherwise 422 'Feature not available'. Send "true"/"false" as strings.

body.name: test_run_eligible_review_statuses
body.description: Comma-separated review statuses a test case must be in before it can be added to a run. An unknown token fails the whole request with 400. Empty string = no gating. Requires a Team Pro plan.

body.name: test_execution_eligible_review_statuses
body.description: Comma-separated review statuses a test case must be in before results can be logged against it. Same validation and plan gate as the run variant.

body.name: default_test_case_approval_state
body.description: The review state newly created test cases start in.

body.name: test_case_id_prefix
body.description: Custom identifier prefix for this project's test cases. 2-10 characters, uppercase letters and digits, must start with a letter, and cannot be "TC". Also checked against reserved prefixes and other projects' prefixes; either check failing returns 400 with the reason.

body.name: tc_sharing
body.description: Allow this project's test cases to be shared into other projects.

body.name: part_11_reauth
body.description: Require re-authentication for regulated (21 CFR Part 11) actions. Requires an Enterprise plan — otherwise 422.

body.name: part_11_reauth_send_for_review
body.description: Require re-authentication specifically when sending for review. Requires an Enterprise plan — otherwise 422.

body.name: preferred_jira_host
body.description: Default Jira site URL used when linking issues from this project.

body.name: preferred_azure_org
body.description: Default Azure DevOps organisation used when linking work items from this project.

body.name: sync_jira_defect_attachments
body.description: Copy attachments to the linked Jira defect when one is raised.

body.name: link_jira_requirements
body.description: Enable linking Jira requirements from this project.

body.name: link_jira_test_case_requirement
body.description: Enable linking a Jira requirement to a test case.

body.name: link_jira_test_run_requirement
body.description: Enable linking a Jira requirement to a test run.

body.name: jira_create_allowed_hosts
body.description: Allow-list of Jira site URLs that may create or update requirements, as a JSON-ENCODED ARRAY STRING (e.g. "[\"https://example.com/jira\"]"). Omitting the key means all hosts are allowed; the string "[]" means none.

body.name: time_tracking_enabled
body.description: Per-project master switch for the manual-execution timer; the feature is on only when this is exactly "true". Requires the project-settings write permission — 403 otherwise.

body.name: timer_auto_start
body.description: Start the execution timer automatically when a tester opens a case. Requires the project-settings write permission.

body.name: timer_elapsed_required
body.description: Require an elapsed time before a result can be submitted. Requires the project-settings write permission.

body.name: timer_min_threshold_seconds
body.description: Minimum elapsed seconds before a result is accepted, as a numeric string. Requires the project-settings write permission.

body.name: test_plan_review_enabled
body.description: Enable the review workflow for test plans.

body.name: test_plan_review_sub_plan_mode
body.description: How sub-plans participate in test-plan review.

body.name: test_plan_review_default_state
body.description: The review state newly created test plans start in.

capabilities.name: update_report

body.name: projectId
body.description: Integer project id the rewritten filter rows are filed under. Not enforced by the server: omit it and rows are written against project 0 and become invisible, at 200. Send the report's own project id.

body.name: project_ids
body.description: Integer project ids for a cross-project report. Only applied when present — omitting it leaves the stored set alone. Max 60 (5 for User Workload Report), and multi-project only for the seven supported types; the cap is checked against the report_type in THIS body.

body.name: report_type
body.description: Report type as its DISPLAY NAME. Required, and it also selects which filter-rewrite branch runs — omit it and the report_type column is nulled AND the filters are silently left untouched. `Defects Summary` / `Defects Detailed Report` have no data branch and no filter branch.

body.name: title
body.description: Written unconditionally — omit it and the title is set to null.

body.name: description
body.description: Written unconditionally — omit it and the description is set to null.

body.name: report_timeframe
body.description: The window the report covers. `custom` REQUIRES `custom_date_range` (omitting it is an unhandled 500); any other value NULLS the stored custom_date_range. The five entity timeframes carry no dates and each reads one matching `report_filters` key.

body.name: report_creation_mode
body.description: Written unconditionally. Unlike create, `system_generated` here does NOT re-fetch requirements for a traceability report — send `report_filters.requirements` yourself.

body.name: is_dynamic
body.description: Written unconditionally from the body — omit it and the report's dynamic flag is set to null (unlike create, it is not inferred from the filters).

body.name: grain
body.description: Immutable after creation. Send the report's persisted value or omit it; anything different is 400 'grain cannot be changed after report creation'.

body.name: test_run
body.description: Dynamic run selection, accepted under either `dynamic_filters` or `filters`. Only rewritten for a Requirement Traceability Report; on other types it is read but the JQL config is not updated.

body.name: test_runs
body.description: Run ids as INTEGERS — a quoted id or TR-NNN fails the request 400 'Invalid report filters'. Omitting the key DELETES the stored run selection.

body.name: test_plans
body.description: Plan ids as INTEGERS — a quoted id or TP-NNN fails the request 400 'Invalid report filters'. Omitting the key DELETES the stored plan selection.

body.name: test_cases
body.description: Case selection — must be an OBJECT (an array is 400), folder-keyed like SelectionData: folder ids are STRING keys, case ids INTEGERS. Read the current value from get_selected_report_testcases and send it back; omitting the key deletes the saved selection.

body.name: shared_selection
body.description: Cross-project case selection: { "<project_id>": <same shape as test_cases> } for non-primary projects. A project id outside the report's project set is dropped silently.

body.name: session_ids
body.description: Exploratory session ids — pairs with report_timeframe=specific_sessions.

body.name: requirements
body.description: { issue_type: [issue_id, ...] } — must be an object, not an array. Pairs with report_timeframe=requirements and is NOT auto-populated on edit even for system_generated reports.

body.name: test_plan_selection
body.description: Per-plan sub-plan selection: { plan_id: { select_all, selected_sub_plan_ids, deselected_sub_plan_ids } }. A malformed entry is discarded silently rather than rejected.

body.name: test_runs_by_project
body.description: Cross-project run selection: { "<project_id>": [run_id, ...] }. Numeric-string keys and numeric-id arrays only, else 400. Replaces the flat `test_runs` key when present.

body.name: test_plans_by_project
body.description: Cross-project plan selection: { "<project_id>": [plan_id, ...] }. Replaces the flat `test_plans` and `test_plan_selection` keys when present.

body.name: builds
body.description: Internal build ids paired with `test_runs`. The report read returns them as `build_ids`; send them back unchanged or the paired rows are wiped on the next write.

body.name: tc_custom_fields
body.description: Keyed by custom-field id (an OBJECT, not an array). ONLY consumed for `Test Run Summary`, `Test Run Detailed Report` and `Test Case Activity`; elsewhere it is dropped silently. Persisted and read back under the name `custom_fields`.

body.name: custom_date_range
body.description: "YYYY-MM-DD YYYY-MM-DD", space separated. REQUIRED when report_timeframe is `custom` (omitting it is a 500); NULLED on the record for every other timeframe.

body.name: users
body.description: TM user ids to mail the report to. Every id must be in your group or the request is 400. Only applied when the report is already scheduled.

body.name: external_mails
body.description: Email addresses outside the group. Only applied when the report is already scheduled.

body.name: frequency
body.description: Send with `frequency_details` to keep or change the schedule. Omitting EITHER unschedules the report — both columns are nulled and it stops emailing. `once` is not a value: it passes validation and then raises a 500.

body.name: time
body.description: 24-hour HH:MM, UTC. Required whenever frequency is sent.

body.name: day
body.description: Required for weekly (lowercase English day name) and monthly (integer 1-28). Omit for daily.

capabilities.intent: Rewrite a saved report — its type, window, filters, schedule or recipients — replacing the whole definition in one call
guidance: This PATCH is a FULL REPLACE, not a merge. `title`, `description`, `report_type`, `report_timeframe`, `report_creation_mode` and `is_dynamic` are written from the body unconditionally, so any one you omit is set to NULL. Read the report first and send the complete object back with your change applied.

Omitting `frequency` / `frequency_details` UNSCHEDULES the report: both columns are nulled and it stops emailing. Resend the persisted values to keep the schedule. Likewise `custom_date_range` is nulled whenever `report_timeframe` is not `custom`.

`projectId` in the body is effectively required even though it is not marked so: it is the project every rewritten filter row is filed under. Omit it and the rows are written against project 0, which no read ever finds — the call still returns 200 with a report whose filters have silently vanished.

`report_filters` is authoritative: a key you omit has its stored rows deleted. Send the full filter set, not a delta. Use the report read and get_selected_report_testcases to recover the current values first.

Filters are only rewritten for Test Run Summary, Test Run Detailed Report, Test Plan Summary, Test Plan Detailed Report, Test Case Activity, User Workload Report, Requirement Traceability Report and Exploratory Session Summary. On `Defects Summary` / `Defects Detailed Report`, or when `report_type` is omitted, the filter update is skipped entirely and `report_filters` comes back null — at 200.
There is no undo and no version history. The previous definition and its filter rows are gone once this returns.
`grain` cannot be changed after creation — a differing value is 400. Resending the persisted value is accepted.
`mail_to` is only applied when the report is already scheduled AND `mail_to` is present in the body; on an unscheduled report recipients are ignored.

The response is NOT the create envelope: there is no `success` key. The report is at `data`, the computed figures at `report_data`, the resolved filters at `report_filters`. `report_data` is computed inline here, so a large report makes this call slow.

The report is resolved by id within your group — the project in the path does not scope the lookup, so a report belonging to a sibling project still resolves (404 `Schedule not found` only when no such report exists in the group). Requires the report_update permission.

The same cross-project caps as create apply, and they are re-checked against the incoming `report_type`: 60 projects overall, 5 for User Workload Report, and multi-project only for the seven supported types.

capabilities.name: update_shared_step_v1

body.name: title
body.description: Required on every call even when you are only changing steps. Read the shared step first and resend its current title; whatever you send becomes the new title.

body.name: folder_id
