The returned custom_field is partly an echo of the request: options, assigned_projects, applies_to_all_projects and link_to_future_projects are replayed from what you sent (or defaulted to false / empty), not read back from storage. Only id, field_name, field_type, entity_type and is_required are authoritative.

assigned_projects takes PR-NNN identifiers, not numeric project ids, and one unresolvable identifier fails the whole create with 400 — resolve the projects first. applies_to_all_projects:true instead walks every project in the workspace (up to about 3000) and links them all, which is a slow call on a large account.
default_value cannot be set at create time for any type. Create the field, then set it through the field edit capability, where a boolean default is sent as the string 'true' or 'false'.

These names are reserved and rejected with 400 'Field with same name already exists. Use a unique name.': Title, Description, Preconditions, Steps, Result, Attachments, State, Owner, Priority, Type of Test Case, Automation Status, Tags, Jira Issues, Asana Issues, Review Status.
Choose the type carefully — it can never be edited. Changing a field's type in practice means deleting it and creating it again, which destroys every value already stored on test cases.

nested_dropdown needs levels with at least two entries (name + level_type each) and the parent_custom_field_id key present even when null. To append one more tier to an existing nested field, send parent_custom_field_id plus field_name and nothing else.

Same stored fields as the admin-settings create capability, different contract: this route is TestCase-only, takes PR-NNN project identifiers rather than numeric ids, and answers with a serialized custom_field object instead of the raw upstream record.
Needs the field-write permission; 403 otherwise. The new field can be removed again, but any values captured on test cases in the meantime go with it.

capabilities.name: get_custom_field_v2

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: The field's numeric id, as the custom-fields listing returns it. It is validated as a positive integer before anything else runs: a non-numeric or non-positive value is 400 'Invalid Params: id must be a positive integer'. The published spec showing a prefixed 'cf-123' string is wrong.

query.name: page
query.description: Page of the datasets fetched behind this field, reflected in dataset_ids / dataset_urls. `p` is accepted as a legacy alias for the same thing. Zero or non-numeric falls back to 1 instead of erroring.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Datasets per page behind this field. Defaults to 20 here (not 30) and is clamped at 300 rather than refused. Most fields have a single dataset, so this rarely matters.

capabilities.intent: Read one custom field by its numeric id — confirm its name, type, placeholder, default and whether it is mandatory, and pick up the ids of the datasets that hold its option values
guidance: applies_to_all_projects and link_to_future_projects come back hardcoded false on this read. They are shape fillers, not the field's real project configuration — never report project scope from this response; read the field's datasets for that.
No option values are included. What you get is dataset_ids plus ready-made dataset_urls and datasets_url; follow one of those to see the choices a dropdown offers and which projects it is linked to.
An id that exists nowhere is 404 'Custom field not found', while an id that is not a positive integer is 400 — the two are distinguishable, so do not treat a 400 as 'no such field'.
The `project` query parameter documented in the spec is not read by this route. Filtering a field's option values by project is done on the dataset listing, not here.
Needs the field-view permission when role-based access is on; 403 otherwise.

Same stored definition as the admin-settings single-field read, but a different body: that one returns the field with its datasets and options inline, this one returns metadata plus dataset references.

capabilities.name: update_custom_field_v2

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: The field's numeric id. Validated as a positive integer before the field is loaded: a non-numeric or non-positive value is 400 'Invalid Params: id must be a positive integer', and an id with no field behind it is 404 'Custom field not found'.

body.name: field_name
body.description: New label. Omit it to keep the current one — this is a partial update. An empty string does NOT clear the name, it leaves the stored value untouched. Renaming onto a reserved system-field name is refused with 400.

body.name: is_required
body.description: Whether the field must be filled. Omit to keep the current setting; false is honoured (unlike the text attributes, this one is applied even when falsy). Must be a real JSON boolean.

body.name: place_holder_text
body.description: New hint text, trimmed before storage. Omit to keep the current one. An empty string does not clear it — the stored value survives.

body.name: default_value
body.description: New default. Unlike the create call this one is applied, for every field type. On a boolean field send the STRING "true" or "false" — it is coerced to "1"/"0", a real JSON boolean is rejected by the body schema, and an empty or falsy value leaves the stored default in place.

body.name: options
body.description: Replaces the dropdown's option list WHOLE on the field's existing dataset — options you leave out are removed and the values test cases hold for them are gone, in every linked project, with no undo. Send the full intended list. Ignored on non-dropdown field types.

fields.name: option_value
fields.description: The choice as the user sees it.

fields.name: is_default
fields.description: Pre-selected choice.

body.name: assigned_projects
body.description: The COMPLETE set of projects the field should apply to, as PR-NNN identifiers. It is diffed against the current links: anything currently linked and missing here is unlinked, which destroys the values stored in those projects. Use linked_projects / unlinked_projects for an incremental change.

fields.name: identifier
fields.description: A project identifier such as PR-12345.

body.name: linked_projects
body.description: Projects to ADD, as PR-NNN identifiers. Sending this (or unlinked_projects) switches off the assigned_projects diff entirely, so existing links you do not mention are left alone. An identifier that resolves to no project fails the call with 400.

fields.name: identifier
fields.description: A project identifier such as PR-12345.

body.name: unlinked_projects
body.description: Projects to REMOVE, as PR-NNN identifiers. Unlinking discards the values those projects' test cases hold for this field and cannot be undone. An unresolvable identifier fails the call with 400.

fields.name: identifier
fields.description: A project identifier such as PR-12345.

body.name: link_to_future_projects
body.description: Whether projects created later automatically offer this field. Applied to the field's dataset; sending it is itself enough to trigger the dataset write.

body.name: applies_to_all_projects
body.description: Legacy alias that here ONLY sets the future-projects flag — it does not link the projects that already exist, unlike the same flag at create time. An explicit link_to_future_projects wins over it. Use linked_projects to reach existing projects.

body.name: levels
body.description: Nested-dropdown tiers, forwarded upstream but currently ignored there for renames. Rename or retype a tier by editing that tier's own field id instead.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Existing tier field id.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Tier label.

fields.name: level_type
fields.description: Widget for the tier.

fields.name: index
fields.description: Position of the tier.

capabilities.intent: Change an existing test-case custom field — rename it, make it mandatory or optional, adjust its placeholder or default value, replace a dropdown's choices, or change which projects offer it
guidance: This is a PARTIAL update: every attribute you leave out keeps its stored value, so sending field_name alone is a valid rename. It differs from the admin-settings update capability, which is a full replace demanding field_name, field_type and is_required together.

None of it can be undone. Option lists and project links are rewritten in place, there is no bin and no prior revision: an option dropped from `options` is removed from the dataset and every value test cases hold for it disappears across all linked projects.

assigned_projects is read as the complete desired set, not an addition — any currently linked project you omit is unlinked, and the values stored there go with it. Count and name the projects you are about to drop before sending, or use linked_projects / unlinked_projects to change links one at a time.

field_type is not editable here. A field_type in the body is ignored, the stored type is kept and the call still answers 200, so never report a type change as done. A guard meant to refuse it with 400 exists but cannot fire, because the stored field is loaded after that check runs.

Empty strings do not clear anything: field_name, place_holder_text and default_value are applied only when non-empty, so the stored value survives an attempt to blank it. is_required is the exception — false is written.

Dataset-side changes (options, assigned_projects, linked_projects, unlinked_projects, link_to_future_projects, applies_to_all_projects) only take effect on dropdown, multi_dropdown and nested_dropdown fields. On any other type they are accepted, answered 200 and quietly ignored. If the field has no dataset yet, one is created.
applies_to_all_projects means something different here than at create time: it only toggles the future-projects flag and never links existing projects.

The two halves are not atomic. Field attributes are written first, the dataset second, so a failure on the dataset call leaves the rename or required-flag change already applied. Re-read the field before retrying.

The response replays options, assigned_projects, applies_to_all_projects and link_to_future_projects from your request rather than from storage — only the field attributes in it are read back. Confirm project links and option values by reading the field's datasets.
Needs the field-write permission; 403 otherwise. Unknown id is 404, a non-integer id is 400.

capabilities.name: list_reports_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

query.name: p
query.description: PAGE NUMBER, and the parameter really is named `p`. `page=2` is not read: you silently get page 1 again with a 200. Rows come back newest-created first.

query.name: page_size
query.description: Rows per page, and NOT a free range: only the literal values 30 and 300 are accepted. Anything else (5, 50, 100, 301) is refused with a 400 naming the two allowed values rather than clamped, so ask for 300 directly when you want a whole project in few calls.

query.name: is_scheduled
query.description: Narrows to recurring (scheduled) reports only, and it is a one-way switch: the filter is applied only when the value is exactly the string 'true'. is_scheduled=false applies NO filter and returns both kinds, so it cannot be used to find one-off reports — read the is_scheduled flag on each row for that.

query.name: report_type
query.description: Exact-match filter on the stored report type DISPLAY NAME, including spaces and capitals. A near-miss ('test run summary', 'Test Runs Summary') is not an error — it returns 200 with an empty list, which reads exactly like 'this project has no such reports'.

query.name: q[query]
query.description: Case-insensitive substring search across report title AND report type, matched together. The parameter is nested and must go on the wire as q[query]=term. A flat q=term is not an error and not a search: the filter is skipped and you get the full unfiltered list with a 200.

capabilities.intent: Find a project's reports — search saved and scheduled reports by title or type, see which ones run on a recurring schedule and when each next fires, or pick up the SC-NNN identifier of a report you then want to read or download
guidance: Page with `p` (NOT `page`) and `page_size`. page_size is an allow-list of exactly 30 and 300 — any other number is a 400, not a clamp — so pass 300 when you want the project in as few calls as possible.
Both one-off and scheduled reports are listed by default; is_scheduled=true narrows to scheduled ones, and nothing narrows to one-off ones.

scheduled_report_count and total_report_count describe the WHOLE filtered result set, not the page you are holding — use them to answer 'how many?' without paging, but remember any report_type / q / is_scheduled filter you sent is already baked into both numbers.

Each row's `id` is the SC-NNN identifier, and that is what the v2 single-report read and the v2 download take. It is NOT the integer report id the v1 report capabilities (report detail, report sections, drilldown, send-email-now) require: SC-NNN is a per-group sequence number, so stripping the prefix gives the wrong id. Get the integer from the v1 schedules listing, which returns `id` and `identifier` side by side on the same records.
Rows carry the report's CONFIGURATION only — type, timeframe, filters, schedule, recipients. No figures, no report data. Reading the numbers a report contains is a separate call.

`latest_attachment` is derived from the newest generated file in the whole PROJECT, not from this report — a row can advertise an attachment produced by a different report. Treat it as 'something was generated here recently', not as this report's output.
`dynamic_filters` is always null on every row, even for reports created with dynamic filters; only `report_filters` echoes back what was configured.
Cross-project reports appear under every project they cover, so the same SC-NNN can show up in more than one project's listing.

capabilities.name: create_report_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project the report is filed under, in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all. For a multi-project report this project is still the owner; the full set goes in project_ids.

body.name: report_type
body.description: What the report reports on, as a DISPLAY NAME — the set is closed and matched exactly, spaces and capitals included. Anything else is a 400 'Validation error. Invalid report type'. Never substitute a neighbour: an activity question is 'Test Case Activity', not 'Test Run Summary'.

body.name: report_timeframe
body.description: What the report covers: either a rolling window, or a mode that says the scope comes from report_filters (specific_test_runs / specific_test_plans / specific_sessions / requirements). 'custom' pairs with custom_date_range. 'specific_test_cases' exists in the data model but is rejected here with a 400 'Specific test cases are not supported yet'.

body.name: report_creation_mode
body.description: Required — a create without it is a 400 'Invalid report creation mode', despite reading like an internal flag. Use custom_report for anything a caller is setting up; system_generated marks reports the product creates for itself.

body.name: title
body.description: Display name. NOT required despite the spec marking it so: omit it and the server fills in '<report_type>-MM/DD/YYYY' (today's date), which is easy to mistake later for a report someone else made. Titles are not unique, and this is the field the list search matches on.

body.name: description
body.description: Free-text note stored with the report. Not searched by the list endpoint's query filter, which looks only at title and report type.

body.name: custom_date_range
body.description: The window for report_timeframe='custom', as ONE string holding two YYYY-MM-DD dates separated by a space — not an array and not two fields. Read only when the timeframe is 'custom'; omitting it there is accepted silently and leaves the report with no window. A start after the end, or a start later than tomorrow, is a 400.

body.name: frequency
body.description: How often the report is generated and mailed. 'once' (or omitting this) means a one-off, unscheduled report. A recurring value only takes effect when frequency_details is sent with it — frequency alone is silently ignored and you get a one-off back with a 201.

body.name: frequency_details
body.description: The when for a recurring report. Must travel WITH frequency: send either both or neither. Ignored when frequency is 'once'.

fields.name: time
fields.description: 24-hour HH:MM. Anything else ('9am', '25:99', '5:00 PM') is a 400 'Invalid report frequency'.

fields.name: day
fields.description: Required for weekly as a lowercase English day name (monday…sunday), and for monthly as a day number 1-28. Unused for daily. 29-31 are rejected.

body.name: mail_to
body.description: Recipients of the generated report. Only used when the report is genuinely recurring — for a one-off it is accepted and then ignored entirely, so nobody is emailed.

fields.name: users
fields.description: EMAIL ADDRESSES (the v1 surface took integer user ids here). Every address must belong to a user in your group; one that does not is a 400 naming the field and the address. Send [] rather than omitting the key.

fields.name: external_mails
fields.description: Addresses outside the group, not validated against any user. Send [] rather than omitting the key: a missing key fails mid-write, after the report row exists, and the server then deletes it again and answers 422.

body.name: project_ids
body.description: PR-NNN identifiers for a cross-project report. Defaults to just the project in the path. Every identifier must resolve or the call is a 400 listing each bad one. More than 60 is a 400; more than one is allowed only for the multi-project report types and, for all of them except Test Case Activity, only with the cross-project feature enabled.

body.name: report_filters
body.description: What the report is scoped to. STRICT ALLOW-LIST of exactly these four keys — any other key, including a typo or an advanced-filter name such as status, priority, assignee, requirements, folder, tc_custom_fields, is a 400 "Filter '<key>' is not supported yet". Nothing is silently dropped.

fields.name: test_runs
fields.description: TR-NNN identifiers, resolved against this project. One that does not resolve is a 400 naming the index, not a partial report.

fields.name: test_plans
fields.description: TP-NNN identifiers, or STP-NNN for a sub-plan. A sub-plan is stored without its kind, so it reads back as TP-NNN.

fields.name: session_ids
fields.description: Exploratory session ids, for the Exploratory Session Summary report. Passed through as given — not identifier-resolved.

fields.name: projects
fields.description: Project scope filter kept alongside project_ids for reports that filter by project rather than span them.

body.name: dynamic_filters
body.description: Saved filter criteria re-evaluated each run, keyed by base entity (test_run / test_case / test_plan). Custom fields and automation_state are accepted; owner, last_executed_by, created_at and updated_at are rejected with a 400. Whatever you send here is NOT echoed back on any read — the report detail always reports dynamic_filters as null.

fields.name: test_run
fields.description: Test-run criteria, e.g. status. owner / last_executed_by / created_at / updated_at inside this object are a 400.

fields.name: test_case
fields.description: Test-case criteria, e.g. custom fields or automation_state.

fields.name: test_plan
fields.description: Test-plan criteria, same rejected keys as above.

capabilities.intent: Set up a new report over a project's test data — either a one-off you will download, or a recurring daily/weekly/monthly schedule that emails chosen people; this saves the report's definition (type, window, scope, recipients) and hands back its SC-NNN identifier, it does not produce any figures
guidance: This returns a report DEFINITION, not report content. The 201 body is the saved configuration echoed back — identifier, type, timeframe, filters, schedule, recipients — and contains no counts, rows or figures at all. Never present it as the report's findings.

Getting the content afterwards is a separate, ASYNCHRONOUS step: request a download for the new SC-NNN and the server answers 202 with a job_id and a status URL, having queued the generation; then poll the matching download-status read until status flips from 'processing' to 'ready' and a file_url appears (pdf or csv only). Nothing in this create waits for that.

The alternative route to content is the v1 report reads (report detail and its section/widget reads), but those take the INTEGER report id and this API never exposes it — SC-NNN is a per-group sequence, so you cannot derive it. Resolve it through the v1 schedules listing, which carries `id` and `identifier` on the same record.

The real required set is only report_type, report_timeframe and report_creation_mode. The published spec additionally marks title, frequency, mail_to and report_filters required — they are not, and title silently defaults to '<report_type>-MM/DD/YYYY'.

Scheduling needs frequency AND frequency_details together, with frequency one of daily/weekly/monthly. Send frequency alone, or frequency:'once', and you get an unscheduled one-off back with a 201 and no warning — check is_scheduled and next_run_at in the response before telling anyone a schedule exists.

Recipients are wired up only for a recurring report: mail_to on a one-off is accepted and then ignored, so nobody is emailed. When you do send it, include BOTH users and external_mails (empty arrays are fine) — a missing key fails after the record is written, and the server deletes the half-built report and answers 422 'Failed to create report'.

Every identifier in the body is resolved before anything is written: an unknown email, TR-, TP- or PR- value comes back as a 400 with field-level errors, and nothing is persisted. Validation errors otherwise arrive as a single 400 message string prefixed 'Validation error.'

Cross-project: more than one entry in project_ids is allowed only for Test Run Summary, Test Run Detailed Report, Test Plan Summary, Test Plan Detailed Report, Test Case Activity, Requirement Traceability Report and User Workload Report (a 400 otherwise), is capped at 60 projects, and for every one of those except Test Case Activity also needs the cross-project feature enabled for the group — without it the answer is 403 'Operation not permitted'.

The only way back from this call is deleting the report, which is itself irreversible — there is no archive or trash for reports. Re-running a create with the same title does not replace anything: titles are not unique and you get a second report.

capabilities.name: get_report_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all. It is authoritative: the report must belong to this project or the read is a 404, even inside the same group.

path_params.name: report_id
path_params.description: Report identifier in SC-NNN form — the `id` field of the v2 report listing. The route is constrained to SC-\d+, so the integer report id used by the v1 report capabilities gives a routing 404 here, and SC-NNN is a per-group sequence number that cannot be converted to that integer by stripping the prefix.

capabilities.intent: Read one report's setup by its SC-NNN identifier — what it covers (type, time window, the runs/plans/sessions it is scoped to), whether it is on a schedule and when it next runs, who receives it, and whether a generated file exists; configuration only, no figures
guidance: This returns the report's CONFIGURATION, never its data — there is no report_data, no counts and no rows in the response. For the numbers inside a report, either fetch the generated file (request a download for this SC-NNN, then poll the download status until it is ready) or use the v1 report detail / section reads, which take the INTEGER report id this API never exposes; the v1 schedules listing is where SC-NNN and that integer appear together.

Every miss is the same 404 'Report not found': an identifier that does not exist, one from another group, and one that exists but belongs to a different project. A 404 therefore does not mean the report is gone — retry under the project that actually owns it, and for a cross-project report any of its projects will serve it.

`latest_attachment` is NOT this report's attachment. It is the newest generated file anywhere in the project, so it can belong to a different report, and it reports ready:true whenever it is present. Its file_type is a MIME type such as application/pdf, not the 'pdf'/'csv' the spec advertises. Only a download job you started yourself tells you about this report's file.
`dynamic_filters` is hard-coded to null on this read even when the report was created with them; only report_filters reflects configured scope.

report_filters echoes public identifiers rather than the internal ids stored (TR-NNN, TP-NNN, assignee emails). Two caveats: a sub-plan filter comes back as TP-NNN because the sub-plan marker is not kept, and if the upstream identifier lookup fails the values degrade to prefix+raw-id which may not be a real identifier.

`frequency` reads 'once' for an unscheduled report — that is a substitution for a stored null, not something the report was created with. Trust `is_scheduled` and `next_run_at` for whether anything will actually fire.
`project_ids` lists every project a cross-project report covers, and `project_id` is only the owning one.

capabilities.name: list_entity_attachments_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

path_params.name: entity_type
path_params.description: Which kind of parent item to read attachments from. A CLOSED set of exactly these three hyphenated plurals, enforced in the route. Singular or snake_case spellings (test-case, test_case, testcase, test_results) do not match the route and come back as a routing 404 with no JSON body, not a validation error naming the field. Test runs and exploratory sessions are not attachable here.

path_params.name: entity_id
path_params.description: Form depends on entity_type: TC-NNN identifier for test-cases (resolved by identifier lookup; the internal integer case id gives 404 'Test case not found'), the plain INTEGER result id for test-results (no TR- prefix - that is a run), TP-NNN or STP-NNN for test-plans. The route leaves this segment unconstrained, so a wrong form is a 404 from the resolver rather than a 400.

query.name: p
query.description: PAGE NUMBER, and the parameter really is named `p`. `page=2` is not read: you silently get page 1 again. 0 is treated as 1.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Rows per page. Unlike the v2 run and result listings this is a real range, not an allow-list of 30/300 - any value up to 300 is honoured. Above 300 the call is refused with 400 'parameter_error' ('Page limit exceeds the maximum limit of 300'). A non-numeric or absent value is NOT an error: it silently falls back to 30, so a typo quietly shortens your page.

query.name: file_type
query.description: Filter by the attachment's content type, matched as a prefix - `image` keeps every image/* row, `application/pdf` only PDFs. Applied upstream; an unmatched value returns an empty list rather than an error.

query.name: uploaded_by
query.description: Filter by uploader, as the INTERNAL NUMERIC user id - not an email and not a username. The value is coerced with to_i, so a non-numeric value such as an email address becomes 0 and matches nothing while still returning 200. Resolve the user id from a project users read before filtering.

capabilities.intent: List the files attached to one test case, test result or test plan - use this to see what screenshots, logs or evidence are on the item and to get the URL for reading each file
guidance: One route serves all three parent types; entity_type is a closed set of exactly `test-cases`, `test-results` and `test-plans`, spelled hyphenated and plural. Anything else, including the singular or snake_case form, fails to match the route and returns a bare 404 rather than telling you the value was wrong.

entity_id is the trap: it is an IDENTIFIER for two of the three types and an integer for the other. test-cases wants TC-NNN (the internal integer id 404s 'Test case not found'), test-plans wants TP-NNN or STP-NNN, and test-results wants the plain integer result id - the one a v2 test-results listing returns as `id`. There is no route constraint on the segment, so the wrong form always surfaces as a 404 from the resolver, never a 400.

A test-result id that belongs to another project is rejected with 404 'Test result not found' rather than an empty list, so a 404 here means wrong id or wrong project, not an item with no attachments.

Page with `p` (NOT `page`) and `per_page`. per_page defaults to 30 and the real ceiling is 300; ask for 300 directly instead of walking pages of 30. Over 300 is a 400 'parameter_error'; a non-numeric value is silently treated as 30.

Rows are deliberately thin: id, name, size in bytes, created_at and url. Despite what the reference spec shows, this listing carries no content_type, byte_size, checksum or download_url. Read the file straight from `url` - there is no separate download capability for these attachments.

Inline attachments are always included. Images embedded in a description through the rich-text editor come back alongside real file attachments and carry an extra `data_id`, so this count can exceed what the item's attachment panel shows.

Prefer this over the v1 test-case attachments read whenever you hold a TC-/TP- identifier, need a test result's or plan's files, or want paging and file-type / uploader filtering. The v1 read handles test cases only, needs the integer project, folder and case ids, and returns every row in one unpaginated response.
`info` carries page, page_size, count, prev and next - use `count` to decide whether another page is worth fetching instead of paging until you get an empty array.

capabilities.name: search_test_results_v1

query.name: issue_id
query.description: The tracker issue whose linked results you want — the issue KEY as the tracker shows it (Jira 'BUG-123', not a numeric id). Forwarded verbatim with no validation, so a wrong or unknown key comes back as an empty list with success:true, never an error. This is the filter the Jira/ADO issue panel uses.

query.name: issue_type
query.description: Which tracker issue_id belongs to. Send it alongside issue_id — results store the tracker name on each link, so omitting it can match links from another tracker. Trackers the product stores links for: jira, azure, asana, linear, clickup, confluence, figma, devrev, gitlab, github, trello, onedrive, google-drive, sharepoint, zoho, custom. Not validated here.

query.name: priority
query.description: Narrow to results whose case carries this priority. Forwarded verbatim, matched against the project's configured priorities — the out-of-the-box set is low / medium / high / critical, but a project may rename or add values, so resolve the real list rather than assuming. An unmatched value yields an empty list, not an error.

query.name: compact
query.description: Shape switch, compared as a literal STRING against 'false'. Only compact=false expands each row with its test_run and test_case objects; every other value (including omitting it, and including boolean false serialised oddly) gives the lean shape with issues and configuration only. Rows always carry issues and configuration whatever you send.

query.name: include_relations
query.description: Read and then thrown away: the action overwrites it unconditionally from the compact switch before the search runs, on BOTH branches. Asking for a relation here has no effect at all and no error. Use compact=false to get test_run and test_case; there is no way to request any other relation on this endpoint.

query.name: p
query.description: PAGE NUMBER, and the parameter is named `p` — `page=2` is not read and silently returns page 1. A value that is not a strictly positive integer (0, -1, 'abc', or a repeated/array form) is rejected before the action with HTTP 400 {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'}.

query.name: per_page
query.description: NOT a page size — a presence flag, and its value is discarded. Sending per_page at ALL (per_page=100, per_page=1, anything non-blank) SHRINKS the page to 10 rows; omitting it entirely gives 30 rows, the maximum this endpoint can return. Omit it whenever you want the fewest round trips.

query.name: q
query.description: Optional wrapper for the same filters, e.g. q[issue_id]=BUG-123&q[issue_type]=jira. When q is present the flat top-level filters are IGNORED and only q's contents are read, and they reach the search service in a different (query_object) shape. It must be a nested param hash — a JSON-encoded STRING here raises and 500s. p and per_page are still read from the top level. Prefer the flat form.

fields.name: issue_id
fields.description: Same as the top-level issue_id.

fields.name: issue_type
fields.description: Same as the top-level issue_type.

fields.name: priority
fields.description: Same as the top-level priority.

fields.name: compact
fields.description: Same string-literal 'false' switch as the top-level compact.

fields.name: include_relations
fields.description: Overwritten from compact exactly as at the top level; it does nothing.

capabilities.intent: Find test results anywhere in the account without knowing the project, run or case — above all, list every result linked to a tracker issue (a Jira/ADO ticket key) to answer 'what testing covers this bug?', optionally narrowed by case priority
guidance: This is NOT a project read and it takes no project. The action replaces whatever project context arrived with a placeholder before calling the search service, so the search spans every project in the authenticated user's group (account) and is scoped by nothing but your filters and that group. Passing a project_id query param cannot narrow it — a numeric one you lack access to only makes the call 404 before the search runs, and a PR-NNN one is ignored outright.

Use this when the only handle you have is an issue key, or when you need results across projects and runs. When you already know project + run + case and want that case's result history, use the per-case reads (get_test_results_for_test_case / get_test_results_for_test_case_v2) instead — they are scoped, richer, and cannot silently span the account.

Failures are swallowed. An upstream search error is logged and the request STILL answers HTTP 200 with success:true, an empty test_results array and info:null. An empty list is therefore not evidence that nothing matched — treat info:null as 'the search did not run' and retry rather than reporting zero results.

Page with `p`, never `page`, and do NOT send per_page: its value is discarded and its mere presence cuts the page from 30 rows to 10. 30 is the hard ceiling here; there is no way to ask for more, so a large issue's results must be walked page by page.

The only filters that exist are issue_id, issue_type and priority. There is no status, date, project, run, case or assignee filter on this endpoint — anything else you need must be filtered from the returned rows yourself.

Row shape changes with compact. With compact=false you get test_run and test_case objects, and `test_run_id` is then overwritten with the run's TR-NNN identifier string. Without it there are no test_run/test_case objects and test_run_id / test_case_id come from the result mapping as integers — so the same field name carries a different type depending on one query flag. Never assume test_run_id is numeric.

Rows carry no custom fields and no step results, and `links.self` appears only for rows that came back with a project_id. To read a result's custom fields, follow up with the project-scoped single-result reads using the row's project_id and id.

issue_id and issue_type are always forwarded even when absent, so calling with no filters at all is a legal account-wide dump of recent results — expensive and rarely what you want. Send at least one filter.

capabilities.name: list_test_run_test_case_comments_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Numeric project id (the v1 route accepts only digits here, not PR-NNN). Resolve it from the project listing.

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Test run identifier as TR-NNN (preferred), or the run's bare integer id. A pair that does not resolve to a case in this run is a 400 'TRTC not found', not a 404.

path_params.name: test_case_id
path_params.description: The test case's NUMERIC id, not its TC-NNN identifier — the route only matches digits, so TC-12 never reaches the API. Take it from the `id` field of a v1 test case read or of a row in the v1 run test-case listing (the TC-NNN is that row's `identifier`).

query.name: mappingId
query.description: Id of the test-case-in-run mapping row (one per configuration the case is mapped to). The spec marks it REQUIRED; the server accepts the call without it and resolves the pair itself, but when a case is mapped to several configurations only this picks the exact cell, and threads differ per cell. Send it when you have it. A value that does not match this run/case pair is a 400.

query.name: p
query.description: PAGE NUMBER — the parameter really is named `p`; `page=2` is ignored and you get page 1 again. Page size is fixed at 30 and cannot be changed. A page past the end does NOT error or come back empty: the server serves the LAST page again, so stop when info.next is null rather than when a page is empty. 0 or a non-number is a 400.

capabilities.intent: List the comments left on a test case inside a specific test run — use this to read the discussion or review feedback on that execution, find who said what and when, or discover a comment's id
guidance: Needs the test-case VIEW permission (a 403 'This action is not permitted for the user' otherwise) AND a paid plan: on a free plan the call still returns HTTP 200 with {success:false, error:'This Feature is only for paid customers'} — check `success` in the body, not the status code.

Three ids in the path, two conventions: project_id and test_case_id are plain INTEGERS (a TC-NNN in the case slot never matches the route), while test_run_id takes the TR-NNN identifier or the bare integer. Get the numeric case id from the `id` field of a v1 test case read or of the v1 run test-case listing.

A run/case pair that does not resolve is a 400 with message 'TRTC not found for given testrun_id:…' — not a 404 — and an automation (Automate/Observability) run is a 400 'Can't comment on automation test'. A test case that does not exist in your group is a bare {success:false} 404.

Comments are threaded per run/case/configuration cell. If the case is mapped to more than one configuration in the run, pass mappingId to pick the cell; without it the server resolves a cell itself and you may read a different thread than the UI shows.

Newest first (by id), 30 per page, no page-size control. `info.count` is the total across pages; walk `p` until `info.next` is null — asking for a page beyond the end silently returns the last page again, so an 'empty page' loop never terminates.

Each row's `comment` is HTML with @mentions already rendered to display names; `user_id` is an OBJECT {id, full_name, email} whose `id` is the internal TM user id (null for imported comments, which show the original author's name). `edited` is true when the comment was changed after posting.
This is the only way to discover comment ids. Reading comments still works on an archived test case; posting does not.
Comments on a test case outside a run (folder-scoped) and on test plans are separate surfaces not exposed in this pass.

capabilities.name: create_test_run_test_case_comment_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Numeric project id (the v1 route accepts only digits here, not PR-NNN). Resolve it from the project listing.

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Test run identifier as TR-NNN (preferred), or the run's bare integer id. A pair that does not resolve to a case in this run is a 400 'TRTC not found', not a 404.

path_params.name: test_case_id
path_params.description: The test case's NUMERIC id, not its TC-NNN identifier — the route only matches digits, so TC-12 never reaches the API. Take it from the `id` field of a v1 test case read or of a row in the v1 run test-case listing (the TC-NNN is that row's `identifier`).

query.name: mappingId
query.description: Id of the test-case-in-run mapping row (one per configuration the case is mapped to). The spec marks it REQUIRED; the server accepts the call without it and resolves the pair itself, but when a case is mapped to several configurations only this picks the exact cell, and threads differ per cell. Send it when you have it. A value that does not match this run/case pair is a 400.

body.name: comment
body.example: Failed on Safari 17 only — retest after the fix for TM-1234 lands.
body.description: Comment body as HTML (rich text), nested as {"comment": {"comment": "..."}}. Whitespace-only or tag-only content is a 400 'Please enter valid comment' (an counts). Any other key inside the `comment` object is a 400 'Invalid JSON data'. To @mention: Name with the BrowserStack user id; someone outside the group is a 403.

capabilities.intent: Post a comment on a test case within a test run — use this to leave review feedback on an execution, ask the run owner a question, record why a result was marked as it was, or @mention a colleague
guidance:
Send the body as application/json with the nested shape {"comment": {"comment": "

text

"}} — the field is named comment inside an object also named comment. Without a JSON content type the schema check is skipped and the call fails later with a less helpful 400.

Needs the test-case VIEW permission (not a write permission) and a paid plan. Below a paid plan the call returns HTTP 200 with {success:false, error:'This Feature is only for paid customers'} and nothing is posted — check `success` in the body.

SIDE EFFECT: the run owner is notified of every new comment, and every @mentioned user gets a mention alert, immediately and outside this API. The author never alerts themselves. Confirm wording with the user before posting on their behalf.

Cannot post on an automation run (400 'Can't comment on automation test') or on an ARCHIVED test case (bare {success:false} 400 — reading still works). A run/case pair that does not resolve is a 400 'TRTC not found for given testrun_id:…', not a 404.

If the case is mapped to several configurations in the run, pass mappingId so the comment lands on the intended cell; each cell has its own thread and the listing for a different mappingId will not show it.

@mentions must be the span markup with data-id set to the person's BrowserStack user id; a mention with no id is a 403 'Missing User Id in comment', one for a user not in this group is a 403 'User does not belong to this project', and either fails the whole post. Plain '@name' text mentions nobody.

Link markup in the HTML is normalised server-side and mention spans are rewritten, so the stored `comment` returned in the response can differ from what you sent; use the returned `id` for any follow-up.

Success is HTTP 200 (not 201) with the new comment under data.comment. Recoverable: the author can edit or delete the comment afterwards in the product (delete hides it rather than destroying it) — those operations are not part of this pass.
Only the in-run variant is published here; commenting on a test case outside a run, or on a test plan, is a separate surface not exposed in this pass.

capabilities.name: export_test_run_csv_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Numeric project id. This older route does not accept the PR-NNN form: a PR- prefixed value skips project resolution and the call fails with a 500 rather than a clear 404. Take the integer id from the projects listing.

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Run identifier TR-NNN, or the plain integer run id. Anything else does not match the route. An identifier that resolves to no run in this project is a 404 'Test Run ID is invalid'.

body.name: file_type
body.description: Export format. Only 'csv' is accepted; any other value is a 422 'Only CSV file type is supported.' before anything is queued.

body.name: required
body.description: Optional column selection keyed by entity: {test_run_test_case:{fields:[..]}, test_run:{fields:[..]}, test_result:{fields:[..]}}. Omit to export EVERY supported column. `fields` may be an array or comma-separated string; 'all' expands to every supported column. Unknown column names are NOT rejected: the call still returns 200 and the export fails later on the realtime channel.

fields.name: test_run_test_case
fields.description: {fields:[...]} — supported: id, title, priority, test_case_status, owner, folder_id, folder_path, case_type, automation_status, description, preconditions, template, steps, issues, tags, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by, attachments, result_status, assignee, configurations, dataset_values, project, estimated_duration_seconds.

fields.name: test_run
fields.description: {fields:[...]} — supported: id, title, created_at, created_by, state, tags, owner, type, updated_by, updated_at, requirements.

fields.name: test_result
fields.description: {fields:[...]} — supported: attachments, defects, updated_at, updated_by, description, time_elapsed.

capabilities.intent: Start a CSV export of a test run's cases and their latest results — use this when the user wants the run's contents as a downloadable spreadsheet file rather than data returned inline
guidance: The response carries no file and no download link. It only confirms that a background job was queued and returns a `channel` uuid. The CSV is built asynchronously, stored, and its time-limited download link is pushed to the requesting user's web session over a realtime channel; that push carries the same uuid as `id` so the UI can match it. Nothing in this HTTP API returns the link afterwards, so tell the user the file will appear in their Test Management browser session (download notification) rather than promising to hand it back.

A 200 means 'queued', not 'exported'. Failures inside the job (bad column names, upstream errors) surface only as a failure message on that realtime channel, never as an HTTP error, so this call cannot be polled for completion.
The whole run is exported: no filter or search criteria are honoured, and the export is capped at 20,000 rows fetched 300 at a time — a larger run is silently truncated at 20,000 rows.

Column selection defaults to ALL supported columns when `required` is omitted. Each test-case step after the first becomes its own extra row under the case, so row counts in the file exceed the case count.

This is a write only in the sense that it creates a stored export artifact; it does not change the run. It carries no run-specific permission check in this service (the action is absent from the permissions map), so any user who can reach the project can trigger it; plan or product-access gates still apply as a 403.
Works for automation runs as well as manual ones (the run lookup deliberately ignores run type). Closed runs export too.
Unlike the newer run endpoints, project_id must be the plain integer; the run may be given as TR-14 or its integer id.

404.description: Project not found, or the test run identifier resolves to no run in this project ('Test Run ID is invalid. Please enter valid Test Run ID and try again' / 'Test run not found.').

422.description: file_type was not 'csv': {success:false, message:'Only CSV file type is supported.'}

capabilities.name: get_test_run_progress_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Numeric project id. This older route does not accept the PR-NNN form: a PR- prefixed value skips project resolution and the call fails with a 500 rather than a clear 404. Take the integer id from the projects listing.

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Run identifier TR-NNN, or the plain integer run id. Anything else does not match the route. An identifier that resolves to no run in this project is a 404 'Test Run ID is invalid'.

query.name: configuration_id
query.description: Narrow to ONE configuration of the run. Changes the response shape: with it you get a single `overall_progress_by_status_id` breakdown (an empty object when there is no data); without it you get a paginated `configurations` array, each row carrying its own breakdown. Configuration ids come from the run detail's `configurations` list.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number for the configurations list, and the parameter really is named `p` (`page` is ignored). Only meaningful without configuration_id. 0, negative or non-numeric is a 400 'Invalid Params'. Page size is fixed at 30 and cannot be changed — there is no per-page parameter on this endpoint.

capabilities.intent: Get pass/fail/untested progress of a test run broken down by result status — per configuration (browser/device) across the whole run, or for one configuration — to answer 'how far along is this run on each configuration?'
guidance: Two response shapes from one endpoint, chosen by configuration_id. Without it: {success, configurations:[{id, name, ..., overall_progress_by_status_id}], info}. With it: {success, overall_progress_by_status_id}. Read the shape you asked for.

overall_progress_by_status_id is a map keyed by result-status id (as a string), each value {count, result_status:{id, field_value, internal_name, field_name, colour}}. Status ids are project-specific — use result_status.internal_name (e.g. 'passed') to compare across projects, not the numeric key.

A configuration row without any executed results may carry no overall_progress_by_status_id key at all, and the single-configuration form returns {} when there is no breakdown. Treat a missing or empty breakdown as 'nothing recorded', not as an error.

Paging: pass `p`; the page is always 30 configurations and there is no way to ask for more per page. When `p` is omitted no paging hints are sent upstream and the default page size is decided by the backing service, so send p=1 explicitly when you intend to walk pages. `info` is the backing service's paging block, passed through unchanged.
For a run-wide total (not per configuration) use the single-run detail instead — its overall_progress already aggregates across configurations.

Any upstream failure inside the calculation is reported as a 500 {success:false, message:'Failed to calculate configuration progress: ...'}, not as a 404 or 400. An unknown run identifier is still a 404 because the run is resolved before the calculation.
No run-specific permission is checked in this service (the action is absent from the permissions map); it is also one of the endpoints reachable with a public share-link token for a run.

400.description: `p` was 0, negative or non-numeric: {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'}

404.description: Project not found, or the test run identifier resolves to no run in this project.

500.description: Progress calculation failed (including upstream errors): {success:false, message:'Failed to calculate configuration progress: <reason>'}

capabilities.name: generate_test_case_automation_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id (the v1 route only matches digits; a PR-NNN identifier never reaches the API).

path_params.name: test_case_id
path_params.description: Integer test case id (not TC-NNN). The case is loaded from the entity store first, so an unknown id is a 404 before anything is submitted.

body.name: version
body.description: Payload flavour forwarded to the automation service. Anything other than 'v2' takes the v1 path and forwards `steps`; 'v2' forwards `test_case_details` + `tags` (+ preTestConfig) instead and REQUIRES test_case_details — with version=v2 and no test_case_details the request 500s.

body.name: test_name
body.description: Display name for the generated automation test. Forwarded verbatim; not validated here.

body.name: base_url
body.description: URL the generated automation starts from. Forwarded verbatim (also lifted into batch defaults on the bulk-pipeline path); not validated here.

body.name: credentials
body.description: Login credentials the automation may use, forwarded verbatim to the automation service. Not stored in Test Management.

body.name: local_enabled
body.description: Run against a BrowserStack Local tunnel. Defaults to false when omitted.

body.name: lcnc_link
body.description: Existing automation build link (the case's metadata.lcnc_build_map link) when RE-automating. Its mere presence switches the submission from mode 'new' to 'reautomate'; omit it for a first-time automation.

body.name: steps
body.description: v1 flow only: the test steps as plain strings. Ignored when version=v2.

body.name: test_case_details
body.description: v2 flow only: {name, identifier, description, preconditions, test_case_steps[]} of the case, echoed to the automation service (it does not re-read the case). Required when version=v2 (missing → 500); ignored otherwise.

body.name: feedback
body.description: v2 flow only: free-text feedback on a previous generation, forwarded inside test_case_details.

body.name: score
body.description: v2 flow only: rating of a previous generation, forwarded inside test_case_details.

body.name: tags
body.description: v2 flow only: tags forwarded with the payload. Elements are strings.

body.name: preTestConfig
body.description: v2 flow only: pre-test configuration object (setup steps/profile) forwarded verbatim when present.

body.name: test_case_folder_id
body.description: Folder id of the case. Only read on the bulk-pipeline submission path (environment flag); harmless otherwise.

body.name: folder_id
body.description: Folder id of the case; when sent the folder is loaded for an ownership check and passed to the case lookup. Optional; an unknown folder fails the call.

capabilities.intent: Kick off no-code (LCNC / Low Code Automation) generation of an automated test for ONE test case — use this when the user wants a manual case automated or re-automated; it queues work in the automation service and returns immediately
guidance: Asynchronous and non-blocking: a 200 means the request was handed to the automation service, not that a test exists. Completion arrives later via a webhook that stamps the case's automation metadata (lcnc status 'done' + build link); re-read the case to see it.

The response is a WRAPPER {status, body}: `status` is the automation service's own HTTP code and `body` is its response as a JSON-ENCODED STRING you must parse — except the 'already in progress' short-circuit, where body is a plain object. Check body.status/body.message: a 4xx inside the wrapper (still HTTP 200 outside) means nothing was queued.

One generation at a time: while the case's automation status is 'in_progress' every call returns 200 with body.message 'Test case automation already in progress.' and does nothing. The in-progress lock is only set when the upstream accepted the request, and a worker clears it after 1 hour even if no webhook came back — so a stuck case becomes resubmittable after an hour.

No field is validated in Test Management: the body is assembled from whatever you send and forwarded. Missing test_name/base_url/steps are not rejected here; the automation service decides. Only version=v2 without test_case_details fails locally (500).
Re-automation is signalled ONLY by lcnc_link being present. To generate a fresh automation for a case that already has one, omit lcnc_link.
Groups flagged for regional data restriction (GRR) are refused with 451 {success:false, error:'grr_restricted'} unless the group's region is allow-listed (currently only 'in').
There is no RBAC permission on this action beyond project access and authentication — any project member can trigger generation.
Recoverability: the only thing changed in Test Management is the case's automation metadata (status/link), which the next generation or the expiry worker overwrites; the case itself is untouched.

451.description: Group is GRR-restricted and its region is not allow-listed for automation generation.

message.example: This action is restricted for GRR enabled users

capabilities.name: list_binned_test_cases_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id (the v1 route only matches digits; a PR-NNN identifier never reaches the API).

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. `page` is accepted as an alias and WINS if both are sent. Only `p` is validated (non-positive / non-numeric → 400 'Invalid Params'); a bad `page` is forwarded as-is.

query.name: limit
query.description: Rows per page, forwarded unchanged to the backing service, which owns the default and the ceiling (its client docs say default 25, max 100; not enforced in this codebase — see open questions). Ask for what you need and trust metadata.page_size for what you got.

query.name: search
query.description: Free-text match on test case title or identifier.

query.name: folder_id
query.description: Only cases that lived in this folder when they were binned.

query.name: moved_to_bin_by
query.description: Filter by who moved the case to the bin, as BrowserStack user id(s), comma-separated. `updated_by` is an accepted alias (moved_to_bin_by wins). These are browserstack_user_ids, NOT the internal user ids the review endpoints take.

query.name: owner
query.description: Filter by case owner as BrowserStack user id(s), comma-separated.

query.name: date_from
query.description: Binned on or after this ISO 8601 date.

query.name: date_to
query.description: Binned on or before this ISO 8601 date.

query.name: sort_by
query.description: Sort column; default is when the case was binned.

query.name: sort_order
query.description: Sort direction; upper-case only.

query.name: status
query.description: Filter by status as numeric status ID(s), comma-separated — despite the UI-style name this takes ids, not display values (resolve them via get_system_field_values_v1). `status_id` is an accepted alias (status wins).

query.name: priority
query.description: Filter by priority as numeric priority ID(s), comma-separated, not display values. `priority_id` is an accepted alias (priority wins).

query.name: type
query.description: Filter by case type as numeric category ID(s), comma-separated, not display values. `category_id` is an accepted alias (type wins).

query.name: automation_state
query.description: Filter by automation state as numeric ID(s), comma-separated. `automation_state_id` is an accepted alias (automation_state wins).

query.name: tags
query.description: Filter by tag name(s), comma-separated.

capabilities.intent: List the test cases sitting in a project's recycle bin (moved to bin / soft-deleted, awaiting purge) with who binned them and when — use this to find a case to restore or inspect; for just 'how many are in the bin' use count_binned_test_cases_v1 instead
guidance: Feature-gated: when the project/user lacks the Move to Bin or New Project Settings flags the call is 403 {success:false, error:'... is not enabled for this user'} — that is a feature gap, not a permission problem. Needs the tc_view permission under RBAC.
Paging metadata is under `metadata` {total, page, page_size, total_pages}, NOT the `info` {count, next, prev} envelope other v1 listings use — there is no `next`; stop when page >= total_pages.

Rows carry the integer `id`, the TC-NNN `identifier`, `trashed_at`, `days_remaining` until automatic purge, and `folder_name`/`folder_path` of where the case was. `updated_by` and `owner` are raw BrowserStack user ids; the resolved people are in `updator_details` (who binned it) and `owner_details` {id, browserstack_user_id, full_name, email}.
priority and status come back as small objects {id, field_value, internal_name} (status also has colour), not strings.
Only the filters listed exist. Binned cases are excluded from every other test case listing and search, so this is the only way to see them.
A backing-service failure is rendered as {success:false} with that service's status and no message.

capabilities.name: count_binned_test_cases_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id (the v1 route only matches digits; a PR-NNN identifier never reaches the API).

capabilities.intent: Return just the number of test cases currently in a project's recycle bin — the cheap way to answer 'how many binned/deleted cases are there?' without pulling any rows into context (use list_binned_test_cases_v1 when you need the cases themselves)
guidance: Same feature gate as the bin listing: 403 {success:false, error:'... is not enabled for this user'} when Move to Bin / New Project Settings are off for this user. Needs tc_view under RBAC.
Counts the whole bin; it takes no filters. For a filtered count, call the listing with the filter and read metadata.total.
A backing-service failure is {success:false} with that service's status and no count.

200.description: Number of test cases in the bin.

capabilities.name: submit_test_cases_for_review_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id (the v1 route only matches digits; a PR-NNN identifier never reaches the API).

body.name: ids
body.description: Integer ids of the test cases to send for review. A single case is just a one-element array. Ignored when select_all is true (the set then comes from q/folder_id). Send ONE of ids, select_all or folders; a selection that resolves to zero cases is a bare 400 {success:false} with no message.

body.name: select_all
body.description: Apply to every case in scope (the top-level q filter plus folder_id, or the whole project when neither is sent) minus de_selected_ids. Compared as the string 'true'. Scope is resolved by a count first, and a count above 100 flips the call to the async path.

body.name: de_selected_ids
body.description: Integer ids to exclude. With select_all it is subtracted from the resolved scope; with an explicit ids list it is subtracted from ids.

body.name: folders

fields.name: <folder_id>
fields.description: One entry per folder id: {select_all: bool, ids: [int], de_selected_ids: [int]}. Unknown keys inside an entry are dropped.

body.description: Cross-folder selection keyed by folder id, each value {select_all, ids[], de_selected_ids[]}; the union of all entries is the target. Takes precedence over ids/select_all when present. An empty map selects nothing (400), never the whole project.

body.name: q
body.description: SCOPE for select_all — the same filter object the test-case search takes (see bulk_archive_test_cases_by_project / search_test_cases_by_folder_v1), sent as a SIBLING of test_case, not inside it. Only read when select_all is true. An unrecognised key is SILENTLY DROPPED, which widens the scope to the whole folder/project — verify the count before sending.

body.name: folder_id
body.description: Folder to scope a select_all selection to (merged into q as folder_id, overriding any q.folder_id). With explicit ids it only makes the folder be loaded for an ownership check; an unknown folder id fails the call.

body.name: include_subfolders_tc
body.description: Extend a folder-scoped select_all into subfolders of folder_id. Compared as the string 'true'.

body.name: reviewers
body.description: INTERNAL Test Management user ids of the reviewers (the `id` from search_project_users / get_project_users_v2_v1 — not browserstack_user_id, not email). Replaces the current reviewer set. Each id must belong to the caller's account (else 422 reviewer_not_found) and, when the project keeps an allowed-reviewer list, be on it (else 422). Omit to change status only. Elements are integers.

body.name: review_status
body.description: The review state to move the selected cases into. Send 'in_review' to submit for review; it is forwarded to the backing store as a replace. Verdicts (approved/rejected/changes_requested) are NOT applied here — use apply_test_case_review_verdict_v1.

body.name: comment
body.description: Note to the reviewers. It is only carried in the reviewer notification when reviewers are given — it is NOT stored as a comment on the cases.

body.name: reauth_token
body.description: Single-use e-signature token from the Part 11 re-authentication step (the caller re-enters email + password at the reauth endpoint, which is not in this index, and gets back reauth_token). Valid 5 minutes, consumed atomically on first use — a retry needs a fresh token. Only checked when the project's Part 11 setting for this action is on.

capabilities.intent: Send one or many test cases for review — set them to 'in review' and assign the reviewers who must approve them; use it for a single case (ids with one element) or a whole selection/folder at once
guidance: Needs the project setting review_approve ON (else 400 {errors:'Please enable review approve feature ...'}) and a Team or Pro plan (else 422 {success:false, message:'Feature not available'}). No RBAC permission entry exists for this action, so any authenticated project member with those two passes.

Part 11 e-signature: when the project setting part_11_reauth_send_for_review is 'true', the caller must first re-authenticate (email + password at the reauth endpoint, not in this index) and pass the returned reauth_token; missing/expired/reused → 401 {success:false, error_code:'reauth_required'} and the block is written to the audit log.

Selections over 100 cases run asynchronously: the response is {success:true, async:true, unique_id} with NO testCases — the change lands in the background and you re-read the cases to confirm. Under the threshold the updated cases are returned inline.

Reviewer ids are the internal Test Management user id; the same people are addressed by browserstack_user_id in the bin listing filters, so do not carry ids across. A reviewer who is not on the project's allowed-reviewer list is refused (422) for the whole call — nothing is partially applied.
Cases locked by another bulk operation are refused with 400 {success:false, message:'TestCases in progress with another operation'}; retry after it finishes.
Every other failure collapses to 400 {errors:'An error occurred during bulk review'} — including backing-service errors — so a 400 is not necessarily a bad request.
Recoverable: review state is a tracked status; a reviewer verdict or a later edit moves the case on, and each case keeps version history.
Sending reviewers notifies them (in-app alert / email) immediately.

capabilities.name: apply_test_case_review_verdict_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id (the v1 route only matches digits; a PR-NNN identifier never reaches the API).

body.name: ids
body.description: Integer ids of the test cases to give a verdict on. A single case is just a one-element array. Ignored when select_all is true (the set then comes from q/folder_id). Send ONE of ids, select_all or folders; a selection that resolves to zero cases is a bare 400 {success:false} with no message.

body.name: select_all
body.description: Apply to every case in scope (the top-level q filter plus folder_id, or the whole project when neither is sent) minus de_selected_ids. Compared as the string 'true'. Scope is resolved by a count first, and a count above 100 flips the call to the async path.

body.name: de_selected_ids
body.description: Integer ids to exclude. With select_all it is subtracted from the resolved scope; with an explicit ids list it is subtracted from ids.

body.name: folders

fields.name: <folder_id>
fields.description: One entry per folder id: {select_all: bool, ids: [int], de_selected_ids: [int]}. Unknown keys inside an entry are dropped.

body.description: Cross-folder selection keyed by folder id, each value {select_all, ids[], de_selected_ids[]}; the union of all entries is the target. Takes precedence over ids/select_all when present. An empty map selects nothing (400), never the whole project.

body.name: q
body.description: SCOPE for select_all — the same filter object the test-case search takes (see bulk_archive_test_cases_by_project / search_test_cases_by_folder_v1), sent as a SIBLING of test_case, not inside it. Only read when select_all is true. An unrecognised key is SILENTLY DROPPED, which widens the scope to the whole folder/project — verify the count before sending.

body.name: folder_id
body.description: Folder to scope a select_all selection to (merged into q as folder_id, overriding any q.folder_id). With explicit ids it only makes the folder be loaded for an ownership check; an unknown folder id fails the call.

body.name: include_subfolders_tc
body.description: Extend a folder-scoped select_all into subfolders of folder_id. Compared as the string 'true'.

body.name: review_status
body.description: The verdict: 'approved' passes the case, 'rejected' fails it, 'changes_requested' sends it back to the author for edits. Applied to every selected case; there is no per-case verdict in one call.

body.name: comment
body.description: Review comment. Unlike the submit-for-review comment this one IS stored: one comment is created on each selected case, tagged with the verdict, and echoed back under `comment`. Strongly recommended for rejected/changes_requested.

body.name: notify
body.description: Compared as the string 'true'. Also email the case owners the verdict (in-app personal alerts go out regardless).

body.name: reauth_token
body.description: Single-use e-signature token from the Part 11 re-authentication step (the caller re-enters email + password at the reauth endpoint, which is not in this index, and gets back reauth_token). Valid 5 minutes, consumed atomically on first use — a retry needs a fresh token. Only checked when the project's Part 11 setting for this action is on.

capabilities.intent: Record a reviewer's verdict on test cases that are under review — approve them, reject them, or request changes — for one case or a whole selection in a single call
guidance: Every selected case must currently be 'in_review'. If any is not (the author edited it and it dropped back to pending, or it was already decided) the WHOLE call is refused with 422 {success:false, error_code:'invalid_review_state'} and nothing is applied — re-read the cases and resubmit only the ones still under review.

Needs project setting review_approve ON (else 400 {errors:'Please enable review approve feature ...'}) and a Team or Pro plan (else 422 'Feature not available'). No RBAC permission entry exists for this action beyond project access.

Part 11 e-signature: when project setting part_11_reauth is 'true', every verdict value requires a fresh reauth_token from the re-authentication step (not in this index); missing/expired/reused → 401 {success:false, error_code:'reauth_required'}.

Selections over 100 cases are applied asynchronously: {success:true, async:true, unique_id} with no testCases; re-read to confirm. Below that the updated cases come back inline, plus `comment` (the created comment objects) when a comment was sent.
Cases locked by another bulk operation → 400 {success:false, message:'TestCases in progress with another operation'}.

When the backing store rejects the verdict (e.g. the audit-log write fails) its status is passed through with {success:false, error_code, errors}; the verdict was not applied. Any other failure is a generic 400 {success:false, errors:'An error occurred during bulk approval'}.
Recoverable: a verdict is a tracked review status — the author can edit and resubmit, a reviewer can decide again, and every case keeps version history. Nothing is deleted.
Side effects outside the data: owners get an in-app alert for every verdict, an email too when notify is 'true', and Part 11 projects write an audit-log row.

422.description: Verdict refused: a selected case is no longer under review (error_code invalid_review_state), or the account plan lacks the feature.

error.example: Test case in Pending state cannot be approved. It was modified and moved back to Pending — refresh to review the latest changes.

message.description: Present instead of error/errors on the plan gate ('Feature not available').

capabilities.name: validate_bdd_export_selection_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id (the v1 route only matches digits; a PR-NNN identifier never reaches the API).

body.name: ids
body.description: Integer ids of the cases you intend to export. Non-BDD cases among them are silently skipped by the validator. Send ONE of ids, select_all or folders.

body.name: select_all
body.description: Validate every BDD case in scope (q + folder_id, or the whole project) minus de_selected_ids. Compared as the string 'true'.

body.name: de_selected_ids
body.description: Integer ids to exclude from a select_all scope.

body.name: folders

fields.name: <folder_id>
fields.description: {select_all: bool, ids: [int], de_selected_ids: [int]} for that folder.

body.description: Cross-folder selection keyed by folder id; the union is validated. Takes precedence over ids/select_all. An empty map validates nothing (400 'No BDD Test Case(s) selected.').

body.name: q
body.description: Filter scope for select_all — same filter object as the test-case search, sent as a sibling of test_case. Only read when select_all is true; an unknown key is silently dropped (scope widens).

body.name: folder_id
body.description: Folder to scope a select_all validation to. Ignored for explicit ids.

capabilities.intent: Check, before exporting test cases to a BDD feature file, that every selected BDD case shares the same Feature and Background text so they can be merged into one file — returns a pass/fail verdict and message, nothing is exported or changed
guidance: Pure check despite the POST: it only reads the selected cases' steps and compares them; no export job, file or record is created. Run it before the real export when the user wants a single merged feature file.

Pass and fail share ONE body shape {success, message}: HTTP 200 + success:true on pass, HTTP 400 + success:false on any failure. Read `message` to tell the failures apart — 'No BDD Test Case(s) selected.' means the selection contained no BDD-template cases at all.

Hard cap: a selection resolving to more than 300 BDD cases is refused with 400, but with the MISLEADING message 'Validation failed. Selected test cases belong to different features or backgrounds.' — the same text as a genuine mismatch. Check the selection size yourself before trusting that message.
Only BDD-template cases are considered: text/step cases in the selection are filtered out silently and a pass says nothing about them.
Comparison is exact after trimming whitespace, on the Feature and Background of each case's FIRST step only.
No RBAC permission is attached to this action; project access and authentication suffice.

capabilities.name: add_test_case_comment_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Numeric id of the project. Not the PR-NNN identifier shown in the UI.

path_params.name: folder_id
path_params.description: Numeric id of the folder the test case sits in. The comment thread is resolved from the test case id itself, so this segment only has to be a real folder id in the project.

path_params.name: test_case_id
path_params.description: Numeric id of the test case whose comments these are. Not the TC-NNN identifier.

body.name: comment
body.example: Checked against the latest build - step 3 still fails on Safari.
body.description: The comment text, as rich text (HTML); plain text is accepted and kept as sent. Content that is only whitespace or empty tags is rejected as invalid, though an image on its own counts as content. To mention a colleague, include a span carrying data-lexical-mention="true" and data-id set to their BrowserStack user id; mentioning someone outside the account is refused.

capabilities.intent: Post a comment on a test case.
guidance: The comment is attributed to the calling user and the case owner is notified the moment it lands; anyone mentioned in the text is notified separately. Those messages leave the product and cannot be recalled, so confirm the wording before sending.

The author can edit or delete their own comment afterwards - each is a separate operation - which is what makes this recoverable; an edit replaces the earlier text and keeps no previous version, and a delete leaves no self-serve way back.
Only the author can change a comment, so posting on someone's behalf leaves them unable to correct it.
Commenting on an archived test case is refused; restore the case first.

This is a paid-plan feature. On a plan without it the call still succeeds at the transport level and reports in the payload that the feature is unavailable, so check the success flag rather than assuming the comment landed.
Comments are flat: every one is posted against the case itself, and there is no way to reply beneath an existing comment.

capabilities.name: create_folder_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: The project's PR-NNN identifier string as shown in the UI and returned by the projects list. This is NOT the numeric project id that v1 capabilities take; a numeric id does not match this path and returns 404.

query.name: auto_rename
query.description: Only the literal value true has any effect. When true, a name that clashes with a sibling (case-insensitive, trimmed) is created as '<name> (1)' with the name lowercased, instead of failing with 400. Check the returned name.

body.name: name
body.description: Folder name. Trimmed; must not be empty after trimming and must be unique among siblings ignoring case, otherwise 400 'Folder with same name exists in this location' (unless auto_rename).

body.name: description
body.description: Free-text notes shown on the folder. Use this key, not `notes` (the internal-API key): `notes` and any other unknown key inside `folder` are rejected with 400 'Invalid JSON data'. HTML is sanitised on save.

body.name: parent_id
body.description: Integer id of the existing folder to nest under. Omit it to create a root folder (null cannot be sent through this transport). An id not in this project returns 404. 0 is not an alias for root.

body.name: attachments
body.description: Array of integer ids of already-uploaded attachment blobs to attach to the folder. Any invalid id fails the whole create with 422.

capabilities.intent: Create a folder, or a sub folder under a parent.
guidance: Resolve the project's PR- identifier first via the projects list; the numeric project id used by v1 capabilities is not accepted here.
