Send the description as `description`. The `notes` key used by the internal API, and any other unknown key inside `folder`, is rejected with 400 'Invalid JSON data' — the body is schema-validated with unknown keys forbidden.

Sibling names must be unique ignoring case and surrounding whitespace; a clash returns 400. auto_rename=true creates '<name> (1)' with the name lowercased instead, so read the returned name rather than assuming the one you sent.
parent_id 0 is not root: omit the field for a root folder. An unknown parent_id returns 404.
The response carries the new folder's integer id — carry it forward as parent_id for sub folders, as folder_id when creating test cases, or as the move destination.

capabilities.name: create_test_case_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: The project's PR-NNN identifier, as v2 addresses projects. This is NOT the integer project id that every v1 capability takes; read it as `identifier` from the projects list.

path_params.name: folder_id
path_params.description: Integer id of the folder the case is created in. This is authoritative: a different folder id in the body is ignored. Discover it from the folder listing.

body.name: name
body.description: Title of the test case. The only always-required field; comes back as `title` in the response.

body.name: description
body.description: Rich-text body. Send plain text or HTML, not a JSON document.

body.name: preconditions
body.example: User account exists and is verified.

body.name: template
body.description: Step style. `test_case_steps` takes `test_case_steps` rows; `test_case_bdd` takes Gherkin in `feature` / `background` / `scenario` and refuses step rows (422). Mixing the two is refused with 422.

body.name: template_id
body.description: Id of a test-case template from list_templates_v2. Omit or send null for the project's default template. An unknown id, or one from another workspace, is refused with 400 rather than falling back to the default. Choose one whose step_type matches `template`.

body.name: test_case_steps
body.description: Ordered step rows for a `test_case_steps` case. `order` is assigned by array position, so any `order` you send is overwritten. Not allowed for `test_case_bdd` (422). A differently named key such as `steps` is dropped and the case is created with NO steps, so verify against `steps` in the response.

fields.name: step
fields.description: Action the tester performs.

fields.name: result
fields.description: Expected result of this step.

fields.name: shared_step_id
fields.description: Reuse a shared step instead of inline text.

body.name: feature
body.description: Gherkin Feature text. REQUIRED when template is `test_case_bdd` (422 if blank); refused with 422 on a non-BDD case.

body.name: background
body.description: Gherkin Background text; optional, BDD cases only (422 otherwise).

body.name: scenario
body.description: Gherkin Scenario text. REQUIRED when template is `test_case_bdd` (422 if blank); refused with 422 on a non-BDD case.

body.name: owner
body.description: Owner as a workspace user's email (a user id is also accepted). An owner that cannot be resolved silently falls back to the caller — check `owner` in the response.

body.name: status
body.description: Matched against the project's configured status display values (defaults: Active, Draft, In Review, Rejected, Outdated; a numeric option id also matches). Unknown value → 400 'Invalid default field value'. Omit for the project default. Resolve the live set with get_system_field_values_v1.

body.name: priority
body.description: Matched against the project's configured priority display values (defaults: Low, Medium, High, Critical; a numeric option id also matches). Unknown value → 400. Omit for the project default.

body.name: case_type
body.description: Matched against the project's configured type display values (defaults include Functional, Regression, Smoke & Sanity, Acceptance, Security, Performance, Usability, Accessibility, Compatibility, Destructive, Automated, Manual, Other). Unknown value → 400. Omit for the project default.

body.name: automation_status
body.description: Built-in values: not_automated, automated, automation_not_required, cannot_be_automated, obsolete (matched case-insensitively by internal name or display label). Workspaces that manage their own automation statuses accept their custom labels too. Unknown value → 400.

body.name: tags
body.description: Free-text tag names; created if new.

body.name: issues
body.description: Linked issues. Either bare issue keys (treated as Jira) or objects {issue_id, issue_type}. Linking is processed asynchronously after the create returns.

fields.name: issue_id
fields.description: Issue key, e.g. TES-204.

fields.name: issue_type
fields.description: Tracker name, e.g. jira.

body.name: custom_fields
body.description: Map of custom-field DISPLAY NAME → value. Dropdown: option label; multi-dropdown: array of labels; user: email; boolean: true/false; date, int, url, text as typed. A name that is not a custom field on this project is SILENTLY SKIPPED (200, value absent); a reserved system-field name (e.g. 'Automation Status') is refused; a value failing its type check fails the whole call with 400.

body.name: identifier
body.description: Custom identifier for the case. Honoured ONLY when the workspace uses project-level custom ids; otherwise ignored. A duplicate is refused with 400 'Test Case ID already exists'.

body.name: review_status
body.description: Review assignment state. Reviewer write: gated on a Team Pro plan and the project's Review & Approve setting when the reviewer API is enabled for the workspace. Omit unless the user asked to put the case in review. Known states include pending and in_review; the accepted set is not enforced here, so an unknown value is refused by the server.

body.name: reviewers
body.description: Reviewer emails. Requires Team Pro plan and Review & Approve enabled on the project (422/400 otherwise). The owner cannot be a reviewer (422). A non-array value is silently ignored.

body.name: send_for_review
body.description: Moves the new case into review and emails reviewers. Same plan/project gates as `reviewers`. Ambiguous strings like 'yes'/'no' are refused with 422.

body.name: created_at
body.description: Backdated creation timestamp for migrations. Honoured only when the workspace has the external-API timestamp feature enabled; otherwise dropped silently.

body.name: updated_at
body.description: Backdated update timestamp for migrations. Same feature gate as `created_at`; must not be earlier than `created_at` (400).

capabilities.intent: Create a test case in a folder.
guidance: Resolve the project's PR-NNN identifier and the destination folder's integer id first; the folder in the path is authoritative and a folder id in the body is ignored.

Decide the step style before writing: a Gherkin case needs template=test_case_bdd plus feature and scenario and must carry no test_case_steps; a classic case must carry no feature/background/scenario. Either mix is refused with 422, and a template_id whose step_type disagrees is the usual cause.

status, priority and case_type take the project's DISPLAY values (e.g. 'Active', 'High', 'Functional'), which a workspace can rename or extend — resolve them with get_system_field_values_v1 rather than guessing; unknown values are refused with 400.

custom_fields is keyed by display name and an unknown name is dropped without error, so confirm each field exists on the project (get_project_id_custom_fields_v2_v1) and verify the response's custom_fields before reporting them saved.

The response echoes the case with `title` (not name), `steps` as [{step, result}] and `owner` as an email, and carries NO integer id — carry data.test_case.identifier forward for later reads, updates and moves.
Recoverable: the new case can be deleted or archived afterwards, so this is an ordinary write.

502.description: error_code=review_approve_unknown — the project's Review & Approve setting could not be read, so nothing was written. Retry.

capabilities.name: edit_project_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id (the numeric `id`, not the PR-NNN identifier). Discover it through the projects list. A project the caller cannot see returns 404, not 403.

body.name: name
body.description: New project name. Leading/trailing spaces are trimmed. Must be unique within the account and must not contain | ; > < ` + ? % " / or backslash; violations return 400 with the reason in `error`. Omit to keep the current name.

body.name: description
body.description: New description. HTML is escaped on the way in and anything past 16 KB is silently truncated. Send an empty string to clear it; omit to keep the current one.

body.name: access_type
body.description: Project visibility: `private` (owner only), `restricted` (owner plus named users), `org_wide` (everyone in the account). Other values return 400 'Invalid access type'. Honoured only on accounts with project-level access control; elsewhere silently ignored and the response still says success. Server may adjust it: private with named users becomes restricted, restricted with none becomes private.

body.name: users

fields.name: user
fields.description: Email address of a user in the same account.

fields.name: role
fields.description: Product role name to grant on this project (account-configured, e.g. Product Admin, Tester, Viewer).

body.description: Per-user access grants. Processed only when `access_type` is also sent, otherwise ignored. Each entry is added or has its role changed; users not listed keep their existing access, so this does not replace the list. Entries whose email is not in the account or whose role is not recognised are skipped silently, not rejected.

capabilities.intent: Rename a project, or change its description or visibility.
guidance: There is no undo. The previous name and description are overwritten; the change is logged in the project's activity feed and version history, so the old value can be looked up and re-entered by hand, but nothing restores it.
Send at least one of name, description or access_type inside the `project` object; an empty `project` object is rejected 400 before anything is looked up.
Only account owners/admins or the project owner may edit; anyone else gets 403 with the reason in `error`. A project the caller cannot see comes back 404, not 403.
Visibility is silently ignored on accounts without project-level access control: the call returns 200 and the unchanged value. Read `access_type` back from the response to confirm the change took.
The `users` list is only read alongside `access_type`. To change one user's role without touching visibility, resend the current access_type with the users entry.

Name conflicts and blocked characters are enforced by the backend and surface as 400 with a human-readable `error`; validation runs after the permission check, so a 403 means permissions, not the name.

200.description: Project edited. Envelope is data.success and data.project, same as the single-project read; project also carries access_type, normalisedName and projectVisibilityBanner, and the counts are carried over from before the edit rather than recomputed.

capabilities.name: folder_attachments_v1
capabilities.intent: List the files attached to a folder itself.
guidance: This is the folder's own shelf of files. Files attached to the test cases in the folder are a separate list and none of them appear here.
It does not look inside subfolders, so walk the folder tree and ask for each folder you care about.
Each entry carries links to the stored file; read the file from there, as there is no separate download step.
A folder with nothing attached comes back as an ordinary success with an empty list, so an empty list is an answer and not a failure.
Alongside the exact byte count each entry also carries a ready-formatted size for display; use the byte count when you need to compare or add sizes up.

capabilities.name: get_exploratory_session_form_fields

query.name: values
query.description: Set to true to get each field's configured choices alongside its definition. Left off, the reply is a compact list of the field definitions with the choice lists omitted, which is enough to learn the field names but not the values they accept.

capabilities.intent: List the form fields for authoring an exploratory session.
guidance: Ask for the choices when you intend to write a session; without them you get field names and types only, and you will be guessing at what a dropdown accepts.

Only the fields your team added are listed. The built-in session details such as name, charter and status are not returned here, so an empty list means nothing extra was configured, not that the session has no fields.
Configuration is per project, so fetch it again for each project - a field set up in one project need not exist in another.
Each field carries both an internal name and the display name your team sees; when a person names a field in plain words, match it against the display name.
A field describing a dependent choice points at the field it hangs off, so resolve the parent's value first when one is present.

capabilities.name: get_lcnc_user_test_config_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Numeric id of the project the setup is read for.

capabilities.intent: Get the caller's saved low-code test setup for a project.
guidance: The setup itself belongs to BrowserStack's low-code automation product and is handed back exactly as that product produced it. Test Management does not define, validate or reshape those fields, so they are not guaranteed here and may change without a change in Test Management - read them each time rather than relying on a remembered shape.
The status reported inside the payload is the one the other product returned, echoed as the transport status as well, so its failure surfaces as that same code here with the detail in the payload.

The setup is per person: it is the calling user's own default, so two people on the same project can correctly get different answers, and it is not a project-wide setting you can read on someone else's behalf.

200.description: The low-code automation service's own response, passed through unchanged. `status` echoes that service's status code and `body` is its parsed payload, whose fields are owned by that service and are not guaranteed by Test Management.

status.description: Status code echoed from the upstream service.

body.description: Upstream payload, passed through unchanged. Field set may vary; see the `discovered` shape.

capabilities.name: get_shared_components_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Numeric id of the project whose shared fields are listed.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number, starting at 1. The page size is fixed by the service and cannot be raised from here; read the returned page details to see the total and whether another page exists.

query.name: q[query]
query.description: Text matched against the shared field's title only - its step content is not searched. Send it in this bracketed form; a bare q value is ignored and the unfiltered list comes back looking like a successful search.

query.name: q[tags]
query.description: Comma-separated tag names. Only shared fields carrying at least one of them are listed.

query.name: q[empty][system_fields][]
query.description: Lists shared fields that have nothing set for a system field. Only tags is understood; any other name is dropped without an error, which silently widens the result. Combines with a tag filter as an either/or rather than narrowing it.

query.name: field_type
query.description: Restrict the listing to one kind of shared field. Omit to list every kind.

query.name: folder_id
query.description: Collection to list from: the collection's numeric id, or the literal four-character text null to list the Unassigned root where uncollected fields sit. That is the word null as a value, not an absent one. Omit the parameter entirely to list the project's shared fields regardless of collection.

query.name: include_sub_collections
query.description: Set true to include the chosen collection's sub-collections as well as the collection itself. Only the exact value true turns it on, it does nothing without a collection, and it never applies to the Unassigned root, which has no children.

query.name: sort_by
query.description: Sort order for the listing, passed straight through to the service that stores shared fields. Omit it for the default order; an unrecognised value is not reported as an error here.

query.name: pre_fetch
query.description: When true the response also carries the steps of the first shared field on the page, saving a follow-up call. Honoured only on page 1 and only when the page has at least one row.

capabilities.intent: List or search a project's shared fields.
guidance: Shared fields and shared steps are different objects with separate listings and separate id sets; an id taken from one will not resolve in the other, so confirm which the user means before acting.
The listing carries each field's title, type and usage count but not its step content - fetch a single shared field when the actual steps are needed.
The usage count is what tells you how wide the blast radius of an edit would be; read it before suggesting a change to a field.
Filtering by collection is the only way to reproduce what the user sees in a collection view - an unfiltered list spans the whole project and will look like the filter was ignored.

capabilities.name: get_test_case_comments_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Numeric id of the project. Not the PR-NNN identifier shown in the UI.

path_params.name: folder_id
path_params.description: Numeric id of the folder the test case sits in. The comment thread is resolved from the test case id itself, so this segment only has to be a real folder id in the project.

path_params.name: test_case_id
path_params.description: Numeric id of the test case whose comments these are. Not the TC-NNN identifier.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number, starting at 1. Each page holds at most 30 comments and the size cannot be raised; the response reports the total and the next page number.

capabilities.intent: Read the comments on a test case.
guidance: The newest comment is first on page 1, so a 'what was said last' question is answered without paging; page on only when the reported total exceeds what you already hold.
Comments deleted by their author are gone from every page and from the total, so a thread can be shorter than a screenshot or an email suggests.
Bodies are rich text (HTML). A mention of a colleague arrives as markup whose visible text is that person's display name, so strip tags before showing the text plainly.
An archived test case still returns its comments, even though nothing new can be added to it.

capabilities.name: get_test_case_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: The project's PR-NNN identifier, as v2 addresses projects. This is NOT the integer project id that every v1 capability takes; read it as `identifier` from the projects list.

path_params.name: test_case_id
path_params.description: The case's TC-NNN identifier, or its customer-defined identifier when the workspace uses project-level custom ids; matched exactly within the project. A bare integer id is NOT accepted here (404) — use get_test_case_by_integer_id_v1 for integer ids.

capabilities.intent: Get one test case in full by its TC-NNN identifier.
guidance: Returns `title` rather than name, `steps` as [{step, result}], custom_fields as [{name, value|values}] and owner as an email; there is no integer id in the body.
feature/background/scenario are present only for a Gherkin (test_case_bdd) case and `steps` is then empty; reviewers/review_status appear only when the project has Review & Approve enabled.
A 404 means the identifier does not resolve in THIS project; a case moved to another project keeps its identifier but must be read there.

502.description: Upstream read failed with an unknown status; retry.

capabilities.name: global_search_v1

query.name: entity
query.description: Comma-separated list of the entity types to search. Allowed tokens: test_case, test_run, test_plan, project, shared_step, report. They are snake_case and SINGULAR — the hyphenated plurals used by the project-scoped search (test-cases, test-runs) are rejected here with a 400 naming the invalid token. Omitting this is a 400, not a search of everything.

query.name: q[query]
query.description: The text to search for. Required — a blank or missing value is a 400. %, _ and \ are literal characters here and are not escaped or treated as wildcards.

query.name: q[project_ids]
query.description: Comma-separated NUMERIC project ids to restrict the search to. These are integer ids, not PR-NNN identifiers. Omit to search every project the caller can see.

query.name: q[owner]
query.description: Comma-separated Test Management user ids; the server converts them to the underlying user ids. Applied to test cases, runs and plans, and to reports. Deliberately NOT applied to project or shared_step hits, whose stored user is a creator rather than an owner, so an owner filter does not narrow those two at all.

query.name: q[tags]
query.description: Comma-separated tag ids applied to every entity type being searched. A per-entity tag filter overrides it for that entity.

query.name: q[issue_ids]
query.description: Comma-separated linked-issue ids. Applied to test cases only at the shared level; use the per-entity form for runs.

query.name: q[created_at]
query.description: Relative token `<n>_<unit>` with a SINGULAR unit (day, hour, week, month, year) — e.g. 7_day, 24_hour; a `_gte` suffix inverts it (7_day_gte = older than). Also accepts `all_time` (resolved as one year) or an absolute "YYYY-MM-DD YYYY-MM-DD" range. A plural unit such as 7_days raises server-side rather than returning a 400.

query.name: q[updated_at]
query.description: Same form as q[created_at].

query.name: q[created_between]
query.description: Absolute creation range as a positional 2-element array: index 0 is the start, index 1 the end, ISO 8601. Takes precedence over q[created_at] when both are sent.

query.name: q[updated_between]
query.description: Absolute last-updated range, same positional 2-element form as q[created_between]. Takes precedence over q[updated_at].

query.name: q[test_case][tags]
query.description: Comma-separated tag ids, test cases only. Overrides the shared q[tags] for this entity.

query.name: q[test_case][priority_id]
query.description: Comma-separated priority option ids. Ids, not labels — resolve them from the project's system field values first.

query.name: q[test_case][status_id]
query.description: Comma-separated status option ids.

query.name: q[test_case][automation_state_id]
query.description: Comma-separated automation-state option ids.

query.name: q[test_case][category_id]
query.description: Comma-separated case-type (category) option ids.

query.name: q[test_case][issue_ids]
query.description: Comma-separated linked-issue ids, test cases only.

query.name: q[test_run][tags]
query.description: Comma-separated tag ids, test runs only.

query.name: q[test_run][issue_ids]
query.description: Comma-separated linked-issue ids, test runs only.

query.name: q[test_plan][tags]
query.description: Comma-separated tag ids, test plans only.

query.name: q[project][tags]
query.description: Comma-separated tag ids, project hits only. Projects and shared steps accept tags and the date ranges only — no owner, priority or status filter reaches them.

query.name: q[shared_step][tags]
query.description: Comma-separated tag ids, shared-step hits only.

query.name: q[match][tags]
query.description: How to combine the tag values supplied elsewhere — an OPERATOR, never the values themselves: all (has every tag), any, none. A value placed here instead of beside it sets a meaningless operator and applies NO filter, silently widening the result. The operator is broadcast to every entity being searched.

query.name: combine
query.description: true merges all entity types into one list sorted newest-first with an entity_type on each row. Case-insensitive. It forces page 1 and caps the merged list at 5 rows while info.count still reports the real total, so it is a preview, not a way to read results.

query.name: typeahead
query.description: true takes a fast path returning only entity_type, id, identifier, name, project_id and owner per hit, with no folder path, status or description enrichment. It also DROPS reports from the search entirely even when they are listed in `entity`. Case-insensitive.

query.name: filter_details
query.description: Exactly the lowercase string `true` adds a filter_details block resolving the filter ids you sent back to names. Any other spelling, including True, is ignored. If resolution fails the block is simply absent — the search itself still succeeds.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number, applied to every entity type at once. A value below 1 becomes 1. `page` is accepted as an alias. Ignored when combine is true.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Rows per entity type per page, ceiling 30. A larger value is silently reduced to 30 rather than refused. `count` is accepted as an alias.

capabilities.intent: Search every entity type across the account at once.
guidance: Account-wide by default. There is no project path segment; narrow it with the numeric project-ids filter when the user did name a project, otherwise every project the caller can see is searched.

Entity tokens here are snake_case and singular (test_case, test_run, test_plan, project, shared_step, report). This is a different vocabulary from the project-scoped searches, which take hyphenated plurals — passing those gets a 400 that names the invalid token.

Both the entity list and the query text are mandatory and each missing one comes back as HTTP 400 whose body is a bare `error` message with no `success` key, so do not look for success: false to detect the failure.

Pagination is per entity type, not overall: page 2 advances every type together, so a type with 3 hits contributes nothing to page 2 while another is still producing rows. Read each type's own info block to know when that type is exhausted.

Combining results is a preview only — it pins you to page 1 and returns at most 5 rows across all types while still reporting the true total in the count, so a count of 200 beside 5 rows is expected and not a bug. Leave it off and read the per-type results when you actually need the matches.

Priority, status, automation-state and case-type filters take option ids, not the labels a user says. Resolve them first; a wrong-form value matches nothing and still returns a successful empty result.
Projects and shared steps only honour tags and the date ranges. An owner filter does not narrow them at all, so a query scoped by owner still returns every matching project.

capabilities.name: initiate_export

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Numeric project id, not the PR-NNN identifier.

path_params.name: entity_type
path_params.description: Only test cases can be exported through this capability. Dashboard analytics has its own export capability; asking for it here is accepted, records an export and returns an id, then the background job fails.

path_params.name: file_type
path_params.description: csv produces a spreadsheet of every field, custom field and step. bdd produces Gherkin .feature output and silently restricts the export to BDD-template cases only.

body.name: ids
body.description: The exact test cases to export, by NUMERIC id. A TC-NNN identifier or a customer-defined id is not matched here. Ignored when select_all is true or when a folder selection map is sent. Omit the whole test_case object at your peril: with no selection form at all the export job is started against an empty id set.

body.name: select_all
body.description: true exports everything matching the q filters within folder_id instead of an explicit id list, minus de_selected_ids. Sent as false (or omitted) the explicit id list is used instead.

body.name: de_selected_ids
body.description: Numeric ids to exclude from a select_all export. Has no effect unless select_all is true.

body.name: folders
body.description: Cross-folder selection: an object KEYED BY FOLDER ID, each value carrying that folder's own select_all / ids / de_selected_ids choice; the server resolves it to a union of case ids. Present, it WINS over both select_all and ids at the top level. An empty map resolves to no cases, never to the whole project.

body.name: folder_id
body.description: Folder to scope a select_all export to. Only the folder itself unless subfolders are opted into.

body.name: include_subfolders_tc
body.description: true also pulls cases from the folder's descendants. Off by default, so a folder export silently returns only the cases sitting directly in that folder.

body.name: q
body.description: Filters selecting which cases a select_all export covers. Same vocabulary and same id-based values as the project test-case search, so resolve option ids first. An unrecognised key is dropped rather than refused, which widens the export instead of erroring.

body.name: merge_into_single_file
body.description: BDD exports only: merge every selected case into one .feature file instead of one file per case. The merge needs a single shared feature and background across the selection.

body.name: common_feature
body.description: BDD merge only: the Feature block to write at the top of the merged file. Omit it and the first exported case's own feature is used.

body.name: common_background
body.description: BDD merge only: the Background block for the merged file. Omit it and the first exported case's background is used.

capabilities.intent: Start a background export of test cases to CSV or Gherkin.
guidance: THE FILE NEVER COMES BACK THROUGH HERE. This only queues the job and hands you an export id. Downloading the finished file is deliberately not part of this catalogue — a file download cannot be served over this transport — and there is no status or polling capability either. So after a successful call, tell the user plainly that the export is being prepared and that they must collect it from the exports list in the Test Management UI. Do not promise to fetch, attach or summarise the file.

A 200 with an export id means the job was accepted, not that it succeeded. The work runs afterwards and can still fail, in which case the id stays valid and no file ever appears — which the caller cannot observe from here.

Selection has three forms and the server picks one in a fixed order: a folder-keyed selection map beats everything; otherwise select_all exports everything matching the filters within the folder minus the de-selected ids; otherwise only the listed ids. Send exactly one form — the losing ones are silently ignored, not merged.
Explicit ids are matched on the numeric primary key only. Feeding TC-NNN identifiers there exports nothing and still returns a successful export id.

Choosing BDD restricts the selection to BDD-template cases behind your back, so exporting a folder of step-template cases as BDD produces an empty file with no error. Validate a BDD selection for a shared feature and background before merging into one file.
This creates an export record against the caller's account each time it is invoked; repeating it produces a new id and a new job rather than reusing the previous one.

capabilities.name: link_entities_to_jira_issue

body.name: issue_id
body.description: The external tracker's own ticket key, e.g. the Jira key TES-121. It is not a Test Management id and is not minted here — take it from the tracker. A missing value is refused with 400 'Missing issue_id'; a key that does not exist in the tracker is NOT validated and the link is stored anyway.

body.name: project_id
body.description: Integer id of the Test Management project that owns the entities being linked, sent as a string. A missing value is refused with 400 'Missing project_id'. This endpoint does not check it is numeric, so a non-numeric value fails deeper as a 500 rather than a clean 400.

body.name: entity_type
body.description: What is being linked. Matched case-insensitively. Anything outside the list is refused with 400 'Unsupported entity_type'. This also decides which other body field is required: 'test-case' requires `selection`, 'test-run' requires `entity_ids`.

body.name: entity_ids
body.description: Integer ids of the test runs to link. Required ONLY when entity_type is 'test-run' (400 'Missing entity_ids for testrun' otherwise). For 'test-case' this field is read but never used — cases are resolved from `selection`, so ids sent here are silently discarded.

body.name: selection
body.description: Which test cases to link, in the same folder/filter selection shape the selection preview returns. Required ONLY when entity_type is 'test-case' (400 'Missing selection for testcase' otherwise). Ignored for 'test-run'.

fields.name: select_all
fields.description: Select every case matching the selection rather than an explicit list.

fields.name: unique_test_case_count
fields.description: Caller-supplied count of cases this selection resolves to. The server trusts it: it is the only input to the >200 async decision and is never recomputed against the selection.

fields.name: folders
fields.description: Folder-keyed selection map, taken verbatim from the selection preview.

body.name: shared_selection
body.description: Additional selection covering test cases shared in from other projects. Only read on the synchronous test-case path; the queued path above 200 cases drops it, so shared cases are not linked in an async batch.

body.name: build_ids
body.description: Build ids matching `entity_ids` one-for-one, for accounts on build-based run ingestion. Omit the field entirely to let the server resolve runs the legacy way. If you do send it, it must hold exactly one positive integer per entry in `entity_ids` with no duplicates, or the call is refused with 400.

capabilities.intent: Link test cases or runs to a tracker ticket.
guidance: Which body field carries the entities depends on what you are linking: cases are selected by a selection object, runs by an explicit list of ids. Sending ids alongside a case selection links nothing extra.

Above 200 entities the work is queued to a background worker and the response comes back immediately with async true and no per-entity outcome. Nothing has been linked yet at that point, and a worker failure is never reported back — re-read the ticket's linked test cases to confirm.

The 200 threshold for a case selection is read from the count you supplied, not from the selection itself. Understate it and the call takes the synchronous path, which resolves at most 200 cases and links only those — reporting success for the whole selection.
Build the case selection from the selection preview for the same ticket and project rather than assembling it by hand; the preview returns exactly the object this field expects.
The ticket key is not verified against the tracker. A typo produces a link to a ticket that does not exist, with a 200 and a success message.
Linking is additive and idempotent per entity; relinking an already-linked entity does not duplicate it.
Every failure on the argument-validation path comes back as 400 with a plain message, including cases that are really 'not found'.

200.description: `{"success": true, "message": "<entity_type>s linked successfully", "async": false}` when the entities were linked in-request, or the same shape with `"async": true` and a 'queued for linking' message when the batch exceeded 200 entities and was handed to a worker. No entity ids or per-entity results are returned in either case.

capabilities.name: linked_test_cases_selection_v1

path_params.name: issue_type
path_params.description: Which external tracker the caller is acting from. Only these values are routable — anything else does not match the route at all and comes back as a 404 rather than a validation error. Use 'jira-app' for Jira; the server normalises it to 'jira' internally.

query.name: issue_id
query.description: The external tracker's ticket key whose current test-case selection is wanted. Not validated here: a blank or unknown key returns an empty selection rather than an error.

query.name: project_id
query.description: Integer id of the Test Management project the selection is scoped to. This endpoint does not check it is present or numeric, so a missing or non-numeric value fails deeper as a 5xx instead of a clean 400 — always send a real project id.

capabilities.intent: Preview the test cases a tracker ticket would link.
guidance: This is the step before linking, not the list of what is already linked. The selection object it returns is the exact object the link call expects, folder structure and all — pass it straight through rather than rebuilding it.

The count the link call uses to decide between the immediate and the queued path is the one you carry from this selection. Change the selection by hand and that count stops matching what it resolves to.
Unlike its Jira-specific twin, this route validates neither the ticket key nor the project id, so a missing argument surfaces as a server error rather than a 400.
During a platform downtime window this returns an empty test-case list rather than a selection object.

200.description: `{"success": true, "selection": {...}}`. The selection object is passed through from the backing service and is folder-shaped (a `folders` map plus selection counts); it is the same object the link call takes as its case selection. During downtime an empty test-case collection is returned in its place instead.

capabilities.name: list_configuration_groups

query.name: p
query.description: Page number. Page 0 is treated as page 1.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Rows per page, ceiling 30. Anything above 30 — and 0, a negative, or a non-numeric value — is silently replaced with 30 rather than refused, so a big page never arrives and you must walk pages. Above 300 the call is refused outright with a page-size error instead.

capabilities.intent: List the account's configuration groups and their ids.
guidance: A group carries only the dimension's name — the selectable values live under it as its options and are fetched separately using the group id returned here, so this is step one of two whenever you need a concrete value.

Nothing here is project-scoped: the same groups come back whichever project the user is working in, and they cannot be filtered to one project. Do not offer this as a way to see what a particular project can run against.
Page number travels as `p`; a `page` parameter is not read on this call and is ignored, which silently pins you to page 1.
There is no name search or sort on this listing — walk the pages and match names yourself.

capabilities.name: list_tags_v3

query.name: entity_type
query.description: Which kind of record's labels to list. There is no option meaning 'all kinds'. Leaving it out or sending anything outside the listed set is refused outright rather than answered with an empty list.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number, counting from 1. Anything that is not a positive whole number is refused before the labels are read.

query.name: page
query.description: Accepted as an alternative spelling of the page number, and used only when the page number was not supplied under the shorter name. Prefer the shorter name, which every other listing here uses.

query.name: per_page
query.description: How many labels to return per page. The default is small, so ask for the largest page you need. A value above 100, zero, a negative number or anything non-numeric is refused rather than quietly clamped.

query.name: search
query.description: Narrows the list to labels matching this text. Surrounding spaces are trimmed and an all-blank value counts as no filter at all. 'query' and 'q' are accepted as equivalents; whichever of the three is non-blank first is the one used.

capabilities.intent: List or search a project's labels, with their ids.
guidance: This is the only label listing that reaches records other than test cases, and the only one that hands back the id a rename or a merge needs. The test-case-only listings return names and usage counts, so start here whenever an id is required downstream.
Name the kind of record explicitly every time. There is no way to ask for every kind at once, and a misspelling is refused rather than silently widened.
Labels are scoped to a project and to a kind of record, so the same word can exist as separate labels for test cases and for test runs, each with its own id.
Ask for a large page in one go rather than walking small pages; the ceiling is 100 per page.

200.description: A page of labels for the requested kind of record. Each entry carries the label's id and its name; a companion block reports the total and the current page.

capabilities.name: list_users

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Integer project id. It gates access only; the returned list is not filtered to this project's members.

capabilities.intent: List the account's active users, for assigning a case or run.
guidance: Returns all active users of the caller's account, alphabetical by full name, in one unpaginated response. Appearing here does not mean the user has access to the project.
No role field. For project membership with roles use search_project_users; for a paged, name-filterable list of account users use get_project_users_v2_v1.
Assign owners and assignees with `id` (the TM user id), not `browserstack_user_id`.
`myself` is the caller, reduced to id, full_name and reports_and_notification_enabled; look the caller up in `users` for the full record.
Deactivated users and users with no name are omitted, so a colleague missing from the list may simply not have completed onboarding.

capabilities.name: move_folder_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: The project's PR-NNN identifier string as shown in the UI and returned by the projects list. This is NOT the numeric project id that v1 capabilities take; a numeric id does not match this path and returns 404.

path_params.name: folder_id
path_params.description: Integer id of the folder to move; everything nested inside it moves with it. Never an FL- string.

query.name: auto_rename
query.description: Defaults to true: if a folder with the same name (case-insensitive, trimmed) already exists under the destination, the moved folder is silently renamed to '<name> (1)' with the name lowercased. Send false to get a 400 on a clash instead.

body.name: parent_id
body.description: Integer id of the new parent folder in the SAME project. To move the folder to the project root, omit this field entirely: the server treats a missing key as root, and null cannot be sent through this transport. 0 is not root and is refused with 422. Must differ from folder_id.

capabilities.intent: Move a folder and its contents under a different parent.
guidance: Only moves within the same project are possible here; a destination in another project is refused with 422. Cross-project moves exist only in the internal API.

To move to root, omit parent_id; the server treats the missing key as root. A body that accidentally lost the key therefore also returns 200 and re-parents the folder to root, so double-check before sending without it. 0 is refused (422) rather than treated as root.
Name clashes at the destination are resolved by renaming the moved folder to '<name> (1)', lowercased, unless auto_rename=false is sent. Read the returned name either way.

Every pre-flight failure — same source and destination, unknown destination, unknown source folder, other-project destination — is a 422 whose text sits under `error`, not `message`. Only a failure inside the storage update comes back as 400.
Reversible by moving the folder back to its previous parent_id, so read the folder before moving; a name changed by auto-rename is not restored by moving back.
Completes synchronously and returns the moved folder; there is no async job id to poll, unlike the internal cross-project move.

400.description: The storage update was refused (e.g. an invalid destination such as the folder's own subtree).

422.description: A pre-flight validation failed: cross-project destination, destination equal to source, destination not in this project, or source folder not found. The reason is under `error`.

capabilities.name: rename_folder_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: The project's PR-NNN identifier string as shown in the UI and returned by the projects list. This is NOT the numeric project id that v1 capabilities take; a numeric id does not match this path and returns 404.

path_params.name: folder_id
path_params.description: Integer id of the folder to update, as returned by the folder list or create. Never an FL- string. 0 is rejected.

query.name: auto_rename
query.description: Only the literal value true has any effect. When true, a new name that clashes with a sibling (case-insensitive, trimmed) is saved as '<name> (1)' with the name lowercased, instead of failing with 400. Check the returned name.

body.name: name
body.description: New folder name. Optional server-side despite the spec marking it required — a description-only update is valid. Must be unique among siblings ignoring case, otherwise 400 (unless auto_rename).

body.name: description
body.description: New notes for the folder; replaces the existing text. HTML is sanitised on save, so tags may come back stripped or escaped.

capabilities.intent: Rename a folder or change its description.
guidance: There is no undo and folders keep no version history: read the folder first and keep the old name and description if you may need to put them back.
The body must contain a `folder` object (400 otherwise), but neither field inside it is required — a description-only change is fine even though the spec marks name required.
Unknown keys inside `folder` are silently dropped rather than rejected, so a misspelt key returns 200 with nothing changed. Compare the returned folder to what you sent.

A new name matching a sibling's (case-insensitive, trimmed) returns 400 'Folder with same name exists in this location'. auto_rename=true makes the server lowercase the name and append ' (1)' instead — that is a different result from the rename you asked for.
Renaming does not move the folder; use the move capability to change its parent.

capabilities.name: test_case_results_v1

path_params.name: issue_type
path_params.description: Which external tracker the caller is acting from. Only these values are routable — anything else does not match the route at all and comes back as a 404 rather than a validation error. Use 'jira-app' for Jira; the server normalises it to 'jira' internally.

path_params.name: test_case_id
path_params.description: Integer id of the test case whose details and execution results are wanted. Must belong to the caller's own group.

query.name: p
query.description: Page of execution results. Sending it also switches the read to include every result rather than the server default set, so send p=1 explicitly when you want the full result history — omitting it quietly narrows what comes back.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Results per page. Only read when `p` is also sent; on its own it has no effect.

capabilities.intent: Get a test case's linked tracker tickets.
guidance: Everything is nested one level under a `data` wrapper, with the case itself under `test_case` inside it; reading the top level finds nothing.

The linked tickets are on the `issues` field of the returned case, each carrying the tracker's own ticket key. That is the list to read before unlinking, because unlinking does not let you choose between several linked tickets.

Ownership is checked against the caller's own group, so a case id from another account comes back as a body saying access was denied while the transport status is still 200 — check the success flag rather than the status.
During a platform downtime window this returns a success body with a null case instead of failing; treat a null case as 'unknown', not as 'no such case'.

200.description: `{"data": {"success": true, "test_case": <TestCase>}}`. The case object also carries `test_run_results`, the page of execution results, and `issues`, the tracker tickets it is linked to. Also returned with `test_case` null during a downtime window.

capabilities.name: unlink_test_case_v1

path_params.name: issue_type
path_params.description: Which external tracker the link belongs to. Only these values are routable — anything else does not match the route at all and comes back as a 404 rather than a validation error. Use 'jira-app' for Jira; the server normalises it to 'jira' internally. The link is matched on this tracker type, so the wrong value finds nothing to unlink.

body.name: test_case_id
body.description: Integer id of the test case to unlink. This, the caller's group and the tracker type are the whole match key — the case must belong to the caller's own group or the call is refused.

body.name: issue_id
body.description: The tracker ticket key the case should be unlinked from. Accepted and echoed through, but NOT used to select which link is removed: the server matches on the case, the group and the tracker type only. Send it for the refreshed list that comes back, and see the guidance if the case has more than one linked ticket.

body.name: p
body.description: Page of the refreshed linked-test-case list returned on success. Pages are fixed at 10 per page. Must be a plain scalar — an array or hash value is ignored and the first page is returned.

capabilities.intent: Unlink a test case from a tracker ticket.
guidance: A failure does not change the transport status: the refusal arrives as a 200 carrying a success flag set to false and a 404 inside the body. Always read the success flag — checking the status alone reports every miss as a win.

Which link is removed is decided by the test case, the caller's group and the tracker type, not by the ticket you name. If the case is linked to several tickets in the same tracker, the first matching link is removed and it may not be the one you meant — read the case's linked tickets first and expect to verify afterwards.
On success the refreshed list of test cases still linked to the ticket is returned, so no follow-up read is needed to confirm.
Nothing is deleted: the case, the run and the ticket all survive and the same link can be created again.
Nothing is written back to the external tracker — the ticket itself is not modified.
During a platform downtime window an empty list with a success flag is returned and nothing is unlinked.

200.description: On success, the refreshed list of test cases still linked to the ticket: `{"success": true, "test_cases": [...], "info": {...}, "recent_folder": ..., "recent_project": ...}`, 10 per page. ALSO returned, with this same 200 status, as `{"success": false, "status": 404}` when no matching link was found, and as `{"success": false, "error": "Invalid Access", "status": 401}` when the test case is not in the caller's group — the numbers in these bodies are not the transport status.

capabilities.name: unlink_test_run_v1

path_params.name: issue_type
path_params.description: Which external tracker the link belongs to. Only these values are routable — anything else does not match the route at all and comes back as a 404 rather than a validation error. Use 'jira-app' for Jira; the server normalises it to 'jira' internally. The link is matched on this tracker type, so the wrong value finds nothing to unlink.

body.name: test_run_id
body.description: Integer id of the test run to unlink. Must belong to the caller's own group, and the run is looked up inside `project_id`, which therefore becomes mandatory as soon as this is sent.

body.name: project_id
body.description: Integer id of the project that owns the run. Required whenever `test_run_id` is sent; omitting it is refused with a body saying the project id was not provided.

body.name: issue_id
body.description: The tracker ticket key the run should be unlinked from. Accepted and echoed through, but NOT used to select which link is removed: the server matches on the run, the group and the tracker type only. Send it for the refreshed list that comes back.

body.name: build_id
body.description: Build id for the run, for accounts on build-based run ingestion. Omit the field entirely and the server resolves the run itself — that is the normal call. Sending a value that is not a positive integer is refused with 400.

body.name: p
body.description: Page of the refreshed linked-test-run list returned on success. Pages are fixed at 10 per page.

capabilities.intent: Unlink a test run from a tracker ticket.
guidance: A failure does not change the transport status: the refusal arrives as a 200 carrying a success flag set to false and a 404 inside the body. The same is true when the project id is missing or the run belongs to another group. Always read the success flag.

Which link is removed is decided by the test run, the caller's group and the tracker type, not by the ticket you name. If the run is linked to several tickets in the same tracker, the first matching link is removed — verify afterwards.
The run is resolved inside a project, so the project id must accompany the run id even though the ticket is the subject of the call.
On success the refreshed list of test runs still linked to the ticket is returned.
Nothing is deleted: the run and the ticket both survive and the same link can be created again. Nothing is written back to the external tracker.

Read the link first and look at its entity_type. When it is 'Build', this project stores runs as builds and the call needs build_id set to the run's uuid — omitting it returns a 200 with success false and a 404 body that looks exactly like 'no such link'. Observed on preprod: two identical calls without build_id refused, the same call with it succeeded.
During a platform downtime window this refuses with a success flag set to false and a 404 in the body, on a 200 — indistinguishable from 'no such link' without checking platform status.

200.description: On success, the refreshed list of test runs still linked to the ticket: `{"success": true, "test_runs": [...], "info": {...}}`, 10 per page. ALSO returned, with this same 200 status, as `{"success": false, "status": 404}` when no matching link was found or during downtime, and as `{"success": false, "error": ..., "status": 400|401|404}` for a missing project id, a run outside the caller's group, or a run that does not exist — the numbers in these bodies are not the transport status.

capabilities.name: update_tag_v1

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: The label's own id, which only the listing that returns ids gives you. The label's name will not work in its place, so look the id up first.

body.name: new_name
body.description: The label's new wording. Surrounding spaces are trimmed, and a blank or spaces-only value is refused. This is the only thing a rename changes - nothing else about the label can be edited here.

capabilities.intent: Rename a label across a project.
guidance: The new wording replaces the old one everywhere the label is already applied, in one step, with no per-record confirmation.
There is no undo and no saved history for labels, so the only way back is to rename it a second time - note the old wording before you start, because nothing else records it.
In production only account owners and admins may do this; anyone else is refused, so check who is asking before promising it.
This changes wording only. Folding two labels into one is a different operation, and renaming one to match another does not combine them.
Look up the id first: this addresses a single label by id, and a project can hold same-named labels for different kinds of record, each needing its own rename.

200.description: The renamed label, carrying its id and its new name.

capabilities.name: verify_test_case_tags_v1

body.name: tags
body.description: The label wordings to check, as a list of plain strings. Omit the whole list and the request is refused. An empty list is accepted and simply reports nothing new.

capabilities.intent: Check which label names a project already uses.
guidance: Nothing is saved by this check, despite how it reads. A label only comes into being when it is actually applied to a test case, so follow this with the step that puts the label on the case.

Two lists come back: one holds the wordings not yet used on the project's test cases, the other holds the ones already in use. Neither is an error - being already in use is usually the answer you wanted.
The accompanying message says to verify the labels whenever any wording is already in use. It reads like a failure and is not one; go by the two lists.
Comparison is exact, so a difference in capitalisation or spacing counts as a brand new label and will leave you with two near-identical ones if you apply it.
Only labels on test cases are considered. A wording already used on test runs or plans still comes back as new here.
Every outcome, including the one where no wording is new, is returned as an ordinary success - read the flag and the lists rather than the status.

200.description: The verdict on the submitted wordings. 'tags' holds those not yet used on the project's test cases, 'error_tags' those already in use, and 'error' carries an advisory message whenever any wording was already in use.

success.description: False only when none of the submitted wordings were new.

tags.description: Wordings not yet used on this project's test cases.

error_tags.description: Wordings already in use on this project's test cases. Present only when at least one was.

error.description: Advisory message shown when some or all wordings were already in use. Not a transport failure.

id.description: Unique ID for the project.

description.description: A brief description of the project.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the project was created.

import_id.description: An optional import identifier. May be null.

test_cases_count.description: Number of test cases under the project.

test_runs_count.description: Number of test runs under the project.

test_runs.description: Endpoint for the project's test runs.

users.description: Endpoint for the users associated with this project.

project_creator.description: Indicates whether the current user is the creator of the project.

details.description: Optional field with additional error details.

V1TestPlanBulkResponse.description:
Dual-shape response. Below the bulk threshold the work is done and you get
`plans` + `count`. Above it the work was handed to a background job and you get
`async: true` + `unique_id` — the plans are NOT changed yet at that point; re-read to
confirm (see the async-jobs concept).

async.description: Present and true only when the operation was dispatched asynchronously.

unique_id.description: Correlation id of the async job. Present only when async is true.

plans.description: Affected plans. Present only on the synchronous path.

count.description: Number of affected plans. Present only on the synchronous path.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user.

browserstack_user_id.description: BrowserStack user ID associated with this user.

group_id.description: Group ID the user belongs to.

reports_and_notification_enabled.description: Indicates if reports and notifications are enabled for the user.

browserstack_user_id.description: BrowserStack user ID associated with this user.

group_id.description: Group ID the user belongs to.

group_id.description: Group ID the user belongs to.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user.

browserstack_user_id.description: BrowserStack user ID associated with this user.

group_id.description: Group ID the user belongs to.

reports_and_notification_enabled.description: Indicates if reports and notifications are enabled for the user.

PageInfo.description: Pagination metadata returned with paged API responses.

prev.description: Previous page number if applicable; null otherwise.

next.description: Next page number if applicable; null otherwise.

id.description: Unique identifier for the configuration.

group_id.description: ID of the group associated with the configuration.

is_suggested.description: Indicates if the configuration is suggested.

row_data.description: Array of values for the row.

rows_count.description: Total number of rows in the dataset.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the dataset was created.

ExploratorySessionUserRef.description: A user reference object returned in exploratory session responses.

id.description: TCM user ID.

group_id.description: Group ID the user belongs to.

ExploratorySessionIssue.description: A linked issue / defect associated with an exploratory session or session log.

issue_id.description: Identifier of the issue in the external issue tracker (e.g. Jira key).

issue_type.description: Type of the issue in the external tracker.

ExploratorySessionTimelineEntry.description: A single timeline event recorded against an exploratory session.

action.description: The lifecycle action that was performed.

timestamp.description: UTC timestamp when the action occurred.

id.description: Unique identifier for the exploratory session.

description.example: Exploring the checkout flow for edge cases.

charter.description: Testing charter describing the scope and goals of this session.

session_state.description: Current lifecycle state of the session.

timebox_duration.description: Planned duration of the session in minutes.

duration.description: Actual duration tracked during the session in minutes.

session_log_count.description: Number of logs recorded in this session.

folder_id.description: ID of the folder this session belongs to.

ExploratorySessionLog.description: A log entry recorded within an exploratory testing session.

Filter.description: Filter object representing a saved filter view

id.description: Unique identifier for the filter

entity_type.description: Entity type the filter applies to

is_project_level.description: Whether this filter is available at project level

filters.description: Filter criteria object containing the actual filter conditions

created_at.description: Timestamp when the filter was created

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the filter was last updated

project_id.description: Project ID this filter belongs to

ReportType.description:
Report type, sent as its DISPLAY NAME (not a machine slug).

Seven types produce data. `Defects Summary` and `Defects Detailed Report` are
accepted on create/update but have no data branch on the server, so such a report
always reads back with `report_data: null` — never offer them as a way to report
on defects (use `Test Run Summary`, whose sections include `issues_by_priority` /
`issues_by_status`).

Pick by what the user asked about:
  - test cases created / updated / deleted, churn, top creators → `Test Case Activity`
  - run execution + pass rates                                 → `Test Run Summary`
  - per-case results within runs                               → `Test Run Detailed Report`
  - plan-level rollup                                          → `Test Plan Summary`
  - requirement/issue coverage                                 → `Requirement Traceability Report`
  - exploratory sessions                                       → `Exploratory Session Summary`
  - per-user workload                                          → `User Workload Report`

ReportFrequency.description:
Scheduling cadence. Send `frequency` and `frequency_details` TOGETHER, or omit
BOTH — omitting both creates a valid unscheduled, on-demand report.

Two consequences of omitting them: `mail_to` is only persisted for scheduled
reports (recipients on an unscheduled report are silently dropped), and
`next_run_at` stays null.

There is no `once` value — the server's cadence enum is daily/weekly/monthly only.

ReportTimeframe.description:
The window a report covers. Also the value of the `reportTimeRange` query param
on the report-detail read.

The four relative windows compute a date range from "now". `custom` computes it
from `custom_date_range` and **requires** that field — sending `custom` without it
is an unhandled server error, not a 422.

The five remaining values carry no dates; they select entities through
`report_filters` instead:
  `specific_test_runs`  → report_filters.test_runs
  `specific_test_plans` → report_filters.test_plans
  `specific_test_cases` → report_filters.test_cases
  `specific_sessions`   → report_filters.session_ids
  `requirements`        → report_filters.requirements

FrequencyDetails.description:
Shape depends on `frequency` — the server rejects the wrong shape with
"Invalid report frequency", which names `frequency` even when `frequency` itself
was fine and only `day` was missing:

  daily   → { "time": "08:00" }
  weekly  → { "time": "08:00", "day": "monday" }   day = lowercase day name
  monthly → { "time": "08:00", "day": 15 }         day = integer 1-28

`time` is 24-hour `HH:MM`, interpreted as UTC.

day.description:
Required for weekly (lowercase day name) and monthly (integer 1-28).
Omit for daily.

Required for weekly (lowercase day name) and monthly (integer 1-28).
Omit for daily.

FolderHierarchy.description: Folder hierarchy mapping. Each key is a folder ID (as a string), and the value is an array of ancestor folder objects ordered from the folder itself up to the root.

test_data.description: Optional test data for the step

configuration_id.description: ID of the configuration this test result is associated with

id.description: Report ID

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the scheduled report was created

next_run_at.description: Next scheduled iteration, or null when the report is not scheduled

day.description:
Required for weekly (lowercase day name) and monthly (integer 1-28).
Omit for daily.

id.description: Id of the report owner

email.description: Email to which the report is to be sent

id.description: Unique identifier for the configuration.

group_id.description: ID of the group associated with the configuration.

is_suggested.description: Indicates if the configuration is suggested.

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

uuid.description: Unique identifier for the dataset column/variable.

dataset.description: Dataset information that this column belongs to.

count_rows.description: Number of rows in the dataset.

success.description: Indicates if the request was successful.

id.description: User ID

full_name.description: Full name of the current user

email.description: Email address of the current user

reports_and_notification_enabled.description: Whether reports and notifications are enabled for the user

V1ProjectDetail.description: v1 project-detail envelope (GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}, by INTEGER id). The translation output is data.project.identifier (the PR-NNN form), alongside data.project.id (the integer id you queried by).

identifier.description: PR-NNN identifier — the v2 {project_id}. (Integer -> PR-NNN translation output.)

id.description: Integer project id — the value passed in the path. Same as thProjectId.

description.example: This project contains test cases and test runs for the demo project

SelectionData.description:
A folder-keyed test-case selection: which cases, grouped by the folder they live in.
All three keys are required. Widen with `select_all` (whole project) or a folder's
`test_case_select_all` (whole folder), then subtract with `deselected_test_cases`;
otherwise the cases are listed explicitly in `selected_test_cases`.

select_all.description: Select every case in the project.

folders.description: Map of folder id (as a STRING key) to that folder's selection.

unique_test_case_count.description: Number of distinct cases the selection resolves to.

V1TestCaseDetail.description: v1 test-case detail (GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/folder/{folder_id}/test-cases/{test_case_id}, by INTEGER ids). Translation output: data.test_case.identifier (the TC-NNN form).

identifier.description: TC-NNN identifier — the v2 test-case id (read via ?id=TC-NNN). (Integer -> TC-NNN translation output.)

id.description: Integer test-case id — the value passed in the path.
history record ID

entity_id.description: test case ID this history belongs to

modified_fields.description: List of fields that were modified in this version

modified.description: Details of what was modified (field changes)

self.description: API endpoint to retrieve this specific history record

histories.description: List of history records for the test case

V1TestPlanDetail.description: v1 test-plan detail (GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/test-plans/{test_plan_id}, by INTEGER ids). NOTE: there is NO `data` wrapper — the plan sits at the top level under `test_plan`. Translation output: test_plan.identifier (the TP-NNN form).

identifier.description: TP-NNN identifier — the v2 {test_plan_id}. (Integer -> TP-NNN translation output.)

V1TestRunDetail.description: v1 test-run detail (GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/test-runs/{test_run_id}, by INTEGER ids). Translation output: data.test_run.identifier (the TR-NNN form). The integer run id is surfaced as data.test_run.uuid.

identifier.description: TR-NNN identifier — the v2 {test_run_id}. (Integer -> TR-NNN translation output.)

id.description: Also the TR-NNN identifier (string form).

uuid.description: Integer test-run id — the value passed in the path.

internal_name.description: Internal system name for the status

is_default.description: Whether this is the default status (1 or 0)

colour.description: Hex color code for the status

value.description: Numeric value identifier for the status

values.description: Array of test result status values

total_count.description: Total number of test result status values

id.description: Unique identifier of the custom field

is_required.description: Whether the custom field is required

place_holder_text.description: Placeholder text for the custom field

default_value.description: Default value for the custom field

entity_type.description: Type of entity this field is for

options.description: Options for dropdown or multi-dropdown fields

applies_to_all_projects.description: Whether the custom field applies to all projects

assigned_projects.description: List of project identifiers this field is assigned to

link_to_future_projects.description: Whether to link this field to future projects

default_fields.description: Default field values for test results. Only 'status' field is included by default.

custom_fields.description: Custom fields array. Only present when 'all' parameter is true.

rows_count.description: Total number of rows in the dataset.

test_cases_count.description: Number of test cases using this dataset.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the dataset was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the dataset was last updated.

success.description: Indicates if the request was successful.

V1DuplicatesListResponse.description:
Suggested-duplicate list. NOTE this exact shape with an empty `duplicates` is also what
the server returns when the group lacks the dedupe feature flag, so an empty list is not
evidence that the project has no duplicates — check .../ai-duplicates/status.

count.description: Total number of sessions matching the query.

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful.

data.description: Contains an array of Scheduled reports

scheduled_report_count.description: The total number of scheduled reports in the project.

total_report_count.description: The total number of reports in the project.

created_at.description: When the tag was first used

usage_count.description: Number of test cases using this tag (optional)

id.description: User ID

has_access.description: Whether user has access to the project

permissions.description: List of permissions granted to user

is_delighted_visible.description: Whether Delighted feedback widget is visible

is_lcnc_explore_dismissed.description: Whether low-code/no-code explore banner is dismissed

reports_and_notification_enabled.description: Whether reports and notifications are enabled

is_build_listing_enabled.description: Whether build listing feature is enabled

is_new_project_settings_visible.description: Whether new project settings UI is visible

is_jira_app_project_panel_visible.description: Whether Jira app project panel is visible

id.description: Attachment ID

url.description: Pre-signed S3 URL for viewing (inline, ~26 min expiry)

download_url.description: Pre-signed S3 URL for downloading (attachment, ~26 min expiry)

TestRunTestCaseV2.description: One test case AS MAPPED INTO A TEST RUN — a case-plus-configuration row, not the project-level test case record. A case mapped to several configurations appears once per configuration.

latest_status.description: Latest execution status for THIS run row, e.g. untested / passed / failed.

latest_result_id.description: Id of the latest result recorded against this row; use it to read or amend that result.

assignee.description: Assignee of this row within the run.

configuration_id.description: Configuration this row is for; null when the case is mapped without a configuration.

project_id.description: Project of the run being read.

source_project_id.description: Project the case itself lives in; equals project_id unless the case is shared in from elsewhere.

V2BulkResultOutcome.description: Per-test-case outcome of a bulk result submission. Reports whether the entry was accepted for async processing, not whether it was applied.

error.description: Present only when status is FAILED.

V2TestResultListItem.description: One recorded result for a test case in a test run, as the v2 read returns it.

created_by.description: Email of the user who recorded the result; null when the user is not in the caller's group.

test_case_id.description: Echoed back as the TC- identifier that was requested, not a numeric id.

step_result.description: Present only for step-level results; null otherwise.

dataset.description: Dataset row this execution used, as {variable, row} pairs. Empty for non-data-driven runs.

V2TestRunResultDetail.description: The single result written by a v2 result submission.

id.description: Id of the created result. Carry this forward for a follow-up update; it is the id domain the server expects back.

test_run_test_case_step_details.description: Present only when the submission carried step_results.

Template.description: A test-case template as returned in list responses: metadata and counts, without the field layout.

id.description: Template id — a plain integer.

entity.description: What the template applies to. Always TestCase on this surface.

enabled.description: True when the template is active. False means disabled — still stored, with its fields and project links, and re-enablable.

step_type.description: Step style identifier for test-case templates; null for templates that do not define one.

is_default.description: True for the workspace default template for this entity type. The default cannot be disabled or deleted.

is_system.description: True for a built-in template. System templates cannot be deleted.

future_projects_applicable.description: True when projects created later are linked to this template automatically.

field_count.description: Number of fields in the template. Null when the count was not computed for this response.

project_count.description: Number of linked projects. Null when the workspace-wide count was skipped server-side — treat null as 'not computed', not zero.

TemplateFieldMapping.description: One field placed on a template, as returned by a template read. Note these are mapping records, not the ids sent when writing a template.

id.description: Id of the mapping row, NOT the field id. When resending a field on an update, use custom_field_id or system_field_id, not this.

field_category.description: Which section the field sits in.

custom_field_id.description: Set for a custom field; null for a system field.

system_field_id.description: Set for a built-in field; null for a custom field.

field_data.description: The underlying field definition — the system field when custom_field_id is null, otherwise the custom field. For custom fields the field type is returned as a name, with the raw numeric type alongside it.

TemplateWithFields.description: A test-case template together with its full field layout, as returned by a single-template read or a create.

description_fields.description: Fields in the description section, ordered.

properties_fields.description: Fields in the properties section, ordered. The Review & Approve fields (reviewers, review status) are filtered out of this surface even when stored on the template.

step_fields.description: Step-level custom fields, ordered. Always an empty array for workspaces without step custom fields enabled; the key is always present.

V2PublicTestCase.description: A test case as the v2 public project API serialises it on read and on write. NOT the same shape as the `TestCase` schema the older endpoints return: the title is `title` (not `name`), priority/status/case_type are plain display strings (not objects), owner is an email string (not an integer id), custom fields are name/value pairs, and there is no integer `id` — the case is identified by `identifier`.

identifier.description: TC-NNN, or the third-party identifier when the workspace issues project-level ids.

title.description: The case title. Sent as `name` on a write, returned as `title`.

folder_id.description: Integer id of the folder the case now sits in.

folder_path.description: Ancestor folder ids, root first. Only present on the reads that resolve the folder tree; absent from write responses.

priority.description: The project's display value, e.g. 'Medium'. Null when unset.

status.description: The project's display value for the case's own lifecycle status, e.g. 'Active'.

case_type.description: The project's display value for the case type, e.g. 'Smoke & Sanity'.

automation_status.description: Internal name, e.g. not_automated / automated / obsolete.

owner.description: Owner's EMAIL, or the imported owner name for cases brought in from another tool. Null when the owner does not resolve to a user in this group.

template.description: Template name, e.g. test_case_steps or bdd.

issues.description: Linked defects. Each entry comes back as {jira_id, issue_type} — note the key is jira_id on read even though a write sends plain issue-id strings.

steps.description: Step list, flattened to step/result only — test_data, shared-step links and per-step custom fields are not echoed here.

feature.description: BDD-template cases only; omitted entirely for other templates.

custom_fields.description: Name/value pairs, never the id-keyed map a write sends. A multi-select field carries `values` (array) instead of `value`. Always present, as [] when the case has none.

attachments.description: Present only when the case has attachments. Size is a human-readable string, not bytes.
