reviewers.description: Omitted entirely unless the project has Review & Approve enabled on a Team-Pro plan. Shape depends on the workspace's read-shape flag: [{email, review_status}] or full user objects.

review_status.description: Aggregate review state of the case. Omitted when the review workflow is off or unset.

last_updated_at.description: Last update timestamp — named last_updated_at here, not updated_at.

updated_by.description: Email of the last user to write to the case.

urls.description: Web-app link for the case, for showing a human where it lives.

V2History.description: One revision of a test case as returned by the v2 history listing. The internal record id, entity_id, entity_type, project_id, group_id, the nested user object and the links block are stripped before the record is returned.

version_id.description: Opaque version identifier for this revision.

version_name.description: Positional label for the revision — V1, V2, V3 … — where V1 is the oldest revision visible under the caller's plan. The number is what the single-version read takes.

source.description: What produced the revision: 'create' for the original, 'update' for an edit, 'restore' after a rollback.

modified_fields.description: Names of the fields this revision changed. Null on the creating revision.

modified.description: Per-field before/after map, e.g. {"title": {"old": "...", "new": "..."}}. Only the newest record on each page is enriched with this detail; other rows may come back without it. Rows whose old and new are both empty are dropped.

comment.description: Optional note recorded with the change.

updated_by.description: Email of the user who made the change. Null when the user id cannot be resolved to a user in this group.

user_id.description: BrowserStack user id of the editor — the raw id updated_by is resolved from.

testcase_id.description: Identifier of the test case this revision belongs to — the third-party identifier when one is set, otherwise the TC-NNN identifier. Falls back to TC-<internal id> if the case cannot be fetched.

TestPlanV2.description: A test plan or sub-plan as the v2 plan surface serializes it. Note there is no numeric id field — `identifier` (TP-NNN / STP-NNN) is the only id in this payload, and project_id is the PR-NNN identifier, not the numeric project id.

identifier.description: TP-NNN, or STP-NNN for a sub-plan. The id every v2 plan path takes.

description.description: Rich text, sanitised on write; links are rewritten on read, so it can differ from what was sent.

active_state.description: Derived: 'completed' once the plan is completed, otherwise 'active'. Does not distinguish new from started.

issues.description: Linked tracker issues, each with issue_id / issue_type and any resolved metadata.

test_runs_count.description: This plan's own runs, split by state. Sub-plan runs are not rolled up.

test_runs.description: Present ONLY on the single-plan read, and only when the run fetch succeeded: a preview of at most the first 30 runs, each with identifier and name alone.

sub_plans_count.description: Children of a top-level plan; null on a sub-plan.

parent_plan_id.description: The parent's TP-NNN identifier — present only when this plan is a sub-plan.

project_id.description: PR-NNN identifier of the owning project, not a number.

links.description: API self / test_runs links. Present only on the single-plan read, alongside test_runs.

urls.description: Web-app deep links for a human, plus a sub_test_plans link on top-level plans only.

TestRunSummaryV2.description: A test run as the v2 plan's run listing serializes it — a summary shape. It carries NO numeric id and no uuid: `identifier` (TR-NNN) is the only id present, and configurations are bare integer ids rather than objects.

run_state.description: Lifecycle state; a brand-new run reports 'new_run'.

active_state.description: Derived: 'closed' once the run is closed, otherwise 'active'.

assignee.description: Email of the run's owner; null when it cannot be resolved.

overall_progress.description: Map of result status name to case count, e.g. {Passed: 12, Failed: 1}. Omitted entirely when nothing has been executed.

filter_test_cases.description: Carries is_dynamic — whether the run's case list is filter-driven.

test_plan.description: The plan this run belongs to; its `id` field holds the TP-NNN identifier, not a number.

links.description: API self / test_cases links for the run.

V2ReportDetail.description: A report's public v2 configuration record. Identifiers replace internal integer ids, and it carries no report data — only how the report is set up.

id.description: The report's identifier. A per-group sequence number, unrelated to the integer report id the v1 report capabilities take.

project_ids.description: Every project the report covers. A single-project report lists just its own.

report_type.description: Display name of the report type, e.g. 'Test Run Summary'.

title.description: Display name. Auto-generated as '<report_type>-MM/DD/YYYY' when the creator omitted it.

report_timeframe.description: Rolling window or scope mode, e.g. last_one_week, custom, specific_test_runs.

custom_date_range.description: Two space-separated YYYY-MM-DD dates; set only for the custom timeframe.

frequency.description: 'once' is substituted for an unscheduled report whose stored frequency is null.

next_run_at.description: When the schedule next fires. Null for a one-off report.

is_scheduled.description: True only when a valid frequency and frequency_details pair was supplied.

owner.description: Creator, as email and full_name. No user id is exposed.

mail_to.description: users (email + full_name objects) and external_mails (plain addresses). Populated only for scheduled reports.

report_filters.description: Configured scope echoed back as public identifiers (TR-NNN, TP-NNN, assignee emails). Sub-plans collapse to TP-NNN; values fall back to prefix+internal id if the lookup fails.

dynamic_filters.description: Always null on this surface, whatever was sent at create time.

latest_attachment.description: Newest generated file in the PROJECT, not necessarily this report's: generated_at, file_type (a MIME type such as application/pdf) and ready, which is true whenever the object is present.

AttachmentListItem.description: One attachment row as the v2 per-entity attachment listing serializes it - a deliberately thin projection, not the full stored attachment record.

id.description: Attachment id. This is the id the delete-attachment capabilities take.

size.description: File size in bytes. Renamed from the stored byte_size field, which is not present under this name here.

url.description: Location to read the file from. There is no separate download endpoint for these attachments.

data_id.description: Present ONLY on inline attachments (images embedded via the rich-text editor). Its presence is how an inline row is told apart from a real file attachment.

TestResultSearchItem.description: One test result row from the account-wide result search. Leaner and differently keyed than TestResult: no custom_fields, no step result and no configuration_id, but it carries the owning project, run and case so a cross-project row can be traced back.

id.description: Result id. Project-scoped single-result reads need this together with project_id.

author.description: Who logged the result. Absent entirely when the result came from an import and no matching user exists; then only full_name and email are present, sourced from the import.

updated_by.description: Who last changed the result; null when the updating user is not resolvable. Carries id, browserstack_user_id, full_name and email only.

description.description: Result notes as rich text. User mentions are rewritten to display names in this payload.

created_by_imported.description: Name carried over from an import when the result has no BrowserStack author.

attachments.description: Each entry also carries a human-readable `size` string derived from byte_size.

issues.description: Linked tracker issues. Each entry carries issue_id and issue_type, plus a duplicate `jira_id` mirroring issue_id whatever the tracker actually is.

configuration.description: Configuration the result was logged against. Always requested, so present whatever compact is set to.

test_case.description: Present ONLY when compact=false was sent; absent otherwise.

test_run.description: Present ONLY when compact=false was sent. Its `id` is overwritten with the run's TR-NNN identifier string, not a number.

test_case_id.description: Integer case id from the result mapping; omitted when the mapping is absent.

test_run_id.description: Integer run id from the result mapping — but replaced by the run's TR-NNN identifier STRING whenever the test_run relation is present (compact=false). Type-check before using it.

test_run_results_mapping_id.description: Id of the run/case mapping the result hangs off.

project_id.description: Numeric id of the project the result lives in. This is how you tell cross-project rows apart; it is present only when the search service returned it.

links.description: Present only when the row carried a project_id. Holds `self` only — no custom_fields link on this path.

Comment.description: One comment as the v1 serializer emits it — a flat object (the published spec wraps it under an extra `comment` key that the server does not send).

id.description: Comment id; the handle for later edit/delete.

user_id.description: The AUTHOR, despite the name. `id` is the internal TM user id (not the BrowserStack user id) and is null for comments imported from another tool, whose original author name is carried in full_name.

group_id.description: Internal TM group id of the owning workspace.

parent_id.description: Always null through this path; replies are not threaded.

entity_id.description: Id of the run/case mapping cell the comment is attached to — not the test case id and not the run id.

entity_type.description: 'TRTC' for a comment on a test case inside a test run.

comment.description: HTML body with @mentions rendered to display names and links decorated; can differ from what was posted.

edited.description: True once the comment has been changed after posting.

is_editable.description: False for system/imported comments that cannot be edited.

review_status.description: Present only on comments that were recorded as part of a review verdict.

StatusProgressBreakdown.description: Per-result-status progress of a run or one of its configurations. Keys are result-status ids as STRINGS ('1', '2', ...); each value is the count of run test cases currently in that status plus the status definition. Statuses with no cases may be absent. Empty object when nothing has been recorded.

count.description: Number of test cases in the run (or configuration) whose latest result has this status.

internal_name.description: Stable machine name (passed, failed, blocked, untested, ...). Use this to compare across projects; ids differ per project.

BinnedTestCase.description: A test case as it appears in the recycle-bin listing: a slim row from the bin store plus resolved people, not the full TestCase shape.

id.description: Integer id — what restore/purge selections take.

owner.description: Raw BrowserStack user id of the owner; see owner_details for the person.

owner_details.description: Resolved owner {id, browserstack_user_id, full_name, email, group_id}; absent when owner is null or unknown.

folder_path.description: Breadcrumb of the folder the case was in when binned.

updated_by.description: Raw BrowserStack user id of who moved it to the bin; see updator_details.

updator_details.description: Resolved person who binned the case {id, browserstack_user_id, full_name, email, group_id}.

trashed_at.description: When the case was moved to the bin.

days_remaining.description: Days left before automatic permanent purge.

V1DuplicatePair.description: One AI-suggested duplicate test-case pair as this product serialises it. Used by the single-duplicate read and as the element type of the duplicates listing and search.

id.description: The duplicate id. This is the value the read, resolve and discard calls take.

ai_score.description: Model confidence for the pair. A score below 100 is a semantic match; 100 is an exact one.

reason.description: The model's stated reason for believing the two cases are duplicates.

test_cases.description: The two test cases in the pair. Always exactly two — except in a listing filtered by entity_id, where the filtered-on case is removed and only the other one remains.

id.description: Integer test case id — what the resolve call takes as source/target/archive id.

identifier.description: Display identifier (TC-NNN), or the third-party identifier when the case came from an external tool.

folder_id.description: Id of the folder holding the case.

title.description: The test case name (renamed from `name` on the way out).

description.description: Empty string rather than null when the case has no description.

owner_id.description: Raw BrowserStack user id of the owner.

owner.description: Resolved owner display name; an empty string when the user cannot be resolved in this group.

FolderV2.description: Folder as returned by the public (v2) folder write endpoints. Leaner than the internal Folder shape: no project_id, group_id, is_automation or total_cases_count.

name.description: Final saved name — may differ from what was sent when auto-rename resolved a clash (lowercased, ' (1)' appended).

description.description: Sanitised HTML notes; null when never set.

parent_id.description: Integer id of the parent folder; null for a root folder.

cases_count.description: Test cases directly in this folder (not descendants).

attachments.description: Present only when the folder has attachments.

sub_folders.description: API path that lists this folder's sub folders.

self.description: Web UI URL that opens this folder.

ConfigurationGroup.description: An account-level configuration dimension (for example Operating System, Browser or Device) whose selectable values are held as its options.

id.description: Integer id of the group; use it to read or change the group's options.

is_system.description: True for groups the product ships rather than ones the account created.

group_id.description: The owning account (BrowserStack group). Identical on every row of a single response.

record_status.description: Lifecycle state of the record, e.g. active.

LinkedIssueTestCase.description: A test case as returned in a tracker ticket's linked-case list. Leaner than the full test case read, and carries issue-panel-only fields.

identifier.description: The case's TC-NNN identifier, or the third-party identifier when the case was imported.

owner.description: The resolved owner user, or null when the owner id cannot be resolved in the caller's group.

project.description: Summary of the owning project, supplied so the panel can render across projects.

priority.description: Flattened to the priority's internal name or display value, unlike the object form used elsewhere.

issues.description: The tracker tickets this case is linked to.

dropdown.description: The project's default field option sets, repeated per case so the panel can label status and priority ids.

self_ui_link.description: Web app path for this case — a link for a human, not an API path.

last_test_info.description: Present only when the case has been executed at least once. Absent — not null — for a never-run case.

last_run_id.description: The run's TR-NNN identifier, not its integer id, despite the name.

SharedComponent.description: A shared field (called a shared component by the API) as it appears in a project listing.

step_count.description: Number of steps inside this shared field.

test_case_count.description: Number of test cases embedding it - the blast radius of any change.

created_by.description: Null when the author's user record can no longer be resolved.

V2TestCaseDetail.description: A test case as the v2 public API serializes it (create, get, update and move). Differs from the internal `TestCase` shape: `title` instead of name, `steps` [{step, result}] instead of test_case_steps, owner/created_by/updated_by as emails, custom fields by display name, and NO integer id — `identifier` is the handle.

identifier.description: TC-NNN, or the customer-defined identifier when the workspace uses its own ids. Use this in later calls.

title.description: The case name (sent as `name` on write).

template.description: Step style: test_case_steps or test_case_bdd. The template id itself is not returned.

folder_path.description: Folder ids from root to the case's folder. Only present on list responses, not on single-case responses.

owner.description: Owner's email; falls back to the imported owner label for migrated cases.

steps.description: Ordered steps for a classic case; always [] for a Gherkin case.

feature.description: Gherkin cases only; absent on classic cases.

background.description: Gherkin cases only; absent on classic cases.

scenario.description: Gherkin cases only; absent on classic cases.

custom_fields.description: One entry per set custom field, keyed by display name. Multi-dropdowns carry `values` (array) instead of `value`.

value.description: Scalar value; dropdown option label, user email, boolean, etc.

review_status.description: Only when the project has Review & Approve enabled.

reviewers.description: Only when the project has Review & Approve enabled; shape depends on the workspace's reviewer-API flags (emails with review_status, or user objects).

last_updated_at.description: Note the name: last_updated_at, not updated_at.

self.description: Deep link to the case in the Test Management UI.

GlobalSearchEntityResults.description: One entity type's slice of an account-wide search result. Present only for the types that were asked for.

data.description: The matching records for this entity type. Row shape follows the entity, and carries a display_meta block enriched with owner, project and folder names except on the typeahead fast path.

folders.description: Folder-hierarchy lookup for the test-case results only, keyed by folder id.

TestRunWriteResponse.description:
REPLACEMENT for the existing key of the same name — adds the top-level `skipped_test_case_ids`
sibling the handlers actually render. Successfully returned the test run after a WRITE
(create / edit / assign / close / delete). NOTE the envelope key is `data.testrun` with NO
underscore on these operations, unlike clone and the plain reads, which use `data.test_run`.
`skipped_test_case_ids` is a SIBLING of `data`, not inside it, and lists cases the review gate
refused to add. Client errors from the backing service replace the payload with
{data: {success: false, error: <message>}} at the 4xx status. Verified against
TestRunsHelper#update_testrun_th, BuildsSerializationHelper#builds_public_update_testrun_th
and Api::V1::TestRunsController#create / #destroy.

error.description: Only present when success is false; the backing service's message.

skipped_test_case_ids.description: Top-level sibling of `data`. Cases the review gate excluded from the write. Always [] on the build-backed flow.

BadRequest.description: Bad request due to invalid parameters.

NotFound.description: The requested resource was not found.

Forbidden.description: Forbidden access. You don't have permission.

UnprocessableEntity.description: The request was well-formed but contains semantic errors.

BulkDeleteTestCasesResponse.description: Response after bulk deleting test cases

BulkMoveTestCasesResponse.description: CORRECTION of an existing key (only bulk_move_test_cases uses it). A synchronous bulk move renders the refreshed source listing, not {success, folders}. Above the async threshold the same 200 carries {success, async:true, unique_id} and none of these keys.

cases_count.description: Case counts keyed by folder id, for the source and destination folders.

source_path_folders.description: Only present when the request scoped a source folder.

moved_cases_count.description: Only present on a cross-project move.

TestRunResponse.description:
REPLACEMENT for the existing key of the same name — the current definition declares a
`data.project` that the handlers never render. Successfully returned a test run under a
`data` envelope, keyed `test_run` WITH an underscore. Used by the v1 run reads and by clone.
NOTE the write operations on this entity (create / edit / assign / close / delete) return
`data.testrun` with NO underscore instead, and the v2 run endpoints have no `data` envelope
at all. Verified against the render calls in Api::V1::TestRunsController#clone,
#clone_via_preprocessor, #show and #show_cases.

unique_id.description: Tracking ID for async operation (present when async=true)

RootFolderDetailsResponse.description: Response containing only root folder details including test case counts, and links.

SharedStepsPostResponse.description: Response containing details of a shared step.

test_case_count.description: Number of test cases using this shared step

step_count.description: Number of steps in this shared step

TestResultCreateResponse.description: Successful response for creating a test result

configuration_id.description: ID of the configuration this test result is associated with

scheduled_report_count.description: The total number of scheduled reports in the project.

total_report_count.description: The total number of reports in the project.

channel.description: Unique channel identifier for streaming or polling download status.

export_id.description: Export record ID for tracking progress

ActiveTestRunsInfo.description: REPLACEMENT for the existing ActiveTestRunsInfo (single-use, only get_active_test_runs_info_v1 points at it). The handler renders an OBJECT with a `data` array; the shipped version declares a bare top-level array.

data.description: One entry per result status across the project's active test runs. When more than six statuses exist only the top six by count are kept and the remainder are collapsed into a single 'Other' entry that has links but NO result_status.

name.description: Status display name, or the literal 'Other' for the collapsed bucket.

y.description: Number of results in this status.

links.description: Present on the collapsed 'Other' entry; carries a UI filter URL covering the statuses that were merged in.

filter_details.description: Merged in only when filter_details=true and q was present.

AutomationStats.description: Response containing the automation statistics for the test cases.

ClosedTestRunsInfo.description: Closed test runs analytics data by month

ClosedTestRunsSplit.description: Closed test run results split by month and status

RemoveFolderSummaryResponse.description: A summary of entities that would be deleted when removing a folder

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful

has_other_product_entity.description: Indicates if the folder contains entities from other products

test_recordings_count.description: Number of test recordings that would be deleted

active_test_case_count.description: Number of active test cases that would be deleted

archived_test_case_count.description: Number of archived test cases that would be deleted

sub_folders.description: Number of sub-folders that would be deleted

IssuesCountInfo.description: Response containing the issue count trend for each month.

CustomFieldsV2Response.description: Successful response with paginated custom fields list

id.description: Unique identifier for the custom field

entity_type.description: Entity type this field belongs to

is_bulk_editable.description: Whether the field can be bulk edited

is_filterable.description: Whether the field can be used in filters

linked_projects_count.description: Number of projects this field is linked to

group_id.description: Group ID this field belongs to

selection.description: The primary project's persisted folder-structured test-case selection (with select_all / per-folder flags + unique_test_case_count), in the same shape as the test-run edit/selection endpoint. `{}` when the report has no saved selection for the primary project. Used by the Edit dialog to re-check saved test cases (including folder/project-level select_all, which the flat ids cannot represent).

shared_selection.description: Per-project folder-structured selection for the report's non-primary projects, keyed by project id ({ "<project_id>": <selection> }). Present only for cross-project Test Case Activity reports; `{}` otherwise.

SharedStepsIDResponse.description: Response containing details of a specific shared step by ID.

SharedStepsGetResponse.description: Response containing a list of shared steps with pagination info.

test_case_count.description: Number of test cases using this shared step

step_count.description: Number of steps in this shared step

prev.description: Previous page number if applicable; null otherwise.

next.description: Next page number if applicable; null otherwise.

pre_fetched_shared_step.description: Pre-fetched details for the first shared step (when pre_fetch=true)

prev.description: Previous page number if applicable; null otherwise.

next.description: Next page number if applicable; null otherwise.

TestCaseCountTrend.description: The response contains the trend data for each test case category over the months.

HistoryDiffResponse.description: Response containing the diff of test case steps between two histories.

TestCaseTypeSplit.description: Test case count split by case type

TestResultCustomFieldsResponse.description: Successfully retrieved custom fields for test results

TestRunFormFieldsResponse.description: Successfully retrieved test result form fields

TestRunsSelectionResponse.description:
REPLACEMENT for the existing key of the same name — adds the `selected` array the handler
renders. The test CASES a selection resolves to (this endpoint returns cases, not runs).
`selected` is present only when show='all', and lists the ids of the returned rows that also
match the `q` filter. Verified against Api::V1::TestRunsController#selection.

selected.description: Test case ids, among those returned, that also match the `q` filter. Only rendered when show='all' and at least one row matched.

FolderDetailsResponse.description: Response containing folder details including subfolders, counts, and links.

tags.description: Simple array of tag names (for backward compatibility)

users.description: List of users with access to the project

generic_attachment.description: List of uploaded attachments with metadata

TestRunTestCasesV2Response.description: Paginated test cases of a test run. `info` carries the paging counts and reflects any filters applied.

V2TestRunResultSubmitResponse.description: Result submission accepted. The single form returns the written result under `test-result` (or `test-run-step-results` + `overall-result-status` for a step submission). The bulk form returns only `success: true` when everything was accepted, or `success: false` with `status: "PARTIAL"` and per-case `results` when some entries were rejected — still HTTP 200.

success.description: false on a PARTIAL bulk response even though the status is 200.

status.description: Present only when some bulk entries were rejected.

overall-result-status.description: Status rolled up from the submitted step results.

attachments.description: Attachments bound on a multipart submission.

dropped_attachments.description: Files that were uploaded but belonged to an entry that got rejected.

V2BulkResultStatusAcceptedResponse.description: The bulk status change was queued. It says nothing about which cases were changed or whether the work succeeded.

V2TestResultListResponse.description: Recorded results for one test case in one test run, newest executions included as separate entries. Note the key is `test_results` with an underscore, unlike the v1 list's `test-results`.

TemplateListResponse.description: A page of test-case templates with pagination metadata.

TemplateDetailResponse.description: A single test-case template with its full field layout.

TemplateWriteAckResponse.description: Bare acknowledgement of a template write. Carries no template body, so re-read the template to confirm the result.

success.description: True on success. A free-plan refusal also arrives with HTTP 200 but sets this false and adds a message, so check this flag rather than the status code.

V2HistoryListResponse.description: A page of test case revisions, newest first.

history.description: Revision records for the test case, newest first. Note the key is singular `history`, unlike the v1 listing's `histories`.

TestPlanV2Response.description: A single test plan (or sub-plan read through the plan route). No data wrapper — the plan sits at the top level under `test_plan`.

SubTestPlanV2Response.description: A sub-plan returned by the parent-scoped route. The plan sits under `sub_test_plan`, NOT `test_plan`, and its identifier is STP-NNN.

TestPlanV2ListResponse.description: A page of test plans. Rows omit the embedded test_runs preview and links that the single-plan read adds.

TestRunsListV2Response.description: A page of v2 test runs — the shape returned by both the project-wide run listing and a plan's linked-run listing, which share one serializer. success is hard-coded true even when the upstream run fetch failed; in that case test_runs and info are null and the HTTP status carries the failure.

CustomFieldV2DetailResponse.description: A single custom field after a create or edit. The options, assigned_projects, applies_to_all_projects and link_to_future_projects keys are replayed from the request rather than read back from storage, and are omitted when the request did not carry them.

id.description: Numeric field id — the value the single-field read and the field edit take in their path.

field_type.description: Stored type. Always the stored value, never the one sent on an edit.

is_required.description: Whether a test case must fill the field.

default_value.description: Stored default. Null after a create, because a default cannot be set at create time. On a boolean field it is stored as "1" or "0".

place_holder_text.description: Hint text. Absent when the field has none.

options.description: Echo of the options sent in the request, NOT the stored option list. Absent when the request sent none, even if the field has options stored.

applies_to_all_projects.description: Echo of the request flag, defaulting to false — not a statement about the field's stored project links.

assigned_projects.description: Project identifiers echoed back from the request, truncated to the first 30. Absent when the request sent none.

link_to_future_projects.description: Echo of the request flag, defaulting to false.

CustomFieldV2WithDatasetsResponse.description: A single custom field read by id: stored metadata plus references to the datasets that hold its option values. Carries no option values and no real project configuration.

default_value.description: Stored default; "1" / "0" on a boolean field.

place_holder_text.description: Absent when the field has none.

applies_to_all_projects.description: Always false on this read — a placeholder, not the field's real project scope.

link_to_future_projects.description: Always false on this read — a placeholder, not the field's real future-project setting.

dataset_ids.description: Ids of the datasets holding this field's option values and project links. Empty for a field type that has no options.

datasets_url.description: Ready-made link to this field's dataset collection.

dataset_urls.description: Ready-made link per dataset, in the same order as dataset_ids.

V2ReportListResponse.description: Paginated list of a project's report configurations, plus group/project totals for the filtered set.

info.description: Pagination metadata: page, next, prev, count, page_size.

count.description: Total matching rows, not rows on this page.

scheduled_report_count.description: Scheduled reports within the filtered set, across all pages.

total_report_count.description: All reports within the filtered set, across all pages.

V2ReportDetailResponse.description: A single report configuration, returned by the v2 report create (201) and single-report read (200). Carries no report data.

AttachmentListV2Response.description: A page of attachments on one test case, test result or test plan.

TestResultSearchResponse.description: Account-wide test result search page. Always HTTP 200 with success:true — an upstream search failure is swallowed and shows up as an empty test_results array with info null, not as an error status.

success.description: Always true on this endpoint, including when the search itself failed. Do not use it as a success signal.

test_results.description: Matching results, at most 30 per page (10 if per_page was sent at all). Empty both when nothing matched and when the search errored.

info.description: Paging metadata from the search service. NULL when the search failed — that, not the status code, is how you detect the failure.

CommentsListResponse.description: A page of comments on one run/case cell, newest first, fixed 30 per page. info.count is the total across pages; a page past the end repeats the last page rather than returning an empty array.

CommentResponse.description: The comment just posted, wrapped as data.comment. HTTP 200, not 201.

TestRunConfigurationProgressResponse.description: Execution progress of a test run by result status. TWO shapes: when configuration_id was sent the body is {success, overall_progress_by_status_id} and `configurations`/`info` are absent; when it was not, the body is {success, configurations:[...], info} and the top-level `overall_progress_by_status_id` is absent. `info` is the backing service's paging block passed through unchanged (its exact fields are not fixed by this service).

overall_progress_by_status_id.description: Only in the single-configuration form. {} when no results exist for that configuration.

configurations.description: Only in the all-configurations form. One page of the run's configurations, each with its progress attached.

overall_progress_by_status_id.description: Omitted for a configuration with no recorded progress.

info.description: Only in the all-configurations form. Paging metadata from the backing service, passed through as-is.

BinnedTestCasesListResponse.description: A page of binned test cases. Paging lives under `metadata` (total/page/page_size/total_pages), not the usual `info` envelope. Field names follow the backing service's client model; confirm against a live call if a field is missing.

TestCaseReviewOutcomeResponse.description: Outcome of a bulk review submission or verdict. Under 100 cases: the updated cases inline (testCases) — verdicts with a comment also carry `comment`. Over 100: {success, async:true, unique_id} and NO testCases; the change lands in the background.

testCases.description: Updated cases (serialized test case, including review_status and reviewers). Absent on the async path.

comment.description: Verdict only, when a comment was sent: the created comment objects {id, comment, review_status, user{id, full_name, email}, created_at ...}.

async.description: true when the selection exceeded 100 and was queued.

unique_id.description: Identifier of the queued background operation (async path only).

ReauthRequired.description: Part 11 e-signature required: the reauth_token was missing, expired (5 min) or already used. Re-authenticate and resend with a fresh token.

LcncCreateWrapperResponse.description: Wrapper around the automation service's reply. `status` is the upstream HTTP code and `body` is the upstream body as a JSON-encoded STRING to parse (except the 'already in progress' short-circuit, where body is an object {message, title} and status is 'ok'). HTTP 200 outside does not mean success inside — inspect status and body.

status.description: Upstream HTTP status (an integer), or the string 'ok' on the already-in-progress short-circuit.

body.description: Upstream body as a JSON string; typically {status:'submitted'|'failed', message, test_id?, test_version_id?, reason?} on the bulk-pipeline path.

BddExportValidationResponse.description: Verdict of the BDD export pre-check; the same shape is returned on pass (200, success:true) and on every failure (400, success:false) — read message.

message.example: Validation successful. All test cases belong to the same feature and background.

TestRunV2Response.description: The test run, at the top level of the body. The v2 run endpoints do NOT use the `data` envelope the v1 run endpoints use.

TestRunWriteV2Response.description: The updated test run under `testrun` (no underscore between test and run) at the top level. No `data` envelope.

CustomFieldAdminWriteResponse.description: A custom field definition after a create or edit on the workspace settings surface. The field is echoed under `data` exactly as storage returned it — no options, no datasets and no project links, so confirm those with a separate read.

data.description: The stored field. Take `id` — it is what every other custom-field call puts in its path.

field_type.description: Canonical spelling, not the legacy field_* form the project form-field reads return.

default_value.description: Stored as "1" / "0" on a boolean field; null on every other field type, because this surface forces it to null for non-boolean types.

CustomFieldAdminDetailResponse.description: One custom field definition read by id, with its datasets and their linked projects. Carries no option values and no entity_type.

info.description: Paging over the datasets list; page size is fixed at 30.

system_name.description: Internal name; null for user-defined fields.

place_holder_text.description: Read from the upstream `placeholder` attribute and renamed here.

default_value.description: Converted to a real boolean when field_type is `boolean`; returned as stored otherwise.

type.description: Always the literal "Custom" on this read.

levels.description: Present only for a nested_dropdown field.

datasets.description: Empty array when the field has none. Options are NOT included — read them from the dataset options list.

id.description: Dataset id — what the dataset, option and project-mapping calls take in their paths.

linked_to_all_projects.description: Derived per request by comparing linked_project_count against the workspace project count; not a stored flag.

WorkspaceFieldsListResponse.description: A page of the workspace's fields, system and custom together. Page size is fixed at 10; system fields are injected on page 1 only.

info.description: Paging metadata. On this endpoint it is {count, page, page_size, total_pages} — there is no prev/next.

count.description: Total matching fields; includes the matched system fields when field_source is `all`.

id.description: Numeric field id — absent on the injected system-field rows, which are identified by system_name instead.

field_type.description: Canonical spelling. Injected system-field rows always report `dropdown`.

system_name.description: Internal name, e.g. priority / case_type / status / automation_state on system rows.

dataset_count.description: Number of datasets behind this field; 0 on system rows.

field_values.description: Populated for system rows on page 1; always an empty array for custom fields on this listing.

linked_to_all_projects.description: Derived by comparing linked_projects_count against the workspace project count; always true on system rows.

CustomFieldAdminDatasetResponse.description: One dataset of a custom field — its project links and, when the read asked for them, its option values. There is no paging metadata even though the linked-projects list is paged.

id.description: Dataset id — what the option and project-mapping calls take in their paths.

linked_project_count.description: Total linked projects, not the number in this page of `linked_projects`.

linked_to_all_projects.description: Added by this layer by comparing linked_project_count against the workspace project count. Absent when linked_project_count is not set.

linked_projects.description: One page of the linked projects (30 per page, selected by `p`).

options.description: Present only when the request asked for options (fetch_options), and always present on the project-mapping update response. Absent otherwise — which is indistinguishable from a dataset with no options.

CustomFieldDatasetProjectMappingUpdateRe.description: Result of relinking a dataset's projects. Two different shapes: synchronously the re-read dataset under `data`; above 300 affected projects a bare async acknowledgement with no dataset at all.

async.description: Present and true only when the change was handed to a background job (more than 300 projects affected). When it is true there is no `data`, and the path ids were never validated.

unique_id.description: Job handle for the async case only. There is no endpoint on this surface to poll it — verify by re-reading the dataset.

data.description: The dataset re-read after the change, with its options included. Absent on the async path.

CustomFieldAdminDatasetOptionsResponse.description: A page of a dataset's option values. When any option has a parent the list is returned as a tree and children move under their parent's `children` key rather than appearing at the top level.

info.description: Paging over the options; page size is fixed at 30.

data.description: Empty array when the dataset has no options.

id.description: Option id — what the option update and delete calls take in their paths.

children.description: Present only when the page was rebuilt as a tree and this option has children.

CustomFieldAdminOptionResponse.description: One option value after a create or rename. Always the five serialised keys — keys the request did not set come back null rather than absent.

id.description: Option id — carry this forward; the update and delete calls take it in their paths.

parent_option_id.description: Null unless the option was created under a nested_dropdown parent. The update call cannot change it.

CustomFieldAdminAckResponse.description: Bare success acknowledgement returned by the custom-field delete calls. Nothing about what was removed is echoed back.

ProjectFormFieldsV2Response.description: One project's test-case form: its custom fields, the pick lists behind the standard dropdowns, and the built-in system fields. Three top-level lists, no data envelope and no paging.

custom_fields.description: Every TestCase custom field this project shows, unpaginated. Same row shape as the test-result custom fields listing; rows on a nested_dropdown field additionally carry parent_custom_field_id. `field_type` is the legacy field_* spelling. Empty when the path carried no project.

default_fields.description: Pick lists for the standard test-case dropdowns, keyed by field name (priority, case_type, status, …), each {values, total_count}. `automation_status` is assembled in this layer rather than read from storage.

system_fields.description: Built-in fields available on the test-case template, with id, field_name, field_type, system_name and whether they can be removed from a template.

CustomFieldValuesResponse.description: The values one custom field offers in one project. The payload sits under a DYNAMIC key — the field id exactly as it was spelled in the request path — so there is no fixed property name to read.

info.description: Paging metadata from the backing service. Null when the project id in the path was not numeric.

<field_id>.description: Dynamic key: the field id as sent in the path, e.g. "4821". Not a literal property name.

field_type.description: LEGACY spelling, not the canonical vocabulary the admin write calls take. Null for a nested_dropdown field, which has no legacy spelling, and null when the project id was not numeric.

values.description: The allowed values. Converted to real booleans for a boolean field. Null when the project id in the path was not numeric.

ExploratorySessionListV1Response.description: Paged list of exploratory sessions. Top level, no data envelope.

info.description: Pagination metadata. Falls back to {page:1, page_size:<default>, count:0, prev:null, next:null} when upstream omits it.

count.description: Total rows matching the query — this, not the top-level `count`, is the number to paginate against.
Per-state session totals for the project — NOT the number of rows returned or matched.

ExploratorySessionLogListV1Response.description: Paged list of log entries for one exploratory session. Top level, no data envelope.

info.description: Pagination metadata. Falls back to {page:1, page_size:<default>, count:0, prev:null, next:null} when upstream omits it.

status_counts.description: Intended as whole-session per-status log totals, unfiltered by q[status]. Currently always rendered as an empty object because the upstream response object does not expose the field — do not depend on it.

ExploratorySessionDefectsV1Response.description: Paged list of issue links raised on an exploratory session and on its log entries. Top level, no data envelope.

id.description: Id of the link record itself, not of the ticket.

issue_id.description: Ticket key in the external tracker.

issue_type.description: Tracker the ticket lives in (e.g. jira, zoho).

entity_type.description: What the ticket is linked to — ExploratorySession for a session-level link, ExploratorySessionLog for a link made on one log entry.

entity_id.description: Id of the session or log the link belongs to, interpreted per entity_type.

metadata.description: Free-form tracker metadata captured at link time — ticket url, title, display_category, issue_category.

info.description: Pagination metadata. Falls back to {page:1, page_size:<default>, count:0, prev:null, next:null} when upstream omits it.

ExploratorySessionCloneSyncResponse.description: Clone completed inline (source session had fewer than 50 logs). Status 201.

async.description: false on this branch — the clone and all its logs already exist.

unique_id.description: Always null on the synchronous branch.

ExploratorySessionCloneAsyncResponse.description: Clone accepted and the log copy handed to a background job (source session had 50 or more logs). Status 202. The new session's id is NOT returned.

async.description: true on this branch — the session shell exists but its logs are still being copied.

unique_id.description: Realtime broadcast channel name for the completion event. It is not a job id and no endpoint reports the job's status — to confirm the clone, re-read the sessions listing.

SharedStepDeleteResponse.description: Shared step deleted. Status is 200 with this body — NOT 204 with an empty body.

TestCaseTagListResponse.description: The tags on one test case, as a BARE JSON ARRAY at the top level — there is no object envelope, no `data` and no `success`. Items are tag name strings for projects served from the test-hub backend. For legacy Rails-backed projects the same action renders tag records, whose items are objects {id, name, taggings_count}; treat a non-string item as that shape.

ConfigurationCreateResponse.description: Configuration created. The record is under `configuration` (not `data`), beside a `success` flag. It is the backing service's raw configuration object, not the serialized listing row, so the os/browser/device breakdown may be absent here even though the listing carries it.

FolderWriteResponse.description: Single-folder write acknowledgement used by the v1 folder create and rename actions. The folder is nested under `data` — there is no top-level `folder` and no top-level `success`.

project.description: Present only on root-folder creation; the sub-folder and rename actions omit it.

UserWorkloadDrilldownResponse.description: Single-user workload breakdown, returned verbatim from the analytics service with no envelope and no success flag.

tcs.description: Test cases this user executed in the report's window, with per-case execution counts.

trs.description: Test runs this user participated in over the report's window.

days.description: Day-by-day activity timeline for this user over the report's window.

TestCaseAttachmentDeleteResponse.description: Acknowledgement for a v1 test-case attachment delete. The payload is wrapped in `data` — unlike the attachment list and upload on the same path, which return their payload at the top level.

data.description: Envelope. Reading a top-level `attachments` finds nothing on this action.

attachments.description: The attachment record that was removed. Its stored file is purged, not just unlinked.

BulkRetrieveTestCasesResponse.description: Bulk un-archive acknowledgement: folder case counts after the restore, not the restored test cases. Above the async threshold the same 200 instead carries {success, async:true, unique_id}.

success.description: false with an `error` string and still HTTP 200 when the workspace is not on a paid plan.

folders.description: Per-folder case counts after the restore.

error.description: Present only on the plan-gated 200 refusal.

TestRunCasesBulkEditResponse.description: Synchronous bulk edit of a run's cases: the refreshed run listing. Above the async threshold the same 200 instead carries {success, async:true, unique_id} and no listing.

test_cases.description: The run's per-case rows (mapping id + latest result), not bare test cases.

folder.description: Only present when the request scoped a folder_id.

ancestors.description: Only present on the folder-scoped response.

skipped_test_case_ids.description: Cases the edit could not be applied to.

V1TestCaseCreateResponse.description: v1 single test-case create. Everything is inside `data`, including `success`.

test_case.description: The created case. `id` is the integer id, `identifier` the TC-NNN form, `estimate` always null.

folder.description: The destination folder, with its case counts already incremented for this create.

path_folders.description: Root-to-folder breadcrumb for the new case.

request_trace_id.description: Trace id for the AI enrichment that continues after the response; null when no enrichment was queued.

V1TestCaseWriteResponse.description: v1 full test-case edit (POST .../edit). The updated case sits under `data`, alongside `success` — there is no top-level success key.

TestCaseWriteAckResponse.description: Bare acknowledgement — `{success: true}` and nothing else. The updated record is NOT returned; re-read the case to see the new values.

V1TestCaseDetailResponse.description: v1 test-case detail (slide-over). Everything is inside `data`, including `success`.

test_case.description: Also carries testcase_template, using_fallback_template, folder_path (with include=folder_path), test_run_results and duplicates_tc_count.

pagy.description: Always an empty object on this path.

ArchivedTestCasesListResponse.description: Archived test-case listing. Plan-gated: on a non-paid workspace the same 200 carries {success:false, error} and no test cases.

test_cases.description: Archived cases, each with its original folder path.

cases_count.description: Single-entry map keyed by the requested folder id — null on this route, since it takes no folder.

error.description: Present only on the plan-gated 200 refusal.

SystemFieldValuesResponse.description: Option list for one system field. The options hang off a key NAMED AFTER the field you requested (priority / status / case_type / automation_state / defects), so the path is <field_name>.values.

<field_name>.description: Key is the field_name from the path.

value.description: The numeric option id — this is what the write paths take.

name.description: The project's display name for the option.

TestCaseFolderListResponse.description: Folder-scoped test-case listing. `folders` appears only when the request asked for subfolders.

info.description: page_size is the server-clamped value, not necessarily the per_page you sent.

LegacyTestCaseSearchResponse.description: BARE JSON ARRAY of rows from the deprecated local test-case table — no success, no info, no test_cases wrapper. Empty for any project whose data lives in the current backend.

items.description: Legacy table row: id, name, identifier, project_id, group_id, template, steps and the other legacy columns. Not the serialised TestCase the rest of this surface returns.

TestPlanCloneAcceptedResponse.description: A clone was QUEUED, not completed. The new plan does not exist yet and nothing identifying it is returned — no id, no identifier, no name echo. `unique_id` is a correlation id for the background job only; there is no job-status endpoint for it in this profile. Poll the project's plan listing for the name you sent to find the result.

unique_id.description: Correlation id of the clone job (32-character hex). Not a plan id.

V1TestPlanListResponse.description: A page of v1 test plans. Rows use the same serializer as the single-plan read. `count` is a project-wide {active, completed} rollup, NOT a page total — page with `info`. `filter_details` appears only when filter_details=true was sent together with an owner or custom-field filter. In id-picker mode (filter_mapping=true) each row is reduced to {id, identifier} only.

id.description: Integer plan id — the value every v1 plan route takes in its path.

identifier.description: TP-NNN (STP-NNN for a sub-plan). Display form; not accepted in a v1 path.

owner.description: Owner as a BrowserStack user id; `assignee` carries the resolved user object.

custom_fields.description: Empty ARRAY (not an object) when the plan has no custom-field values.

parent_plan_id.description: Null on a top-level plan; set on a sub-plan.

test_runs_count.description: {active, closed} for runs linked directly to this plan.

total_test_runs_count.description: {active, closed} including the runs of its sub-plans.

test_plan_progress_v2.description: Result rollup keyed by status id. test_plan_progress is always {} and carries nothing.

count.description: Project-wide plan rollup, not a page total.

active.description: Plans whose status is not completed.

filter_details.description: Present only when filter_details=true was sent. Resolves the owner and custom-field filters back into displayable values.

V1ArchivedTestPlanListResponse.description: A page of ARCHIVED v1 test plans. Rows are serialized exactly like the active listing (so record_status is 'archived'), but there is no `count` rollup on this response and archived sub-plans are never included.

id.description: Integer plan id — pass this to bulk-retrieve to restore the plan.

record_status.description: 'archived' on every row of this listing.

BulkAssignTestCasesResponse.description:
Result of a bulk assign on a test run. TWO shapes, decided by the size of the selection.
Under the async threshold the write is applied inline and the body is the run's test-case
listing re-read afterwards: {success, info, test_cases} (plus `folder` when a folder_id was
sent, and a top-level skipped_test_case_ids when the review gate excluded cases). At or above
the threshold the write is queued and the body is {success, async: true, unique_id} with NO
test_cases. Branch on `async`.

async.description: Present and true only when the assignment was queued rather than applied inline.

unique_id.description: Handle for the queued bulk operation. Only present on the async shape.

test_cases.description: One entry per case x configuration mapping, each carrying both `id` (test case) and `mapping_id` (the run mapping). Absent on the async shape.

folder.description: Only present when a folder_id was sent; the folder's status breakdown.

skipped_test_case_ids.description: Cases the review gate excluded. Top level, a sibling of test_cases.

ConfigurationGroupListResponse.description: Successfully retrieved the account's configuration groups

UsersListResponse.description: All active users in the caller's account plus a reduced record for the caller.

users.description: Every active user in the account, ordered by full_name; not filtered to the project.

CommentCreateResponse.description: The comment just posted, wrapped in a data envelope.

ExploratorySessionFormFieldsResponse.description: The extra fields configured for exploratory sessions in this project. The list of built-in fields is always empty on this path.

default_fields.description: Always empty on this path - built-in session details are not described here.

id.description: The field's identifier, used when referring to this field elsewhere.

field_user_name.description: The name your team sees in the product; match a person's plain-words request against this.

field_type.description: The kind of input, for example a single-line string, a dropdown, a date or a user picker.

entity_type.description: The record kind this field belongs to.

is_required.description: True when a session cannot be saved without this field.

optional.description: The inverse of is_required; both are returned.

option_values.description: The choices a dropdown offers. Returned only when the request asked for the choices.

field_values.description: Current values recorded for the field. Returned only when the request asked for the choices.

default_value.description: Pre-filled value, if the field has one. For a yes/no field this comes back as a true or false rather than as a number.

placeholder.description: Hint text shown in the empty field.

is_bulk_editable.description: True when the field can be set on many records at once.

is_filterable.description: True when the field can be used to narrow a list.

parent_custom_field_id.description: Present only for a dependent field; names the field whose value decides this one's choices.

links.description: Where the field's own choices can be read from.

SharedComponentsGetResponse.description: A page of a project's shared fields with page details, optionally carrying the first field's steps.

pre_fetched_shared_step.description: Only present when the pre-fetch option was used on page 1; null otherwise.

CommentListResponse.description: A page of comments on an item, newest first, with page details.

FolderAttachmentsResponse.description: The files attached to the folder itself.

attachments.description: One entry per file on the folder, empty when the folder has none. Alongside the fields below each entry also carries 'size', a ready-formatted version of byte_size for display.

V2TestCaseResponse.description: v2 public-API single-case envelope: {data: {success, test_case}}. Note the case is under `data`, uses `title` (not name) and has no integer id.

GlobalSearchResponse.description: Account-wide search results. By default one group per requested entity type; when results are combined, a single sorted data list plus one info block instead.

report.description: Report matches. Absent on the typeahead fast path even when reports were requested.

project_details.description: Id-to-name lookup for every project referenced by the hits, so a row's project can be named without another call.

data.description: Only when results are combined: all types merged, newest first, each row carrying an entity_type. Capped at 5 rows.

test_case_folders.description: Only when results are combined: the folder lookup for any test-case rows in the merged list.

filter_details.description: Only when explicitly requested: the filters that were applied, with ids resolved to names. Absent if resolution failed.

FolderV2WriteResponse.description: Public (v2) envelope returned after creating, renaming or moving a folder: the affected folder in its public shape.

activity.title: Activity feed (audit trail)
activity.description: Group-wide audit trail of who changed what, on which entity, and when.
key_facts: READ-ONLY by design. Activity events are emitted by the system as a side effect of other writes — there is no create, update, or delete, and there never will be. If asked to edit or remove an audit entry, say it is immutable.

HARD 15-DAY WINDOW. The server clamps every query to the last 15 days no matter what you ask for. For anything older, say the history is not retrievable through the API and point to the Test Management UI — do NOT report 'no activity' for an older period, which would be a false negative.

CURSOR pagination, not page numbers. Follow pagination.next_cursor and stop when pagination.has_next_page is false. There is no p param and no info.count, so you CANNOT state a total number of events or jump to a page.
Not project-scoped in the path — it is group-wide. Pass project_id as a QUERY param to narrow it to one project.

starred_only=true restricts to the caller's starred projects. When they have none the response is {events: [], no_starred_projects: true} — that means 'no starred projects', NOT 'no activity'. Check for that flag before reporting emptiness.
The response carries a projects map (project id → metadata) so you can resolve the project an event refers to without extra reads.
Gated by a group feature flag. If the call is refused, report that the activity feed isn't enabled for the group rather than that there is no activity.

attachment.title: Attachments
attachment.description: A file hanging off a parent test case or test result.
key_facts: ai_uploads uploads a file as AI CONTEXT (restricted types, smaller cap) for seeding case content — see create-test-case.
Each blob/attachment row carries an integer id and a url (the file's location) — read the file from that url; there is no dedicated download endpoint.
A file is attached in TWO steps: upload it to the project to get a numeric blob id, then link that id to the test case, result or step. The link calls take ids, never file content or filenames.
A blob can be linked ONCE. Attaching one that is already referenced elsewhere fails the whole request; upload a separate copy for each place the file should appear.

Putting a NEW file into the product cannot be done through this interface at all — an agent can link an already-uploaded file, remove one, and read attachment metadata, but the upload itself has to happen in the product UI.
Removing an attachment purges the stored file, not just the link. There is no recycle bin for attachments and no undo.
The view and download URLs handed back on upload are pre-signed and expire after about 30 minutes — fetch the file promptly or re-read the attachment to get a fresh one.
The older per-test-case attachment reads return metadata only (id, filename, type, size) with no URL; the newer entity-attachment listing is the one that hands back a readable URL per file.

configuration.title: Configurations
configuration.description: An operating system, browser or device combination that a test run executes against.
key_facts: Configurations live at workspace level, not per project: one created while working in a project appears in every project in the workspace, and the project listing returns the same workspace-wide set everywhere.
Only a configuration's name can be set when creating one. The operating system, browser and device breakdown that reads return cannot be supplied through the API.
Test runs reference a configuration by its integer id, never by name or by the configuration object.
Configurations are gated on the test-run permissions rather than the test-case ones, and there is no way to delete or rename one through this profile — cleanup is a UI operation.

custom_field.title: Custom fields & system fields
custom_field.description: A user-defined field on test cases, results or plans, alongside the built-in system fields.
key_facts: A field applies to ONE entity type (TestCase | TestResult | TestPlan) — pick the matching entity_type; project scope is via the integer project id in the path.
A definition write is workspace-wide, not project-scoped: it affects every project the field's datasets link to. Say which projects are affected BEFORE writing.

field_name IS editable via .../update; field_type is SILENTLY immutable — sending a new type returns 200 and changes nothing. Never report a type change as done; a real one means delete-and-recreate, which destroys every stored value.
Update is a full REPLACE: field_name + field_type + is_required must all be present (missing is_required = 400, missing field_name = 500). Read the field first and resend the whole set.
The project-mapping endpoint uses link_projects / unlink_projects — NOT the linked_projects of the create bodies. The wrong spelling is silently dropped: 200, nothing changed.

Three operations destroy stored data across every linked project: deleting a field, deleting an option, and unlinking a project. There is no bin. Count and name the affected projects before asking to proceed.

Don't confuse a DEFINITION with a VALUE. A definition is which attributes exist; a value is what one case holds. Only values are writable here, through the test-case create/update body's custom_fields.

A field applies to ONE entity type (TestCase | TestResult | TestPlan | ExploratorySession | TestCaseStep) and cannot be moved later. TestCaseStep fields need the group's step-custom-fields feature, and cannot be url or nested_dropdown.

A field DEFINITION is workspace-wide; a DATASET is what makes it visible in a project, by pairing an option list with a set of projects. A field with no dataset, or a dataset with no linked projects, exists but appears nowhere.
A project may belong to only one dataset per field. Linking a project that a sibling dataset already holds is rejected — read the field's existing datasets before linking.

Editing a field definition is a full REPLACE: the label, the mandatory flag and the type must all be resent, and a placeholder or boolean default you leave out is cleared. Read the field first and send back everything you want to keep.

Three operations destroy stored values across every linked project and cannot be undone: deleting a field, deleting an option, and unlinking a project from a dataset. There is no bin. Count and name the affected projects before asking to proceed.
Renaming an option keeps its id, and stored values point at the id — so a rename loses nothing and is the safe way to correct a wrong label. Deleting and recreating is not.

Field types have two spellings. Definitions are written with the canonical names (string, text, user, dropdown, multi_dropdown, url, boolean, int, date, nested_dropdown); the project form-field and field-value reads return the legacy field_* forms (field_dropdown, field_string, …). Translate between them, and expect null where a nested_dropdown has no legacy name.

Don't confuse a DEFINITION with a VALUE. A definition is which attributes exist; a value is what one case holds. Nothing here writes values — those are set when creating or editing the test case, result or plan itself.
A default value can only ever be set on a boolean field. On every other type the admin write calls force it to null, so a default cannot be created or preserved there.

dataset.title: Dataset
dataset.description: A named table of variables and rows that drives data-driven execution of a test case.
key_facts: Team Pro plan gated: without it EVERY dataset endpoint returns 422 "Feature not available". A 422 here means NOT-ENTITLED, not a bad payload — say so and stop, don't retry with a different body.
Datasets keep NO version history and there is no restore: an update replaces the whole table of columns and rows, and the previous contents are unrecoverable. Read a dataset before writing to it.

What you send is not what gets stored. Blank rows and columns that are empty in every row are dropped, cell values are trimmed, rows that end up identical are collapsed to one, and row numbers are reassigned from 1. Always read the stored result back.
Column names are restricted to letters, digits and underscores, must start with a letter, and must be unique within a dataset (compared case-insensitively).
Default size limits are 40 columns and 100 rows per dataset; groups on the raised-limit flag get 100 columns and 200 rows.
Deleting a dataset is permanent and is not blocked by test cases still bound to it — check what it drives first.

duplicate.title: Duplicate recommendation (AI dedupe)
duplicate.description: A machine-suggested pair of near-identical test cases, for a human to review and merge.

relations.via: links the pair it believes are duplicates

key_facts: There is NO create. Duplicate suggestions are produced by the dedupe pipeline; a caller cannot author one.
Only status=suggested can be read or resolved; already-merged/archived/discarded suggestions return 404. A 404 here usually means 'already handled', not 'never existed'.
source_tc works ONLY for status=merged, and the snapshot may legitimately be absent (404 with error 'Source test case snapshot not available'). Treat that as 'not retained', not as a retryable error.
This list family pages with `page`, not the `p` used elsewhere in the profile.
Dedupe REVIEW is exposed here; TCG test-case GENERATION is not. Don't offer to generate cases.

Duplicate review can be paused entirely while the dedupe data is migrated — resolving or discarding then fails with a conflict and an explicit 'try again shortly' message. Nothing was changed; it is safe to retry later.
Resolving a duplicate requires the same permission as removing a test case, while discarding one needs only edit permission. A reviewer who can dismiss suggestions may still be unable to merge them.

Merging archives the source test case and tags it 'Archived as Duplicate', posts a comment on the surviving case, and stores a frozen snapshot of the source. Archived cases are recoverable; the comment and the status change are not undone by recovering one.
The review queue is served ten pairs at a time, ordered by model confidence rather than age, and the page size cannot be increased — the oldest suggestion is not reachable by asking for more rows.
A pair whose test case can no longer be resolved is dropped from the queue, so the reported total can exceed the pairs actually returned.

exploratory_session.title: Exploratory session
exploratory_session.description: An unscripted, charter-driven testing session and the observations recorded during it.
key_facts: session_id and log_id are plain INTEGERS; the parent project takes the INTEGER project id (v1).
Logs hold rich-text HTML sanitised on write (off-project anchor/image links stripped); defects are the issues linked to the session.
Clone runs async when the session has many logs → re-fetch to confirm (see async-jobs).
No convert endpoint: turn session notes into test cases via the create-test-case flow.
session_id and log_id are plain INTEGERS; the parent project takes the INTEGER project id (v1). The display identifier (ES-NNN) is never accepted as an input.
A log entry belongs to exactly one session — both the session id and the log id are needed to change or remove a log, and a log id is not addressable under a different session.

Logs hold rich-text HTML sanitised on write (anchors and images pointing outside the project or group are stripped); screenshots are attached by uploading the image first and referencing its id inside the HTML, never by sending bytes.
Session-level 'defects' are the issue-tracker links recorded during the session — both links on the session and links made on individual logs; each row says which it is.
Closing a session is one-way: nothing accepts a state change and there is no reopen, so a closed session only leaves the default listing, it never comes back to it.
Neither sessions nor logs keep version history, and neither has a recycle bin — a deletion or an overwritten note cannot be recovered.
Listing sessions shows only ACTIVE ones unless the closed state is asked for explicitly.
Cloning a session with 50 or more logs is handled in the background and returns before the copy exists; re-read the session list to confirm. A clone does not carry over the charter or the folder.
Exploratory sessions are governed by the same permissions as test runs; deleting a closed session needs the closed-run delete permission specifically.

filter.title: Saved filter view
filter.description: A saved, named set of filter conditions a user can reapply to a list view.
key_facts: A saved filter view persists a reusable filter: { name, entity, filters, is_project_level }. entity = testcase | testplan | testrun | exploratory_session; filter_id is an integer.
is_project_level scopes the view to the whole project vs. just the creator.
A saved filter view has no version history and no bin — an overwritten name or condition set, and a deleted view, cannot be restored. Read one before changing it if the conditions matter.
Reading a single saved view can change it: conditions on custom fields that no longer exist are pruned from the stored filter as a side effect of the read. The listing does not do this.
Saving a view as project-level publishes it to everyone on the project, and anyone with project access can then edit or delete it — there is no owner-only protection.

folder.title: Folder
folder.description: A container organising test cases inside a project; folders nest to form a tree.
key_facts: Folder ids are plain INTEGERS (e.g. 54) — never FL-… strings. Nesting is via parent_id (integer, null = root).
mv cross-project and copy run ASYNC ({ success, async, unique_id }) — confirm by re-reading the destination (see async-jobs).

Deleting a folder is recursive and takes every subfolder and every test case beneath it. Nothing in this product restores a deleted folder — only the test cases can come back, and only from the recycle bin when that feature is switched on for the group.
Folders keep no version history, so a rename or a notes edit cannot be rolled back to a previous value.
Folder names must be unique among their siblings. Creating or renaming into a clash fails unless auto-rename is asked for; copying a folder resolves the clash silently by prefixing the copy's name.
Folder notes are stored as sanitised HTML with signed image links injected on read, so the text that comes back is not byte-identical to the text that was sent.
Copying a folder, and moving one to a different project, are background jobs: the call returns a tracking id and nothing else, and the only way to confirm the outcome is to re-read the destination.

project.title: Project
project.description: The top-level container that owns every folder, test case, run, plan and report.
key_facts: Project ids come in two forms that are not interchangeable: an integer id and a PR-NNN identifier. Nearly every v1 project capability takes the integer; the v2 routes take PR-NNN. Read a project once to get both.
A project the caller cannot see is reported as 'not found' rather than 'forbidden', so a missing project and a permission gap look identical.
Projects are never deleted through the capabilities in this index — a project created by mistake can only be removed in the product UI.

Project settings are stored as free-form name/value pairs and keep no history: overwriting one loses the previous value, and a setting that was never written simply has no entry rather than a default.
Project-level analytics are aggregate counters only; none of the dashboard figures can be drilled down to the individual cases or runs behind them.
Listing projects and searching inside a project are different surfaces with different pagination: project listings cap at 300 per page, in-project search at 300 for test cases and 30 for test runs.

report.title: Report
report.description: A saved, optionally scheduled analytics view over a project's test data.
key_facts: report_id and schedule_id are INTEGERS; the parent project takes the INTEGER project id (v1).

report_type on create/update is a DISPLAY NAME and the set is CLOSED — exactly these nine: Test Run Summary, Test Run Detailed Report, Test Plan Summary, Requirement Traceability Report, Test Case Activity, Exploratory Session Summary, User Workload Report, Defects Summary, Defects Detailed Report. Never invent one and never substitute a neighbouring type: if the user asks for activity, it is 'Test Case Activity', not 'Test Run Summary'.

Defects Summary and Defects Detailed Report are accepted on create but have no data branch — they always read back report_data: null. For defect counts use Test Run Summary's issues_by_priority / issues_by_status sections instead.

null inside report_data means NOT COMPUTED, not 'no data'. A Test Case Activity report fills its headline counts on a bare read; a Test Run Summary leaves issues_data / test_run_status / test_cases_status / issues_by_priority / issues_by_status null until you name them in sections. Never conclude 'there is no defect or status data' from a null — request the section; an empty payload like {total: 0} is a real finding, null is not. And never answer a 400 on sections by retreating to a bare read.
*_drilldown sections return PAGINATED ROWS, not aggregates — never tally rows into a count; read the aggregate section or report_data.

frequency + frequency_details travel together or not at all; omit both for an unscheduled on-demand report. weekly needs day as a lowercase name, monthly needs day as an integer 1-28. There is no 'once'. report_timeframe: custom REQUIRES custom_date_range.
"Understand a report" = fetch the report + its section/widget data and summarise agent-side; the API returns structured data, not narrative.
There is a tenth report type, Test Plan Detailed Report, hidden behind a per-group feature flag — creating, reading or exporting one without the flag is refused as not permitted.

A report is found by its id within your group, not within the project you name: the project you address it through does not narrow the lookup, so an id belonging to a sibling project still resolves (and still deletes).

Reports are not versioned and there is no undo. An edit replaces the entire definition — every field you leave out is cleared, and filters you leave out are deleted — and a delete is permanent, silent, and reports success even for an id that never existed.

Whether a report is scheduled is inferred, never declared: it is scheduled exactly when both a cadence and its details are present. Drop either one on an edit and the report stops emailing. Recipients are only stored on a scheduled report.

A report can span up to 60 projects, but only for Test Run Summary, Test Plan Summary, Test Run Detailed, Test Plan Detailed, Test Case Activity, Requirement Traceability and User Workload — and User Workload stops at 5.

Exporting a report is asynchronous and the finished file never comes back through the API: the export hands over a job channel only. Mailing the report to an address is the only way to obtain the file itself.
Listing reports is fixed at 30 per page and always newest-first; the page size cannot be changed and asking for a page past the end is an error rather than an empty page.
Requirement Traceability reports have a grain — test case (default) or test plan — fixed when the report is created and refused on any later edit.

result.title: Result
result.description: The recorded outcome of one test case in one run: its status, and who set it.
key_facts: Bodies are wrapped in test_result; set status by NAME (status) or id (status_id) — use a real configured status (see statuses-and-states).

bulk-delete SUCCEEDS PARTIALLY and still returns 200.
